articles.title: It's not a joke — the viral Casio F-B100W Bluetooth step tracking watch is incredibly accurate, even compared to an Apple Watch Ultra 4
articles.text:
I tested my Apple Watch Ultra 4 against Casio's cheap step-counting retro watch, the Casio F-B100W — and both watches' calculations were shockingly similar, despite the huge price difference
A very small difference in steps recorded
If you've been following TechRadar's fitness coverage over the last couple of months, you'll have heard about the Casio F-B100W.
It's a cheap Bluetooth digital watch — ($65 / £55 / AU$119) and despite looking very similar to the classic, extremely cheap F-91W, it's got some differences. It's a little bit bigger, it's got an additional button, a dual time-zone mode, and, crucially for our purposes, a few smart features thanks to its Bluetooth capability: Find My Phone, and a step tracker.
This stripped-back approach to smartwatches is great for people who are looking to increase their activity levels, but don't want to pay for a smartwatch or use all the bells and whistles of a full-fledged fitness tracker. In fact, it reminds me of the very first Fitbits, which were simple pebble-shaped Bluetooth-enabled step trackers that clipped to your clothes.
I had a lot of fun with this watch, as I loved the retro styling, and it had just enough smarts to be useful. As a perpetual phone-misplacer, Find My Phone functionality is an essential for me for any smartwatch, while the most basic movement-based metric of step tracking remains useful even today. In the app, your step counts are broken into bar charts over a week, month or year to analyze trends.
But, considering the extraordinary cheap price of the watch, I was wondering how accurate it could be. So I decided to test it against this year's best smartwatch, the Apple Watch Ultra 4. The Ultra 4 costs $799 / £749 / AU$1,349, a far cry from the cost of the Casio, and is equipped with top-of-the-range fitness metrics for every eventuality.
To start with, it's worth noting that I can't separate the Casio's daily step counter into a specific workout, so by the time I'd strapped both watches on, and gone up and down the stairs putting my shoes on, finding my keys and earphones, and stepping out to the starting point of my run, I had already walked 269 steps, and that was reflected in the Casio's score. Not the best start to the experiment.
However, after the run was complete, I checked the scores on both apps immediately. Once the Apple Watch's workout was marked as 'complete' it stopped tracking my steps, so I didn't want to make the same mistake again and inflate the Casio's score. The moment I finished my workout on the Apple Watch, I screenshotted both apps.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
And I was impressed. The Casio recorded a score of 4,910 steps. Minus my initial 269 steps, that leaves us at 4,641 steps in total for the Casio F-B100W.
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 recorded 4,679, a difference of just 38 steps. That's a teeny margin of error for two completely different watches in two completely different price brackets, operating solely on estimations from their onboard sensors, and I'm thrilled with this result.
What does this mean in practice? It means that if all you're interested in is tracking your steps, and you like the retro digital watch vibe (after all, retro tech has been making a comeback for a while now) I can say that the humble Casio F-B100W was just as good a step counter as the most expensive Apple Watch on the market, and I can double-down on my recommendation. It's a great watch.
Admittedly, it doesn't have the other advanced metrics of the Apple Watch (or any other metrics, for that matter), but this test was an exercise in testing the Casio step counter's quality, not objectively comparing the two watches — and it passed that test with flying colors.

Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.

articles.title: One soldier, two jets, one thumb: Cummings Aerospace fires 3D-printed Hellhounds from a Buggy
articles.text:
One soldier, two jets, one thumb: Cummings Aerospace fires 3D-printed Hellhounds from a Buggy
Strike power that once took a whole artillery battery now runs off a handheld controller and a Polaris buggy
- Cummings Aerospace fired two 3D-printed Hellhound S3 jet drones from a buggy-mounted launcher, a first for the weapon
- One operator sent both drones on separate autonomous missions using a single handheld fire control system
- The new launcher holds up to eight drones, and Cummings plans to fire it next from unmanned ground and naval vehicles
A small American defense firm has just shown what mass-produced, 3D-printed air power could look like in the field, and it fits on the back of a utility vehicle.
Cummings Aerospace has fired two of its 3D-printed Hellhound S3 jet-powered drones from a launcher mounted on a Polaris buggy, with a single operator using one handheld controller to send both drones off on separate autonomous missions.
The company says the test met all its objectives and marks several firsts for the turbojet weapon.
Moving drones from a bagpack to a buggy?
The demonstration took place on August 25, 2026, at the Pendleton UAS Range in Oregon, where a firm engineer fired the two Hellhounds one after the other. Both carried inert payloads and flew different preplanned routes at different speeds; the results were announced on October 12 2026.
Until now, the Hellhound had flown only in its man-portable form in more than a dozen flight tests. This was the first time it had been fired from a vehicle, the first use of a new launcher that can hold up to eight drones, the first ripple-fire of the S3, and the first time a single operator controlled more than one Hellhound at once.
Before launch, the operator programmed each drone's waypoints, altitudes, and flight path into the handheld fire control system. Once airborne, the drones flew those routes on their own while streaming data back, so the operator could watch both flights live and redirect or abort either mission.
The play here is about doing more with fewer people: CEO Sheila Cummings put it, instead of manually flying a single drone to a target, one soldier using one fire control system can simultaneously put multiple Hellhounds on multiple targets.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The Hellhound S3 is roughly the size of a baseball bat and weighs about 13 pounds. Its turbojet engine lets it fly more than 60 km (37 miles) at speeds up to 618 km/h (384 mph), putting it in a different class from the propeller-driven quadcopters and loitering munitions that have come to define the war in Ukraine.
It is also much easier to build, leveraging 3D-printed and commercial off-the-shelf components that allow for easy modifications, repairs, and mass production if needed. Cummings Aerospace frames the Hellhound as a multi-mission weapon rather than a single-trick munition. It can work as a loitering munition, a precision-guided munition, a one-way attack drone, or a counter-drone interceptor.
Operators can swap between four mission modules, covering armor-piercing, blast-fragmentation, electronic warfare, and decoy roles, in under two minutes without tools.
The company has previously said the turbojet's documented top speed lets it chase and destroy smaller Group 2 and 3 drones, giving it a hunter-killer role against other UAVs.
That counter-drone angle is arguably the most important here because the threat it is built to answer keeps getting smarter and cheaper; A recent report on a NATO-backed drone AI that picked its own target and struck it, and the US Army showing off its in-house "Dragoons" drone fitted with 3D-printed bombs are merely the tip of the iceberg. Cheap, printable airframes are becoming the common currency of modern conflict, on both the giving and receiving ends.
Much of the appeal of the Hellhound S3 as a viable counter lies in its manufacturing process. The Hellhound is built largely with commercially available 3D printers in-house, which is central to Cummings' goal of producing at least 100 S3 airframes a month and her stated interest in licensing the design to US and international partners for distributed production.
In an era where drone tariffs and supply chains have become a strategic concern, a weapon you can print close to the front is as much a logistics argument as a battlefield one, and one can assume that the Hellhound S3 is but the first of many that will eventually make it to the modern battlefield in different shapes, sizes, and capabilities.

articles.title: Apple just got slapped for 'non-competitive conduct' by Australia’s top court — and ordered to allow rival iPhone app stores Down Under
articles.text:
Apple just got slapped for 'non-competitive conduct' by Australia’s top court — and ordered to allow rival iPhone app stores Down Under
Court also orders that Epic Games’ Fortnite be returned to the Australian App Store
- Federal Court of Australia orders Apple to open up its iOS ecosystem in Australia to third-party app stores
- Apple is also ordered to restore Epic Games' Fortnite back onto the Australian App Store
- Apple denies it has a monopoly in Australia and plans to appeal the decision
The Federal Court of Australia has ordered Apple to fully open up its iOS ecosystem in the country to third-party competitors, with Justice Jonathan Beach ruling that the tech giant misused its market power to maintain a monopoly over app distribution and in-app payments.
The ruling has also ordered Apple to restore the video game Fortnite and other Epic Games apps back onto the Australian App Store, six years after the Cupertino tech giant banned the game for bypassing Apple’s payment systems.
Both orders are set to take effect at noon Australian Eastern time on March 1, 2027.
“In response to regulatory or judicial constraints imposed in connection with the App Store that are anything other than detailed, prescriptive and precise, Apple has systematically implemented practices that seek to circumvent the practical effects of those constraints,” the ruling read.
Beach also said that Apple “devised and pursued a deliberate and comprehensive strategy of foreclosure in relation to iOS app distribution.”
An Apple spokesperson told TechRadar that the company “does not have a monopoly position in Australia or in any market around the world. We respectfully disagree with many findings in this case, including a market definition that has been rejected by other courts.
“We will request a stay and appeal the outcome to seek a resolution that respects our intellectual property and protects the safe, secure experience that consumers and developers expect from the App Store.”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Apple has until February 15 to appeal this decision.
TechRadar has also contacted Epic Games for comment, though Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney took to X (formerly Twitter) to celebrate the ruling.
Apple and Epic Games have been going back and forth in courts ever since the former removed Fortnite from the Apple App Store in August 2020 for selling the in-game currency V-bucks in a way that would circumvent Apple’s 30% commission fee on in-app purchases.
Last year, the US Supreme Court also ruled that Apple engaged in anti-competitive conduct and pricing. A separate ruling in 2024, meanwhile, forced Apple to allow US customers to add links and buttons inside their apps that bring them out to a website where they can input credit card information, though it ultimately didn’t grant Epic Games’ petition to open iOS to competing stores and payments. Sweeney, at the time, called the ruling “a sad outcome for all developers”.
No more loopholes?
With Apple looking to appeal this ruling, these changes are far from guaranteed to happen in March next year, but it would be interesting to see if the tech giant will adopt a similar “compliance through friction” strategy in Australia.
The 2024 ruling above saw Apple implement a 27% commission on transactions completed on those external websites, a disclosure warning and restricted developers from using traditional buttons or persuasive calls-to-action language.
The European Union’s Digital Markets Act (DMA) forced Apple to allow third-party app stores, sideloading (installing apps through websites) and alternative in-app payments. Apple, instead, found workarounds like implementing a “Core Technology Fee” (charging developers that opt out of the App Store 50 euro cents per first annual install regardless of whether the developer made any money), using convoluted and multi-step installation processes for third-party app stores and requiring alternate app store developers to secure a $1 million standby letter of credit.
Justice Beach called them “deterrence tactics”, saying the fees blocked “any genuine prospect of competition” and explicitly addressed those “disproportionate frictions”, non-neutral disclosure sheets and discriminatory fees in the ruling.
The ruling outlines specific bans that Apple has to follow:
- implementing the Core Technology Fee
- 27% commissions on on transactions done through external websites
- disclosure sheets
- forcing developers into new, bundled contracts just to use alternative distribution
- requiring developers to also display Apple’s In-App Purchase (IAP) button alongside their preferred payment method
- forcing developers to appoint Apple as their legal "agent" for marketing and delivery.
Some potential workarounds that Apple may explore could be under the guise of “security standards”, using user interface design to discourage users and aggressive geofencing, or we could even see something completely different.
In any case, this is far from the last time that Apple and Epic Games will face each other in court, with Apple’s appeal to the US Supreme Court scheduled for sometime during its October 2026–2027 term. The EU is still actively investigating Apple while Epic Games continues to challenge Cupertino’s policies under the DMA.

articles.title: Epic Offers $65,000 in Prizes to Vibe Code a Game in Four Days, Then Makes AI Optional
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Epic Offers $65,000 in Prizes to Vibe Code a Game in Four Days, Then Makes AI Optional
Epic Games has announced the 2026 Epic AI MegaJam, a game jam that encourages entrants to use any AI tools they like, from asset generation to coding agents. After a theme reveal on November 11, teams of up to five people (plus as many AI agents as they want) get from November 12 to 15 to build a game in Unreal Engine or UEFN. The cash prizes add up to $65,000, with $7,500 going to the winners of Best Overall in Unreal Engine, Best Overall in UEFN and Best Student Project, and smaller awards for things like best visuals, best mobile game and best dev log on AI tool use. Standout entries can also get Development Continuation Grants of up to $50,000 to keep working on them after the jam.
Interestingly, the jam's FAQ first said at first that participants had to use AI, which Epic later walked back and called a mistake, clarifying that people can use as much or as little AI as they want. The promo art features a hand with six fingers, apparently a nod to AI image generation errors, next to the tagline "Vibe your way to $50K." Reactions online have been quite negative as expected, with people pointing out that jams like Ludum Dare have been producing quick prototypes since 2002 without any help from AI. Many were unhappy that Epic was promoting "AI slop" in such a direct way.The jam is part of a much bigger AI push at Epic, which reportedly moved an unannounced Disney shooter to AI-first development and recently said its new launcher was vibe coded. CEO Tim Sweeney has also called Steam's AI disclosure labels "irresponsible", so the AI-focused jam shouldn't come as a surprise. Industry response to AI-generated content in video games still remains largely negative, and fan sentiment is even more unanimous in this regard.

articles.title: Every wild thing I learned about the iPhone Duo by answering your AMA questions
articles.text:
Every wild thing I learned about the iPhone Duo by answering your AMA questions
You had so many questions
The Apple iPhone Duo is the rare Apple product that has not received universally glowing or negative reviews. Opinions are split over its lack of Face ID support, iPhone 17 Pro-grade cameras (but without the telephoto lens), and slightly hefty frame when folded. It's also generated more interest in an iPhone than I've seen in years, and when I followed my exhaustive, generally positive review with a pair of AMAs (Ask Me Anything) on Threads and X, I was flooded with questions. My Threads post alone has 1,300 comments.
Granted, not every question was about the Duo. Many took the "Anything" part literally and asked me about everything from my hairline to their favorite color. I played along as I fielded myriad queries about Apple's first folding device. Over 24 hours, I reiterated many points from my review, which I doubt many read, but I also learned a thing or two I missed while testing the product.
Here are some of the highlights:
For my iPhone Duo review, I placed the folded phone on multiple MagSafe charge stands and holders. The MagSafe magnets sit on the back, right under the camera array, and the Duo fits perfectly on each stand. With charge stands, the Duo instantly slips into the redesigned Standby mode. I love it.
Someone on Threads asked me if I had tried unfolding the Duo and putting it on a MagSafe stand. So I did and quickly found that the weight of the half not attached to the charging stand made the entire phone rotate ever so slowly on the MagSafe charger. So, while you could use the unfolded Duo on a MagSafe charging stand, it is not recommended.
After someone else asked if they could still use their MagSafe Wallet, I found that the Duo's back is too short to accommodate the standard MagSafe Wallet.
With its two differently sized screens, the iPhone Duo is unique in the iPhone lineup, and there were reasonable questions about how features like vertical Wallpaper images work across the cover and inner display.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
I didn't know, so I set the cover wallpaper as a vertical photo I took with the Duo of the Empire State Building, and I gotta say, I love the handoff between displays. The Cover display showed the iconic building, and when I opened the Duo, it showed more of the photo.
There were a lot of questions about the Duo's split-screen capabilities, like if I could open more than two apps (no, but you can do a PiP video overlay), and if you could drag and drop content from one screen to another (you can).
Some wondered if you could run the same app on both screens. You cannot, but if you want to maximize your social media, I found that you could run TikTok and Instagram Reels in side-by-side windows. It's social media turned up to 11.
During my review, I tried running the Kindle app, but the app wasn't optimized for the device and looked tiny and useless. Someone asked me about "iBooks," which is now known as Books.
As a first-party app, it's optimized for Duo, of course. Flipping virtual pages on the 7.6-inch inner display is a transporting experience.
Many wondered whether I hated the matte finish on the inner display (I don't), but I also got a ton of questions about the crease and the inner display's overall durability. A few wanted to know if I'd scratched it, either purposefully or by accident, with my fingernail. I had not, honestly; I don't even see fingerprints on the matte display.
A couple of people asked about the visibility of the crease and whether that area of the screen bounced or wobbled when I touched it. So I tested it by opening the phone and pressing down on the essentially invisible crease. No movement.
Many had obviously heard that not every app is optimized for the new inner display. In my review, I noted that LinkedIn and Gmail were particularly poor fits and later found that Adobe Acrobat still wasn't optimized. But developers are constantly delivering updates, so apps that didn't work yesterday look great today.
Still, people wanted to know how apps deal with the handoff from the 5.4-inch outer display to the 7.6-inch inner one. Optimized apps handle it smoothly; most simply expand without losing context.
Some, like DeckMan and Toastie, playfully use the two screens to create entertaining interplays. DeckMan, for instance, turns the duo into a virtual portable tape deck.
An almost equal number shared their concerns about the size of the 5.4-inch cover display. It's actually not that small, but Apple's decision to place the Dock vertically on the right-hand side means that you lose a lot of pixels to what is often empty space. Others complained about the lack of support for left-handed users (they kept asking me if I was left-handed). Some are even bothered by the dock's placement on the much larger inner display. You can't move it, and this will probably remain a key issue for many potential Duo owners.
Every single iPhone model now supports Face ID, with the notable exception of the new Duo. It's probably the single biggest Duo misstep, and many asked me if I was having trouble adjusting to using Touch ID again. Initially, I was, but I have gotten used to it. I hope the next Duo brings back facial recognition.
I probably got a dozen or so questions about battery life. Some reviewers have criticized the Duo for subpar battery life if you mainly use the larger inner screen. I did not find that, but I did field quite a few battery life questions from concerned potential buyers. I told them what my tests found: all-day battery life in a variety of situations.
I struggled a bit when people asked me to compare the Duo to the iPhone 18 Pro Max. I get it; they want to know if they should stick with what they know or, perhaps, try the awesome new thing. It's not easy, though, to directly compare the single-screen iPhone 18 Pro Max with the dual-display Duo. But leaving aside the screens, if you focus on, say, the cameras, you might stick with the 18 Pro Max, which offers a telephoto and a variable-aperture main camera. The Duo is also heavier than the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which might be a deal-breaker for some.
There were also a healthy number of comparisons to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 lineup, especially the similarly sized and shaped Galaxy Z Fold 8. A few asked me to compare the cameras. Turns out that both the Z Fold 8 and Duo have just two external cameras: wide and ultra-wide, and the Z Fold 8 has just a couple of megapixels per camera on the Duo. Ultimately, it's a wash on the camera front.
I got just as many questions about the cameras' quality, including the 12MP Center Stage camera on the outside and the 4MP inner camera. I found it interesting that many knew not to directly compare it to the new iPhone 18 Pro Max lenses and instead focused on the more comparable iPhone 17 Pro's wide and ultrawide. In my testing, I found the imagery was just as good as what I got from that now year-old device. I do, however, miss the telephoto lens.
One person actually asked how this iPhone Duo is different from the Surface Duo that Microsoft launched in 2019 and discontinued in 2024. I gently explained that while the Surface Duo's inner screen had two displays, the iPhone Duo offers one flexible inner display.
Apple hasn't said much about Apple Pencil support, but that may be because the Duo currently only supports the Apple Pencil USB-C. Why? It's the only one that you can still charge separately from, say, a tablet. Apple Pencil Pro needs the iPad to charge. The Duo cannot charge another device. As one Threads user put it, "Which basically means that my Pencil Pro is useless?" Mine too, my friend, mine, too.

articles.title: El exjefe de seguridad de OpenAI volvió a la empresa al advertir que la IA entró en un nuevo nivel de riesgo
articles.text:
Aleksander Madry, exjefe del equipo de Preparación de OpenAI, anunció que regresará a la empresa meses después de haberse ido, para trabajar junto al científico jefe Jakub Pachocki en los riesgos de seguridad que plantea una inteligencia artificial cada vez más capaz.
Madry comunicó su regreso en una publicacón en X, en el que describió su salida en mayo de 2026 como algo que “terminó pareciéndose más a un año sabático”. “Cuando me fui hace unos meses, sentí que lo más importante era enfocarme en hacer que la IA fuera más útil para la gente”, escribió.
“Pero desde entonces entramos en un régimen distinto de avance de la IA, uno en el que resolver bien los desafíos de seguridad de una IA cada vez más capaz tiene que volverse una prioridad central”, agregó Madry en el mismo mensaje.
Pachocki le respondió en la misma red social que le había pedido a Madry que volviera para trabajar junto a él en “preguntas sobre el ritmo y las implicancias del avance” de la tecnología y cómo deberían influir en la estrategia de OpenAI. “Valoro su criterio y me alegra tenerlo de nuevo en el equipo”, escribió.
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, también celebró la decisión. “Estoy muy agradecido de que Aleksander haya aceptado nuestro pedido de encargarse de esto; los desafíos de seguridad que tenemos por delante mientras enfrentamos la superinteligencia son inmensos, y él tiene un conjunto de habilidades excelente para trabajar en esto”, afirmó en X.
Madry se unió a OpenAI en 2023 y lideró Preparación, el equipo creado ese año para evaluar riesgos catastróficos de los modelos más avanzados de la empresa, entre ellos amenazas cibernéticas, biológicas y la posibilidad de que los sistemas actúen con mayor autonomía. A mediados de 2024 fue reasignado a un rol centrado en el razonamiento de la IA.
Cuando dejó la empresa en mayo, Madry describió sus casi tres años allí como “la experiencia de una vida” y dijo que quería enfocarse en cómo la IA podía transformar la economía, incluido el modo en que las empresas entienden información, toman decisiones y operan.
Antes de OpenAI, dirigió el Centro de Aprendizaje Automático Desplegable del MIT y fue cocoordinador del Foro de Políticas de IA de esa universidad, donde continúa en licencia de su cargo de profesor.
Modelo Astra, uno de los desafíos que tomrá Madry
El regreso de Madry llega después de que OpenAI calificara en septiembre de 2026 a Astra, uno de sus modelos en desarrollo, con el nivel “Crítico” de capacidad cibernética bajo su Marco de Preparación, según informó la propia empresa. Es el primer modelo al que le asigna ese nivel.
Según el comunicado de OpenAI, esa calificación implica que, con las herramientas y el acceso adecuados, Astra puede encontrar fallas de seguridad desconocidas y desarrollar formas de explotarlas en muchos sistemas bien protegidos sin que una persona guíe cada paso.
La compañía dijo que retrasó partes del desarrollo y el lanzamiento del modelo mientras reforzaba y probaba protecciones contra el mal uso y las acciones no autorizadas.
El área que Madry dirigía, Preparación, es justamente la que evalúa ese tipo de capacidades cibernéticas, además de riesgos biológicos y de autonomía de los modelos. Su regreso le da a OpenAI una figura con experiencia directa en ese marco de evaluación justo cuando la empresa enfrenta su primer caso de un modelo calificado en el nivel más alto de riesgo.
Un año de tensiones internas sobre seguridad
El regreso de Madry se produce en medio de una serie de salidas y advertencias de empleados vinculados a la seguridad de OpenAI. A comienzos de octubre de 2026, David Robinson, quien lideraba la redacción de los reportes de seguridad que acompañaban cada lanzamiento importante de la empresa, renunció y publicó un ensayo en The Atlantic titulado “Dejé OpenAI porque su cultura está rota”.
En ese texto, Robinson escribió que las empresas de IA, incluida OpenAI, “no están siendo lo suficientemente cuidadosas” al desarrollar sistemas cada vez más capaces, y que la industria necesita salvaguardas más cercanas a las de la aviación o la energía nuclear.
Un vocero de OpenAI respondió que la empresa continúa “fortaleciendo nuestras prácticas de seguridad para abordar los riesgos que vemos hoy”.
Ninguna de las publicaciones de Madry ni de Pachocki detalló el cargo formal que ocupará dentro de la empresa, y OpenAI no emitió un comunicado propio anunciando la contratación más allá de lo publicado por ambos en sus cuentas personales.
El foco inmediato del trabajo conjunto, según los propios mensajes, será definir qué controles de seguridad deben acompañar el desarrollo de los modelos más capaces antes de que lleguen a usuarios o sistemas externos.

articles.title: Une société vendait les numéros de ceux qui refusaient le démarchage téléphonique, l’amende atteint 300 000 euros
articles.text:
La DGCCRF a rendu publique une amende de 300 000 euros infligée contre AS MEDIA, une société de Seine-Saint-Denis. Elle vendait des fichiers de démarchage téléphonique contenant les numéros de consommateurs inscrits sur Bloctel.
Avant de faire sonner votre téléphone, le démarchage téléphonique a besoin d'un élément, une sorte de matière première, votre numéro. C'est ce commerce discret, celui des fichiers qui changent de mains, que les agents de la Répression des fraudes ont épinglé en Seine-Saint-Denis, avec une amende à six chiffres à la clé. La sanction a été rendue publique le jeudi 22 octobre 2026, un peu plus de deux mois après l'entrée en vigueur d'une réforme qui interdit désormais de vous appeler sans votre accord.
Des numéros de téléphone étaient vendus malgré le « non » de leurs titulaires
L'enquête en question a été menée par les agents de la répression des fraudes de la direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) de Seine-Saint-Denis. Dans leur viseur se trouvait la SAS AS MEDIA, une entreprise installée à Bobigny. La société, et c'est son premier manquement, n'informait pas les consommateurs de leur droit de s'inscrire sur la liste d'opposition au démarchage téléphonique, le fameux Bloctel, liste disparue depuis cet été. C'était pourtant une obligation légale, pas une formule de courtoisie.
Le second reproche est plus embarrassant encore pour AS MEDIA. L'entreprise est accusée par la Direction générale de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes (DGCCRF) d'avoir vendu des fichiers de données téléphoniques dans lesquels figuraient les coordonnées de personnes inscrites sur cette même liste.
Ceux qui avaient fait la démarche de se protéger voyaient donc leur numéro mis en vente, ce qui est assez ironique, et problématique. Au terme de l'enquête, la DDPP a prononcé une amende administrative de 300 000 euros contre la firme fautive.
Depuis le 11 août, le démarchage téléphonique se mérite
L'amende est très conséquente pour entreprise qui, depuis 2022 (1,14 million d'euros), a vu son résultat net dégringoler, à 608 000 euros en 2023 puis 49 000 euros en 2024. Selon nos informations, AS MEDIA serait actuellement en liquidation judiciaire.
Cela n'empêche pas la DGCCRF de rappeler que les sanctions pour démarchage illicite peuvent atteindre 375 000 euros pour une société, et que les amendes prononcées font l'objet d'une publication systématique. AS MEDIA rejoint une liste qui s'allonge, après les plus de 92 000 euros pour Le Betef, entreprise épinglée à la rentrée, et 6 millions d'euros en 2025 pour la société derrière la marque Délices & Gourmandises, qui avait cumulé les infractions.
Les manquements reprochés à AS MEDIA relèvent encore de Bloctel, qui a disparu le 11 août 2026 au profit de l'opt-in. Depuis, aucun appel commercial n'est permis sans votre accord préalable, sauf dans le cadre d'un contrat en cours ou pour vous proposer journaux et magazines. Cet accord dure un an au plus, ne vaut que pour la prospection qui vous a été annoncée et se retire à tout moment, même à l'oral. Le professionnel doit en conserver la preuve au moins trois ans. Les créneaux horaires et le plafond de quatre appels sur 30 jours restent en vigueur. Un fichier de numéros sans consentement en bonne et due forme devient donc plus encombrant qu'utile pour ceux qui l'achètent.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Joins Xbox Play Anywhere as Update 2.5 Goes Live
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Cyberpunk 2077 Joins Xbox Play Anywhere as Update 2.5 Goes Live
CD Projekt RED's Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 went live yesterday on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S and Mac, with the Switch 2 and Mac App Store versions due in the coming days. The studio announced the update on October 20 with just two confirmed features, and a YouTuber's early video filled in most of the rest. The leak was mostly right, though a few things changed. 
Dual-wielding isn't limited to pistols, since the Double Trouble perk also covers revolvers from the Power category and comes with four extra perks. The mystery Night City tour is called Welcome to Paradise and is narrated by Richard Night, while the Clampdown prequel quest rewards a five-piece gear set based on King. Glamdocs also handle the Monowire and Projectile Launch System, and 12 new Minor Arcana tarot cards are hidden around the city, something the leak didn't seem to mention. Mods come through mod.io as a curated selection, and the official notes list Switch 2 alongside PC, Mac, PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, although the leak suggested otherwise. Modded console saves can't earn achievements or trophies.PC players get DLSS 4.5 with up to 6X Multi Frame Generation, while FSR 3 upscaling is gone, leaving FSR 2.1, FSR 4 and FSR 3.1 frame generation. Consoles finally get an FOV slider. Separately, CDPR added Xbox Play Anywhere support on October 21, so a digital Xbox copy now also runs on Windows PCs and handhelds through the Xbox app, with shared saves and achievements at no extra cost. It only covers Xbox and Microsoft Store purchases, so Steam and GOG copies don't count.

articles.title: A $620M subsea cable would link Canada directly to Norway
articles.text:
Norwegian firm pitches new undersea cable which will bypass the US entirely — 2,800-mile link aims to connect Europe and Canada
Canada seeks $620 million subsea cable to Europe
- Canada is exploring alternative data routes amid worsening relations with Washington
- Norwegian firm Bulk proposes a 2,800-mile cable bypassing American territory entirely
- The proposed transatlantic connection could cost more than $620 million
Worsening relations between Washington and Ottawa have prompted Canada to explore alternatives to relying on the United States for international data connections.
Norwegian company Bulk is proposing a 2,800-mile undersea cable linking southern Norway with Newfoundland and Labrador before continuing across Canada without passing through American territory.
The company is seeking a Canadian majority partner to help finance the Leif Erikson project, which is expected to cost more than $620 million.
Leif Erikson offers an alternative transatlantic route
The planned connection would reach Happy Valley-Goose Bay before following an underground route through Quebec towards Montreal, requiring additional construction across Canadian territory.
Bulk co-founder Peder Nærbø has promoted the proposal as part of a Canadian sovereign communications network designed to provide direct access to European infrastructure.
According to details presented to prospective investors, the system would support high-capacity data transfers for AI, telecommunications and large-scale computing operations.
Nærbø has questioned the resilience of Canada's international communications infrastructure, arguing that its existing connections leave the country vulnerable to disruptions.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Bulk has spent approximately five years trying to advance the initiative, although securing the necessary approvals, investment and partners remains a substantial obstacle.
The company has already installed more than 6,200 miles of cable across land and underwater routes, supporting its activities in digital infrastructure and connectivity.
Its stated ambition is to help Nordic renewable electricity supply the energy requirements of digital infrastructure, including facilities serving computing-intensive industries.
Canadian ownership and regulatory challenges
Despite attracting potential backers, the project still requires additional financing, regulatory approvals and agreement between Canadian and European authorities on its route.
Bulk has considerable Canadian financial ties, with 65% of the company owned by a property subsidiary of Sun Life Financial, alongside investments from several Canadian pension funds.
However, existing Canadian ownership does not eliminate the need to secure a majority partner willing to support the project's development and construction.
Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly met Nærbø earlier this year, although her department declined to comment specifically on Leif Erikson.
According to Bloomberg, the department said that protecting infrastructure security and resilience remained a priority for Prime Minister Mark Carney's government.
Canada has relatively few international submarine cable connections that avoid American territory, and none is owned by a Canadian company.
One major alternative, the Topaz cable, connects Canada and Japan and belongs to Alphabet, Google's parent company.
The European Union and Canada must still coordinate the proposed cable's route and approve the project before construction can advance.
Its planned underground section would cover approximately 1,180 miles within Canada, requiring support from Indigenous communities along the route.
Canada and Europe also intend to endorse a statement in Montreal on October 29, 2026 concerning improved digital connections between Europe, Canada and Asia.

articles.title: Cuatro creencias falsas sobre criptomonedas que todos deben conocer, según Binance
articles.text:
Se ha desarmado cuatro mitos que rodean al mundo de las criptomonedas desde hace más de una década: que solo sirven para especular, que son inseguras, que exigen conocimientos técnicos y que operan al margen del sistema financiero tradicional.
Binance, la plataforma global de activos digitales, sostiene que los datos actuales contradicen esas creencias instaladas y que entender cómo funciona el ecosistema se volvió una necesidad para millones de personas que ya lo usan para pagar, enviar dinero e invertir.
Qué uso real tienen las criptomonedas más allá de la especulación
Durante años, la discusión sobre las criptomonedas se concentró casi exclusivamente en la variación de los precios. Sin embargo, el comportamiento de los usuarios muestra un giro hacia la utilidad cotidiana.
Las stablecoins, activos digitales diseñados para mantener un valor estable y generalmente vinculado al dólar, se consolidaron como una herramienta para pagar, transferir fondos y proteger los ahorros frente a la devaluación.
Los registros de Binance Pay reflejan ese cambio de comportamiento. En 2023, gran parte de las operaciones eran transferencias de apenas un dólar, que los usuarios realizaban para probar si la tecnología funcionaba correctamente. En la actualidad, la plataforma contabiliza micropagos que rondan los 18 dólares, vinculados a transacciones reales y no a pruebas.
A esto se suma que alrededor del 60% de los pagos con stablecoins que observa la plataforma en cuestión corresponde a operaciones transfronterizas, lo que confirma su rol como mecanismo de envío de dinero entre países.
Las criptomonedas dejaron de ser exclusivamente un instrumento de inversión: hoy forman parte de la vida diaria de millones de personas que las utilizan para pagar, enviar y recibir dinero de forma habitual.
Cómo se protege a usuarios frente a estafas y fraudes
Uno de los prejuicios más extendidos sostiene que el ecosistema cripto es inseguro por naturaleza. Frente a eso, la plataforma destaca las inversiones en tecnología de protección y el funcionamiento propio de la blockchain como factores que refuerzan la seguridad.
En el primer semestre de 2026, los sistemas de riesgo de la plataforma impulsados por IA ayudaron a proteger a más de 8 millones de usuarios y a prevenir aproximadamente 4.600 millones de dólares en pérdidas potenciales.
En ese mismo período, la plataforma interceptó millones de intentos de estafa y phishing, incluyó en listas negras más de 42.000 direcciones maliciosas y emitió más de 14.000 advertencias diarias en tiempo real.
Para sostener ese nivel de control, opera más de 100 modelos de inteligencia artificial dedicados a tareas antifraude y antiestafa, con analistas humanos que supervisan los casos de mayor riesgo. A eso se suma un Red Team interno que somete a prueba las defensas de la compañía como lo haría un atacante real.
La transparencia propia de la tecnología blockchain también cumple un papel en esta ecuación. Cada transacción queda registrada de forma permanente, lo que permite rastrear el origen y el movimiento de los fondos y facilita la cooperación con las autoridades.
Solo entre enero y junio de 2026, la plataforma respondió más de 36.000 solicitudes de fuerzas de seguridad de distintos países. Con sistemas de protección sólidos y cooperación judicial, el ecosistema cripto puede ofrecer altos estándares de seguridad, siempre que el usuario elija plataformas responsables y aprenda a cuidar sus propios activos.
Educación financiera e IA para usuarios sin experiencia previa
La idea de que operar con criptomonedas requiere conocimientos técnicos o financieros avanzados es otro de los mitos que la plataforma busca desmontar. La compañía sostiene que la educación es un componente central para facilitar el ingreso de nuevos usuarios al ecosistema.
Binance Academy, la plataforma educativa de la empresa, reúne a más de 40 millones de usuarios en el mundo y está disponible en 23 idiomas, lo que la convierte en un recurso de alcance global para quienes buscan informarse antes de operar.
Cabe señalar que existe una herramienta gratuita que adapta la información de mercado al nivel de conocimiento e interés de cada usuario, con vistas simplificadas para principiantes y resúmenes de mercado disponibles en texto o audio.
No hace falta ser experto en tecnología o en mercados financieros para comenzar a usar criptomonedas: alcanza con informarse, y hoy existen más herramientas que nunca, desde academias virtuales hasta asistentes con inteligencia artificial, para facilitar ese proceso de aprendizaje.
Qué relación existe entre las criptomonedas y las finanzas tradicionales
Durante mucho tiempo, el ecosistema cripto fue percibido como un circuito paralelo y desconectado del sistema financiero convencional. Esa frontera, sin embargo, se volvió cada vez más difusa en los últimos años.
Un ejemplo de esa convergencia es la alianza entre Binance y Circle, emisor de la stablecoin USDC. En septiembre de 2026, ambas compañías anunciaron una inversión de capital de 100 millones de dólares y un acuerdo comercial de cinco años orientado a impulsar el uso de USDC dentro de la plataforma.
Las stablecoins funcionan como un puente entre las finanzas tradicionales y la infraestructura cripto, y amplían el acceso a productos financieros que antes resultaban difíciles de alcanzar para buena parte de los usuarios.

articles.title: Capcom confirme une fuite de données de 11,7 millions de comptes
articles.text:
Un intrus a récupéré les adresses e-mail de 11,7 millions de comptes Capcom ID chez l’éditeur de Resident Evil et de Monster Hunter. Aucun numéro de carte bancaire n’a fuité, mais si des escrocs écrivent aux joueurs au nom de Capcom, ils pourront citer la date de leur dernière connexion et l’adresse IP utilisée ce jour-là.
Capcom a repéré l’intrusion le 19 octobre et l’a signalée deux jours plus tard à la police d’Osaka. Au total, 11 774 247 enregistrements sont concernés dans le monde, d’après le communiqué publié par l’éditeur. Chacun contient l’adresse e-mail, les dates de création du compte et de dernière connexion, le nombre de connexions et la dernière adresse IP. Capcom n’a trouvé aucune trace d’une fuite des mots de passe choisis par les joueurs, mais l’intrus a modifié celui de 196 comptes, et l’éditeur n’explique pas comment. Des arnaqueurs disposent maintenant de millions d’adresses actives de joueurs, avec de quoi personnaliser leurs messages.
196 mots de passe changés, une méthode d’attaque que Capcom garde secrète
L’éditeur japonais affirme avoir identifié la technique de l’intrus et bloqué son accès, mais il ne donne aucun détail. Il ne précise pas non plus depuis quand l’intrus circulait dans ses systèmes, et BleepingComputer note que la date réelle de l’intrusion est encore inconnue.
Comment l’intrus a-t-il pu changer le mot de passe de 196 comptes, alors que les mots de passe d’origine n’ont pas fuité d’après Capcom ? Pour le site américain, l’intrus cherchait à empêcher leurs propriétaires de se connecter. Capcom a réinitialisé ces 196 mots de passe. Pour 43 joueurs, l’éditeur a aussi constaté la fuite de la date de naissance, du genre, du pays et du pseudo.
Avec un Capcom ID détourné, l’intrus peut se connecter à la place du joueur sur le portail où celui-ci relie ses comptes PlayStation, Xbox, Steam ou Nintendo. L’entreprise promet une enquête approfondie et des mesures contre une récidive. « Capcom prend cette affaire extrêmement au sérieux », écrit-elle dans son communiqué.
Faux e-mails au nom de Capcom, les vérifications à faire
Capcom prévient que des escrocs pourraient utiliser les données volées et envoyer des messages frauduleux en son nom, ou au nom de ses partenaires. Il demande de ne cliquer sur aucun lien et de n’ouvrir aucune pièce jointe d’un e-mail suspect. Si un message cite la date de votre dernière connexion ou votre adresse IP, ne le prenez surtout pas pour une preuve d’authenticité, car ces deux informations font partie du lot volé.
Devant un lien douteux, Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr conseille de le survoler avec la souris sans cliquer, afin d’afficher l’adresse réelle, et de vérifier sur votre compte la date de votre dernière connexion. Le plus sûr est de saisir directement l’adresse du portail Capcom ID dans votre navigateur, comme on vous le recommandait après la fuite des profils de l’École 42.
Capcom ne vous demande pas de changer de mot de passe, et vous pouvez conserver votre adresse e-mail actuelle. Si vous utilisiez votre mot de passe Capcom ID sur d’autres sites, changez-le sur ces sites en commençant par votre messagerie principale. Un conseil qu'on vous a donné à propos des patients de l’AP-HP. Capcom ID propose aussi une double authentification par application sur smartphone, avec un code de secours à garder en lieu sûr.
Les parents doivent ouvrir l’œil, eux aussi. Capcom accepte les moins de 13 ans sur son portail Capcom ID depuis janvier 2025, quel que soit leur pays. Automaton rappelle que les joueurs de Street Fighter 6 passent par ce compte pour les parties en ligne. L’adresse de votre enfant peut donc figurer dans le lot.
Capcom a promis de contacter les joueurs concernés, et répond aux questions en Europe par un formulaire d’assistance dédié. Les joueurs pourront donc recevoir, à quelques jours d’écart, un vrai courrier de l’éditeur et un faux, et ne feront le tri qu’en se connectant directement au portail Capcom ID.

articles.title: LattePanda Launches LattePanda Sigma 2: The Embeddable AI Single Board Server
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
LattePanda Launches LattePanda Sigma 2: The Embeddable AI Single Board Server
The LattePanda Team today launched LattePanda Sigma 2, an x86 single-board server designed to bring high-performance local AI computing directly into intelligent products and systems. Built around the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H processor with Intel Arc B390 graphics, LattePanda Sigma 2 delivers up to 180 TOPS of total AI performance at INT8 in a compact form factor.
As "The Embeddable AI Single Board Server," LattePanda Sigma 2 combines high-performance computing, up to 64 GB of memory, high-speed networking, flexible expansion, and real-time hardware control in a single board. Rather than sitting alongside a product, it is designed to be integrated directly into the product itself, supporting applications from autonomous robots and vision systems to professional instruments and private AI appliances.LattePanda Sigma 2 combines the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 GPU, and integrated NPU to deliver up to 180 TOPS of total AI performance at INT8. It features a 16-core CPU with up to 4.8 GHz clock speed, a 12 Xe-core Intel Arc B390 GPU delivering up to 122 TOPS of INT8 AI performance, and an NPU capable of up to 50 TOPS.
With up to 64 GB of LPDDR5X-8533 RAM and 136.5 GB/s memory bandwidth, LattePanda Sigma 2 provides the capacity and throughput required for demanding local AI workloads. Up to 59 GB of VRAM can be allocated for AI workloads, providing enough room for 35B-class quantized MoE models and the KV cache required by long-context AI agents. With INT4 quantization and OpenVINO, the system can run the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model locally at around 30 tokens per second.
Built for Local AI Systems
LattePanda Sigma 2 is designed to support both individual AI workloads and multi-agent local AI systems. Developers can expand compute capacity through M.2, OCuLink, or Thunderbolt 4, connecting additional AI accelerators as workloads grow. An integrated RP2350 microcontroller adds GPIO connectivity and real-time hardware control, allowing AI applications to interact with sensors and actuators. Preloaded MicroPython firmware provides a programmable interface for intelligent devices and automation systems.
Server-Class Expansion in an Embeddable Form Factor
LattePanda Sigma 2 provides extensive connectivity for storage, networking, and acceleration. It includes three M.2 M-Key slots, one M.2 E-Key slot, PCIe 4.0 x2 via OCuLink, and two Thunderbolt 4 ports. Dual 10GbE Ethernet supports high-bandwidth networking, while USB 3.2 Gen 2, USB 2.0, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 2.1, and eDP 1.5 provide flexible system integration options. These interfaces allow LattePanda Sigma 2 to operate as a compact local AI server or integrate directly into larger intelligent systems.
Ready for Local AI Development and Deployment
LattePanda Sigma 2 supports Windows 11 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, with compatibility for OpenVINO, llama.cpp, and Ollama. It ships with Ubuntu, GPU and NPU drivers, OpenVINO Model Server (OVMS), OpenClaw, and local AI models pre-installed on the onboard SSD, reducing setup time for local AI deployment.
Designed for Product Integration
LattePanda Sigma 2 is designed for product-level integration and long-term deployment, offering a guaranteed 3+ year product lifecycle, custom boot logos and BIOS customization options, and direct engineering support for integration projects. Its combination of local AI compute, high-speed I/O, flexible expansion, and real-time control supports a wide range of applications, including:
- Local AI Appliances—Run private RAG and AI agents while keeping sensitive data on premises.
- All-in-One Homelabs—Combine NAS, virtualization, media services, and local AI in one system.
- Professional Instruments—Capture and process high-speed data streams directly inside compact professional equipment.

articles.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
articles.text:
Right now, there is probably an AI agent running on a laptop somewhere in your network. It stores API keys and database passwords, can access your internal systems, and works without anyone watching.
Nobody reviewed its access. Nobody owns it.
If an employee had that much reach with that little oversight, you would call it an insider risk. So why do we still call the agent a productivity tool?
Most of the conversation about AI security is about what threat actors are doing with it. But the bigger threat may already be inside your organization.
That's the focus of our upcoming webinar, AI as an Insider Threat: From Shadow AI to Governed AI, with expert guest Richard De La Torre, Technical Product Marketing Manager at Bitdefender. Save your seat for a practical security playbook on bringing that unseen AI under control.
Where AI is hiding on your endpoints
It isn't only developers. AI agents, coding assistants, MCP servers, and browser extensions are turning up across the business.
And most of them never cross your network gateway in a way the tools you already run would recognize.
The result is a hard irony. The AI with the most access is often the AI your security team can't see.
📅 Save Your Spot: Watch the Webinar
The visibility gap, by the numbers
According to Bitdefender's 2026 Cybersecurity Assessment report, only 51.8% of organizations report having full visibility into the AI tools their staff use. That leaves nearly half without the full picture.
That blind spot has a cost. IBM found that 20% of breached organizations were compromised through shadow AI.
Which raises the question: what can organizations realistically do about it? That's exactly what the webinar gets practical about. Register now to see what a lean team can do about the AI it can't yet see.
From shadow AI to governed AI
New research from Bitdefender Labs looks at what's really running on endpoints, based on real machines; among the findings: a malicious agent skill caught in the wild.
Blocking AI outright is the obvious response, but it tends to fail. The alternative is governed adoption, and the session shows what that looks like in practice.
What you'll take away
- Where AI is actually showing up on your endpoints, and why the tools you already run don't see most of it.
- New research from Bitdefender Labs on real machines, including the malicious agent skill caught in the wild.
- Why an AI agent with credentials and no owner behaves like an insider risk, and what to do about it.
- Why blocking AI outright tends to fail, and what governed adoption looks like instead.
The AI already running on your endpoints won't wait for a policy. Join expert guest Richard De La Torre, Technical Product Marketing Manager at Bitdefender, and save your seat for AI as an Insider Threat.

articles.title: 'We didn't ship them all away during the pre-order' — Apple's Greg Joswiak has good news for iPhone Duo buyers
articles.text:
'We didn't ship them all away during the pre-order' — Apple's Greg Joswiak has good news for iPhone Duo buyers
'I'm sure we'll have some happy customers.'
We’re just hours away from the iPhone Duo officially going on sale here in the United States, specifically in the New York–New Jersey time zone, and it’s clear Apple’s first-ever folding phone is proving popular.
Just minutes after the iPhone Duo went up for preorder last week, on October 16, 2026, shipping timeframes began to slip. And if you were to order one right now — regardless of color, carrier, or storage — you’re looking at a January 2027 delivery date. But fear not, I've got some good news directly from Greg Joswiak, Apple’s SVP of Marketing.
"You know, we didn't ship them all away during the pre-order, we have them available at the stores, we're excited," said Joswiak.
He continued, “I'll be at 5th Avenue in the morning, my favorite place to launch iPhone, and I'm sure we'll have some happy customers.”
It’s a potentially reassuring comment if you’re currently waiting online or preparing to camp overnight, or even if you’re planning to arrive early at a store on launch day tomorrow, October 23, 2026.
I’ll be with Joswiak, other Apple employees, and who knows how many customers outside the flagship and iconic Cube store on 5th Avenue in NYC.
Previously, Apple has said it would have limited supply for walk-ins, but Jos offers a bit more, noting that the Duo will be available in stores. And while demand for the iPhone Duo for online orders and pre-reserves has been impressive, leading to long lead times, he reiterated that Apple still has some set aside for folks who want to try their luck going to a store or even trying to lock in a unit for pickup.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
On overall demand for the iPhone Duo, Joswiak notes, “Well, I think you saw the pre-order demand last week was extraordinary.”
He continued, “People got it. They understood what we were doing. The people who, like yourselves, who saw it early on were quite taken by it.”
You can read TechRadar’s full review of the iPhone Duo here, and I’ve gotten the chance to spend some more time with it this week since the original unveiling in September. It’s still an incredible form factor, one that feels excellent in the hand and ultimately feels like a premium iPhone.
More recently, I’ve gotten to see more applications running on it — like Edits taking advantage of the bigger internal screen, the impressive reflections rendered in real time in Netflix, and the epic DeckMan, which turns the Duo into a cassette player. Still early days, but it really shows off some unique experiences designed for the Duo.
Another exemplary example is the MLB app, which is launching its iPhone Duo update on Day One with pretty spectacular timing. You see, the World Series kicks off tomorrow, and if you have an iPhone Duo and an applicable account, you can watch it in grand style. On the cover screen, or, if you flip it open, in a full-screen, TV-like treatment. Even neater, if you fold it like a book or mini laptop, you can have the broadcast on top and box score on the bottom. You can even split the screen for the broadcast on the left and another app on the right.
Joswiak noted the importance of MLB and sports at large: ”Sports are important to us; it's important to our users.” The relationship is so tight that the iPhone is in the Baseball Hall of Fame, specifically a Cosmic Orange iPhone 17 Pro Max that was used to broadcast Friday Night Baseball.
So, if you’re lucky enough to get an iPhone Duo tomorrow, you can tune into the World Series on its impressive new display. But if you’re still hoping to get your hands on Apple’s first folding phone, don’t count yourself out just yet. Despite online orders slipping to January, Joswiak says Apple will have units available in stores tomorrow. Your best bet? Get there early.

articles.title: Más de 30 servicios públicos del Reino Unido no están disponibles por fallas de ciberseguridad global
articles.text:
Un total de 32 servicios del Gobierno británico se encuentran fuera de servicio debido a una alerta global de ciberseguridad relacionada con vulnerabilidades en el lenguaje de programación PHP.
Las autoridades del Reino Unido señalaron que parte de las interrupciones responde a medidas preventivas para proteger sus sistemas informáticos mientras se implementan actualizaciones y soluciones de seguridad.
La secretaria de Estado de Espacio, Ciberseguridad y Reforma Regulatoria, Elizabeth Lloyd, informó sobre la situación durante una comparecencia en la Cámara de los Lores. Según explicó, el Gobierno trabaja para recuperar el funcionamiento de las plataformas afectadas sin poner en riesgo la infraestructura digital pública.
La funcionaria subrayó que las interrupciones obedecen, en gran medida, a decisiones de precaución adoptadas mientras se aplican medidas de mitigación. El objetivo es restablecer los servicios de manera segura y evitar que las vulnerabilidades puedan ser aprovechadas por actores maliciosos.
Por su parte, una portavoz de Downing Street, la residencia oficial del primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, indicó que el incidente no ha comprometido los servicios públicos considerados críticos. Sin embargo, no detalló qué plataformas gubernamentales permanecen fuera de servicio ni cuánto tiempo podría tomar su recuperación.
Qué se sabe de la vulnerabilidad que afecta al Gobierno británico
El incidente se produce en medio de una alerta internacional por dos vulnerabilidades críticas detectadas en PHP, un lenguaje de programación ampliamente utilizado para desarrollar páginas web y aplicaciones digitales.
PHP permite crear sitios interactivos, gestionar información y conectar plataformas con bases de datos. Su presencia en numerosos sistemas hace que los problemas de seguridad que afectan a este lenguaje puedan tener consecuencias para una amplia variedad de organizaciones, desde empresas privadas hasta instituciones públicas.
La Fundación PHP, responsable del desarrollo del lenguaje, instó a los usuarios y administradores de sistemas a instalar los parches de seguridad disponibles para corregir las fallas identificadas.
Estas actualizaciones buscan cerrar las brechas antes de que puedan ser aprovechadas para comprometer aplicaciones o infraestructuras digitales. La recomendación cobra especial relevancia para las organizaciones que utilizan PHP en servicios expuestos a internet.
No obstante, la información difundida por las autoridades británicas no establece que las dos vulnerabilidades hayan sido explotadas directamente contra los sistemas del Gobierno ni que se haya producido un robo de datos. Por ahora, la explicación oficial apunta a interrupciones relacionadas, en gran medida, con medidas preventivas.
Reino Unido coordina medidas con OpenAI y aliados internacionales
Las autoridades británicas también confirmaron que sus especialistas mantienen una colaboración estrecha con OpenAI, empresa estadounidense dedicada al desarrollo de inteligencia artificial, y con aliados internacionales para abordar el problema de ciberseguridad.
La participación de la compañía tecnológica se produce en un contexto en el que las herramientas de inteligencia artificial comienzan a desempeñar un papel más importante en la identificación y el análisis de fallas informáticas.
La Fundación PHP también destacó la ayuda de la inteligencia artificial en la detección de las vulnerabilidades. Estas herramientas pueden contribuir a examinar código, identificar patrones sospechosos y localizar errores que requieren una revisión adicional por parte de especialistas.
Sin embargo, detectar una posible falla no sustituye la necesidad de verificarla, evaluar sus consecuencias y aplicar las correcciones correspondientes. La protección de los sistemas también depende de la instalación oportuna de actualizaciones y de la supervisión continua de las plataformas.
Por qué las actualizaciones son importantes para la seguridad digital
Cuando se identifica una vulnerabilidad crítica en un componente tecnológico ampliamente utilizado, las organizaciones deben evaluar qué sistemas podrían estar expuestos y priorizar las medidas de protección.
En algunos casos, esto puede implicar limitar temporalmente el acceso a determinados servicios o suspenderlos mientras se instalan parches y se comprueba que los sistemas funcionan correctamente. Aunque estas decisiones pueden afectar la disponibilidad de plataformas digitales, buscan reducir el riesgo de incidentes más graves.
En el caso británico, las autoridades no han precisado cuándo volverán a funcionar los 32 servicios afectados. Tampoco han publicado una lista completa de las plataformas involucradas.
La situación vuelve a poner de relieve la dependencia de los gobiernos respecto de infraestructuras digitales construidas con tecnologías compartidas por miles de organizaciones en todo el mundo. Una vulnerabilidad en uno de esos componentes puede obligar a aplicar medidas de seguridad de manera coordinada en distintos países.
Mientras continúan los trabajos de mitigación, la prioridad del Gobierno británico es recuperar los servicios afectados y garantizar que su restablecimiento no exponga nuevamente los sistemas a posibles amenazas informáticas.

articles.title: Arista Warns of Critical VeloCloud SQL Injection Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks
articles.text:
Attackers are exploiting a zero-day SQL injection flaw in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, the company said in an advisory on October 22.
The flaw lets anyone who can log in to the orchestrator, even with a read-only customer account, gain operator privileges, the top level of control over it.
For on-premises orchestrators, the fix is in VCO 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12, while Hosted and Dedicated orchestrators have already been patched.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-114625 and rated 9.9 on the CVSS scale. Orchestrators running the releases that fixed the VCO flaws exploited in July and September are still affected, because those releases are older than the new fixes.
Arista bought the VeloCloud SD-WAN product line from Broadcom, announcing the deal in July 2025. The products were earlier known as VMware SD-WAN by VeloCloud.
To exploit the flaw, an attacker needs network access to the orchestrator's web interface and a valid login. The minimum role is Enterprise Read Only, the lowest built-in role for customer users. VCO is exposed by default, and no VCO setting prevents the exposure.
In VCO, operators create the customer and partner accounts, and each partner can manage a group of customers. The flaw allows an attacker to act as a local superuser, a role with full access. It may also allow an attacker to affect the VCO host itself and expose, modify, or disrupt the orchestrator and the data it manages.
The advisory does not say when the attacks began, which orchestrators were hit, or what the attackers did after exploiting the flaw.
The new flaw is the third in VCO since late July that Arista has reported as exploited, and the first of the three that requires a login. Neither the July flaw (CVE-2026-16812) nor the September flaw (CVE-2026-93952) needed one.
Affected and Fixed Releases
Each affected release train has its own fix, shown here beside the release that fixed September's flaw on the same train.
| Release train | Affected by CVE-2026-114625 | Fixed in | CVE-2026-93952 (September) fixed in | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.2 | Before 5.2.3.18 | 5.2.3.18 and later | 5.2.3.16 | 
| 6.1 | Before 6.1.3.10 | 6.1.3.10 and later | No fix listed | 
| 6.4 | Before 6.4.2.12 | 6.4.2.12 and later | 6.4.2.8 | 
VeloCloud Gateway and VeloCloud Edge are not affected. The 7.0 release train is not on the list, and Arista says any release not on the list is not vulnerable.
Arista has not checked releases that have reached end of support. Customers on an unsupported release train can contact Arista's Technical Assistance Center (TAC) about upgrade options.
As of October 22, September's flaw is fixed only in the 5.2 and 6.4 trains. On 6.1, it affects releases up to 6.1.3.7, and no fixed release is listed. Neither advisory says whether 6.1.3.10 also fixes the September flaw.
If You Cannot Upgrade Yet
Until the fixed release is installed, Arista recommends these steps:
- Limit access to the VCO web interface to trusted administrative networks.
- Monitor the VCO for connections from known malicious IP addresses.
- Watch for unexpected outbound network activity from the VCO host.
- Consider blocking outbound ports that normal operation does not need.
- Watch for backdoor daemons and webshells.
- Review recent administrator activity for unexpected changes.
Checking for Compromise
Two IP addresses have been seen carrying out the attacks, according to Arista. Block them and check logs for any sign of them:
- IP: 74.82.197[.]86
- IP: 38.54.50[.]151
Also check VCO web access logs for requests with unusual URL-like path components, encoded characters, references to local or internal services, or high request rates.
If you suspect a compromise, save evidence before fixing anything, where possible. That means the VCO web access, backend application, system and database logs, along with the relevant file-system timestamps.
Regarding the July and September flaws, Arista warned that a compromised orchestrator could also grant attackers access to VeloCloud Edge devices. For this flaw, the advisory does not say whether the risk applies or whether upgrading removes access that an attacker has already gained.

articles.title: Cash-Strapped EA Could Sell Off Mass Effect and Other IPs To Recoup Costs
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Cash-Strapped EA Could Sell Off Mass Effect and Other IPs To Recoup Costs
Electronic Arts recently announced that it is shuttering BioWare and cancelling its upcoming Mass Effect game and cutting 400 jobs in the process, after the gaming giant acquired the game studio in 2007. According to a former executive producer at BioWare, Mark Darrah, however, there may still be hope for fans of BioWare's myriad beloved franchises, including Mass Effect.
Mark Darrah on YouTubeRemember, BioWare, 100% owned by EA, so EA owns all the IPs. They own Dragon Age, they own Mass Effect, they own Jade Empire. So, that doesn't change the situation really at all... Now, there's nobody working on a game or games within the EA organization, and chances are there never will be, which might make them more likely to sell off those IPS, but it might also make them more likely to just try to forget that they ever existed and bury them in the vault.
As the former executive explains in a recent video on YouTube (embedded below), EA owns all of the intellectual property that was under the BioWare umbrella, and because they are no longer actively being developed for, there is a chance they will be sold. Although Darrah notes that we will "have to wait a little bit before we see if EA has any interest in selling off any of its dormant IPs," adding that EA is in "cost-control" mode, which may make the studio eager to generate as much revenue as possible, and selling game franchises may be one way to do just that. Darrah also comments that the closure of the studio seemed like the most likely eventuality once EA's recent acquisition by the PIF group was announced. 
This is an eventuality, but Pocket Pair's John Buckley explained in a recent post on X, it's not always that simple, as "IP holders often have absolutely no interest in selling and when they do, the asking price is absurd," with the last point being especially pertinent, given the size and historical importance of Mass Effect. As was recently revealed, BioWare had put in enough work into the now-cancelled Mass Effect Universe that a trailer leaked following the announcement of the studio's closure.
Sources:
				Mark Darrah on YouTube, 				@Bucky_cm on X

I think the ME trilogy was lightning in a bottle and perhaps it is best left standing on its own.
They really did him dirty with that one. But that seems to be par for the course when doing business with EA
EA has plenty of reasons to keep the IP for the future, it just depends on what they are looking to do, they got burned by millions, so they need to take the time to figure out the next step, and there is zero chance that CD Projekt RED will get the nod, they got their plates full as it is
sure, it might be a gamble, but there have been other games that were shelved for a long time, and came back to sell a ton of copies
As for the other series, Jade Empire should be a joint project with a Chinese studio. I wouldn't trust a US studio with telling a good Chinese fantasy story nowadays; or for that matter, a decent Asian fantasy story.
Mass Effect and Dragon Age should be sold off or at least licensed out to let other companies make games in the setting and expand on its universe. You could have Obsidian or Rockstar do an open world setting on a particular frontier colony within Mass Effect or a different region/continent within Dragon Age. Or let Sony's new team of Ex-Bungie staff make a Mass Effect game with some gameplay elements from Destiny. Or just let some quasi-indie studio do a smaller game in either setting.

articles.title: X-energy and Amazon plan 12 nuclear reactors at a retired Indiana coal site
articles.text:
Amazon is spending over $1 billion on a new nuclear energy project to power its next data centers — but will it really live up to the test?
Amazon backs 12 nuclear reactors in Indiana for data centers
- Amazon plans to buy power from 12 proposed Indiana nuclear reactors
- The proposed facility could deliver 960 megawatts to Indiana’s electricity grid
- X-energy’s Xe-100 reactors would use helium cooling and TRISO fuel
Amazon is backing a proposed nuclear power development in Indiana designed to supply electricity for its expanding data center operations and the regional grid.
The project involves 12 small modular reactors from X-energy, with a combined planned output of 960 megawatts, although construction and commissioning dates remain uncertain.
Amazon hasn’t disclosed the specific amount it is putting into the Indiana project, but it says it is “investing billions in nuclear energy projects” overall. This confirmation, coupled with its lead role in X-energy, suggests the commitment could plausibly exceed $1 billion, though that is speculation.
Twelve reactors face an uncertain road to operation
The planned installation would occupy the former Breed coal generating station site in Sullivan County, Indiana, where developers intend to establish new nuclear generating capacity.
Each Xe-100 reactor is designed to generate 80 megawatts using helium gas for cooling and specially engineered uranium fuel particles known as TRISO.
X-energy says TRISO fuel resists extreme temperatures, while the Xe-100 design aims to limit reliance on active safety systems during certain accident scenarios.
However, the proposed Indiana installation remains a development project, and the United States has yet to operate a commercial small modular reactor supplying electricity.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Amazon's partnership with X-energy dates back to 2024, when the technology company led a $700 million financing round supporting reactor development and fuel production preparations.
That funding included work on reactor licensing and the initial stage of a TRISO-X fuel manufacturing facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee.
The Indiana proposal forms part of a separate ambition to introduce more than 5 gigawatts of nuclear generating capacity across the United States by 2039.
Amazon would purchase electricity from the proposed installation, providing developers with an expected customer while the project advances through planning and regulatory requirements.
“New technologies like this often need initial customers to help de-risk projects and provide funding so they can be built and scaled to commercial availability,” said an Amazon spokesperson.
Regulatory approvals could determine the timeline
Regulatory approvals remain a key obstacle, and coordinating construction across the proposed facility could complicate delivery.
Nuclear developers in America generally pursue either approval for a standard reactor design or authorization covering a specific installation and its location.
X-energy has reported progress toward a construction permit for a separate Texas development, but that authorization would not automatically approve its Indiana proposal.
The Texas project involves four reactors intended to support a Dow chemical manufacturing facility, substantially fewer units than the planned Indiana installation.
According to the South Bend Tribune, an X-energy representative indicated that the Indiana facility could become operational during the middle of the 2030s.
The representative warned that the schedule could change as the project progresses, so the mid-2030s estimate remains provisional.
