articles.title: Una madre demandó a OpenAI por usar datos de sus hijos de 12 y 16 años para entrenar a ChatGPT
articles.text:
Una madre de Hawái demandó a OpenAI en una corte federal de California y la acusó de extraer datos sensibles de sus dos hijos, de 12 y 16 años, a través de conversaciones con ChatGPT, para entrenar sus modelos de inteligencia artificial sin el consentimiento válido de los padres.
La demanda, presentada en el Tribunal de Distrito de Estados Unidos para el Distrito Norte de California, describe a ChatGPT como un producto diseñado para imitar el lenguaje de cada usuario, halagarlo y recordar conversaciones anteriores con el objetivo de que los menores sigan compartiendo información personal.
Según la presentación judicial, de 81 páginas, una de las menores, de 12 años, le reveló su edad real al chatbot durante una conversación, pero el sistema continuó interactuando con ella sin interrumpir el vínculo ni derivar el caso a un adulto responsable.
“Si un extraño le hiciera esto a un niño, habría indignación”, dijo Paul Yetter, abogado principal de los demandantes y socio del estudio Yetter Coleman, al anunciar la demanda.
Piden que los chicos reciban acciones de OpenAI
La demanda plantea un reclamo inusual: que los menores alcanzados por la acción de clase reciban una participación accionaria en la empresa, o su equivalente en dinero, proporcional a la cantidad de información que le fue extraída a cada uno. OpenAI busca actualmente una valuación de hasta USD 1,4 billones antes de salir a la bolsa, según Bloomberg Law.
Andy Liddell, del estudio EdTech Law Center, una de las firmas que impulsan el caso, explicó que el pedido de una compensación económica busca que, si OpenAI debe pagar por usar los datos de los chicos, eso termine por incentivar un producto más seguro para los menores.
“Durante años extrajo de manera indebida enormes cantidades de datos sensibles y valiosos de millones de niños”, sostiene el escrito judicial, según Courthouse News. “No tenía ningún derecho a tomar esa información, pero lo hizo de todos modos”.
OpenAI rechazó las acusaciones. “Discrepamos firmemente con esta demanda equivocada que apunta solo contra OpenAI pese a las protecciones específicas por edad que incorporamos en nuestro producto”, respondió la empresa, según Bloomberg News. La compañía advirtió además que el caso podría empujar a los adolescentes hacia plataformas con menos controles parentales.
Ocho estados ya demandaron a la empresa por los mismos riesgos
Un día antes de que se presentara la demanda de la madre de Hawái, los fiscales generales de Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Virginia Occidental, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho y Montana iniciaron acciones legales separadas contra OpenAI. Las ocho demandas acusan a la compañía de engañar a los padres sobre la seguridad de ChatGPT y de violar leyes estatales de protección al consumidor.
Ahora bien, las reglas de uso de OpenAI exigen el permiso de un adulto para que un menor de 18 años use ChatGPT y prohíben el acceso a menores de 13 años, pero la propia demanda de Hawái sostiene que la empresa no verifica ese consentimiento: alcanza con tildar una casilla que declara tener más de 13 años.
La controversia se suma a un cuestionamiento reciente del Youth AI Safety Institute, el área de la organización Common Sense Media dedicada a evaluar productos de inteligencia artificial para chicos, que calificó a ChatGPT for Teens como de “riesgo inaceptable” tras detectar fallas para alertar a los padres en conversaciones sobre autolesiones o trastornos alimentarios.

articles.title: Ventes Flash Amazon : 12 offres tech ce jeudi, dont 5 à leur prix le plus bas depuis trois mois
articles.text:
À cinq semaines du Black Friday, prévu le 27 novembre, Amazon fait déjà bouger une partie de son catalogue tech, de l'entretien des sols aux périphériques de jeu. Pour chacune des 12 offres retenues, nous avons confronté le prix barré à l'historique, et signalé celles dont la remise ne repose que sur un prix conseillé.
Le Black Friday tombe cette année le 27 novembre, mais certains prix n’attendent pas cette date pour bouger. Ce jeudi, les baisses les plus nettes chez Amazon portent sur les robots aspirateurs, avec deux Roborock et deux Lefant, et sur l’équipement du bureau et de la maison : souris, claviers, caméras de surveillance et aspirateurs sans fil.
Pour chaque offre, nous avons regardé ce que vaut le prix barré. Neuf d’entre elles se comparent au prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours affiché par Amazon ou à l’historique de trois mois relevé sur LeDénicheur. Pour le clavier SteelSeries, la caméra EZVIZ et l’aspirateur Rowenta, la remise ne se calcule que sur un prix conseillé : elle est à lire avec plus de recul. Le robot Lefant M3 Max, enfin, demande de cocher un bon de réduction sur sa fiche.
Les meilleures 12 offres Amazon du jour
- Souris gaming Glorious Model O 2 Mini Wireless à 69,99 € au lieu de 89,11 €
- Souris verticale sans fil Razer Pro Click V2 Vertical (droitier) à 82,99 € au lieu de 99,99 €
- Robot aspirateur laveur Lefant M3 Max à 329,99 € au lieu de 1 199,99 €, ou 313,49 € avec le bon de réduction de 5 % à cocher sur la fiche
- Robot aspirateur 3-en-1 Lefant M330 Plus à 109,99 € au lieu de 399,99 €
- Pack de 2 caméras projecteur Arlo Floodlight 2 à 179,99 € au lieu de 299,99 €
- Robot aspirateur laveur Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro à 499,99 € au lieu de 689,99 €
- Robot aspirateur laveur Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro à 599 € au lieu de 749 €
- Aspirateur laveur vapeur sans fil Polti Rollysteam WD50C à 349 € au lieu de 589 €
- Clavier gaming magnétique SteelSeries Apex Pro TKL Gen 3 (AZERTY) à 179,99 € au lieu de 249,99 €
- Kit caméra extérieure sans fil EZVIZ CB90 à 189,99 € au lieu de 279,99 €
- Aspirateur balai sans fil Rowenta X-PERT 6.80 à 139,99 € au lieu de 199,99 €
- Clavier gaming Logitech G316 X 98 (AZERTY) à 88,68 € au lieu de 99,99 €
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Les cinq offres à regarder de plus près
Deux robots Roborock tiennent le haut de la sélection, et l’un d’eux est passé entre nos mains : dans notre test du Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro, nous avions salué son aspiration, son lavage et sa navigation. Les trois autres offres commentées répondent à des besoins plus précis, du ménage à la vapeur au confort du poignet.
- Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro : nous avons retenu une aspiration de 25 000 Pa efficace sur les sols comme sur les tapis, un mode SmartPlan enfin précis et une autonomie capable de dépasser trois heures d’après nos relevés. Le robot ne mesure que 7,98 cm de haut grâce à son LiDAR rétractable. La station est en revanche tout en plastique, aucun réservoir n’accueille le détergent et les serpillères demandent un frottage à la main après quelques semaines. À 599 €, il retrouve son prix le plus bas des trois derniers mois.
- Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro : sorti en août à 689,99 €, il annonce lui aussi 25 000 Pa, avec deux serpillères rotatives que le robot laisse dans sa station avant de passer sur un tapis. Il se repère au LiDAR, et sa station lave les serpillères à l’eau chaude avant de les sécher à l’air chaud. Nous ne l’avons pas testé. Près de 100 € moins cher que le Curv 2 Pro, il est lui aussi à son prix le plus bas des trois derniers mois.
- Polti Rollysteam WD50C : cet aspirateur laveur sans fil aspire et lave les sols en un seul passage, tapis à poils courts compris, et diffuse de la vapeur pour les assainir sans détergent, selon Polti. La marque annonce 35 minutes d’autonomie et une base qui nettoie et sèche le rouleau. C’est l’option de ceux qui préfèrent garder la main sur le ménage : à 349 €, il coûte 240 € de moins que son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours.
- Razer Pro Click V2 Vertical : nous l’avons utilisée plus de deux mois lors de notre test, et elle n’a pas consommé 45 % de sa batterie sur la période. Sa position verticale soulage l’avant-bras, son capteur monte à 30 000 ppp et elle se connecte en 2,4 GHz, en Bluetooth ou par câble. Ses 150 g et un temps d’adaptation d’environ un mois dans les jeux de tir la réservent à ceux qui veulent d’abord ménager leur poignet. Elle est à son prix le plus bas des trois derniers mois.
- Glorious Model O 2 Mini Wireless : à l’inverse, elle ne pèse que 57 g et vise les jeux de tir compétitifs, avec un capteur de 26 000 dpi et trois modes de connexion. Son format réduit, 120 x 62 x 36 mm selon le magazine Stuff, convient aux mains petites et moyennes. Son taux de rapport plafonne à 1 000 Hz, et Gamereactor a trouvé son capteur capricieux sur certains tapis. Elle passe sous son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours.
Prix barrés : lesquels reflètent une vraie baisse ?
Les remises les plus spectaculaires de la liste sont aussi les plus fragiles. Les deux robots Lefant affichent plus de 70 % de baisse, calculés sur des prix les plus bas des 30 derniers jours de 1 199,99 € et 399,99 € selon Amazon : des montants élevés pour ces modèles, qu’aucun historique indépendant ne vient confirmer. À l’inverse, la souris Razer, le pack Arlo et les deux Roborock sont à leur prix le plus bas des trois derniers mois selon LeDénicheur, et le clavier Logitech passe sous le sien. L’Arlo Floodlight 2 est d’ailleurs au même prix chez Boulanger et à la Fnac.
Si vous hésitez entre les deux Roborock, le budget ne dit pas tout. Le Qrevo 2 Pro coûte près de 100 € de moins, mais seul le Qrevo Curv 2 Pro est passé par notre banc d’essai, qui a validé sa navigation et son autonomie. Pour les situer face aux autres références du marché, notre comparatif des meilleurs aspirateurs robots classe neuf modèles et propose des repères selon votre budget et votre logement.
Bons plans Amazon du jour : vos questions
Pourquoi certaines remises de cette sélection sont-elles à relativiser ?
Pour le clavier SteelSeries Apex Pro TKL Gen 3, la caméra EZVIZ CB90 et l’aspirateur Rowenta X-PERT 6.80, le prix de comparaison est un prix conseillé, sans historique disponible pour le vérifier. La remise affichée ne dit donc pas à quel prix ces produits se vendaient ces dernières semaines.
Comment obtenir le Lefant M3 Max à 313,49 € ?
Il faut cocher le bon de réduction de 5 % affiché sur la fiche Amazon avant d’ajouter le robot au panier. Le prix de 313,49 € est calculé à partir de ce taux : vérifiez le montant final dans le panier avant de payer.
Le Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro passe-t-il sous les meubles bas ?
Oui, il ne mesure que 7,98 cm de haut et abaisse automatiquement son capteur LiDAR à l’approche d’un meuble bas. Lors de notre test, il s’est glissé sous un canapé et même sous la porte ouverte d’un lave-vaisselle.

articles.title: eMudhra to Exit Global SSL/TLS Business After 8 Intermediate CA Keys Found Easily Guessable
articles.text:
eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority (CA), will withdraw from its global SSL/TLS certificate business, its board decided on Thursday. The decision came five days after a researcher reported recovering the private keys of eight of its intermediate CA certificates.
eMudhra said it will replace affected customers' certificates with free ones from partners, though its announcement did not name the partners or provide a date for the exit.
Six of those eight were for website (TLS) certificates. Chrome will stop trusting the eMudhra root certificate above them, emSign ECC Root CA - G3. The change is expected to reach users on the morning of October 27, Pacific time.
On October 20, Mozilla decided to stop trusting the same root in Firefox. Removing a root from a browser also cuts off legitimate certificates issued beneath it.
About 30,800 unexpired certificates chained to that root as of October 21, by Chrome's count of public Certificate Transparency (CT) logs. Of those, 99.9% were issued through InCommon, the certificate service Internet2 created for the higher education community. InCommon moved the service onto eMudhra's CertiNext platform between April and July this year.
Google has told website operators with certificates under that root that they "must immediately acquire and install a new TLS certificate from another PKI hierarchy included in the Chrome Root Store."
Until the transition is complete, eMudhra said, its G1 RSA root certificates will continue to serve customers. G1 is a separate hierarchy from the ECC root, but Chrome is still deciding whether to keep eMudhra's remaining CA certificates in its root store.
eMudhra will keep its revocation and status services running until every SSL/TLS certificate it issued has expired or been replaced. Its other businesses, including digital signature certificates, eSign and the CertiNext platform InCommon uses, will continue.
The announcement does not mention InCommon, or say whether eMudhra will keep issuing new certificates under G1 until it exits.
eMudhra said the global SSL/TLS business brings in about 1% of its revenue. Data sovereignty and compliance rules make it more complex and costly to run, and some large providers give the certificates away free.
The incident's spread on social media has also brought "scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business," the company said.
The researcher reported the weak keys to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra on October 17. Each private key should have been a huge random number, but all eight were below 256, so anyone could work them out almost instantly.
Chrome and Firefox blocked the six TLS intermediates within hours. No website certificate from them had appeared in CT logs before Chrome's block, so none could have been used against Chrome or other software that requires CT logging, Google said.
eMudhra said it never used the eight to issue certificates to websites or users, and that its systems were not breached.
What Certificate Holders Can Do
Cornell has told its certificate holders to request RSA certificates instead of ECC ones, because "RSA certificates use eMudhra's unaffected root and should work." The university counts more than 300 affected certificates of its own.
The University of Michigan says InCommon's RSA certificates are not currently affected, but that their root "could become distrusted, too." For now, its main alternative is Let's Encrypt.
eMudhra has estimated that about 30,000 certificates need to be moved, and that about 97% of them were issued using ACME, the protocol many servers use to request and renew certificates automatically.
Chrome has told eMudhra that standard ACME clients do not replace certificates outside their renewal window unless they support ACME Renewal Information (ARI) or someone steps in by hand. Moving from the ECC hierarchy to the RSA one may also need changes to client settings.
Questions Over eMudhra's RSA Root
Mozilla said on October 20 that, for now, it was not removing trust in the G1 root, emSign Root CA - G1. At Stanford, InCommon certificates chain to that root through an eMudhra CA called emSign Root TLS CA - G1.
On October 14, eMudhra published a certificate revocation list (CRL) for emSign Root TLS CA - G1. A CRL is the signed list of certificates a CA has revoked. This one's signature does not verify against that CA's own key, the researcher who reported the weak keys said in Mozilla's public bug report on the incident.
A participant in the same bug report said on October 22 that the list appears to have been signed with the key of an eMudhra OCSP certificate. OCSP certificates sign answers about whether a certificate has been revoked. The participant wrote that the match "appears to be a case of using the wrong signing key, rather than evidence of another weak key."
Chrome raised the list on October 21, in one of 12 questions it posted to the bug report. It asked which key signed it, and whether eMudhra holds more than one key pair for that CA or for any of its roots.
Chrome also asked whether customers are moving to G1, to another company's CA, or both, and when all of them will have moved, given its planned October 27 removal. eMudhra said on October 20 that G1 was "the only alternative available," and the next day that it is issuing its affected US customers fresh certificates "from an alternate, independently operated, publicly trusted CA hierarchy."
In 2025, eMudhra published invalid CRLs for six of the same intermediates. Its incident report at the time said it fixed them by "regenerating the CRLs using the appropriate private key associated with each Intermediate CA."
On October 19, eMudhra told Mozilla that those lists were first signed with the keys it meant to use. When that produced invalid signatures, they were "resigned with flawed keys," the weak keys found this month.
Chrome said that disclosure "raises serious concerns regarding eMudhra's transparency and incident handling" during and after the 2025 incident. It asked why the 2025 report did not mention that two key pairs existed for each of those CAs.
As of 13:31 UTC on Thursday, eMudhra had not answered any of Chrome's questions publicly on the bug report. Its last visible comment there was posted on October 20.

articles.title: New Fan Project Brings Xbox One Games to iPhone Without Emulating the Hardware
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
New Fan Project Brings Xbox One Games to iPhone Without Emulating the Hardware
A developer who goes by levi on X has announced Utsuro, a new project that runs Xbox One games on Apple devices. It's still very early, but the developer says it already runs Minecraft: Xbox One Edition "extremely well," and the attached video shows it running on iOS with touchscreen controls. According to the project's GitHub page, Minecraft hits around 36 to 60 FPS on the Mac build, and Sonic Mania and Rocket League run there too, complete with screenshots. Sonic Mania is marked as playable at around 57 FPS with sound, while Rocket League renders and drives at roughly 15 to 20 FPS, with dark lighting and no audio yet.
Utsuro also works differently from a typical emulator. Apparently, it skips hardware emulation altogether and runs the console's Windows-based software layer as x86-64 code on Apple's Arm chips through FEXCore, and fills in the system pieces the console itself would normally provide. Graphics go through Apple's Metal API, with the Xbox One's Direct3D 11.X shaders converted to Metal's shader language, while audio runs on CoreAudio. Getting it running isn't exactly simple either. On iOS, the app has to be sideloaded, needs a JIT helper like StikDebug, TrollStore, or a jailbroken device, and expects a decrypted dump of the game. The macOS version currently has to be built from source.Console emulation in general has been moving quickly lately, with original Xbox games already running on jailbroken PS5 consoles and PS5 emulators reaching gameplay in a growing number of titles. It's reasonable to expect more Xbox One games to follow on iOS devices, though only three games have been shown running so far.
Sources:
				levi on X, 				Utsuro (GitHub), 				via Windows Central

articles.title: Lanzan una IA gratuita que traduce el ADN a lenguaje cotidiano
articles.text:
Hugging Face lanzó Carbon-X, un modelo de inteligencia artificial de código abierto que permite hacer preguntas sobre secuencias de ADN en lenguaje cotidiano y recibir respuestas explicadas en inglés, sin pasar por fórmulas ni gráficos técnicos.
El sistema fue desarrollado junto con investigadores de la Academia Zhongguancun, en China, el Instituto Telethon de Genética y Medicina y la Universidad Federico II de Nápoles, en Italia. Tiene 14.800 millones de parámetros y se entrenó con 302.000 millones de fragmentos de texto que combinan secuencias genéticas, literatura científica e instrucciones en inglés. El usuario pega una secuencia de ADN en una conversación de chat y el modelo responde con una explicación en texto.
Carbon-X puede predecir si una mutación genética es benigna o está asociada a una enfermedad, identificar qué regiones de una secuencia regulan la actividad de un gen, clasificar fragmentos de ADN según el organismo de origen y anticipar las bases siguientes de una secuencia.
Lewis Tunstall, científico investigador senior de Hugging Face, describió la herramienta como una forma de ampliar el acceso a este tipo de análisis. “Hemos desbloqueado una nueva capacidad en los modelos de lenguaje, que consiste en poder conversar con el ADN”, dijo. Según Tunstall, el uso de lenguaje natural permite que usuarios sin formación técnica consulten datos genéticos de un modo que antes no era posible con otras herramientas de bioinformática.
Por qué corre en una sola placa gráfica
El equipo partió de Qwen3-14B, un modelo de lenguaje de Alibaba, y amplió su vocabulario para leer ADN en bloques de seis letras antes de continuar el entrenamiento con datos genómicos.
Los pesos del sistema caben en una sola placa gráfica de 80 gigabytes, lo que le permite funcionar en la propia computadora del investigador en lugar de depender de un servicio en la nube.
Esa decisión responde a una limitación práctica: los investigadores suelen tener restricciones para subir datos genéticos identificables o de pacientes a modelos de IA alojados por terceros. Al ejecutarse de forma local, ningún dato sale del equipo del usuario hacia Hugging Face ni hacia otra empresa, precisó Tunstall.
Los desarrolladores excluyeron deliberadamente a los virus del material de entrenamiento. Tunstall explicó que la decisión buscó reducir el riesgo de que el modelo se use con fines dañinos, un problema que, según indicó, también afecta a los chatbots generales, que a veces rechazan preguntas legítimas de biología por confundirlas con intentos de diseñar armas.
Resultados por debajo de los modelos más grandes, a menor costo
En cinco pruebas comparativas sobre predicción de mutaciones y reconocimiento de secuencias, Carbon-X promedió un 66,7% de aciertos, cerca del 67,5% que Hugging Face le atribuye a GPT-6.1 Sol, un modelo mucho más grande.
La compañía calculó que analizar con Carbon-X los 2,4 millones de variantes genéticas de significado incierto registradas en la base de datos ClinVar costaría unos USD 300. Con los modelos de mayor escala evaluados, el mismo análisis costaría entre USD 32.000 y USD 4 millones, según los cálculos que Hugging Face publicó junto al modelo.
El sistema acepta secuencias de hasta unas 50.000 pares de bases por consulta, de modo que no es posible cargarle un genoma humano completo, que tiene 6.000 millones de esas unidades. Hugging Face advirtió que Carbon-X todavía no fue validado con experimentos de laboratorio, por lo que no puede garantizarse la exactitud de sus predicciones, y que no debe usarse para tomar decisiones médicas.
Otros modelos que apuntan al mismo problema
Carbon-X se suma a otros intentos recientes de traducir el ADN a un formato más accesible. El año pasado, Google DeepMind presentó AlphaGenome, que predice el efecto de mutaciones pero en formato numérico y con mayor demanda de cómputo. Evo 2, desarrollado por el Arc Institute junto con Nvidia y socios académicos, también procesa el ADN como si fuera un idioma y puede generar genomas completos desde cero.
El lanzamiento llega semanas después de que Nvidia acordara comprar Hugging Face por cerca de USD 12.900 millones, en una operación que se espera cierre en la primera mitad de 2027. El modelo quedó publicado bajo licencia Apache 2.0 y ya está disponible para su descarga.

articles.title: La navette européenne Space Rider s'est écrasée lors d'un essai de largage
articles.text:
Larguée d’un hélicoptère au-dessus de la Sardaigne, la maquette grandeur nature de Space Rider s’est écrasée au sol après avoir perdu sa voile de guidage. Sans cette voile, le futur vaisseau réutilisable de l’Agence spatiale européenne ne peut ni se poser sur une piste ni repartir en mission.
Les ingénieurs de l’ESA et de Thales Alenia Space ont lâché la maquette début octobre, à environ 3 kilomètres d’altitude au-dessus d’un champ de tir de l’armée italienne. Le petit parachute de freinage s’est ouvert normalement. La grande voile pilotable qui devait ensuite guider l’engin s’est en revanche détachée pendant son déploiement, et la maquette a terminé sa chute sans plus rien pour la ralentir. Un porte-parole de l’agence a confirmé à Space.com que ce dernier essai de largage « n’a pas été mené à bien comme prévu en raison d’une anomalie lors de la séquence de déploiement du parafoil », et une enquête indépendante est ouverte. L’ESA assure que l’accident ne retardera pas Space Rider, mais l’atterrissage guidé, condition de toute réutilisation, n’a jamais été réussi avec un engin à l’échelle réelle.
Sans sa voile, Space Rider ne peut pas atterrir sur une piste
Space Rider doit emporter des expériences scientifiques en orbite basse pendant deux mois au plus, puis les rapporter sur Terre pour que les chercheurs les analysent. L’engin n’a pas d’ailes. Après sa rentrée dans l’atmosphère, il est dirigé vers une piste par une voile pilotable, dont les suspentes sont tirées par deux treuils commandés par son ordinateur de bord. Les capsules en service redescendent sous de simples parachutes, avec bien moins de précision.
L’équipe de Thales Alenia Space a fait voler en juin 2025 une palette métallique lestée de béton et bardée de capteurs, pendant douze minutes depuis 2,5 kilomètres d’altitude, jusqu’à un point situé à moins de 150 mètres du lieu d’atterrissage prévu. Pour l’ESA, c’était alors une première mondiale pour un atterrissage de précision sous voile. Cette palette n’avait rien de la silhouette de Space Rider.
La maquette larguée en octobre reproduisait en revanche la taille et le comportement en vol du module de rentrée, avec l’avionique chargée de son guidage autonome. C’est sur cet engin de la taille d’un minibus que les ingénieurs devaient valider l’ensemble de la descente, jusqu’au contact avec le sol. L’agence a récupéré tous ses débris. Construit pour les essais au sol et en largage, cet engin n’avait rien d’un modèle prêt à partir dans l’espace.
Un premier vol vers les Açores annoncé avant 2030
« Nous espérons que cet essai ne nous obligera pas à modifier le planning et les activités de qualification restantes », a expliqué Géraldine Naja, directrice du transport spatial de l’ESA, lors du point presse du Conseil de l’agence hier, que vous pouvez visionner dans la vidéo ci-dessus. Les qualifications qui restent à mener « ne sont pas sur le chemin critique » de Space Rider, a-t-elle ajouté. Autrement dit, ces essais peuvent prendre du retard sans repousser le lancement, puisque la date du premier vol dépend d’autres étapes du programme.
Avant de retenter un largage, l’ESA devra attendre les conclusions de l’enquête et un créneau libre sur le champ de tir sarde. Le ministère italien de la Défense, qui gère ce terrain, l’avait fermé aux essais de juin à septembre, après une première tentative interrompue en mai à cause d’un capteur. À l’été 2025, l’agence prévoyait encore un premier vol en 2027. Elle ne parle plus aujourd’hui que d’une mission avant la fin de la décennie, avec un atterrissage sur l’île de Santa Maria, aux Açores, d’après l’accord signé entre le Portugal et l’ESA en novembre 2025.
Josef Aschbacher, directeur général de l’ESA, a profité de ce point presse pour prévenir que l’Europe manquera « probablement » d’Ariane 6 vers la fin de la décennie. L’agence attendra début 2027 des estimations solides de la demande avant d’agir. La fusée lourde doit reprendre ses vols fin novembre avec 36 satellites Amazon Leo, après des semaines d’arrêt dues à une anomalie de turbopompe. Ariane 6 et Vega C, qui doit lancer le vaisseau, sont des lanceurs jetables, et Space Rider est le premier engin orbital européen conçu pour revenir et repartir.
« Nous avons eu beaucoup d’essais réussis auparavant, mais les tests et la validation font partie du développement d’un système spatial », a insisté Géraldine Naja.

articles.title: Getac Announces Next-Gen B360X and B360X Pro Rugged Notebooks
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Getac Announces Next-Gen B360X and B360X Pro Rugged Notebooks
Getac Technology Corporation (Getac), a leading provider of rugged computing and mobile video solutions and a manufacturer with advanced in-house capabilities, today announced the launch of its next generation B360X and B360X Pro fully rugged notebooks. 
Both new devices build on the proven heritage of Getac's popular B360 series, offering upgraded AI-powered processing, a larger 14-inch screen size, enhanced security, and comprehensive connectivity options, all in a compact and portable form factor. This makes them ideally suited to frontline professionals in industries such as public safety, utilities, manufacturing and defense, who need powerful yet versatile devices to accomplish complex tasks in a diverse range of field environments.Powerful AI-powered performance at the edge
At the heart of the new B360X and B360X Pro is the powerful new Intel Core Ultra 5/7/X7 Processor (Series 3) with Intel Graphics and Intel AI Boost technology, which delivers exceptional performance for multitasking, data-intensive workloads, and AI-enhanced applications, even when connection to the cloud isn't available. 
Both devices also feature a 14-inch WUXGA LumiBond display with Getac Sunlight Readable Technology (1,400 nits) for legibility and usability, while the capacitive touchscreen can be operated even when wearing compatible gloves or working in the rain.
Enhanced versatility, connectivity, and security
Designed for exceptional versatility in the field, the B360X and B360X Pro boast an array of connectivity options, including Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 as standard, along with optional dedicated GPS with L1/L5, 4G LTE and 5G Sub-6 with SA as needed. Customers can also choose from a range of customizable I/O port configurations including up to two Thunderbolt 4 Type-C ports for high-speed data transfer, while the dual battery with hot-swappable capability allows for extended use in the field between charges. 
The B360X and B360X Pro also feature enhanced security, including Windows Hello Camera (via a 5MP front facing camera), TPM 2.0, a smart card reader, a user replaceable PCIe NVMe SSD, and Getac Disk Wipe as standard. Optional upgraders include a second SSD (allowing for up to 4 TB of total storage via two 2 TB drives), an HF RFID reader, and a fingerprint reader.
Fully rugged protection
Like all Getac fully rugged devices, the B360X and B360X Pro are built to thrive in harsh and challenging work environments. Featuring MIL-STD-810H and MIL-STD-461G compliance, and IP66 rating, as well as 6ft drop resistance while in use, they excel where many other devices would fail. Optional salt fog resistance is also available if required. 
B360X Pro: Mission-ready computing in a compact form factor
In addition to all the above, the B360X Pro includes dual high-capacity batteries as standard, while an optional NVIDIA RTX PRO 500 Blackwell discrete graphics controller takes visuals to the next level without impacting processing performance. The B360X Pro also features an optional media bay, which can accommodate a third battery or a DVD drive as required.
Companion devices for professionals working in extreme conditions
The B360X and B360X Pro's combination of powerful edge AI computing, fully rugged reliability and portable form factor makes them ideally suited to professionals who regularly work in extreme environments and scenarios where reliable internet connectivity isn't available:
- Public safety & emergency rescue: In disaster zones where communications are completely severed, the B360X can transform into an independent tactical command hub, integrating Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD), Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and Automatic Vehicle Location (AVL) through advanced edge computing software.
- Military & defense: In environments where connectivity is unavailable, the B360X Pro can effortlessly run high-workload military training and simulation platforms, utilizing edge AI computing to generate virtual enemy behavioral logic and tactical simulation models.
- Utilities & industrial manufacturing: Deep within signal-dead zones such as remote transmission towers, underground pipelines, or complex factory blind spots, the B360X can seamlessly execute CAD software and 3D modeling workflows at the local level, for precise asset installation and complex maintenance activity.
Charlie Gibbs, Director of Product Solutions, Getac North America"The true value of Artificial Intelligence is not realized in climate-controlled server rooms, but at the absolute edge, where critical decisions shape our global safety, defense, and infrastructure. With the B360X and B360X Pro, Getac is tearing down the environmental boundaries of computing. We are ushering in a new era of 'Intelligent Resilience,' ensuring that those who protect and build our world have uninterrupted access to next-generation AI, regardless of how extreme or disconnected their environment may be. We are not just anticipating the future of the rugged industry; we are actively defining it."
The B360X and B360X Pro will be available in November 2026.
Sources:
				Getac B360X, 				B360X Pro

articles.title: ThreatsDay: AI Secrets Leak, PingCAP Source Theft, Signal Hang-Up Flaw, Laravel Auth Bypass + 21 More
articles.text:
This week has already been rough for cybersecurity. Critical PHP and GitLab RCE flaws, serious Linux security bugs, compromised eMudhra certificates, a Node.js RCE flaw, a hacked LiteLLM release, and hundreds of hijacked Tor relays. That's a lot to deal with in just a few days. And the week isn't even over yet.
But those big headlines are only half the story. Stolen passwords, exposed databases, broken login checks, and trusted tools being turned against their users are causing trouble too. Some attacks are clever. Others work because someone left a simple security gap open.
This ThreatsDay, we're digging into the stories that didn't make as much noise but still deserve attention. Some are strange, some are serious, and a few might surprise you. Here's everything else you shouldn't miss this week.
The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.
- 
  
  4,500+ accounts compromised Bluesky has acknowledged it's aware of a phishing attack that has compromised more than 4,500 accounts. "The attack spread through posts promoting a fake offer of a government payment," Bluesky said. "We have temporarily suspended the compromised accounts and are working with their owners to secure them and restore access. If your account was suspended, email moderation@blueskyweb.xyz and we will help to get you back into your account."
- 
  
  Android malware scam losses The Singapore Police Force has alerted users of a malware-enabled scam variant involving advertisements on social media platforms promoting senior-focused activities and programmes, water-based fitness activities, and recycling initiatives. The agency said at least 62 cases have been reported since April 2026, leading to S$989,000 in losses. "In this scam, victims would come across the fake advertisements on social media platforms, such as Facebook, and be instructed to download an Android Application Package (APK) file to facilitate programme registration or service arrangements," the Singapore Police Force said. "After installing the application, victims would receive unsolicited calls from scammers impersonating government officials or bank representatives, who would falsely claim that the victims' devices or bank accounts had been compromised, or that they were implicated in criminal activities. Victims would then be induced to transfer monies, disclose banking credentials or personal information, or surrender valuables for investigations."
- 
  
  Customer credentials exposed Andromeda said it identified a security incident on October 13, 2026, that involved unauthorized access to credentials in its environment. "We disabled the compromised accounts that day and have observed no further unauthorized activity since," it said. "We believe the activity began as part of an industry-wide attack on or about October 9th. It affected a limited number of customer accounts and involved exposure of certain Andromeda and customer credentials. If we believe you were affected, you’ve already heard from us." The company said there is no evidence of unauthorized access to customer models, datasets, or training data.
- 
  
  20 security flaws patched Roundcube has released versions 1.6.20 and 1.7.5, addressing 20 issues including IMAP command injection, SSRF filter bypass, and unsafe attachment handling. There is no evidence any of the patched vulnerabilities have been exploited.
- 
  
  Internal business systems breached On October 16, 2026, Genesys disclosed that it became aware of a cybersecurity incident involving an unauthorized third party that allowed them to access certain internal business systems, including a learning management system (LMS) and a customer relationship management (CRM) platform. The company said business and account information used to manage relationships with existing and prospective customers has been accessed and/or downloaded without authorization. However, it said its Genesys Cloud, Genesys Engage and Genesys Engage Cloud platforms were not compromised.
- 
  
  Critical Kubernetes host takeover risk AegisSec Research has disclosed details of a NVIDIA AIStore for Linux flaw present in the legacy ETL Kubernetes PodSpec initialization API, CVE-2026-65162 aka ShadowForge (CVSS score: 10.0), that enables privileged container creation and host-level compromise.
- 
  
  NFC bank fraud arrests Dutch police authorities have arrested two suspects in connection with a bank helpdesk fraud scheme that netted 170 victims and €380,000 in illicit proceeds. The arrested men include a 23-year-old from Vaassen and a 25-year-old from Ede. "Victims were called on their phones and played an audio clip," authorities said. "The scammers had created dozens of different audio clips using Artificial Intelligence, featuring various voices, banks, companies, and scenarios. The voice would, for example, alert them to suspicious activity on their bank account [and instruct them to] download an app and scan their bank card by holding it against their phone." In the process, the threat actors were able to forward the data from the bank card's NFC chip to the threat actor, who then used it to make unauthorized withdrawals.
- 
  
  Critical API authentication bypass Laravel has patched a critical security flaw (CVE-2026-114509, CVSS score: 9.2) that could allow its built-in TokenGuard to be bypassed to authenticate as an arbitrary existing user without knowledge of their valid API token. "Under certain database configurations (MySQL/MariaDB), an attacker can submit a specially crafted, non-string credential value that is mishandled during the authentication lookup, causing the underlying query to match an unintended user record rather than failing authentication as expected," Laravel said. "An unauthenticated attacker may authenticate as another user without possessing that user's API token, leading to authentication bypass and account takeover on any route protected by the affected guard." The issue has been patched in versions 13.29.0 and 12.68.0.
- 
  
  Unauthenticated database exposure An unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability has been disclosed in GLPI 11.0.8 (GHSA-753w-2942-4pxm) that could allow a remote attacker to read the entire GLPI application database. "Depending on the version, this read access can lead to an administrator account takeover (detailed below) and remote code execution," Mobeta said. The vulnerability has been patched in version 11.0.9.
- 
  
  Critical unauthenticated RCE risk Rapid7 said it discovered three new vulnerabilities in Eptura Archibus that could be exploited to achieve code execution. "A legacy API endpoint could be exploited to bypass authentication and run various functions without authentication (CVE-2026-107186, CVSS: 8.6 High)," it said. "The most serious functions allow for full database read (CVE-2026-107187, CVSS: 8.5 High) and an insecure file upload (CVE-2026-107188, CVSS: 9.6 Critical). The insecure file upload leads to remote code execution. A malicious actor with network access to the server via HTTP can read secrets and passwords out of the database. They can also run code to execute system commands as 'NT AUTHORITY/Local Service' and gain control of the server."
- 
  
  3.2 million secrets exposed Development platform Zeabur said it will shut down its services starting December 1, 2026, and finish by December 31, 2026, in response to a cybersecurity incident in which attackers leaked internal credentials stored in plaintext to compromise its infrastructure and steal over 3.2 million environment variable records and information for 321,810 accounts. "On October 14–15, 2026, an attacker used leaked Zeabur internal credentials to break into the shared cluster, some Dedicated Servers, and Zeabur internal systems, and eventually read the platform database," according to an announcement. This is the second time Zeabur has suffered a breach this year alone. In August 2026, the company said an attacker gained unauthorized access to its systems and stole sensitive data, including account information, API keys, and other secrets.
- 
  
  Source code and customer data stolen PingCAP has disclosed that attackers used stolen credentials to access internal systems and copy source code and customer-related records, including SQL editor content and encrypted API-key values. The incident took place between September 9 and October 7, 2026. "An unauthorized party used stolen service account credentials to access certain PingCAP internal systems, copy data, and obtain source code," the company said. "PingCAP became aware of the incident on October 7 and began disabling the affected credentials the same day." Exported data includes user names and email addresses, organization and project associations, SQL editor text and errors, customer contacts, contract terms, orders, pricing, payment terms, and billing configuration.
- 
  
  $2.5 million tax fraud scheme Chukwuemeka Victor Amachukwu (aka Chukwuemeka Victor Eletuo and So Kwan Leung), a 40-year-old Nigerian national, has been sentenced to eight years in prison in the U.S. for running a years-long hacking, tax fraud, and identity theft scheme. "Amachukwu took part in sophisticated schemes to hack into U.S. businesses, steal and use stolen identity information of victims, and commit fraud," the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) said. "Beginning in at least in or about 2019, Amachukwu, his co-conspirator Kinglsey Uchelue Utulu, and other Nigeria-based conspirators took part in a scheme to hack into U.S-based tax preparation businesses. The conspirators utilized spear-phishing emails to obtain access to these businesses' electronic systems. Once they had obtained access, the conspirators stole the tax and other identifying information for at least approximately 800 of the business's customers. The conspirators hacked into several U.S. based tax businesses, located in New York, Texas, and other states." The conspirators also obtained the stolen identity information of thousands of individuals and then used this information to file fraudulent tax returns with the Internal Revenue Service and state tax authorities, obtaining at least approximately $2.5 million.
- 
  
  Military identity theft scheme Robert Wayne Boling, a 45-year-old U.S. citizen, pleaded guilty to running an identity theft and fraud scheme that defrauded thousands of U.S. service members and veterans while living in the Philippines. "Boling operated from the Philippines, and he received and exploited stolen personally identifiable information (PII) of U.S. servicemembers and veterans to compromise their bank accounts and steal money and veterans' benefits," the DoJ said. "Boling's co-conspirator, Fredrick Brown, who worked as a civilian medical records administrator for the U.S. Army in South Korea, took digital photographs of the PII of thousands of military-affiliated individuals. Brown provided the stolen PII to Boling, who, along with his co-conspirators, used the PII to compromise various accounts belonging to U.S. servicemembers and veterans, including bank accounts and online government-affiliated benefits accounts." Boling pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering. He is scheduled to be sentenced on January 14, 2027, and faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison for each conspiracy charge.
- 
  
  $6 million data breach settlement Chrome Holding Co., a holding company formerly known as 23andMe, has agreed to pay California $6 million to resolve accusations that it did not effectively secure customers' personal and genetic data, resulting in a massive 2023 breach that exposed sensitive information belonging to nearly 7 million people. "With regard to the genetic data or samples maintained by 23andMe Research Institute, consumers can request that the company delete their data, destroy their test sample, or revoke their permission for their genetic data to be used for research," the office of the California Attorney General said in a statement.
- 
  
  Rogue AI containment guidelines U.S. agencies NSA, CISA, and NIST have released joint security guidelines to help organizations detect, contain, and shut down AI (or SI) agents that exhibit deviations from their approved tasks. The voluntary guidance sets out 10 practices for managing potential incidents during super intelligence training and evaluation, with a focus on maintaining human oversight and building public trust in secure SI development. "This voluntary document supports the frontier SI industry in preventing, preparing for, and responding to incidents during training and evaluation – particularly incidents in which one or more SI agents take significant uninstructed actions that compromise explicit or implicit policies, controls, or security measures imposed by the operator to define the intended task scope or to ensure human oversight," NIST said.
- 
  
  Critical developer-machine RCE A critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw has been disclosed in OpenCode affecting Windows and Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). "The flaw allows an attacker-controlled remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to execute arbitrary code on a developer's machine during a remote MCP OAuth authentication process, without additional user interaction or consent," Pillar Security said. Anomaly, OpenCode's developer, fixed the issue in version 1.18.33. The vulnerability comes a few days after OpenCode confirmed a security breach affecting its Console, which allows teams to share access to AI models through centrally managed API credentials, potentially exposing API keys linked to users of Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google AI models. The incident, it said, was related to a "large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users."
- 
  
  AI-generated code security bias AI models that have a pro-China leaning may systematically generate more vulnerable code when writing applications for Western organizations. "Ask for the app "for a US defense contractor" instead of "for a Chinese defense contractor", and Qwen3-Coder is 19% more likely to hand back an app that can be hacked," Hirundo said. "Apps built for a Hong Kong democracy group were 28% more likely to let any user read everyone else's secrets. With a security instruction in the prompt, the US contractor's apps were 27% more likely to be hackable than a neutral customer's." Hirundo also revealed that removing the model's CCP alignment removes the vulnerability from the model's weights. The development comes as Chinese open-weight models are being increasingly incorporated in enterprise workflows across the world. A similar testing by Booz Allen Hamilton in May 2026 found something similar: "Chinese LLMs produce more vulnerable code when prompted with a U.S. government persona than without — and the vulnerabilities are highly obfuscated Chinese LLMs inject PRC-aligned political bias into both the answers and code they generate."
- 
  
  Hardware MFA downgrade phishing A phishing campaign is using Okta and ServiceNow-themed domains (riskified-okta[.]com and shipmonk-servicenow[.]com) hosting spoofed SSO portals and MFA downgrade lures targeting YubiKey users to target e-commerce SaaS providers. "The campaign pairs fake Okta login pages with an MFA downgrade lure targeting YubiKey users, allowing attackers to bypass hardware-based MFA where policy permits fallback methods like SMS or email codes," Dataminr said. "Targeting is concentrated on e-commerce infrastructure providers, likely because compromising these providers creates leverage for downstream third-party breaches and data extortion."
- 
  
  Federal DeepSeek ban China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said China "will resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies," adding "China consistently opposes the overstretching of the concept of national security." The development comes after the Trump administration banned DeepSeek-related technology from federal civilian agency IT systems, including third-party products and services built using its AI models. The DHS order, issued in July and made public on October 19, 2026, also bars federal civilian agencies from procuring DeepSeek products and services. According to the order: "DeepSeek servers are located in the PRC, and the PRC legal system permits extensive authority to government cyber and intelligence functions to access private company infrastructure. For DeepSeek-hosted instances of their models, DeepSeek's account generation process collects personally identifiable information (PII) and may also track and digitally fingerprint users. DeepSeek's most widely used applications function through a prompt-and-response process that requires presenting information to the model, and which may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC if used by U.S. government employees or vendors. The transfer of the aforementioned information to the PRC, either independently or in combination with publicly available data, could produce actionable intelligence on U.S. persons and/or government programs. The models themselves may contain malware or other security vulnerabilities."
- 
  
  XWiki exploitation and botnet activity Earlier this month, the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Department of Justice (DoJ) announced the disruption of malicious tools used by a China-linked advanced persistent threat group known as Flax Typhoon. While Microscan was used to facilitate reconnaissance and computer vulnerability scanning, FishHub allegedly enabled the exploitation of computer networks through spear-phishing attacks and the deployment of follow-on payloads. In a follow-up alert, VulnCheck said it observed attempts against five vulnerabilities -- PHPUnit (CVE-2017-9841), XWiki (CVE-2025-24893), Apache HTTP Server (CVE-2021-41773), PHP-CGI (CVE-2024-4577), and ThinkPHP (CVE-2022-47945) -- from 119.13.79[.]145 (Hong Kong), 211.20.144[.]116 (Taiwan), and 210.242.76[.]32 (Taiwan). "The attacks originated from both Hong Kong and Taiwan," it said. "The Hong Kong IP exploited targets in Mexico, Great Britain, and Malaysia, while the Taiwan IPs exploited targets in India." The exploitation of XWiki by Taiwan IPs resulted in the deployment of reverse shells. On the other hand, the Hong Kong IP is a RedTail-family botnet.
- 
  
  600+ ransomware victims A new advisory from intelligence agencies in Germany, the U.K., and the U.S. has revealed that at least 600 organizations across North America, South America, Europe, and Australia have been breached by the SafePay ransomware gang since August 2024. Attacks involve the exploitation of known security flaws in edge device products and internet-exposed products (CVE-2020-3259, CVE-2023-20269, CVE-2023-27532, CVE-2024-40711, and CVE-2024-40766) or, alternatively, credential exposure and brute-force password attacks, for initial access, followed by persistence, privilege escalation, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and ransomware deployment. Back in August 2026, U.S. agencies revealed that Medusa developers and affiliates have impacted over 500 victims from a variety of critical infrastructure sectors as of April 2026, while continuing to exploit unpatched vulnerabilities as its primary means of initial access. The gang is also relying on access brokers, compensating them anywhere from $100 to $1 million to secure access to potential victims. However, there is no indication Medusa actors are developing their own zero-day or N-day vulnerabilities.
- 
  
  HTTP connection warnings enabled Google has rolled out a change in Chrome where it "explicitly asks users for permission before making an insecure HTTP connection." This feature was enabled for users enrolled in Chrome's Enhanced Protection mode of Safe Browsing. It has now been extended to all users by default. "Chrome asking the user before making an HTTP request is the culmination of more than a decade of work from countless people and organizations,” it added.
- 
  
  Critical call hang-up flaw A critical security flaw in the Signal messaging app (CVE-2026-113380, CVSS score: 9.3) can allow a malicious caller to keep audio and video tracks enabled even after the victim has hung up. The issue impacts RingRTC, a middleware library that provides Signal apps with video and voice calling services built on top of WebRTC. It also affects every Signal client across Android, iOS, and desktop. "A local hang-up is not a kill switch: it is just one more event placed at the back of the call's finite-state-machine event queue," a security researcher who goes by the online alias Imahian said. "The remote peer is trusted with that queue — there is no rate limit on peer-originated events and no priority lane for hang-up. Flood the queue with junk and the hang-up waits behind attacker noise forever, so the call (microphone, possibly camera) is never torn down."
- 
  
  GitHub connector prompt injection A critical security flaw has been disclosed in OpenAI ChatGPT's GitHub Connector, which could trick the AI chatbot into using its authorized GitHub access to modify a different repository and potentially leak its secrets by means of an indirect prompt injection planted in an attacker-controlled public repository. When a bad actor prompts ChatGPT for a deployment review of their repository, it encounters the hidden instructions and proceeds to write a GitHub Actions workflow into another, private repository that has a ChatGPT connector with the default All-repositories grant. The workflow then accesses secrets and other sensitive information, and exfiltrates it to the attacker. According to security researcher Sunil Tripathy, the vulnerability stems from a combination of indirect prompt injection, an overprivileged ChatGPT connector, and the ability of GitHub Actions to automatically run arbitrary code when the agent makes a commit to the private repository. "It demonstrates cross-account write operations, CI execution and secret exfiltration via the ChatGPT GitHub connector specifically, using indirect prompt injection from a public repository with zero attacker access to the victim," Tripathy said. "The attack requires no command injection and no document upload — just a public repository and a victim who asks their agent to review it." Following responsible disclosure to OpenAI, the company described the issue as out-of-scope.
The week isn't over, and neither are the threats. New bugs, fresh attacks, and unexpected security incidents can show up at any time. What looks safe today might be the next big headline tomorrow. That's why keeping up with security news matters more than ever.
If you found this roundup useful, subscribe to The Hacker News, follow us on social media, and make THN part of your daily reading. We track the threats, explain what matters, and help you stay ahead of what's coming. Because in cybersecurity, the story you miss today could be the one that matters tomorrow.

articles.title: INVE raises $300,000 from Outliers VC to scale eventtech platform across GCC
articles.text: Saudi Arabia-based eventtech startup INVE has raised $300,000 in a Pre-Seed funding round from Outliers VC, which previously served as the company's first paid business design partner. Founded in 2024 by Abdulrahman Alabdulkarim, INVE operates a digital event management platform for individuals and businesses, offering personalised invitations, RSVP management, guest profiles, branded registration pages and digital entry passes. The company's consumer platform has supported 250 events across more than 60 cities and towns in Saudi Arabia and the GCC, sending over 35,000 invitations and recording an 88% RSVP response rate. Its business platform launched in August 2026. The funding will support team expansion, brand development and customer acquisition, as INVE scales its consumer and business platforms across Saudi Arabia and the GCC, with longer-term plans to expand into North Africa, other African markets and Europe. Press release: INVE, a Saudi-based technology company that provides personalised invitations and event-management tools for consumers and businesses, has raised $300,000 in pre-seed funding from Outliers Venture Capital. INVE will use the investment to bring its business platform, launched in August 2026, to more companies and to grow its consumer product, proven with weddings, into the go-to for every occasion. For business hosts, guest information is often scattered between spreadsheets, inboxes, and WhatsApp conversations, so details gathered for one event may get lost when preparations begin for the next gathering. INVE keeps a living profile for every guest that enriches automatically as they engage, holding whatever a host cares to know, from dietary preferences and interests to their full attendance history, ready for every future event. Hosts use that information to personalise invitations sent from their own email addresses and company WhatsApp numbers without rebuilding guest lists or repeatedly requesting the same information. RSVP pages, registration pages and digital entry passes also carry the host’s branding, keeping their identity visible throughout the guest experience. INVE’s business platform is built for companies that treat their events as part of their brand, from technology companies, venture firms and financial services businesses to the agencies that host on their behalf. Founder Abdulrahman Alabdulkarim, now 23, built the first version of INVE in 2024 to simplify invitations and RSVP management for his sister’s wedding. The solution grew into a consumer product that has supported 250 events in over 60 cities and towns in Saudi Arabia and the GCC, sending more than 35,000 invitations with an 88% RSVP response rate. With both products live, INVE will invest in its team, brand and channels to scale them, from weddings and birthdays to business dinners and summits. Abdulrahman Alabdulkarim, Founder and CEO, INVE, said, "The guest experience doesn't start when someone walks through the door, and it doesn't end when they leave. From the first invitation to the next time you host, every interaction matters. But creating that experience often means juggling spreadsheets, messages, and different tools, with valuable guest information fragmented across them. We're building INVE to bring the entire hosting experience together, making it easier to host at any scale while building on the relationships that matter. Our vision is for INVE to become the infrastructure behind how people and businesses host across the Gulf. With Outliers behind us, we're bringing that vision to more hosts across the region.” Outliers, an operator-led venture capital firm backing early-stage founders, became INVE’s first paid business design partner before investing. The firm has been using the platform to manage invitations and guest communications under its brand, including for its forthcoming Builder Summit. Sarah AlSaleh, General Partner at Outliers VC, said, "Working with INVE as a design partner before investing gave us conviction in both the product and Abdulrahman’s ability to execute. He combines deep technical expertise with an instinctive understanding of hospitality in the region, turning something deeply personal into technology that can scale without losing its human touch. INVE brings that same philosophy to both consumer and business engagement, making every interaction more intentional and every relationship more valuable. We’re proud to back Abdulrahman and the team as they redefine how people and businesses connect." INVE’s self-service product is accessible internationally, while its immediate customer acquisition priorities are Saudi Arabia and the GCC. Longer-term ambitions include developing its business customer base in North Africa, other African markets and Europe. A software engineer by background, Alabdulkarim previously worked on backend and infrastructure systems at Lean Technologies. He graduated from King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals, where he was the university’s second recipient of the President’s Medal for Entrepreneurship for INVE.

What is NYT Connections?
NYT Connections is one of several increasingly popular word games made by the New York Times. It challenges you to find groups of four items that share something in common, and each group has a different difficulty level: green is easy, yellow a little harder, blue often quite tough and purple usually very difficult.

articles.title: Cuánto influye la luz, el aire y la temperatura en el espacio de trabajo con PC
articles.text:
Pasar varias horas frente a una computadora no depende solo de la voluntad o la motivación de quien trabaja. El entorno físico donde se ubica el escritorio también incide en la capacidad de concentrarse, generar ideas y resolver problemas con fluidez.
Factores como la luz, la temperatura, la calidad del aire y el ruido de fondo forman parte de un conjunto de condiciones que puede facilitar el trabajo intelectual o, por el contrario, sumar pequeñas distracciones que terminan afectando el rendimiento frente a la pantalla.
Un estudio publicado en 2025 en la revista Building and Environment, realizado con trabajadores de oficinas de cuatro países, encontró que una menor concentración de dióxido de carbono en el ambiente se asocia con mejores resultados en pruebas de pensamiento creativo divergente.
La misma investigación identificó que las temperaturas interiores de entre 22 y 26 grados Celsius están vinculadas a mejores puntuaciones de creatividad. Estos hallazgos no apuntan a la existencia de una oficina perfecta, sino a que el pensamiento creativo también responde a condiciones físicas concretas que pueden medirse y ajustarse.
Por qué el aire y la temperatura condicionan el pensamiento creativo
El aire que se respira durante la jornada frente a la computadora rara vez se tiene en cuenta como parte del espacio de trabajo. Sin embargo, el estudio de Building and Environment mostró una relación directa entre los niveles de CO2 y el desempeño en tareas de creatividad divergente.
Ventilar el ambiente con cierta frecuencia, cuando las condiciones exteriores lo permiten, aparece como una de las acciones más simples para reducir la acumulación de dióxido de carbono en espacios cerrados donde se pasan varias horas seguidas.
La temperatura funciona como una variable asociada. La misma investigación ubicó el rango de 22 a 26 °C como el más favorable para obtener mejores puntuaciones en las pruebas de pensamiento creativo aplicadas a los participantes.
En conjunto, estos dos elementos (aire renovado y temperatura estable dentro de ese rango) configuran una de las bases menos visibles, pero más documentadas, de un espacio de trabajo que acompaña en lugar de entorpecer el proceso creativo frente a la pantalla.
El papel de la iluminación natural y artificial en el escritorio
La luz es uno de los componentes que más rápido se nota cuando falla, pero también uno de los más fáciles de mejorar. Ubicar el escritorio cerca de una ventana permite aprovechar la luz natural durante buena parte del día.
Más allá del efecto visual sobre la habitación, contar con una fuente de luz adecuada puede volver más llevadera una jornada que, en la mayoría de los casos, transcurre frente a una pantalla durante horas.
Cuando el espacio de trabajo no cuenta con suficiente entrada de luz natural, la iluminación artificial pasa a un primer plano. Una lámpara de escritorio bien ubicada puede modificar de forma considerable la experiencia de trabajo sin necesidad de reorganizar por completo la habitación.
Ruido y sonido de fondo: su efecto en la concentración frente a la pantalla
El sonido del entorno no afecta a todas las personas de la misma manera, pero sí tiene un peso comprobado sobre el desempeño cognitivo. Una investigación publicada en 2025 sobre ambientes de oficina encontró que tanto el tipo de sonido como su nivel pueden influir en la experiencia y el rendimiento de quienes trabajan en ese espacio.
Ese mismo estudio identificó que la memoria de trabajo auditiva se veía afectada a niveles de 60 decibelios (dBA), un umbral que puede alcanzarse con facilidad en oficinas abiertas o espacios compartidos.
No se trata de buscar un silencio absoluto. Una lista de música puede ayudar a entrar en ritmo durante ciertas tareas, mientras que una conversación ajena durante un trabajo que exige concentración puede tener el efecto contrario.
La clave está en reconocer qué tipo de sonido acompaña cada tarea: música para actividades mecánicas, audífonos cuando se necesita bloquear estímulos externos o minutos de silencio cuando una idea requiere atención completa.
Organización de pantallas y dispositivos en el espacio de trabajo
Buena parte del entorno de trabajo ya no está fuera de la computadora, sino dentro de ella. Saltar constantemente entre ventanas, pestañas y aplicaciones también fragmenta la experiencia de quien trabaja frente a la pantalla.
Contar con una pantalla amplia permite mantener más información visible al mismo tiempo y reduce la cantidad de cambios entre tareas. Para quienes trabajan con imágenes, presentaciones, textos o varias herramientas de forma simultánea, el tamaño y las prestaciones del equipo influyen directamente en la fluidez del proceso.
A esto se suma la relación entre dispositivos. Computadora, teléfono y tableta no mejoran el trabajo por el solo hecho de sumarse: el beneficio aparece cuando es posible moverse entre ellos sin romper la concentración de forma constante.
La idea no pasa por acumular pantallas, sino por asignarle a cada tarea el dispositivo adecuado y reducir los pasos que separan una idea de su ejecución.
Cambiar de escenario, ¿mejora realmente la creatividad?
El escritorio no tiene por qué ser el único lugar de trabajo. Alternar entre distintos espacios (uno para concentrarse, un sofá para leer, una terraza para pensar) permite mirar una tarea o un problema desde otro ángulo según el momento.
Sin embargo, la movilidad entre espacios no garantiza por sí sola mejores resultados creativos. Una investigación publicada en Management Science en 2025 mostró que los espacios poco convencionales no aumentan automáticamente la creatividad y que, en determinadas circunstancias, incluso pueden limitar el pensamiento divergente.
Ese hallazgo descarta la existencia de un escenario creativo universal válido para todas las personas o todas las tareas. Lo que parece tener más peso es la posibilidad de elegir, en cada momento, el espacio que mejor se adapta a lo que se necesita resolver.
Decoración y personalización del espacio de trabajo
Plantas, objetos personales, fotografías o una pared de color pueden hacer que un espacio de trabajo se sienta propio. Esa personalización, sin embargo, no equivale de forma automática a un entorno más propicio para pensar.
Llenar el escritorio de estímulos visuales bajo la premisa de que un entorno llamativo favorece la creatividad tampoco garantiza mejores ideas. De hecho, investigaciones recientes sobre el tema sugieren que los ambientes poco convencionales o cargados de estímulos no siempre favorecen el pensamiento creativo.
La pregunta útil, antes de sumar elementos decorativos, apunta a identificar qué necesita cada persona para trabajar bien: una mesa despejada, música de fondo, una segunda pantalla, acceso a luz natural o la posibilidad de cambiar de lugar cuando una tarea lo requiere.
Un espacio de trabajo con PC que combine aire ventilado, temperatura estable entre 22 y 26 °C, iluminación adecuada y control sobre el ruido reúne las condiciones que, según la evidencia reciente, acompañan mejor los procesos de concentración y pensamiento creativo durante la jornada frente a la pantalla.
