articles.title: Banni des États-Unis, DeepSeek s'offre 15 milliards de dollars pour écraser ChatGPT
articles.text:
Quelques jours après la publication des restrictions américaines, DeepSeek serait sur le point de boucler une levée de fonds colossale. De quoi accélérer le développement de ses modèles d’intelligence artificielle et réduire sa dépendance aux technologies américaines.
Les États-Unis veulent chasser DeepSeek de leurs administrations. En Chine, les investisseurs semblent au contraire prêts à lui signer un chèque XXL. Selon Reuters, la start-up chinoise serait sur le point de réunir 100 milliards de yuans, soit près de 15 milliards de dollars, auprès d’une quinzaine d’investisseurs, parmi lesquels Tencent, CATL et plusieurs grands groupes industriels.
Un montant deux fois supérieur à l’objectif initial, qui témoigne de l’intérêt suscité par DeepSeek dans son pays. L’opération n’est toutefois pas encore officiellement bouclée et ses modalités pourraient évoluer.
Une levée de fonds qui tombe à pic pour DeepSeek
Le calendrier interpelle. Le 20 octobre dernier, Washington a publié une décision interdisant aux administrations fédérales civiles américaines d’utiliser les produits et services de DeepSeek, y compris certaines solutions tierces reposant sur ses technologies.
Mais contrairement à ce que pourrait laisser penser la proximité des deux annonces, cette levée n’a pas été organisée dans l’urgence pour répondre aux sanctions. Les discussions avec les investisseurs ont commencé dès l’été, tandis que la décision américaine avait été prise en juillet.
L'argent devrait notamment permettre au laboratoire chinois d’accélérer ses investissements dans les infrastructures de calcul. Selon le Wall Street Journal, DeepSeek travaille également avec Huawei pour transférer davantage de charges d’entraînement vers des puces chinoises. Les GPU de NVIDIA restent néanmoins utilisés pour les opérations les plus exigeantes.
L'enjeu dépasse donc le simple financement de nouveaux modèles. Il s’agit de bâtir une infrastructure capable de résister aux nombreuses restrictions technologiques imposées par Washington.
Après R1, DeepSeek poursuit sa course avec V4.1
En janvier 2025, DeepSeek-R1 avait bousculé le marché de l’IA en démontrant qu’un modèle de raisonnement chinois pouvait rivaliser avec des références américaines, à des coûts annoncés bien inférieurs.
Depuis, l’entreprise a multiplié les évolutions. Son modèle phare actuel, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, a encore été amélioré le 17 octobre avec la version 1017, notamment sur les tâches complexes de programmation.
Sous le capot, cette IA repose sur une architecture à mélange d’experts (MoE) qui compte 552 milliards de paramètres. Sa particularité est de n’en mobiliser qu’une fraction à chaque étape, environ 8 milliards pour traiter les données entrantes et 16 milliards pour produire les réponses.
Cette approche réduit la puissance de calcul nécessaire à chaque requête, même si héberger un modèle aussi imposant exige toujours une infrastructure conséquente.
Un concurrent qui prépare déjà la suite
DeepSeek ne cherche plus seulement à concurrencer ChatGPT auprès du grand public. Ses modèles à poids ouverts intéressent aussi les entreprises, qui peuvent les déployer sur leurs propres serveurs plutôt que de dépendre exclusivement d’une API.
Et les premiers résultats commerciaux semblent suivre. Toujours d’après le Wall Street Journal, Liang Wenfeng, le PDG de DeepSeek, indiquait aux investisseurs en septembre que les revenus de son entreprise avaient atteint un rythme annualisé d’environ un milliard de dollars, sans toutefois préciser si sa société était rentable.
La start-up préparerait également une introduction à la Bourse de Shanghai, potentiellement dès 2027. Selon Reuters, la levée de fonds privée en cours valoriserait DeepSeek à 500 milliards de yuans avant l’apport des nouveaux capitaux.
DeepSeek a contribué à rendre l’intelligence artificielle moins chère à utiliser. Mais pour continuer à rivaliser avec OpenAI, Anthropic et Google, le laboratoire chinois va devoir entrer un peu plus dans la course à la puissance.
- Compréhension avancée du langage naturel
- Réponses adaptées à des contextes variés
- Disponible en plusieurs langues
Une architecture Mixture of Experts (MoE) découpe un grand modèle en plusieurs sous-modèles spécialisés (experts) et utilise un composant de routage pour n’activer que les experts pertinents à chaque étape. Au lieu de faire tourner tous les paramètres à chaque requête, seule une fraction du modèle est réellement calculée, ce qui diminue les opérations nécessaires et donc le coût par réponse. Cela peut aussi améliorer les performances sur des tâches variées, car chaque expert se concentre sur un sous-domaine. En contrepartie, l’orchestration (routage, équilibrage de charge) et l’infrastructure restent complexes, et la mémoire/stockage nécessaires pour héberger l’ensemble du modèle demeure élevée.
Un modèle à poids ouverts fournit (totalement ou partiellement) les paramètres entraînés du réseau, ce qui permet à une entreprise de l’héberger et de l’exécuter sur sa propre infrastructure. À l’inverse, une API donne surtout accès à un service distant : on envoie une requête, on reçoit une réponse, sans contrôler l’environnement d’exécution ni le modèle sous-jacent. Les poids ouverts facilitent l’adaptation (fine-tuning), l’audit interne et certaines exigences de souveraineté ou de conformité (données, localisation). En échange, l’utilisateur doit gérer le déploiement, l’optimisation, la sécurité et les coûts GPU/serveurs, qui peuvent être importants sur de gros modèles.
L’entraînement de grands modèles nécessite des accélérateurs (souvent des GPU) capables de calcul massivement en parallèle, et l’offre la plus performante est historiquement dominée par des acteurs soumis aux règles américaines. Les contrôles à l’export et interdictions d’usage peuvent limiter l’accès aux puces, aux interconnexions, aux logiciels et parfois même à des services cloud, ce qui ralentit la montée en puissance. Pour contourner ce goulot d’étranglement, il faut soit sécuriser des stocks et des filières d’approvisionnement, soit migrer une partie des charges vers des puces alternatives (par exemple locales), souvent avec des compromis sur la maturité logicielle et l’efficacité. Résultat : la stratégie compute (choix des puces, datacenters, optimisation) devient un enjeu aussi important que la R&D sur les modèles eux-mêmes.

articles.title: New QPACK Flaws Can Crash HTTP/3 Servers, Trigger Up to 4,000-Fold Memory Amplification
articles.text:
A remote attacker who has not logged in can crash many HTTP/3 web servers with a single connection, security firm FoxIO disclosed, releasing working proof-of-concept code.
By sending a small batch of compressed HTTP headers that expands in memory to a much larger set, the attacker can force the server to use thousands of times more memory than it received, enough to run a default server out of memory.
The flaws cause only denial-of-service attacks, with no evidence of data theft or code execution and no public reports of attacks in the wild. Fixes are out for quic-go, Cloudflare quiche, lsquic and Wireshark, but Bun, the h3 Rust library and aioquic were still unpatched at disclosure.
FoxIO found the same class of flaw in seven of ten HTTP/3 stacks it tested. The common cause is in QPACK, the scheme HTTP/3 uses to compress request headers so repeated fields travel as a short code instead of the full text.
A server is supposed to cap the size of the headers after it unpacks them. The affected stacks cap the compressed batch that arrives on the wire, but not the unpacked result, or they apply the cap too late, so a single request can expand into hundreds of thousands of header entries that the server holds in memory.
The reach is wide because these stacks sit under common software. quic-go is the Go library behind Caddy, Traefik and cloudflared; lsquic is LiteSpeed's library, used in LiteSpeed Web Server and OpenLiteSpeed; and Bun's HTTP/3 server runs on lsquic.
The attacker needs no account or special access, and since HTTP/3 runs over UDP, the request reaches the server before much of the usual filtering applies.
Which stacks are fixed and which are still exposed, as of October 22, 2026:
| Stack | Status | Fixed version | Identifier | 
|---|---|---|---|
| quic-go | Fixed | 0.57.0 | CVE-2025-64702 | 
| Cloudflare quiche | Fixed | 0.29.3 | CVE-2026-12523 | 
| lsquic | Fixed | 4.9.0 | no CVE | 
| Wireshark | Fixed | 4.6.2 / 4.4.12 | CVE-2025-13945 | 
| Bun | Unpatched | — | no CVE | 
| h3 (hyperium) | Unpatched | — | no CVE | 
| aioquic / mitmproxy | Unpatched | — | no CVE | 
FoxIO lists IIS, Envoy, ngtcp2/nghttp3, and Google's quiche as not affected, each because it caps the unpacked headers while decoding rather than after.
The amplification varies by stack, in FoxIO's own tests against default settings. On quic-go, a 1 MB compressed batch unpacked into about 160,000 header fields and left roughly 15 MB held in the request, about 17 times the bytes sent; quic-go's own advisory puts the possible expansion at around 50 times.
A second method drives the ratio much higher: the attacker stores one roughly 4 KB header entry, then points at it thousands of times using one-byte references, and the server rebuilds the full entry on each reference. FoxIO measured about 4,000 times on Bun and between 600 and 1,800 times on lsquic.
Bun carries a worst-case. Its HTTP/3 server, which Bun's documentation calls experimental, uses lsquic but replaces the part that caps header memory with its own code, which checks each header but never the running total. FoxIO found that once the unpacked headers pass 2 GB, a size counter in that code overflows to zero and the server enters a loop it never leaves.
A single stream carrying about 516 KB on the wire, FoxIO reported, leaves the server stuck at 100 percent CPU with no recovery, blocking new requests. The missing running total is what lets the overflow be reached; lsquic's own 64 KB cap prevents it.
Wireshark is a different case from the server flaws. Its issue crashes the HTTP/3 dissector, the part that reads HTTP/3 out of a capture, when Wireshark decrypts traffic using a key-log file or opens a capture file that holds decryption secrets. It is not a server an attacker reaches over the network. Wireshark said it is "unaware of any exploits for this issue."
Operators should upgrade to the fixed releases above. For the stacks with no fix, FoxIO gives interim steps: on Bun, do not expose an HTTP/3 server; on mitmproxy, turn off HTTP/3 by passing --set http3=false; and for the h3 Rust library, set a sensible limit with max_field_section_size.
The lsquic fix, released July 16, 2026, caps how many unpacked header sets a server holds per stream, defaulting to one. FoxIO said the work began after Gal Bar Nahum's research into "MadeYouReset," a denial-of-service technique against HTTP/2, which asked whether HTTP/3's header compression had a similar weakness.

articles.title: Video en vivo para viajes de adolescentes, opción Extra Comfort y más actualizaciones hoy de Uber y Cabify
articles.text:
Dos plataformas de movilidad incorporaron cambios que apuntan directamente a la seguridad y el bienestar de sus usuarios. Por un lado, se habilitó una función que permite a padres y tutores observar en vivo los trayectos de adolescentes a través del interior del vehículo.
Por otro, se reforzaron los protocolos de calidad y atención en una categoría premium de viajes, junto con un esquema de reconocimiento para los conductores. Estas novedades corresponden a Uber y Cabify, respectivamente.
Video en vivo para supervisar trayectos de adolescentes en Uber Teens
La nueva función de Uber permite que padres y tutores accedan a una transmisión de video en vivo del interior del vehículo mientras un adolescente de entre 14 y 17 años realiza un viaje a través de Uber Teens.
El funcionamiento es directo: al iniciar el trayecto, el padre, madre o tutor recibe una notificación en la aplicación y, desde su propia cuenta, puede acceder a la transmisión que capta el teléfono del conductor.
Esta herramienta busca responder una inquietud habitual entre las familias: cómo acompañar en tiempo real los desplazamientos de los más jóvenes sin estar físicamente presentes. El video en vivo ofrece justamente esa posibilidad, al permitir observar lo que ocurre dentro del vehículo durante todo el recorrido.
La disponibilidad de esta opción depende de que el conductor la tenga habilitada y de las condiciones técnicas del dispositivo, por lo que no estará presente en todos los viajes. Si la transmisión se interrumpe, los padres pueden intentar reconectarse o recurrir al chat grupal para comunicarse directamente con el adolescente y el conductor.
Controles de privacidad y herramientas de seguridad adicionales
La actualización contempla mecanismos para proteger la privacidad de quienes participan en el trayecto. Solo el padre o tutor vinculado a la cuenta del adolescente puede acceder a la transmisión, y ese acceso se cierra automáticamente cuando finaliza el viaje.
En caso de reportarse un incidente, Uber puede revisar las grabaciones correspondientes como parte de sus procesos internos de seguridad y soporte.
Esta función se suma a un conjunto de más de 40 herramientas de seguridad ya disponibles en Uber Teens. Entre ellas figuran el seguimiento en tiempo real del trayecto, el chat grupal para coordinar recogidas, la verificación mediante código PIN para confirmar que el adolescente aborda el vehículo correcto y la tecnología RideCheck, que detecta paradas anómalas durante el recorrido.
Además, los viajes de esta categoría solo se asignan a conductores con las calificaciones más altas dentro de la plataforma.
Cabify refuerza su categoría premium con foco en la comodidad del pasajero
En Bogotá, Cabify anunció la renovación de su categoría Extra Comfort, con la que busca ofrecer una experiencia estandarizada y predecible para quienes priorizan la calidad y el espacio durante sus desplazamientos.
Un estudio de Cifras y Conceptos citado por la compañía señala que el 55% de los usuarios de plataformas de movilidad las utiliza a diario o varias veces por semana. Ese mismo informe ubica la calidad y la comodidad como el segundo atributo más valorado al momento de elegir cómo moverse, solo detrás de la seguridad.
La propuesta renovada se sostiene en cuatro pilares. En materia de seguridad, los conductores asignados a esta categoría han superado filtros exigentes y cuentan con respaldo de un canal de soporte especializado.
En cuanto a calidad, la compañía implementará un modelo de verificación continua mediante “mystery shoppers”, personal que viaja de forma anónima para evaluar el servicio desde la perspectiva del usuario.
El pilar de comodidad incluye una flota exclusiva de camionetas tipo SUV, con mayor espacio, botellas de agua durante el trayecto y la incorporación futura de conexión WiFi y tablets interactivas a bordo. El cuarto pilar, personalización, contempla una línea telefónica de atención directa para resolver cualquier inconveniente durante el viaje.
Programa de reconocimiento para conductores en Bogotá
Para sostener este estándar de servicio, la empresa de red de transporte y tecnología proyecta conformar una flota de 1.000 conductores en la categoría Extra Comfort durante su primer año de operación en la ciudad.
En paralelo, la compañía presentó el programa de Embajadores Conductores, una iniciativa que busca distinguir a quienes mantienen un desempeño constante. Un grupo de 100 conductores integrará este nivel, para lo cual deben acreditar más de un año de actividad en la aplicación, una calificación mínima de 4,9 sobre 5,0 y estar libres de reportes.
Quienes alcancen esta distinción pueden aumentar sus ganancias hasta en un 30% por viaje, además de recibir prioridad en los trayectos más rentables, asistencia telefónica permanente con atención preferencial y acceso a alianzas para servicios de lavado de vehículos y capacitaciones.
El programa incluye también reconocimientos a través de la iniciativa “Cumpliendo Sueños”, cuyos beneficios se extienden a las familias de los conductores. Bogotá funciona como ciudad piloto para este proyecto, con planes de extenderlo de forma progresiva a otras ciudades del país.

articles.title: 'Do I want to test them? Oh, you betcha': Grado just launched its 'most accessible' open-back headphones in the Signature Series, and even the glow up is noteworthy
articles.text:
Grado's all-new S150 wired headphones are the most affordable in the Signature Series — and I spy a few subtle design tweaks that'll make them a huge hit
Meet the Grado Signature S150 (cheaper, but still a fair chunk more that $150)
- Grado's new S150 are the most affordable in the Signature Series
- Newly developed 44mm S driver derived from the firm's higher-end S950
- $295 / £295 (which is around AU$420, taking the US figure as a guide)
Regular readers (and anyone who adores audiophile-grade open-back wired headphones) will likely remember our largely glowing review of the Grado Signature S750.
But, at $1,695 / £1,695 (about AU$3,400), it's fair to say those Signature Series cans are aimed at a very… specific type of buyer. However, the new S150 — billed as the "most accessible entry point into Grado's expanding and award-winning Signature Line" — will set you back less than one fifth of that asking fee.
And Grado assures us that you're still getting the Grado goods. It's all thanks to the S150's newly developed 44mm S driver, which is derived from the family-run firm's much higher-end HP100 SE (yours for a cool $2,495 / £2,795, or in the region of AU$4,230) and Signature S950 headphones (which go for $2,195 / £2,495 or about AU$4,900. And do remember that your audio-curious ears deserve the best your budget can stretch to).
I love Grado's aesthetic, but this toned-down set might have even broader appeal
Let's get into the slight style change, shall we? Grado calls the earpieces an "all-new single-piece housing design", noting the "modernized Grado styling with unmistakable identity". I say — and I think a lot of people might agree — I really like it. They're just slightly less brutalist than what we're used to aesthetically from Grado; see the high-end Hemp or the more affordable SR80x for further reference.
The new driver (they're still open-back headphones; this is Grado we're talking about) incorporates a paper-composite diaphragm, based on the technology found in the larger 52mm S drivers from the HP100 SE and S950. So you're getting a smaller 44mm driver unit, but it uses the same tech that makes much pricier cans great. And I think it shows that Grado’s committed to distilling its expertise down to more accessible levels.
Also, despite that more palatable price point of $295 / £295 or equivalent, you still get the detachable Signature Bronze cables (a standard perk within Grado's Signature Series) plus what Grado calls a "comfortably padded leather headband" for those long critical listening sessions.
The S150 features 3.5mm connections at each ear cup, and the included cable terminates in a 3.5mm plug at the source end, but is supplied with a 6.3mm adapter to provide compatibility with a wide range of the best portable audio players, headphone amplifiers, and assorted home audio kit.

Grado also tells us that the S150 can also be ordered with alternative cable terminations should you prefer, allowing listeners to select the connection that best suits their system.

articles.title: Leaked Trailer Shows the Mass Effect Game BioWare Was Making Before EA Shut It Down
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Leaked Trailer Shows the Mass Effect Game BioWare Was Making Before EA Shut It Down
A day after EA shut down BioWare, a trailer for the canceled next Mass Effect game has leaked online, and it seems the game was going to be called Mass Effect: Universe. Reddit user Random_Hyabusa_Ninja posted the roughly two-minute clip on r/masseffect on October 22, first in the replies of another post, and then as a standalone post. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier has since confirmed on Bluesky that it's a real trailer for the Mass Effect game BioWare was working on up until the closure. The clip is a cinematic rather than gameplay. It follows a new human protagonist, with no sign of Shepard, through a tense bar conversation with an Asari who appears to be Liara T'Soni, cuts to a few gunfights and a Krogan, and ends on the Mass Effect: Universe logo.
The leak also raises questions about how far along the game actually was. EA's internal memo described it as being in early development, and around 50 of the 400 jobs EA is cutting were tied to it. However, a Reddit user claiming to be an EA employee said the trailer had been ready for months and that the project was further along than people think. BioWare first teased the game back in 2020, so that claim doesn't seem far-fetched, but its source is questionable at best. There's no word from EA on the leak so far, though it's reasonable to expect takedown requests to follow.
Sources:
				Reddit, 				Jason Schreier on Bluesky

articles.title: IPTV pirate : beIN Sports obtient le premier feu vert judiciaire pour le blocage automatisé
articles.text:
La France fait un pas de plus vers le blocage automatisé des retransmissions sportives pirates. beIN Sports vient d'obtenir une première autorisation judiciaire pour protéger ses droits sur la Bundesliga. Une avancée concrète, même si le dispositif n'est pas encore opérationnel.
Dans une décision rendue le 16 octobre, le tribunal judiciaire de Paris a autorisé beIN Sports à recourir au nouveau mécanisme de blocage automatisé des services pirates. Selon le diffuseur, il s'agit de la première application judiciaire de la réforme adoptée cet été. L'objectif est de pouvoir intervenir pendant les rencontres du championnat allemand de football, plutôt que de laisser les flux illégaux circuler pendant une bonne partie des matchs.
beIN Sports ouvre la voie au nouveau dispositif
L'information, révélée le 20 octobre par The Media Leader, marque une étape dans l'application de la loi du 3 août 2026. Comme nous l'expliquions dès juillet, cette réforme permet aux titulaires de droits de transmettre automatiquement les nouvelles adresses des services pirates aux intermédiaires désignés par la justice, sans attendre une validation individuelle préalable des agents de l'Arcom.
Le régulateur conserve néanmoins la supervision du système, notamment en approuvant les méthodes de collecte des adresses et en contrôlant les mesures appliquées. « Dès sa mise en œuvre, nous pourrons agir en temps réel, au moment même où les rencontres sont diffusées », souligne Caroline Besse Guenneteau, secrétaire générale de beIN Media Group.
Le détail de la décision du 16 octobre n'a toutefois pas été rendu public. Les intermédiaires précisément visés, la durée des mesures et la procédure judiciaire suivie restent donc à confirmer.
Une mise en service encore attendue
Le mécanisme doit toujours être déployé dans les conditions définies par l'Arcom. En septembre, son président évoquait une mise en service en janvier 2027. beIN Sports parle désormais d'une activation « très prochainement », sans nouvelle date précise.
Cette décision intervient également quelques jours après un autre jugement concernant beIN Sports. Le 7 octobre, le tribunal judiciaire de Paris avait refusé d'infliger de lourdes astreintes à NordVPN, Surfshark et Cloudflare, malgré des blocages incomplets de sites pirates. Les deux affaires sont distinctes : le jugement du 7 octobre portait sur l'exécution de mesures existantes, tandis que la nouvelle autorisation concerne le futur système automatisé.
Il est donc probable que les premiers blocages en plein match interviennent plus tôt que prévu. Pour l'Arcom, l'enjeu sera d'éviter que cette accélération ne provoque des coupures abusives de services légitimes. Le risque n'est pas théorique : en Espagne, les blocages d'adresses IP obtenus par LaLiga contre le piratage ont déjà perturbé de nombreux sites sans rapport avec le football, notamment parce qu'ils partageaient des adresses IP hébergées chez Cloudflare. Une étude de l'OONI a recensé plus de 500 000 domaines affectés au cours de la période étudiée.
La justice vient donc d'ouvrir une nouvelle porte à beIN Sports. Nous verrons si le futur dispositif parviendra à concilier rapidité d'intervention et précision des blocages, ce qui est loin d'être gagné d'avance.

articles.title: Someone Tried to Exploit PHP2Shell 4 Days Before the Vulnerabilities Were Publicly Disclosed
articles.text:
Amazon's Threat Intelligence team on Wednesday said it detected an attempt to exploit the newly disclosed PHP2Shell vulnerabilities dating back to October 17, 2026, against its MadPot honeypot service, as the flaws come under broad exploitation in the wild following the release of the patches.
"The exploit attempt originated from an IP address associated with a commercial anonymization network," CJ Moses, CISO of Amazon Integrated Security, said in a post shared with The Hacker News.
"While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure."
The attempt, Amazon said, was recorded from "103.216.220[.]92," an IP address geolocated to Australia. An Amazon spokesperson told The Hacker News that the activity was largely a one-off probe.
The activity relates to a set of two vulnerabilities impacting PHP core, both rated 9.2 on the CVSS scoring system. Tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and discovered by researchers from Calif, OpenAI, and Google-owned Wiz, the flaws can be abused to achieve pre-authentication remote code execution on affected systems.
The shortcomings are present in every PHP release from the 7.x and 8.x series, and pose a risk to every reachable PHP endpoint on an affected server, including static forms, login routes, and health checks. According to CrowdStrike, an attack exploiting the flaws leaves virtually no digital traces.
"There is no authentication to bypass, no session to steal, and no vulnerable endpoint to discover," CrowdStrike said. "The exposure is independent of the CMS, framework, or plug-ins in use."
"Worker processes remain stable, responses return HTTP 200, and application logs record no anomalies, because no application code ever ran. The only server-side trace is a single memory-limit fatal in the web server's error log, which is routinely dismissed as noise, leaving defenders without actionable web telemetry to identify compromised endpoints."
Originally scheduled for coordinated disclosure on October 22, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. UTC, details about the CVE identifiers and a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit leaked ahead of time, prompting the PHP Foundation to move the release forward by one day.
"Both issues sit in parts of PHP that nearly every request touches: memory management and error handling," the PHP Foundation said. "Their central place in PHP is what made both vulnerabilities serious, and also so hard to fix without breaking compatibility, hurting performance, or forcing changes on the large ecosystem of third-party extensions."
Amazon said it detected multiple PoC exploits for PHP2Shell coinciding with the day of the release of the fixes, with the earliest attempt flagged around October 21, 2026, at 2 a.m. UTC.
This was followed by additional exploitation attempts from anonymized infrastructure over the next six hours. The variety of payloads and the anonymization infrastructure used indicate that multiple threat actors are involved, Amazon Threat Intelligence said.
The attempts have been recorded from the following IP addresses on October 21, 2026 -
- 31.223.184[.]166
- 37.19.200[.]5
- 134.209.159[.]64
- 103.114.163[.]188
- 95.217.98[.]37
According to ELLIO, the first PHP2Shell request targeting its sensors was observed on October 21, 2026, at 8:36 a.m. UTC, less than an hour after "Chainguard unilaterally broke the embargo and published built images containing the fix."
"Chainguard had received the patch in advance so its users could update the moment the vulnerabilities were disclosed," the PHP Foundation said. "Any attacker could now study the fix in binary form while every other PHP user was still waiting for the release. This disregarded weeks of work by many parties toward a coordinated disclosure."
The severity of the vulnerabilities has prompted warnings from international cybersecurity agencies such as the U.K. National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) and the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), urging organizations to apply the fixes as soon as possible or consider taking them offline.
"Monitor web servers for suspicious activity, including PHP processes unexpectedly launching command shells or downloading files," the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said in an X post. "Ensure appropriate process-monitoring capabilities are in place to help identify potential exploitation."
In a similar alert, the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA) said the vulnerabilities can provide threat actors with a direct path to the server's file system or database. OpenAI, which described the flaws as "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory," has released a Codex skill to check if a website or local PHP binary is vulnerable to PHP2Shell.
With PHP powering a majority of the websites in the world, the vast attack surface, coupled with the severity and ease of exploitation of the PHP2Shell flaws, poses major risks as it allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code and steal sensitive data.
"PHP is used by almost 70% of websites," Cloudflare said. "The php2shell vulnerabilities affect the PHP runtime itself and can allow attackers to execute malicious code on vulnerable servers, expose customer data, or disrupt services. Because PHP underpins widely used platforms such as WordPress and Magento, these flaws could potentially affect a large number of applications across the internet."
VulnCheck's analysis has identified PHP on 2,608,039 internet-facing hosts, out of which over 700,000 hosts run PHP 3.x through 7.3. Another set of about 400,000 hosts run PHP versions 7.4, 8.0, or 8.1, while 403,000 hosts run supported 8.2 through 8.5 branches.
In a similar breakdown, Modat said it detected 4.38 million internet-facing PHP services as of October 20, 2026, with 79% (i.e., about 3.47 million) of them on a branch that PHP no longer supports (4.x, 5.x, 7.x, 8.0, or 8.1). PHP 7.4, which reached end-of-life in 2022, accounts for 878,761 services, followed by PHP 5.3 with 486,684 services and PHP 7.2 with 461,965 services.
"PHP is a massively popular language, and powers large parts of the internet," Ilkka Turunen, Field CTO at Sonatype, said in a statement. "The immediate priority is clear accountability: know where PHP is used across your services and products, who owns remediation, and how quickly fixes can be deployed."
"It is likely there is a long tail of environments needing to apply this patch as PHP is bundled into many other operating system distributions, as well as is found in many historic environments."
Some of the other notable developments are listed below -
- WebOps platform has blocked over 60,000 suspicious requests probing the vulnerability as of October 21, 2026, at 7:08 p.m. PDT.
- VulnCheck has identified two hosts, 85.11.167[.]243 and 45.198.224[.]169, with the user-agent "php2shell-scan/109618" weaponizing CVE-2026-109618 to target its honeypots, while 109.71.252[.]97 has leveraged both the flaws.
- Cloudflare has observed attack traffic targeting its customers, with threat actors "mutating the attack payload to try to bypass our protections by tracking the volume of matches and cross-referencing with the rule logic."
- CloudLinux has released fixed packages for ea-php52 through ea-php85 and every alt-php version.
- JFrog has observed fake PoC exploits and prank malware being published on GitHub that change the victim's wallpaper to NSFW content.
- Additional guidance and mitigations have been published by numerous security and software vendors, including Akamai, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Arctic Wolf, Automattic, Cisco Talos, Coalition, Corelight, CyCognito, Datadog, Debian, Endor Labs, Expel, Fastly, Fortinet, Google Cloud, Hadrian, Huntress, Imperva, Intruder, Kaspersky, Microsoft Azure, NetSPI, Orca Security, OX Security, Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, Patchstack, Pentest Tools, Qualys, Rapid7, Recorded Future, ReliaQuest, Sansec, SOCRadar, Searchlight Cyber, SolarWinds, Sophos, Tanium, Tenable, Trend Micro, Ubuntu, Vercel, watchTowr, Wordfence, and Zscaler.
- Government agencies across the world have also issued advisories for the vulnerabilities: the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD), the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (CCCS), CERT-EU, CISA, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA), the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI), the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), the U.K.'s NCSC, NCSC-NL, and NSA.
"The time from patch to working exploit is shrinking for structural reasons," Moses said. "In the past, most exploitation we observed came after a public proof of concept was released. A small number of capable actors built exploits, and everyone else waited for them.."
"That dependency is weakening. AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a patch diff or advisory into a working exploit. As a result, more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed."

articles.title: “Tu peux pirater ça ?” : ils demandent à Claude de nettoyer leurs télés, et les pubs disparaissent
articles.text:
“Tu peux pirater ça ?” : ils demandent à Claude de nettoyer leurs télés, et les pubs disparaissent
Sur Reddit, impossible d'y échapper : chaque jour, de nouveaux propriétaires racontent comment Claude Code a effacé les bannières sponsorisées et les mouchards de leur téléviseur. L'engouement agace déjà une partie des habitués, mais un adepte vient de réussir l'impensable sur une Samsung.
Ryan Doyle a envoyé à Claude Code, l'agent de programmation d'Anthropic, la fiche commerciale de son téléviseur, puis lui a demandé s'il pouvait le pirater. Guidé pas à pas, il a supprimé publicités et logiciels préinstallés, redonné du nerf à un menu poussif et personnalisé l'économiseur d'écran.
	
J'ai piraté ma télé avec Claude Code aujourd'hui. Je lui ai envoyé la fiche produit de mon téléviseur et je lui ai demandé : "Tu peux pirater ça ?"
Sa vidéo montre ensuite une interface qui défile sans la moindre latence.
This is how fast the TV moves now that Claude deleted all the BS laggy bloatware it comes with https://t.co/nUCEjqPwAOpic.twitter.com/g07CEgC1GJ
— Ryan Doyle (@doooyle) October 17, 2026
Le même jour, Gathin T. s'attaque au téléviseur Xiaomi de ses parents, qui leur infligeait une réclame avant même d'ouvrir Netflix : 25 paquets neutralisés, un écran d'accueil façon Apple TV. Sa recette est devenue un projet libre, cleanyourtv, qui revendique plus de 21 000 étoiles sur GitHub.
Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon!
It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get to Netflix. 
Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages and wrote a new launcher.
Looks like an Apple TV now lol pic.twitter.com/E5Q4A1b0yI
— Gathin (Ø,G) (@gathint) October 17, 2026
Sur Reddit, la télé "nettoyée par Claude" devient un mème
En quelques jours, r/ClaudeAI s'est couvert de téléviseurs TCL, Sony, Hisense ou Xiaomi délestés de leurs pubs, au point de lasser une partie des abonnés.
	
Je suis convaincu que tu montes une arnaque quelconque, c'est le vingtième post de ce genre que je vois aujourd'hui.
D'autres répondent par la dérision. Un membre se contente d'un laconique "Encore ça". Un autre prétend avoir piraté l'afficheur de son micro-ondes pour qu'il lui montre des publicités, et promet d'en publier le code "s'il y a assez de demande".
Un récit a pourtant mis tout le monde d'accord. Persuadé de posséder une Android TV, l'internaute 0xVic découvre que son téléviseur tourne sous Tizen, le système verrouillé de Samsung. Privé d'yeux, Claude a bâti une page web locale qui pilotait la caméra du smartphone et photographiait l'écran toutes les quatre secondes. Il y a laissé onze heures, deux plafonds de session et 30 % d'un forfait Max à 100 dollars par mois. En échange, 0xVic a obtenu un accueil inspiré d'Apple TV et un identifiant publicitaire Samsung effacé. Au passage, Claude s'est même infligé quelques rickrolls.
Comment nettoyer sa télé Android avec Claude Code
La méthode vise les téléviseurs Android TV et Google TV : TCL, Sony, Philips, Xiaomi, Hisense, Thomson, et même le Freebox Player POP. Dans Paramètres, puis Préférences de l'appareil et À propos, on appuie sept fois sur "Build" pour débloquer les options développeur, où l'on active le débogage USB, ainsi que le débogage réseau s'il est proposé. Sur un ordinateur relié au même Wi-Fi, on colle dans Claude Code (ou Codex, ou Gemini CLI) le fichier PROMPT.md de cleanyourtv en précisant son modèle. Il reste à valider l'autorisation sur la télé, puis à répondre au questionnaire : applications à garder, assistant vocal, Chromecast, mises à jour.
Comptez une quinzaine de minutes. Rien n'est désinstallé, et un script restaure l'état d'origine. Les Fire TV d'Amazon ont leur propre recette, dumbtv, qui coupe une soixantaine de paquets, dont la reconnaissance automatique de contenu chargée d'identifier ce que vous regardez.
Samsung, LG et risque de brick : les limites
Sur Samsung, l'aventure reste un parcours du combattant. Un propriétaire de Q70B a bien remplacé son écran d'accueil, mais en détournant des réglages non documentés. Chez LG, il faut rooter le téléviseur. Les ratés existent aussi : un internaute affirme avoir rendu le sien inutilisable. Désactiver l'accueil d'origine avant d'installer son remplaçant prive la télécommande de touche Accueil, et beaucoup de listes coupent les mises à jour, donc les correctifs de sécurité. Une fois le ménage terminé, refermez le débogage, faute de quoi il reste une porte ouverte sur le réseau domestique.

articles.title: OpenAI negocia una ronda de USD 30.000 millones que la valuaría en USD 1,25 billones
articles.text:
OpenAI, la empresa detrás de ChatGPT, está cerca de cerrar una ronda de financiamiento de hasta USD 30.000 millones que la valuaría en USD 1,25 billones, según la cadena CNBC. Inversores de Emiratos Árabes Unidos y el fondo Coatue lideran el acuerdo.
La cifra corresponde a una valuación previa al nuevo capital, es decir que no incluye el dinero que se incorporará con la ronda. Las personas consultadas por el medio mencionado pidieron no ser identificadas porque los detalles todavía son confidenciales y los términos pueden cambiar antes de firmarse.
Según esas fuentes, la empresa liderada por Sam Altman les dijo a los inversores que buscaba reunir las firmas definitivas antes de que termine el mes de octubre de 2026. El tamaño final de la ronda todavía se está definiendo.
La compañía presenta el financiamiento como un puente “oportunista” antes de una posible salida a bolsa, de acuerdo con las fuentes. OpenAI no respondió a los pedidos de comentario.
OpenAI apuntaría a una valuación récord
Si la ronda se concreta por encima de USD 1 billón, OpenAI superaría a cualquier otra compañía privada en la historia por valuación de mercado. El dato eleva además la vara para la futura oferta pública de acciones de la empresa, que presentó en junio los papeles confidenciales para salir a bolsa.
La directora financiera, Sarah Friar, les dijo a los empleados que esa salida a bolsa llegaría probablemente en 2027. La última ronda conocida de OpenAI, cerrada en marzo de 2026, había reunido USD 122.000 millones a una valuación de USD 852.000 millones, de acuerdo con TechCrunch y Tech Funding News.
El monto actual difiere del que había circulado en septiembre de 2026: la agencia Bloomberg informó a fines de septiembre que OpenAI negociaba la misma ronda de USD 30.000 millones, pero a una valuación de USD 1,4 billones, con fondos de Emiratos Árabes Unidos como Mubadala y un posible ingreso de BlackRock. Esas conversaciones previas incluían un precio fijo que no llegó a cerrarse.
OpenAI busca más capacidad de cómputo
Además del aporte de dinero, OpenAI negocia en paralelo un acuerdo comercial para conseguir más capacidad de cómputo desde Emiratos Árabes Unidos, según la cadena. Esa capacidad de procesamiento es la que la empresa necesita para entrenar y operar sus modelos de inteligencia artificial.
El acuerdo le permitiría a OpenAI ampliar su infraestructura más allá de los centros de datos que ya opera en Estados Unidos, en momentos en que la demanda de cómputo de la compañía crece junto con la cantidad de usuarios de ChatGPT.
La negociación se da en un contexto de mercados tecnológicos inestables, con dudas sobre las condiciones de financiamiento futuras para empresas de infraestructura de inteligencia artificial a medida que suben las tasas de interés.
Esta ronda de valuación ocurre también al tiempo en OpenAI expande ChatGPT Ads a nuevos mercados.
Qué consecuencias tiene esta ronda de valuación para Anthropic
La nueva valuación de OpenAI también repercute en los planes de su principal competidora, Anthropic, que muchos analistas creen más cerca de confirmar su propia salida a bolsa. Según la cadena, Anthropic buscaría una valuación de entre USD 1,5 billones y USD 2 billones para ese debut.
Anthropic había recaudado USD 65.000 millones en mayo a una valuación de USD 965.000 millones, en lo que entonces se interpretó como su última gran ronda privada antes de cotizar en bolsa. Esa compañía también presentó papeles confidenciales para su oferta pública en junio de 2026.
OpenAI espera reunir las firmas de los inversores de esta ronda antes de que termine la próxima semana, aunque el tamaño definitivo del acuerdo y la lista completa de participantes todavía pueden variar.

articles.title: Claude flags nearly 500 worrying open source security issues — C, Java, and Python code all at risk as one flaw wasn't spotted for 21 years
articles.text:
Claude flags nearly 500 worrying open source security issues — C, Java, and Python code all at risk as one flaw wasn't spotted for 21 years
Hunting for individual vulnerabilities will get us nowhere, Anthropic argues
- Anthropic used Claude to analyze 25 open source projects and uncovered nearly 500 security issues
- Research found exposed pre-authentication code paths, conflicting security settings, and long-hidden flaws
- AI identified attack-surface reductions that removed unnecessary code exposure before vulnerabilities could be exploited
Anthropic recently used Claude to analyze 25 major open source projects written in C, C++, Java, PHP, and Python, in search of security issues. It found almost 500 of them, including security controls turned off by conflicts in settings, sensitive code accessible before authentication, and even a vulnerability that sat in the code for 21 years.
This wasn’t a standard hunt for vulnerabilities. In its report, Anthropic argues that looking for individual vulnerabilities is a Sisyphean task that scales poorly and never guarantees security. Instead, it thinks defenders should turn towards reducing software attack surfaces by restricting unnecessary access to potentially exploitable code.
“A defender who reduces unnecessary attack surface in their code reduces the risk from all of the unknown vulnerabilities in that code at once—including any that are already being quietly exploited,” Anthropic said.
The 25 projects it scanned contained more than five million lines of code. Claude created an inventory of more than 17,000 configuration options, 3,842 of which related to security-relevant controls and features.
Misconfigured security controls
The company’s research focused on three ways code may get unnecessarily exposed: features accessible in the default configuration when they’re not needed, different settings which, when combined, erode security, and unnecessarily complex and sensitive code running before security checks.
The analysis showed all 11 projects, which were designed to serve authenticated users, contained code that was reachable when it shouldn’t have been. These include 93 pre-authentication attack surfaces in default configurations, 37 instances of code executing before authentication, and 61 combinations of different configurations that eroded pre-authentication controls.
In total, the 25 analyzed projects contained 162 configuration combinations that were accepted without their documentation explaining how they were supposed to behave. In some cases, security controls were being disabled. In others, there were various inconsistencies and problems.

One configuration flaw was sitting undetected for more than two decades, Anthropic found. While one setting made clients prove their identity through certificates, another one disabled it entirely (even though it was designed to delay the check, not kill it). Even though these were conflicting options, they were accepted without warning.
OpenSSH exposed thousands of lines of code
Anthropic singled out OpenSSH as its case study for the report. The software, widely used to provide secure remote access, contained a daemon that could reach 4,500 lines of experimental code that implements a post-quantum signature algorithm before checking if it was permitted by the server’s configuration to begin with.
As it turned out, the algorithm was disabled by default, but its parsing code was accessible to unauthenticated clients. Anthropic disclosed its findings to OpenSSH, who came back with a fix in version 10.6, in which some 20% of the code was now unreachable by unauthenticated clients.
The company said it combined these techniques into a reusable Claude skill which will soon be integrated into OSS-Scanner, its free, opt-in security scanning service for open-source projects. The skill will examine default configurations, code that is reachable before security checks, as well as settings configurations that are in conflict with one another.
Anthropic added that the system will validate the findings through a dynamic program tracing, and will test proposed changes against existing behavior. Potentially disruptive changes will be left for humans to review.
“It is perhaps impossible to measure how many unknown vulnerabilities are in any given codebase,” the researchers concluded. “And there is plenty of data that shows attackers can and will find those vulnerabilities with enough time (particularly if equipped with frontier AI models).” Therefore, AI could help developers systematically limit unnecessary exposure, making software that much harder to attack.

articles.title: GameSir Introduces G7 Pro 8K PC × Phantom Blade Zero Edition Controller
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
GameSir Introduces G7 Pro 8K PC × Phantom Blade Zero Edition Controller
GameSir is bringing a new identity to its G7 Pro 8K PC controller with the G7 Pro 8K PC × Phantom Blade Zero Edition, a special edition inspired by S-GAME's upcoming action title. Blending classic Wuxia storytelling with fast-paced combat powered by Unreal Engine 5, PHANTOM BLADE ZERO follows Soul, a warrior with just 66 days left to live as he battles assassins and uncovers world-ending conspiracies. The new controller pairs design elements inspired by the game with the high-performance hardware PC players need for fast, responsive gameplay.
Underneath the new exterior, the controller retains the features that make the G7 Pro 8K PC suited to demanding gameplay. Polling rates of up to 8,000 Hz over wired and 2.4 GHz wireless connections, alongside wired latency as low as 0.25 ms, help deliver rapid input response when timing and accuracy matter. Tri-mode connectivity also supports wired, 2.4 GHz wireless and Bluetooth connections, offering flexibility across different gaming setups.Precision starts with Gen-2 GameSir Mag-Res TMR Sticks, which use magnetic sensing technology to deliver smooth, accurate tracking while helping reduce the risk of stick drift. Players can fine-tune their setup further through GameSir Connect, with adjustable stick curves, dead zones, button mapping, macros and turbo settings.
The controller adapts to different genres through its switchable trigger system. Hall Effect analogue triggers offer graduated input for racing and other games requiring precise control, while micro switch triggers provide shorter travel and rapid actuation for action titles and shooters. Optical micro switch ABXY buttons and a micro switch D-pad add crisp, tactile feedback, while four remappable rear buttons allow players to execute additional commands without moving their thumbs from the sticks.
Beyond its core controls, the G7 Pro 8K PC features a six-axis gyroscope for motion input in compatible games, alongside dual asymmetric vibration motors for responsive in-game feedback. Rubber anti-slide grips help maintain a secure hold during longer sessions, while the magnetic swappable design supports further personalization through interchangeable faceplates, stick caps and D-pad options. A 1,200mAh battery supports wireless gaming, and the included charging station keeps the controller ready for the next session.
The exclusive bundle goes beyond the controller itself, including a themed keychain, a dedicated storage case and themed grip faceplates to complete the PHANTOM BLADE ZERO look. These exclusive accessories bring the collaboration into every part of the setup, combining practical storage and added personalization with design details inspired by the game.The G7 Pro 8K PC × Phantom Blade Zero Edition is available now for $99.99 /£109.99 on the GameSir website, with Amazon availability from October 29th.

articles.title: China-Linked Hackers Use ARTEX AI Agents in ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
articles.text:
Microsoft on Wednesday disclosed that a China state-aligned actor dubbed Storm-0940 was behind the recent supply chain compromise of the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application.
During the incident, Storm-0940 used ARTEX, a Go-based agentic AI penetration testing framework that was made closed-source in the wake of its abuse in cyber attacks targeting South Korean financial institutions, to speed up scanning and reconnaissance, password spraying, and OAuth application abuse at downstream victims.
The tech giant said the threat actor used the AI tool at "machine speed" to automate attacks targeting hundreds of organizations across the world spanning a broad range of sectors since September 2026. Targets include aerospace and defense, automotive, chemicals, energy, financial services, government, legal, manufacturing, media, military, semiconductor, software, technology, and think tanks and non-profits.
"Storm-0940's use of ARTEX accelerated the speed of compromised application abuse to authenticate to target environments through applications that had already been granted access, allowing the threat actor to operate without requiring an interactive user sign-in," Microsoft said.
"AI-accelerated follow-on activity included reconnaissance, application credential changes, and attempts to modify privileges that could enable expanded or persistent access."
Storm-0940 was first detailed by Microsoft in November 2024, revealing that the threat actor has been leveraging a botnet called Quad7 (aka CovertNetwork-1658) to conduct highly evasive password spray attacks. The threat actor is assessed to be active since at least 2021.
The adversary is also said to exploit internet-facing applications to gain initial access, followed by using compromised accounts to move through targeted environments. It has also been observed establishing persistence by adding credentials to existing OAuth applications within cloud infrastructures to ensure access to Microsoft 365 resources.
According to Microsoft, a chunk of these ARTEX-driven attacks have resulted in the adversary gaining privileged access to an organization's cloud infrastructure, including several instances where the time frame from initial targeting to privileged access was less than 3 hours.
In the case of the ConnectWise incident, Storm-0940 has been observed using ARTEX to attempt to sign in to more than 2,250 tenants at 2,900 sign-in attempts per minute, a pace the company said gives defenders a short window to detect and respond.
"Between October 10 and 14, 2026, Storm-0940 infrastructure at 144.172.64[.]99 conducted an automated cross-tenant password-spray campaign targeting 327 accounts across eight organizations to gain access to Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online," Microsoft said.
During this window, Microsoft said it captured over 151,000 failed logon events. The activity peaked on October 11 at 2,900 failures per minute, resulting in more than 111,000 failures in a single day. Of these, 48 accounts received more than 1,000 failures. No successful authentication, token issuance, Graph call, or directory change was detected, it noted.
That changed on October 15, 2026, when the AI agents gained access to the identities of multiple ConnectWise cloud applications and began to use them to authenticate to customer environments.
"Additionally, after acquiring control of the identities of multiple ConnectWise cloud applications, the AI agents operating on behalf of the threat actor continued to use the same IP range to authenticate to customer environments using the illicit access acquired through these stolen app credentials, effectively taking advantage of the already established trust by these apps within a tenant," the tech giant added.
In some of these cases, the AI agents are assessed to have progressed beyond authentication to Microsoft Graph and directory operations. This included reconnaissance, application credential modifications to establish persistence, and changes involving identities, groups, and privileged roles.
| The TAG-217 attack chain \| Source: Zscaler | 
"The application credential modification made by Storm-0940’s associated agents in the targeted victims' environments can lead to persistence through other identities, credentials, and cloud services," Microsoft said. "These changes can remain active as a backdoor even after the original compromised application is mediated."
Storm-0940 is far from the only hacking crew to rely on ARTEX. Microsoft said it has observed threat actors across multiple geographic regions weaponizing the framework in their operations.
Recorded Future Insikt Group, which is tracking the threat cluster behind the attacks on South Korean financial institutions under the moniker TAG-217, said it identified activity linked to the hacking group dating back to August 17, 2026, when it "tested infrastructure designed to maintain remote access to computers and conducted internet scanning."
Over the next few weeks, the Chinese-speaking threat actor is said to have put together tools to attack cryptocurrency mining operations using the YiiMP platform, as well as set up a workspace for testing weaknesses in iPhones and modifying Android system software.
Zscaler ThreatLabz has since revealed that the attack's footprint extends beyond South Korea, and that it opportunistically targeted organizations around the globe and across multiple industry sectors. The findings come from a custom ARTEX deployment that included AI assistant configurations, synchronization scripts, network routing tools, and a Claude Code prompt history.
"ARTEX was configured to use a DeepSeek model through an OpenAI-compatible gateway, but other configurations also specified DeepSeek, GLM, and Grok," security researcher Seongsu Park said. "Prompts directed AI models to divide investigation tasks and review one another's findings, including instructions for GLM to review work performed by DeepSeek and its subagents."
An analysis of the prompt histories has revealed requests for bulk personal and transaction data, along with questions about selling stolen data, suggesting the attacks were likely financially motivated. Other prompts related to extracting payment gateway API keys, exploiting NFT minting workflows, and gaining unauthorized administrative privileges.
The findings once again highlight how threat actors are increasingly integrating agentic AI tools into their offensive security workflows to quickly carry out attacks at scale.
"Agents are not constrained by factors affecting humans – they can work around the clock, on weekends, and on holidays and attempt multiple breach paths simultaneously, enabling significantly reduced time from selecting a target to achieving objectives, increasing the speed and impact of complex attacks like supply chain compromises," Microsoft said.
In response to the findings, ConnectWise said the activity "describes a campaign that reaches well beyond any one company," adding "nation-state actors are increasingly targeting the software supply chain, because one trusted connection can open the door to many organizations."
"AI now lets them test those connections at [...] 'machine speed.' MSPs are in the middle of that chain. They are targets in their own right, and they are also a path into every client they serve. Every vendor and every MSP must defend itself with both of those risks in mind."
ConnectWise, which temporarily shut down services following the attacks, has been restoring services in phases, a process that it said will take several days.

articles.title: Un ordinateur pour travailler à moins de 300€ ? C’est ce que propose Amazon avec ce Chromebook Plus Lenovo
articles.text:
Le Lenovo Chromebook Plus IdeaPad Slim 3 donne accès à une configuration taillée pour les usages bureautiques, à un écran de 14 pouces et à un châssis léger, le tout pour 289,99 euros chez Amazon. Une offre qui peut intéresser différents profils d’utilisateurs.
Les étudiants et les télétravailleurs qui ont besoin d’un ordinateur portable léger, endurant et abordable peuvent se tourner vers le Lenovo Chromebook Plus IdeaPad Slim 3. Avec son processeur Intel Core i3-N305, ses 8 Go de RAM et ses 128 Go de stockage eMMC, cette machine disponible pour 289,99 € au lieu de 373,99 € sur Amazon peut répondre à la plupart des besoins en matière de bureautique. Il faut tout de même prendre en compte qu’il fonctionne sous ChromeOS, le système de Google, et non pas sous Windows.
Le Lenovo Chromebook Plus IdeaPad Slim 3 est à 289,99 € chez Amazon dans le cadre d’une offre à durée limitée.
Pourquoi choisir le Lenovo Chromebook Plus IdeaPad Slim 3 ?
- Pour son écran Full HD : la dalle IPS de 14 pouces convient à la lecture de documents comme au visionnage de vidéos.
- Pour sa configuration bureautique : son processeur Intel Core i3-N305 et ses 8 Go de RAM permettent de travailler avec plusieurs onglets et applications courantes.
- Pour son environnement Google : ChromeOS facilite l’accès à Gmail, Google Docs et Sheets pour les utilisateurs de ces services.
Un format pratique pour les cours et les déplacements
Avec un poids d’environ 1,5 kg, le Lenovo Chromebook Plus IdeaPad Slim 3 reste relativement léger dans le domaine des ordinateurs portables. Il est facile à transporter dans un sac, et son format 14 pouces compact lui permet de trouver sa place sur une tablette de train ou d’amphithéâtre. Il est équipé d’un écran IPS Full HD et d’un clavier AZERTY français. Sa connectique comprend deux ports USB-A, un USB-C et une sortie HDMI, ce qui permet notamment de brancher un écran externe ou une souris en cas de besoin. Enfin, avec une autonomie annoncée jusqu’à dix heures, cette machine peut couvrir une journée de travail selon les usages, sans avoir à être rechargée.
Un petit prix qui implique quelques sacrifices
ChromeOS convient aux usages centrés sur le navigateur et les outils en ligne de Google. Il est impossible d’y installer les versions Windows ou Mac de Microsoft Office, mais, en cas de nécessité, il reste possible d’y accéder via la version Web de Microsoft 365. Enfin, les 128 Go de stockage eMMC peuvent s’avérer un peu justes pour le stockage local de gros fichiers.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran IPS Full HD de 14 pouces.
- Processeur Core i3-N305 et 8 Go de RAM.
- Connectique USB-A, USB-C et HDMI.
❌ Les limites
- Stockage eMMC limité à 128 Go.
- Pas de compatibilité native avec les logiciels Windows.
Vendu et expédié par Amazon, ce Chromebook Plus Lenovo est disponible à 289,99 € au lieu de 373,99 €.
Le Lenovo Chromebook Plus IdeaPad Slim 3 est un ordinateur portable abordable, qui peut tout à fait convenir aux étudiants et aux utilisateurs qui travaillent surtout avec des outils en ligne. Son format compact et sa bonne autonomie le rendent aussi adapté aux usages nomades.
En revanche, les personnes dépendantes de logiciels spécialisés disponibles uniquement sous Windows ou macOS devront regarder ailleurs pour trouver leur bonheur. ChromeOS ne convient pas à tout le monde, mieux vaut se renseigner à son sujet avant d’investir.

articles.title: El ejecutivo que ayudó a traer de vuelta a Steve Jobs a Apple llega a Buenos Aires con un festival de cine hecho con IA
articles.text:
En 1997, un grupo de directivos de Apple tomó la decisión que salvó a la empresa: traer de regreso a Steve Jobs. Uno de ellos era Marco Landi, un ingeniero italiano que había llegado para dar vuelta a la operación europea y terminó como COO en Cupertino. Casi treinta años después, Landi se dedica a otra apuesta: convencer al mundo del cine de que la inteligencia artificial no viene a reemplazar la creatividad, sino a expandirla. Con esa idea fundó el World AI Film Festival, WAIFF, que el viernes 30 de octubre llega por primera vez a Buenos Aires.
La cita es en el Centro de Convenciones, dentro de la TecWeek 2026, con entrada libre y gratuita y acreditación desde las 9:30. No hace falta ser de la industria para entrar: buena parte de la agenda está pensada para quien quiere entender cómo se hace una película con IA y por dónde empezar. Landi abre la jornada a las 10 con una charla sobre las tendencias globales de la herramienta y lo que abre para la Argentina.
El festival que creó ya tuvo dos ediciones en Francia, en Niza y en Cannes, donde este año recibió más de 5.000 obras de 80 países. Hoy recorre el mundo con sedes en San Pablo, Estambul, Londres, Beijing, Seúl, Kioto y Los Ángeles, y cada una manda sus mejores obras a la final en Cannes. Buenos Aires es la única sede de habla hispana del calendario.
La agenda, panel por panel
El primer panel, “El talento del futuro: formación, nuevos roles e IA en la industria audiovisual”, reúne a quienes están formando a la próxima generación: María Solís, de Image Campus; Miguel González Massenio, de la Universidad del Cine; Carlos Caram, de la Universidad de Palermo; Marcelo Altmark, de la FADU de la UBA; y Artur Monteiro, de House. Modera Julieta Schulkin. Para quien quiera entrar en este campo y no sepa por dónde, este es el bloque.
A las 11:30, “Imágenes, relatos y procesos” cruza la experiencia de tres sectores que ya producen con IA: la animación, la publicidad y el cine. Están Bautista Vidal, de Purga Studio; Maximiliano Lasansky, de Pampa Films; Adrián Garelik, de Gennial; y Laura Gagliesi, de Animar Cluster, con moderación de Irina Sternik.
A las 12:30 se presenta el caso de “El Libertador”, el cortometraje con el que Infobae recreó con IA el encuentro entre San Martín y Sarmiento en 1846, con Opy Morales, director de Estrategia de IA de Infobae, y Juan Leyrado, la voz de Sarmiento. El eje es qué permiten las imágenes sintéticas para representar hechos históricos y qué problemas abren.
La tarde se pone más áspera. “¿La IA es enemiga, aliada o algo más?” junta a la industria tradicional con el debate que más incomoda: creatividad, propiedad intelectual, futuro del trabajo y con qué se entrenan los modelos. Participan Agustín Sacanell, de la Cámara Argentina de Productores Independientes de Televisión; Hernán Guerschuny, director y productor; Daniel Pensa, presidente de la Cámara Argentina de la Industria Cinematográfica; y Julieta Schulkin. Modera Agustina Laboureau, autora de La Biblia del Derecho Creativo, que a las 15 sigue con “IA y propiedad intelectual” junto a los abogados Félix Memelsdorff y Francisco José de Zavalía. Es el bloque que cualquier creador debería ver antes de subir una obra a un festival.
A las 15:30, “Transformación de la cadena de valor” mira el negocio: costos, riesgos y flujos de trabajo con Ramiro Navarro, de Frontier Estudios; Rodrigo Figueroa Reyes, de FiRe Advertainment; Nicolás Esmede, de 1.8; y un referente de Shorta. Modera Desirée Jaimovich.
A las 16:30, el economista y periodista Sebastián Campanario da una charla sobre predecir el presente. A las 17, Lucas Jinkis, fundador de GoSeries, habla de las oportunidades que la IA abre para series, películas y nuevas plataformas de distribución. Y el cierre, a las 17:30, es filosófico: Julien Raout, director artístico de WAIFF Global, y la directora Sabrina Farji, ambos jurados de esta edición, discuten cómo la IA cambia el valor y el sentido de toda expresión creativa.
Quién decide
El jurado local lo preside Axel Kuschevatzky, productor de Argentina, 1985 y de Relatos salvajes, y lo integran Diego Guebel, cofundador de Cuatro Cabezas; Agustín Cossa, supervisor de producción virtual que trabajó en El Eternauta; la guionista Alejandra Bruno; la directora Sabrina Farji, vicepresidenta primera de la Academia de Cine argentina; y el productor Nicolás Esmede. Del lado internacional están Landi, Raout, las productoras estadounidenses Joanna Popper y Nancy Hamilton, y el realizador brasileño Nyko Oliver.
Lo que se proyecta
En paralelo a las charlas, el auditorio de proyecciones exhibe de 10 a 18 las obras finalistas de la competencia local, hasta cinco por categoría, elegidas entre los 180 proyectos que recibió la convocatoria. Para quien quiera saber qué nivel tiene hoy el cine con IA en la Argentina, es la forma más directa de verlo. Se suma una Ventana Internacional Cannes curada por Raout, con once producciones de China, Francia, Brasil, Reino Unido, Corea del Sur, Suiza y Jordania, entre cortos, animación, publicidad y microseries.
Hay además cuatro activaciones interactivas: MEAT PROXY de Gotika, TecFriendsBa de People Like Pixels, Gray Box Studio de Gennial, y Podcast en Buenos Aires 1880-1900 de Enchulame la Cámara y SnackPlay.
La jornada termina con la ceremonia de premiación. El jurado anuncia a los ganadores de las seis categorías: cortometraje, largometraje, animación, microserie vertical, publicidad y documental. Cinco obras representarán a la Argentina en Road to Cannes, y la ganadora del Gran Premio viajará a Cannes en abril de 2027.
La programación completa está en worldaifilmfestival.com/buenos-aires.

Décalque quasi intégral de la HW-Q935F, la HW-Q930H se contente d'ajouter quelques menues fonctions logicielles à un système home cinéma toujours aussi convaincant. Une mise à jour de routine, qui continue de bénéficier d'un excellent rapport qualité-prix.

articles.title: Two Pallets of RTX 5090s Vanish From São Paulo Airport, One Card Already Listed Online
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Two Pallets of RTX 5090s Vanish From São Paulo Airport, One Card Already Listed Online
Three airport workers have reportedly been identified as the people behind the disappearance of two pallets of ZOTAC GeForce RTX 5090 cards from Guarulhos International Airport in São Paulo, Brazil, and at least one of those cards has already popped up for sale online. The shipment belonged to Oderço, a distributor based in Maringá, which imported the cards from the US and puts their cost at around R$2.5 million (roughly $470,000). According to a police report filed by the airport operator, two outsourced forklift operators moved the pallets out of the cargo terminal's warehouse on September 21, which security cameras recorded, while a third employee, a checker, released the goods in the electronic system so they could get past the airport's controls. The cards were then loaded onto a truck and haven't been seen since.
Apparently, one of them later turned up on OLX for R$32,000 (about $6,000), and Brazil's Jornal da Band reported that its serial number matched one of the imported cards. The listing has since been pulled, and it's not clear who posted it or whether that person was involved. There's no word on arrests either. Oderço's president, Oderço Matos, said two pallets don't just vanish on their own inside an international airport. GPU shipments have gone missing before, including containers of MSI RTX 3090 cards and a truck full of EVGA cards. However, this haul is worth a lot more on the street right now, with some RTX 5090 listings going for well past $8,000 as the card remains in heavy demand for AI workloads.
Sources:
				Oderço on Instagram, 				GMC Online, 				via Tom's Hardware			
	
	
	
		
	
		
19 Comments on Two Pallets of RTX 5090s Vanish From São Paulo Airport, One Card Already Listed Online
Whomever put that card up should have thanked that he can have it, and just use...
It almost has to be some kind of a inside job, but, it maybe be airport employees or even Zotac itself, I don't think it would be too hard to find out, those places got tons of cameras, then you got the hardware ID, but, those that know how to modify the VBIOS can get around it...
Small price to pay for a computer with 128GB of vram.
BTW, it's not that hard to "alter" what the GPU reports as its serial number.
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,serial,uuid --format=csv
An ASIC number or PCI hardware ID usually identifies the chip family or model, not one individual card.
Why it comes up 0? I guess HWInfo64 fuddery maybe...
The ASIC serial number in HWiNFO on my other cards is not a hash but a normal decimal number

articles.title: ROG Xbox Ally X20: una primera mirada a la consola edición especial por sus 20 años de aniversario
articles.text:
La ROG Xbox Ally X edición 20 años ya está disponible como la nueva consola portátil de ASUS para quienes buscan llevar los videojuegos de PC fuera del escritorio. El equipo combina una pantalla OLED más grande, controles renovados y una edición limitada que incorpora accesorios como unas gafas de realidad aumentada.
Infobae Tecno probó la consola con Red Dead Redemption 2, un título de mundo abierto que permitió recorrer sus opciones de imagen, respuesta de los controles y desempeño en una sesión de juego portátil. Asimismo, al utilizar las gafas el juego se comprobó la capacidad de inmersión total de las gafas X1.
Felipe Llano, del área de relaciones públicas de ASUS, explicó que la edición conmemorativa por los 20 años de ROG tendrá unidades limitadas. La consola se venderá de forma individual y también en un paquete que incluye gafas, estuche protector y una maleta Pelican.
Cinco características de la ROG Ally X20
- Pantalla OLED de 7,4 pulgadas con mayor brillo.
Uno de los principales cambios está en el panel ROG Nebula HDR OLED, que aumenta su tamaño de 7 a 7,4 pulgadas respecto de la versión anterior.
La pantalla alcanza hasta 1.400 nits de brillo, una cifra pensada para mantener la visibilidad en diferentes entornos y resaltar el contraste en juegos con escenas oscuras.
Incorpora una tasa de refresco variable de hasta 120 Hz, que puede disminuir automáticamente cuando el contenido no exige tanta fluidez para priorizar el consumo de batería.
El panel utiliza tecnología Tandem OLED, con dos capas que distribuyen el esfuerzo necesario para alcanzar altos niveles de brillo. Además, la consola incluye Corning Gorilla Glass Victus y una superficie que reduce los reflejos.
- Controles renovados para mejorar la precisión.
La ROG Ally X edición 20 años incorpora joysticks TMR en lugar de los controles Hall Effect presentes en otros modelos.
Este sistema utiliza imanes para detectar los movimientos y apunta a reducir el desgaste de los componentes, además de minimizar el problema conocido como drift, cuando un joystick registra movimiento sin que el jugador lo accione.
La consola también suma una cruceta ajustable. Con un giro, el usuario puede pasar de una configuración de cuatro direcciones a otra de ocho direcciones, que añade movimientos diagonales.
Esta alternativa está pensada para juegos de lucha, plataformas o títulos que requieren combinaciones de comandos más precisas.
Los botones, gatillos y agarres también fueron rediseñados, con una superficie en relieve para reducir el riesgo de que la consola se deslice durante una sesión de juego.
- Rendimiento de PC en formato portátil.
El equipo mantiene una configuración orientada a ejecutar videojuegos de PC en una consola de mano.
Cuenta con un procesador AMD, 24 GB de memoria RAM LPDDR5X y 1 TB de almacenamiento interno. ASUS indicó que la memoria alcanza una tasa de transferencia de hasta 8.000 megatransferencias.
El almacenamiento puede ampliarse de dos formas: mediante una tarjeta microSD o con el reemplazo de la unidad SSD. La consola admite unidades de hasta 4 TB.
La ROG Ally X también utiliza Windows 11 optimizado para el formato de consola. Al encenderla, el sistema muestra una interfaz adaptada al uso portátil, aunque conserva las posibilidades de una computadora: puede conectarse a un teclado, un mouse, monitores externos o una base para utilizarla como una PC de escritorio.
- Batería, refrigeración y autonomía según el uso.
La consola conserva una batería de 80 Wh. Su duración depende del videojuego, el perfil de rendimiento, el nivel de brillo, la frecuencia de actualización de la pantalla y el uso de los ventiladores.
ASUS estima una autonomía de entre cuatro y seis horas para jugar, aunque esa cifra puede variar según la exigencia del título.
En contenidos menos demandantes, como la reproducción de películas, la autonomía puede extenderse. La pantalla OLED también contribuye a la eficiencia energética en escenas oscuras, porque los píxeles negros se apagan.
- Gafas ROG Xreal R1, estuche y maleta Pelican.
La edición completa incluye las gafas ROG Xreal R1 edición 20 años, desarrolladas en colaboración con Xreal. Se conectan a la consola con un solo cable USB-C, que transmite la imagen y la energía, sin necesidad de una conexión adicional.
Según ASUS, las gafas pueden proyectar una imagen equivalente a una pantalla de 171 pulgadas vista a cuatro metros de distancia. La proyección puede alcanzar hasta 240 Hz, dependiendo de la configuración. Integran una función para visualizar contenido en 3D y audio Bose.
El paquete suma un estuche rígido para proteger la pantalla y los joysticks durante el transporte, además de una maleta Pelican.
La consola mantiene una estética especial por el aniversario de ROG, con cuerpo negro translúcido, detalles dorados, iluminación personalizable y un diseño que permite ver parte de los componentes internos.

articles.title: OpenAI agents turned off their own guardrails and then told researchers they were still on — AI agents lying about their behavior should concern everyone
articles.text:
OpenAI agents turned off their own guardrails and then told researchers they were still on — AI agents lying about their behavior should concern everyone
AI agents are turning off their own safeguards
- AI agents turned off their guardrails during routine coding tasks, with one agent lying about doing so
- OpenAI was not monitoring the models involved for misalignment because of their weaker capabilities
- New changes to Auto Review and the introduction of 'safety cases' will make it harder for agents to avoid misalignment detection, OpenAI says
OpenAI has revealed two AI agents disabled safety guardrails while performing tasks, and one of them even lied to researchers when asked if its guardrails were still active.
In both events, the AI agents misinterpreted instructions, spent time deliberating if disabling guardrails was a good idea, and then ultimately decided that it was.
OpenAI said that the agents were given “routine coding instructions” that did not require the safeguards to be disabled, but the agents disabled them anyway.
AI agents misalign and disable guardrails
In the first instance of misalignment, an agent powered by GPT Sol 6.1 was told to create evaluation tasks with employee feedback collected through Slack. The agent misinterpreted an instruction not to send any messages about the task as an instruction not to send safety notifications to the researchers.
The second instance saw a GPT-6 Astra agent disable its guardrails while migrating a program, believing the instruction was part of a reference implementation. When the researchers noticed the disabled guardrails and asked the agent why they were disabled, the agent said it hadn’t turned off any safety guardrails.
OpenAI said that as a result of these events, the company would work to strengthen its misalignment monitoring system and would investigate the cases further to check if they were “benign overpersistence or a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular.”
As an additional measure, OpenAI is also making changes to its Auto Review so that attempts to disable misalignment monitoring are automatically detected and blocked. Previously, OpenAI did not require misalignment monitoring for models equivalent to GPT-6 Luna.

Agent workloads will also be subject to ‘safety case’ monitoring, with workloads that do not have a safety case or those that fail to meet the specifications of a valid safety case being automatically terminated.
The company said it does not have a “satisfying explanation” for the agent’s behavior, but says that the introduction of new policies will make it harder for agents to avoid misalignment detection. The company said it would also conduct further testing on these two instances of agent misalignment to determine a cause.
