articles.title: Microsoft reduce el trabajo remoto en Xbox con la exigencia de cuatro días presenciales
articles.text:
Xbox exigirá a sus trabajadores de la zona de Redmond acudir a la oficina cuatro días a la semana a partir de febrero de 2027, según confirmó la directora de recursos humanos de la división, Jacinda Chislum Pearson, en un comunicado interno.
La medida marca un endurecimiento de la política de presencialidad que Microsoft ya había impuesto meses atrás y confirma que la compañía se suma a la tendencia de otras grandes tecnológicas que buscan recuperar el trabajo en persona tras años de flexibilidad pospandemia.
La noticia llega en un momento en el que Xbox concentra la atención mediática por varios frentes a la vez: desde el precio estimado de su próxima generación de consolas hasta los posibles cambios en Game Pass. Sin embargo, este anuncio sobre la jornada laboral de sus empleados se ha convertido en uno de los asuntos que más repercusión ha generado en las últimas horas.
Xbox amplía la obligatoriedad del trabajo presencial a cuatro días
La nueva política, revelada primero por The Verge, establece que los empleados de Xbox radicados en la región de Puget Sound deberán cumplir con un mínimo de cuatro jornadas semanales en la oficina a partir del 1 de febrero de 2027.
El requisito afecta de forma concreta a quienes residan a menos de 50 millas (80 kilómetros) de distancia de Studio D, el complejo de oficinas donde la compañía concentra buena parte de su operación en la zona.
En el memorando interno, Chislum Pearson explicó los motivos detrás de la decisión: “Tenemos miles de empleados de Xbox a distancia de desplazamiento desde Redmond. Aprovechar esa proximidad y trabajar juntos en persona facilita revisar el trabajo, resolver problemas y tomar decisiones sin la carga de programar otra reunión”.
La directora de recursos humanos también enmarcó el cambio como una respuesta directa a las inquietudes manifestadas por el propio personal. Según el comunicado, la compañía busca con esta medida impulsar una mayor colaboración entre equipos que trabajan de manera presencial.
El antecedente de Microsoft con el regreso a la oficina
Esta decisión no surge de manera aislada. Microsoft, la empresa matriz de Xbox, ya había implementado previamente una política que obligaba a sus trabajadores a asistir a la oficina tres días por semana.
El nuevo esquema de cuatro días representa, por lo tanto, una ampliación de un día adicional respecto a la exigencia anterior, lo que confirma una tendencia progresiva hacia una mayor presencialidad dentro de la estructura corporativa de la compañía.
Un elemento relevante de la medida es su alcance limitado: no se trata de una política global para toda la plantilla de Xbox, sino de un requisito específico para quienes se encuentran dentro del radio geográfico de 50 millas desde Puget Sound, en Redmond.
Xbox se suma a la tendencia de retorno presencial en el sector tecnológico
El movimiento de Xbox se inscribe dentro de una corriente que contradice la flexibilidad laboral que se extendió tras la pandemia de coronavirus. Numerosas compañías tecnológicas que en su momento apostaron fuerte por el teletrabajo han comenzado a revertir esas políticas en los últimos años.
Rockstar Games figura entre los ejemplos previos de esta tendencia, al haber optado también por reforzar la exigencia de trabajo presencial entre sus empleados.
Con esta nueva política, Xbox confirma que el modelo de oficina continúa ganando terreno frente al teletrabajo dentro de las grandes empresas tecnológicas, al menos para aquellos empleados que, por cercanía geográfica, pueden desplazarse con facilidad hasta sus instalaciones centrales.

articles.title: Bose Corporation Acquires Skullcandy, Expanding Its Consumer Audio Portfolio
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Bose Corporation Acquires Skullcandy, Expanding Its Consumer Audio Portfolio
Bose Corporation, a global leader in audio innovation and research, announced today it has acquired Skullcandy, a lifestyle audio brand known for its bold products that bring together sound, style, and performance. Bose and Skullcandy have each spent decades finding new ways to bring people closer to the music they love. Together, they'll combine Bose's audio expertise, technology, and global reach with Skullcandy's design, understanding of its consumers, and authentic community connections to create new products and experiences and accelerate growth.
The acquisition follows a multi-year partnership that has already brought Sound by Bose technology to Skullcandy earbuds and headphones. The companies have seen firsthand how their strengths can come together to create products consumers love while staying true to what makes Skullcandy special, providing a foundation to accelerate further collaboration and innovation.With a strong position at the intersection of audio, lifestyle, and culture, Skullcandy will remain a separate brand within Bose's Premium Consumer Audio business. Skullcandy's deep roots in boardsports, including longstanding relationships with passionate supporters of the culture and its athletes, and authentic connections across music, gaming, fitness, and other communities present new ways for Bose to meaningfully connect with consumers where it has less presence today.
Lila Snyder, Chief Executive Officer of Bose Corporation"For more than 60 years, Bose has been committed to delivering incredible audio experiences however and wherever people choose to listen. As we work to reach even more people, we're expanding how we do that, not only through Bose products, but through technology partnerships and a growing portfolio of brands. As a privately held company, we have the freedom to make bold, long-term investments in opportunities we believe in, and Skullcandy is a great example of that. They have an established, thriving brand, and together we see tremendous opportunity to create new products and experiences and reach more consumers around the world."
Brian Garofalow, Chief Executive Officer of Skullcandy"We believe this is a win for Skullcandy and our fans. Skullcandy was born on a chairlift in Park City, Utah, over 20 years ago, and we've always believed great music should be part of the experiences people love. Joining Bose gives us the opportunity to make those experiences even better by bringing more of their audio expertise and technology to our products, and it opens up even more ways to take Skullcandy further."
Bose plans to invest in Skullcandy's continued growth, providing greater access to technology, resources, global distribution, and commercial relationships while giving the brand the freedom to continue evolving in ways that are authentic to its identity and consumers. Skullcandy will continue to be based in Park City, Utah.
Bose acquired Skullcandy from a fund managed by Mill Road Capital Management LLC, a Connecticut-based private investment firm. Jones Day acted as Bose's legal counsel. Additional information, including financial and other terms of the transaction, will remain confidential.

articles.title: Stranger Than Heaven director says combat was inspired by classic Yakuza movies because of how 'raw and gritty' the action looks — 'We really wanted to make sure that the player feels this atmosphere that it’s either you kill, or you get killed'
articles.text:
Stranger Than Heaven director says the game's combat was inspired by old 'Ninkyo' Yakuza movies because the 'raw and gritty' action scenes fit Daito's character as an inexperienced fighter — 'We felt that atmosphere was what made those genres special'
"It was really, really important that the combat feels intuitive to create this sense of synchronisation between the player and Daito"
- Stranger Than Heaven director Mikinobu Abe says the game's combat system was inspired by classic Ninkyo yakuza movies
- He says the action scenes in those movies were "raw and gritty" and encapsulated the feeling RGG Studios wanted to showcase
- Abe adds that the combat system also correlates with Makoto Daito, who will start as an inexperienced fighter before evolving
Stranger Than Heaven director Mikinobu Abe has revealed that classic yakuza movies inspired the upcoming action game's combat system, and that it will tie into Makoto Daito's character development.
Speaking in an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Abe shared how RGG Studios conceptualized the game's combat, saying that it "really wanted to make sure that the player feels this atmosphere that it’s either you kill, or you get killed," and revealed that "we took a lot of inspiration from the old Ninkyo movies."
Ninkyo is a classic subgenre of Japanese yakuza-themed movies made in the 70s and 80s. Abe said RGG was influenced by movies like New Battles Without Honor and Humanity, starring Bunta Sugawara, who also plays a character in Stranger Than Heaven, because of its unrefined action scenes.
"While we were watching these movies, we noticed that what made those movies special was how raw and gritty the action scenes are in those movies," he said. "No one throws a cool-looking fist punch or anything; it's just people rolling around and fighting. We felt that atmosphere was what made those genres special."
The "raw" action scenes also influenced the game's main character, Makoto Daito, and his gradual progression to becoming a better fighter than he starts; players will see him evolving the more they become attuned to the combat system.
"We took a lot of inspiration from that, and wanted to make sure that Daito is a character who starts out not being too good in a fight," Abe continued. "As he progresses, though, he gets more comfortable fighting people. Because of that, because the game is about one man's life, we definitely wanted to depict how the main character is evolving, or I guess more like ageing, through the narrative. We wanted to make sure that the player can also feel that, while also feeling that tension of kill or be killed."
Abe added that "It was really, really important that the combat feels intuitive to create this sense of synchronisation between the player and Daito" and to allow the player to "immerse themselves in controlling Makoto."

articles.title: Robotics startup Enact Intelligence nabs $30M funding round - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Robotics startup Enact Intelligence nabs $30M funding round
Swiss robotics startup Enact Intelligence today announced that it has raised $30 million in pre-seed funding.
The capital was provided by a consortium that included Yann LeCun, one of the world’s most prominent artificial intelligence researchers. He was joined by Mistral AI SAS Chief Executive Arthur Mensch, Hugging Face Inc. co-founder Thomas Wolf and several venture capital firms.
Enact, officially Eta Robotics AG, was launched earlier this year by CEO Manuel Yves Galliker. The executive earlier held engineering roles at robotics startups Physical Intelligence Inc. and 1X Technologies AS. The Enact team also includes former employees of Google DeepMind, Amazon.com Inc. and other major industry players.
Enact is developing AI models optimized to control robots. Such algorithms were historically tailored to specific robot form factors. As a result, a model built to power a humanoid robot may not be capable of reliably operating a standalone robotic arm. Enact’s algorithms, in contrast, are designed to support a wide range of robot designs.
Early-stage startups often use customized versions of open-source models to power their software. A recent job posting indicates that Enact is pursuing a different approach. The company is hiring an AI researcher with expertise in pre-training, a term for developing AI models from scratch. That task can be significantly more difficult than customizing open-source models.
Enact says that it’s developing not only AI models but also physical robot components, most notably actuators. Those are mechanical subsystems that act as a robot’s muscles. An actuator combines an electric motor with a chip that controls its motion and certain other auxiliary parts.
Enact’s actuators not only produce kinetic energy but also act as sensors. It says they “sense force and touch,” which presumably means they measure the amount of pressure a robot applies to objects when it picks them up.
The company didn’t specify how the technology works. However, earlier attempts to build actuator-based sensors may offer clues. Google LLC and publicly traded chipmaker Allegro MicroSystems Inc. are among the companies that have invested in such projects. Both companies used an approach called Back EMF to turn actuators into pressure sensors.
Running a current through an actuator causes its built-in motor to spin. The rotation of that motor, in turn, generates a second current that flows back into the actuator. Back EMF technologies measure that second current, or counter-electromotive force as it’s most commonly known, to understand what the host system is doing.
If a robotic arm’s actuator is active but not generating any counter-electromotive force, engineers can deduce that the arm is holding a heavy item its actuator is unable to move. By contrast, the presence of a strong counter-electromotive force indicates that the actuator is spinning freely. That often means the robot arm isn’t holding anything. Back EMF sensors can also collect data about a range of other robot activities.
A job posting indicates that Enact plans to use field-programmable gate arrays, or FPGAs, to power its robots. An FPGA is a chip that users can customize more extensively than a central processing unit or a graphics card. That makes it possible to achieve better performance and power efficiency.
Enact will reportedly use its funding round to hire more engineers and enhance its technology.

articles.title: Fin de la panne Orange et Sosh : l'opérateur fait un geste commercial pour se faire pardonner
articles.text:
Au lendemain de la panne géante, Orange passe aux excuses. Les clients concernés, chez Orange comme chez Sosh, verront leur enveloppe data doublée pendant un mois, tandis que l’opérateur pointe son nouveau cœur de réseau comme la cause de ses soucis.
Orange fera bien un geste commercial pour les clients touchés par la panne historique de la veille. Dans un message adressé à Clubic ce jeudi 22 octobre 2026, l'opérateur confirme avoir pris la décision de doubler l'enveloppe data des clients Orange et Sosh touchés par la panne du réseau mobile qui a privé ces derniers, un peu partout en France, d'appels, de SMS et d'Internet mobile mercredi. Les clients Pro sont également concernés. Dans son communiqué, l'opérateur confirme aussi l'origine de l'incident, un équipement de son nouveau cœur de réseau, et écarte toute piste cyber, en faisant référence aux failles PHP, qui n'ont rien à voir. Officiellement, tout est rentré dans l'ordre, même si quelques soucis, très localisés, sont encore signalés ce jeudi.
Panne Orange, le nouveau cœur de réseau officiellement en cause
Retour sur une journée que beaucoup d'abonnés ne sont pas près d'oublier. Vers 11 h 20 mercredi, le réseau mobile Orange et Sosh s'effondre. Les appels, SMS et Internet mobile deviennent inaccessibles pour une partie des clients, partout en France, box 5G comprises. Plus de 11 000 signalements sont recensés sur Downdetector autour de midi. Les appels d'urgence, eux, ne sont alors pas touchés, selon l'opérateur. Le signal revient progressivement autour de 19 h, avant qu'Orange n'annonce un rétablissement complet à 21 h, soit près de dix heures de perturbations. C'est la plus longue des trois pannes nationales subies cette année par le réseau mobile d'Orange, après celle du 30 janvier, qui avait duré environ sept heures et demie, et celle du 29 juin.
Ce jeudi, l'opérateur a plus longuement communiqué officiellement sur l'origine de la panne. L'incident est survenu sur « un équipement de notre nouveau cœur de réseau », écrit Orange, qui précise que la situation n'était pas d'origine cyber, renouvelle ses excuses et remercie ses clients pour leur patience. Mercredi soir, son communiqué évoquait seulement un équipement défaillant de son cœur de réseau mobile, sans le mot « nouveau ». Le cœur de réseau, c'est le centre de tri du réseau mobile. Il reconnaît chaque carte SIM et aiguille appels, SMS et données. Quand il flanche, les antennes ont beau émettre, les téléphones restent muets.
Cette précision donne raison au hacker éthique Clément Domingo, qui évoquait dès mercredi après-midi un nouveau cœur de réseau 5G. Comme nous l'expliquions hier, pour vous donner un petit peu plus de détails, la 5G classique d'Orange s'appuie encore en partie sur le cœur de réseau de la 4G. Pour exploiter pleinement la 5G dite « Standalone », commercialisée sous le nom de 5G+, il faut un cœur entièrement 5G, vers lequel les lignes des abonnés basculent progressivement. Si ce nouveau cœur flanche, seules les lignes déjà migrées décrocheraient, ce qui expliquerait pourquoi des voisins n'étaient pas tous touchés. Orange, lui, ne parle toujours ni de 5G ni de migration.
Data doublée chez Orange et Sosh, le geste pour faire passer la pilule
En guise de dédommagement, Orange va doubler l'enveloppe de data incluse dans le forfait des clients concernés Orange, Sosh et Pro, pendant un mois. Attention, le bonus ne tombera pas tout de suite, puisqu'il s'appliquera à partir du prochain renouvellement du forfait. L'opérateur ne détaille pas encore les modalités, ni la manière dont les clients concernés seront identifiés. Mais ce geste rappelle celui de SFR, qui avait offert de la data à ses abonnés après sa propre panne géante de juin 2025.
Concrètement, si l'on prend les forfaits actuellement commercialisés chez l'opérateur historique, l'abonné à la Série Spéciale 130 Go 5G+ d'Orange profitera de 260 Go, et celui du Forfait 300 Go 5G+ de 600 Go. Chez Sosh, le forfait 20 Go passera à 40 Go, et le 50 Go grimpera à 100 Go. Sur les petits forfaits, le cadeau est plus symbolique. Les 100 Mo d'une offre d'entrée de gamme ne deviendront que 200 Mo. Si le geste est bienvenu, c'est une maigre consolation pour ceux qui comptaient surtout sur leurs appels et leurs SMS. Idem pour ceux qui ont dû engager des frais, hier, pour compenser la perte de leur data avec un petit forfait d'appoint chez un autre opérateur. On pense aussi à ceux équipés d'une unique box 4G ou 5G à la maison, qui n'avaient pas de connexion fibre et de solution de secours. Pour le moment, Orange n'a pas évoqué la possibilité d'une compensation financière. Probablement que cela se fera au cas par cas.
Et maintenant, est-ce que tout fonctionne ? Officiellement, oui. Ce jeudi 22 octobre, quelques abonnés signalaient encore à la rédaction de petits soucis de connexion, mais ces cas restent très localisés et sporadiques, sans commune mesure avec la journée de mercredi. Si votre téléphone affiche toujours « Aucun service », pensez bien à activer le mode avion pendant une trentaine de secondes, avant de le désactiver, ou à redémarrer l'appareil, ce qui suffit souvent à forcer la reconnexion. Et en cas de nouvelle coupure, nos astuces pour rester joignable restent valables.

articles.title: Apple pourrait corriger le plus gros défaut de l'iPhone Duo dès l'an prochain
articles.text:
Alors que l’iPhone Duo, soit le premier pliant d’Apple, sera commercialisé ce 23 octobre, certains regards se tournent déjà vers le modèle de deuxième génération. La question est la suivante : le modèle de seconde génération comblera-t-il les manquements de la première version ? Il faut dire qu’Apple a dû faire quelques compromis, notamment en n’intégrant pas de téléobjectif ni Face ID dans son premier téléphone pliant. Justement, concernant Face ID, son intégration pourrait avoir lieu sur les iPhone Duo de deuxième génération.
Apple travaille à l’intégration de Face ID sur l’iPhone Duo de seconde génération
Selon le toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, Apple testerait actuellement des prototypes d’iPhone Duo qui intègrent FaceID. Le système de reconnaissance spatiale serait par ailleurs dissimulé sous l’écran externe. Intégrer Face ID dans un téléphone pliant constitue un véritable défi logistique. D’une part, un téléphone pliant se doit d’être particulièrement fin, étant donné qu’il double de volume une fois refermé. D’autre part, Face ID nécessite une certaine profondeur pour pouvoir diffuser les milliers de points infrarouges sur le visage de l’utilisateur et ainsi l’identifier en 3D.
En plaçant Face ID sous l’écran externe de l’iPhone Duo de deuxième génération, et en effectuant très certainement d’autres ajustements, Apple pourrait enfin parvenir à intégrer son système de reconnaissance faciale à l’appareil. Au passage, précisons que l’entreprise à la pomme envisagerait également d’intégrer un bouton Action à un futur Duo.
Des avancées plus rapides que prévues ?
En septembre dernier, Mark Gurman prophétisait l’intégration de Face ID et d’un téléobjectif sur l’iPhone Duo de troisième génération. Dorénavant, il estime que l’intégration de ces deux composants pourrait avoir lieu dans l’iPhone Duo de seconde génération, qui devrait sortir à l’automne 2027.
En réalité, Apple doit certainement travailler d’arrache-pied pour combler au plus vite ces deux lacunes. Le plus logique serait d’intégrer Face ID et un téléobjectif dès la deuxième génération de l’iPhone Duo, sans attendre la troisième, qui ne serait pas attendue avant 2028. L’iPhone Duo bénéficierait ainsi de véritables arguments.
À noter tout de même que Mark Gurman précise qu’Apple n’a pas encore décidé si Face ID sera intégré au produit final. Mais tôt ou tard, le capteur d’empreintes digitales Touch ID sera remplacé par FaceID sur l’iPhone Duo. Il reste maintenant à voir quand.

articles.title: Swiggy’s Q2: Net loss drops nearly 16%, revenue rises 36%; What sells? The celebrity or the product?
articles.text:
Swiggy’s Q2: Net loss drops nearly 16%, revenue rises 36%; What sells? The celebrity or the product?
Food and grocery delivery platform Swiggy has narrowed its net loss by 15.6% year on year in the second quarter of FY27. Its revenue rose 36% during the same period.
Dear Reader,
Shiprocket expands into the food commerce market.
The company’s AI-native commerce platform fastrr has partnered with Vegorama Group, which operates Punjabi Angithi, and Bikkgane Biryani, to help the restaurant brands manage direct orders, customer engagement, and hyperlocal deliveries.
In recent times, restaurants have been exploring ways to drive orders through their own digital channels instead of relying solely on third-party food aggregators. Direct channels give restaurants greater access to customer data and more opportunities to engage with diners after a purchase.
Meanwhile, Bengaluru-based digital trust company eMudhra has decided to exit its global website security certificate business, following a security incident involving weak cryptographic keys that prompted action from Google and Mozilla.
In a regulatory filing on Thursday, the company said its board had decided to voluntarily withdraw from the business, citing rising compliance costs, increasing data sovereignty requirements and diminishing commercial returns.
In other news, rural healthcare platform CureBay has raised Rs 100 crore in a pre-Series C funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. The round comprises Rs 69 crore in equity from IvyCap Ventures and existing investors, and more than Rs 30 crore in debt from Trifecta Capital, Alteria Capital, and VentureSoul Partners.
CureBay will use the funds to expand its operations across India, strengthen its healthcare delivery network, and develop its technology and AI capabilities.
Amid increasing AI threats, here’s a new one.
Major US banks have detected AI agents lurking inside customer accounts. Some of these unauthorised third-party agents are even attempting to act independently, Axios reported. Banks including Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo are working to curb these risks.
Lastly, what’s PHP and why did companies worldwide scramble to fix flaws in the programming language used to build websites? Here’s the lowdown.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Swiggy’s Q2: Net loss drops nearly 16%, revenue rises 36%
- What sells? The celebrity or the product?
Here’s your trivia for today: Who was awarded the 2016 Nobel Prize for Literature? (Scroll down for the answer)
Earnings
Swiggy’s Q2 net loss drops nearly 16%, revenue rises 36%
Food and grocery delivery platform Swiggy narrowed its net loss by 15.6% year on year (YoY) in the second quarter of FY27. Its revenue rose 36% during the same period.
The company reported a loss of Rs 922 crore in Q2 of FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 1,092 crore in the same period a year ago. Revenue for the quarter was Rs 7,571 crore, up from Rs 5,561 crore a year ago.
Key takeaways
- Losses at Instamart, Swiggy's quick commerce business, widened to Rs 764 crore, compared with Rs 739 crore a year ago, thus impacting the overall numbers of the company. Instamart’s revenue for the second quarter was Rs 1,306 crore, up from Rs 980 crore in the corresponding year-ago period.
- The gross order value of the food delivery business grew 17.7% YoY to touch Rs 10,054 crore for the second quarter. The adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was Rs 341 crore, an improvement of Rs 101 crore over the last one year.
- In comparison, Swiggy’s rival Eternal reported a 92% rise in net profit at Rs 125 crore, while revenue grew 78% to Rs 24,138 crore in the second quarter of FY27.
TechSparks
Celebrities don’t sell, the product does: Ananth Narayanan
The froth has gone out of D2C, and brands that want to last will have to play the patient game. This was the key message from Ananth Narayanan, Founder and CEO of BRND.ME, at the 17th edition of YourStory’s TechSparks event.
In a fireside chat with Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, Narayanan said, without product-market fit, merely scaling, which a lot of D2C brands used to do, is not valued anymore. “You need real cash flows, you need real product love, which is very hard,” he said.
Key takeaways
- A celebrity may add recall to a brand, but it’s the product that sells, said Narayanan. “A face can give you initial momentum, but I don’t think it can get you repeat consumers.”
- He advised founders to build with heart. “Build products that you love. Otherwise you are becoming a bit of a machine that churns out unit economics.”
- On India as a brand, Narayanan said the country stands for talent and should now move on to culture, from yoga and Ayurveda to mindfulness. “Why can’t we make the Indian way of living the most important thing in the digital age?”
<Funding Alert>

Amount: Rs 63 Cr
Round: Equity & Debt
Startup: TravClan
Amount: $5M
Round: Undisclosed
News & updates
- PHP patch: Companies and governments worldwide rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the widely used PHP programming language, as a cybersecurity company reported millions of hacking attempts after the vulnerabilities were disclosed. This came after governments in Europe and elsewhere took websites offline as a precaution on Wednesday while website operators scrambled to secure systems running the software.
- Nasdaq slide: The tech-heavy Nasdaq slid more than 1% on Thursday as growth stocks weakened after earnings from mega-caps Tesla and Meta failed to allay AI-related concerns, with a recovery in oil prices further adding to market unease, Reuters reported.
- Job cuts: Barclays is cutting around 5,000 jobs or 5% of its workforce this year, as it uses technology such as AI to slash fixed costs and improve returns. The job cuts were revealed as Barclays reported a third-quarter profit of £2.3 billion ($3.08 billion), up 12% from a year ago but undershooting analysts’ forecasts as its fixed income trading business underperformed.

articles.title: Los fallos críticos de PHP acaban de hacerse públicos. Lo misterioso es que alguien ya intentaba explotarlos cuatro días antes
articles.text:
Hay vulnerabilidades que pueden permanecer ocultas durante años y, cuando finalmente alguien las encuentra, todavía no se hacen públicas de inmediato. Comienza entonces una carrera discreta: entender qué permiten hacer, preparar una corrección y coordinar su divulgación antes de que la información llegue a quien pueda aprovecharla. Es un equilibrio delicado y bastante habitual en ciberseguridad. Lo que resulta mucho menos habitual es descubrir después que alguien ya estaba probando suerte cuando, en teoría, casi nadie fuera de ese círculo debía saber lo suficiente.
Eso es precisamente lo que Amazon Threat Intelligence asegura haber observado con PHP2Shell. Su red MadPot registró el 17 de octubre un intento de aprovechar estas vulnerabilidades, cuatro días antes de la divulgación pública coordinada y de la publicación de los parches el día 21. Amazon considera que las características de aquella actividad apuntan a un actor malicioso, pero hay una pieza que sigue sin encajar: no sabe cómo obtuvo información sobre el exploit antes de que fuera pública.
MadPot no es un servidor de producción comprometido, sino una red de honeypots, sistemas señuelo que Amazon expone para atraer actividad maliciosa y observar cómo se comportan quienes intentan atacarlos. El intento procedía además de una IP asociada a una red comercial de anonimización, uno de los indicios por los que la compañía considera probable que detrás hubiera un actor malicioso. Esa telemetría demuestra que el intento existió, pero no que una web real llegara a ser vulnerada. Para Amazon, la consecuencia práctica está en otro lugar: las organizaciones deberían revisar sus registros al menos desde el 17 de octubre, no únicamente desde la publicación del aviso.
Alguien llegó antes que todos
Para entender cómo hemos llegado hasta aquí hay que retroceder hasta agosto. El 11 de ese mes, Calif notificó al equipo de PHP una vía de ejecución remota de código vinculada a un problema que los mantenedores ya habían observado en 2024, y OpenAI llegó de forma independiente a la misma causa. Wiz comenzó su investigación independiente el 19 de agosto y comunicó sus hallazgos al equipo de PHP el día 24. La inteligencia artificial tuvo un papel relevante en varias de esas investigaciones, tanto en el descubrimiento como en el desarrollo y la validación de vías de explotación extremadamente complejas, pero no tenemos ninguna prueba de que explique lo ocurrido el 17 de octubre. La cronología completa está recogida también por la PHP Foundation.
PHP2Shell agrupa dos vulnerabilidades críticas, CVE-2026-109618 y CVE-2026-109619, ambas calificadas con un 9,2 sobre 10. El problema está en partes centrales de PHP relacionadas con la gestión de memoria y los errores, no en un plugin o una aplicación concreta. Según explica Cloudflare, bajo determinadas condiciones, una petición HTTP especialmente preparada puede provocar que el servidor utilice datos internos en un estado inseguro y llegar a ejecutar código sin autenticación. Que los fallos estén en el propio runtime amplía su alcance y obliga a revisar y actualizar las instalaciones afectadas, una recomendación que también hace directamente PHP.
La divulgación coordinada empezó a torcerse el 20 de octubre. Según reconstruye la PHP Foundation, alrededor de las 15:00 UTC comenzaron a circular los identificadores de los dos CVE, aunque sin detalles técnicos y acompañados de información incorrecta, lo que llevó al proyecto a adelantar un día la publicación prevista. Después apareció por error un vídeo de Calif con una demostración limitada y, ya el 21 a las 07:41 UTC, Chainguard publicó imágenes que incorporaban la corrección antes de terminar el embargo. Ninguno de esos episodios conocidos explica, sin embargo, lo ocurrido cuatro días antes.
Lo que vino después sí resulta mucho más fácil de seguir. Cloudflare pasó de registrar miles de intentos de explotación durante las diez horas anteriores al anuncio a decenas de miles en los primeros 45 minutos, cientos de miles en dos horas y finalmente millones, según detalló su CEO, Matthew Prince, en unas cifras recogidas por Reuters. La compañía observó además cómo los atacantes modificaban sus cargas para intentar esquivar las protecciones desplegadas. Amazon observó en paralelo una rápida proliferación de los exploits: aparecieron nuevos ejemplos de prueba de concepto y, una vez levantado el embargo, empezaron a utilizarse contra sus sensores prácticamente de inmediato.
A estas alturas podemos reconstruir casi toda la secuencia: sabemos cuándo se descubrieron los fallos, cómo se trabajó en sus correcciones, cuándo empezó a deteriorarse el embargo y con qué rapidez se multiplicaron los intentos en cuanto circularon más detalles. Lo que sigue faltando está precisamente al principio de esa historia. Amazon vio actividad compatible con un intento de explotación el 17 de octubre, cuando todavía no existía una explicación pública suficiente para llegar hasta ahí. Quién estaba detrás y, sobre todo, cómo obtuvo ese conocimiento siguen siendo preguntas abiertas.

articles.title: Bitchat, la messagerie hors ligne anti-censure, cartonne sur iOS et Android
articles.text:
Depuis quelques jours, l’application de messagerie Bitchat cartonne sur l’App Store et le Google Play Store. La messagerie chiffrée, qui s’appuie sur un fonctionnement indépendant du réseau mobile, s’est en effet hissée à la première place des applications les plus téléchargées dans la catégorie « Réseaux Sociaux », et figure même parmi les dix applications les plus téléchargées en France.
 bitchat 🇫🇷 https://t.co/JesDCw9f4o
— jack (@jack) October 22, 2026
Et ce soudain succès dans l’Hexagone n’est sans doute pas le fruit du hasard. Si BitChat est depuis quelques jours téléchargée massivement, c’est principalement grâce à son mode de fonctionnement.
Une messagerie en peer-to-peer qui échappe à la censure
Lancée il y a un an, l’application de messagerie chiffrée créée par Jack Dorsey, le cofondateur de feu Twitter, s’appuie sur un système de fonctionnement qui ne requiert aucune connexion à Internet. Elle s’utilise par ailleurs sans compte, et ne nécessite ainsi ni numéro de téléphone ni adresse e-mail pour être utilisée.
Contrairement aux applications de messagerie traditionnelles, Bitchat s’appuie sur un système décentralisé de pair-à-pair. Bitchat fonctionne sans connexion à Internet et sans serveur centralisé. Pour ce faire, la messagerie utilise le Bluetooth Low Energy pour établir un réseau maillé local. Cela signifie que tous les appareils utilisant Bitchat à proximité servent de relais pour transmettre les messages de proche en proche, étendant ainsi la couverture réseau.
Et c’est là que réside toute la force de Bitchat : la messagerie fonctionne lorsqu’Internet est coupé et échappe à tout risque de censure. Un système de fonctionnement idéal dans le cadre d’une manifestation, par exemple.
Fonctionnelle avec ou sans Internet
Bitchat sait aussi parfaitement fonctionner avec une connexion à Internet. Lorsqu’une connexion est disponible, l’application bascule sur le protocole ouvert et décentralisé Nostr pour communiquer avec d’autres utilisateurs à plus grande échelle. La messagerie transmet ainsi ses données à travers un réseau mondial composé de plus de 440 relais Nostr. Cela permet ainsi aux utilisateurs de la messagerie d’accéder à des salons de discussion géolocalisés à l’échelle d’un quartier d’une ville ou même d’une région. Là encore, la messagerie sécurise les échanges avec un chiffrement propre à l’application et génère des clés cryptographiques éphémères par zones géographiques.
Bitchat sélectionne automatiquement le canal de transmission le plus adapté à chaque situation. La messagerie passe directement par le réseau maillé Bluetooth si le destinataire est physiquement à proximité. Elle bascule automatiquement sur Nostr si le destinataire est hors de portée Bluetooth mais connecté à Internet. Et si toutefois aucun réseau n’est disponible dans l’immédiat, elle stocke temporairement les missives jusqu’à ce qu’un canal (Bluetooth ou Internet) soit de nouveau opérationnel.
Bitchat, solution de secours en cas de blocage des réseaux sociaux
Si Bitchat truste soudainement le podium des applications les plus téléchargées sur iPhone et Android, c’est principalement à cause du contexte sociopolitique actuel en France. Car parmi les débats menés après les manifestations du 17 octobre dernier, qui ont dégénéré en émeutes destructrices et ont donné lieu à des pillages, l’idée de procéder à un blocage des réseaux sociaux a commencé à émerger.
Invité par RTL lundi dernier, l’ancien Premier ministre Gabriel Attal, candidat Renaissance à l’élection présidentielle a ainsi suggéré de procéder à « un blocage temporaire ciblé sur les territoires où se déroulent les émeutes ».
 Les réseaux sociaux ne peuvent pas être le point de ralliement des casseurs et le moteur du mimétisme violent.
Lors des émeutes, nous devons pouvoir bloquer temporairement et de manière ciblée l'accès à certaines plateformes pour stopper l'effet de meute. pic.twitter.com/MLt8a0SOuQ
— Gabriel Attal (@GabrielAttal) October 19, 2026
En 2024, après plusieurs jours d’émeutes, Gabriel Attal, alors Premier ministre avait fait bloquer Tik-Tok en Nouvelle Calédonie, blocage qui avait été retoqué quelques jours plus tard par le Conseil d’État.
En téléchargeant massivement Bitchat sur leur smartphone, les participants aux manifestations à venir ce samedi 24 octobre, espèrent sans doute esquiver tout risque de voir leurs moyens de communications bloqués.

articles.title: eMudhra to exit global website certificate business
articles.text:
eMudhra to exit global website security certificate business
The move follows scrutiny over weak cryptographic keys, with eMudhra citing rising compliance costs and declining returns from a business that contributes just 1% of its revenue.
Bengaluru-based digital trust company eMudhra has decided to exit its global SSL/TLS certificate business following a security incident involving weak cryptographic keys that prompted action from Google and Mozilla. In a regulatory filing on Thursday, the company said its board had decided to voluntarily withdraw from the business, citing rising compliance costs, increasing data sovereignty requirements and diminishing commercial returns. The decision follows the discovery of eight intermediate certificate authority keys linked to eMudhra that were found to be dangerously weak, potentially allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate websites. The keys were generated in April 2025, but the weakness remained undetected for about 18 months. Google and Mozilla subsequently moved to block the affected certificates to protect users. eMudhra Chairman V Srinivasan said the company had revoked the affected certificate authorities within 14 hours of discovering the incident and promptly disclosed the issue.
The company maintained that its infrastructure had not been compromised, no data had been breached and none of the affected intermediate authorities had issued end-user certificates.
Global SSL/TLS certificates, which help authenticate websites and secure online communications, contribute approximately 1% of eMudhra's global revenue.
Srinivasan said increasing data sovereignty and compliance requirements had made the business more complex and expensive to operate. Competition from large providers offering SSL/TLS certificates free of cost had also reduced its commercial potential and return on investment.
"The level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS's place in our business," Srinivasan said.
He added that the board, following detailed deliberations, had concluded that withdrawing from the global SSL/TLS business was the right decision for the company and its shareholders.
eMudhra said it would now sharpen its focus on core enterprise solutions and digital trust services outside the SSL/TLS segment.
What happens to existing customers?
The company said its G1 RSA root certificates would continue to serve customers during the transition as it works with browser programmes and customers to facilitate the withdrawal.
It will reach out to affected customers and arrange replacement certificates free of cost through partners.
Revocation and certificate status services will continue until every issued certificate has expired or been replaced.
eMudhra also committed to fulfilling its remaining obligations to browser root programmes, including submitting a full root-cause report on the incident. It has not specified a timeline for completing the exit.
Other operations unaffected
The company clarified that its global SSL/TLS infrastructure operates separately from its other businesses, including its Indian digital signature certificate (DSC) and eSign services. Its enterprise public key infrastructure platforms, including emCA and CertiNext, emSigner eSignature Suite and identity and authentication solutions such as SecurePass and emAS, will also continue operating normally. The incident has drawn scrutiny from global browser providers and Indian authorities. Google's Chrome Security team had warned that the weak keys could allow attackers to forge trusted HTTPS certificates, while Mozilla blocked the affected certificates in Firefox.
India's Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) also issued an advisory on October 21, flagging the risks associated with the compromised certificate keys.
eMudhra, which provides digital identity, trust and security solutions across more than 35 countries, said the decision would allow it to concentrate resources on its broader enterprise technology portfolio.

articles.title: Les ventes de voitures électriques explosent en Europe, et la France mène la charge
articles.text:
L’électrique vient de franchir un nouveau cap dans l’Union européenne avec 22,7% des immatriculations neuves depuis janvier. La France et l’Allemagne tirent cette croissance, portées par la hausse des prix des carburants, les aides à l’achat et des modèles enfin plus accessibles.
La bascule est en train de se produire sur le marché automobile européen. Sur les neuf premiers mois de 2026, les voitures 100% électriques devancent les modèles essence sans hybridation dans les immatriculations neuves de l’Union européenne. Selon les chiffres publiés ce 22 octobre par l’Association des constructeurs européens (ACEA), elles représentent 22,7% du marché, contre 16,1% sur la même période de 2025, tandis que l’essence recule à 21,2%.
Un changement de hiérarchie spectaculaire, même si les hybrides non rechargeables restent les voitures les plus achetées, avec 36,3% du marché.
La France et l’Allemagne accélèrent, l’Italie reste à la traîne
L’engouement est particulièrement visible chez les deux poids lourds de l’automobile européenne. En septembre, 41,7% des voitures neuves immatriculées en France étaient électriques, contre 34,6% en Allemagne. À eux deux, les pays représentent plus de la moitié des ventes de véhicules électriques recensées ce mois-là sur les 17 marchés étudiés par New AutoMotive et E-Mobility Europe.
Mais tous les Européens ne roulent pas à la même vitesse. Le Danemark atteint déjà 88,8% de part de marché, tandis que l’Espagne est à 18,2% et l’Italie plafonne à seulement 7,6%. La transition progresse dans la plupart des marchés étudiés, mais les écarts restent quand même considérables.
Carburants chers et batteries moins coûteuses changent la donne
La flambée des prix à la pompe joue évidemment en faveur de l’électrique. Mais elle n’explique pas tout. L’offre s’est considérablement étoffée, les modèles deviennent plus accessibles et les aides publiques continuent de soutenir les ventes.
En France, le leasing social contribue également à cette accélération. Selon l’Avere, ses livraisons ont commencé dès juillet cette année, contre octobre en 2025, ce qui favorise mécaniquement les chiffres de septembre.
Les progrès techniques participent aussi à la baisse des prix. La nouvelle Renault Twingo électrique utilise, par exemple, une batterie LFP de 27,5 kWh, dont les cellules sont directement intégrées au pack. L’association de cette chimie LFP et de l’architecture cell-to-pack permet, selon Renault, de réduire d’environ 20% le coût total de la batterie. La citadine annonce jusqu’à 263 km d’autonomie WLTP.
Tesla domine les ventes, mais les Européens ripostent
Les derniers chiffres de septembre confirment le retour en force de Tesla. Avec 40 971 immatriculations pour le Model Y et 25 057 pour la Model 3, le constructeur américain occupe les deux premières places du classement européen, toutes motorisations confondues, selon les données provisoires de Dataforce.
La concurrence n’est pourtant pas à la traîne. Le Škoda Elroq poursuit sa progression avec 12 129 exemplaires écoulés sur le mois, tandis que les immatriculations de la Renault 5 bondissent de 42% sur un an, à 9 048 unités.
À l’échelle des groupes, Volkswagen conserve d’ailleurs la première place européenne sur le marché du tout-électrique avec des livraisons en hausse de 20% au troisième trimestre.
La voiture électrique n’a donc plus seulement ses performances ou ses arguments écologiques pour convaincre. Face à la flambée des prix à la pompe, elle tient désormais l’un de ses meilleurs arguments commerciaux, celui d’un coût à l’usage bien plus avantageux.

articles.text:
Despencou: Galaxy Z Flip 8 fica R$ 4 mil mais barato com cupom
Galaxy Z Flip 8 (256 GB) com tela dobrável de 120 Hz e 12 GB de RAM atinge o menor preço desde o lançamento, com desconto de 44% no Pix com cupom apenas no app Magalu
O Galaxy Z Flip 8 de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 5.159 no Pix com cupom CUPOMZFLIP30 somente no app do Magazine Luiza. O celular dobrável da Samsung, com tela AMOLED flexível de 120 Hz e 12 GB de RAM, atinge o menor preço desde o lançamento com desconto de 44% sobre o preço original de R$ 9.199.
O novo Galaxy Z Flip 8 chama a atenção para sua tela interna AMOLED Dinâmico 2X flexível de 6,9″, com taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de 2.600 nits. Tal combinação a permite reproduzir imagens com cores vibrantes, alta fluidez e visibilidade garantida. A externa Super AMOLED de 4,1″ suporta Always-On e integração ao Now Brief.
Seu chip Exynos 2600 de 2 nanômetros e os 12 GB de RAM sustentam a execução de apps pesados em multitarefa, games e funções do Galaxy AI. Os 256 GB de armazenamento oferecem espaço interno razoável para guardar vídeos e fotos.
A propósito, o kit de câmeras do celular é formado por uma wide de 50 MP com OIS e uma ultrawide de 12 MP, que captam belas cenas externas, e uma frontal interna de 10 MP que tira ótimas selfies. Todas filmam em 4K a 60 fps.
O corpo de alumínio Armor do Z Flip 8 recebe o vidro Gorilla Glass Victus 2 sobre a tela externa, resistente a quedas e arranhões. A certificação IP48 confere proteção extra contra mergulhos acidentais, mas apenas moderada contra poeira.
Sua bateria de 4.300 mAh resiste a até 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a fabricante. O suporte a carregamento rápido de 25 W via cabo USB-C e de 15 W sem fio o permite ser usado por um dia inteiro, um recurso excelente para usuários com agendas corridas.
O Galaxy Z Flip 8 de 256 GB (R$ 5.159 no Pix com cupom CUPOMZFLIP30 somente no app Magalu) roda Android 17 e deve receber sete atualizações do sistema operacional. O dobrável da Samsung possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.

articles.title: Una simple foto del rostro puede dar pistas sobre la supervivencia de un paciente con cáncer. Esta IA busca encontrarlas
articles.text:
Cuando una persona es diagnosticada de cáncer, es importante comenzar el tratamiento lo más pronto posible. Pero el problema al que se enfrentan los oncólogos aquí es el hecho de decidir cuál es el mejor tratamiento que se puede prescribir, puesto que, aunque se piensa que siempre se puede ir a los fármacos más agresivos, la realidad es que puede ser fatal para el paciente.
El estado general de un paciente es uno de los factores más críticos a la hora de que un equipo decida el tipo de tratamiento, puesto que no es lo mismo hablar de una persona muy mayor y frágil que de un chico joven y entrenado. Aquí la evaluación dependía del ojo clínico del especialista, pero ahora se está trabajando en una IA para poder leer con una precisión asombrosa nuestra cara para sacar un perfil.
Este sistema se ha bautizado como FAHR-Face y a priori busca predecir el riesgo de mortalidad y estimar la edad biológica de pacientes con cáncer basándose únicamente en fotografías faciales.
El trabajo. Para lograr que una máquina entienda los estragos de la enfermedad en el rostro humano, los científicos no empezaron desde cero. Aquí el modelo base fue entrenado utilizando más de 40 millones de fotografías de cara, y a partir de aquí la IA se dividió para entrenarse con 34.363 fotografías de pacientes oncológicos para tener dos modelos:
- FAHR-FaceAge: Diseñado para calcular la edad biológica (qué edad aparenta tener el cuerpo realmente, más allá de la fecha de nacimiento).
- FAHR-FaceSurvival: Entrenado específicamente para predecir el riesgo de mortalidad general.
La revisión. Para comprobar que el sistema realmente funcionaba y no estaba simplemente memorizando los datos de su hospital de origen, el modelo se sometió a una validación independiente en una cohorte distinta con cerca de 5.000 pacientes. Además, los investigadores se aseguraron de que la IA fuera robusta y no se dejara engañar por variables como el maquillaje, la iluminación, la pose o incluso la cirugía estética que se hubiera practicado.
Cómo lo hace. Según la investigación, para estimar la edad biológica, la inteligencia artificial centra su "atención" en los surcos nasolabiales, la frente y las sienes. Sin embargo, cuando se trata de predecir la supervivencia, el algoritmo escudriña la zona situada bajo los ojos y el puente nasal.
Algo que funciona bastante bien, puesto que los pacientes situados en el cuartil de mayor riesgo clasificado por la IA presentaban un riesgo de mortalidad 3,23 veces superior al del cuartil de menor riesgo. Traducido a cifras absolutas de 122 pacientes clasificados como de alto riesgo, el 52,5% falleció en un plazo de 90 días, por lo que demuestra que se acercaba bastante bien a la realidad.
Es un apoyo. A pesar de que hablamos de unas cifras importantes, la realidad es que los expertos piden cautela, puesto que este sistema no diagnostica el cáncer ni pone una "fecha de caducidad" exacta a los pacientes. Se trata de estimaciones puramente estadísticas aplicadas a personas que ya tienen un diagnóstico oncológico.
La realidad es que la tecnología aún debe superar importantes limitaciones. Los datos actuales provienen de estudios retrospectivos basados en cohortes donde los pacientes son mayoritariamente blancos, lo que obliga a seguir entrenando al modelo para que no discrimine por el color de piel. Además, faltan datos detallados sobre la toxicidad específica de los tratamientos y, lo más importante, aún no se ha demostrado mediante ensayos clínicos prospectivos que el uso de esta IA mejore las decisiones médicas ni alargue la supervivencia real de los enfermos.

articles.title: Smarsh EDGE 2026: Anchoring communications intelligence - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
4 insights from Smarsh EDGE: Governance becomes the foundation for communications intelligence
Financial institutions have long treated employee communications as something to archive for regulators. During the Smarsh EDGE event, that archive was recast as a source of business intelligence. Artificial intelligence can now analyze a year of email, messages and AI-prompt traffic and turn it into business context. The catch is that AI is now one of the channels that must be captured, including agents communicating with other agents.
The next phase will be defined by governance built into the foundation rather than bolted on. Customers are building their own agents outside compliance platforms and accessing that data through Model Context Protocol servers. Regulations remain technology-agnostic, however, and financial institutions remain liable for their agents’ actions. A study recently released by Smarsh Inc. found that only 26% of enterprises say their governance frameworks are keeping pace with AI deployment, even as AI in financial services moves beyond pilots.
“I think that move from system of record to system of engagement to system of intent, it’s really won or lost in one battleground, and that is data,” said Gemma Allen (pictured, left), host at theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. “Data is a huge moat for companies in 2026.”
Allen spoke with industry experts during the Smarsh EDGE event in New York. The interviews covered communications intelligence, language models built for compliance, levels of agentic autonomy and the cloud partnerships supporting Smarsh’s platform. (* Disclosure below.)
Here are four standout insights from the event:
1. Communications intelligence turns unstructured messages into client context.
Smarsh is helping customers extract valuable insights from communications that were long too unstructured to use, according to Goutam Nadella, chief strategy officer of Smarsh. A customer relationship management system holds only what someone recorded about a meeting. AI can now classify a year of conversations across email, WhatsApp, Teams and Zoom and suggest how to prepare for the next one. Smarsh was a launch partner for the compliance application programming interfaces from Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC, capturing prompts so that risky outputs can be traced back to their sources. Governance must be foundational rather than episodic, Nadella added, pointing to the billions of dollars in regulatory fines imposed on financial institutions for failing to preserve business communications conducted through WhatsApp and other messaging platforms.
Watch the full interview from theCUBE.
2. Natural-language questions replace Boolean searches for compliance supervisors.
Supervisors who once ran complex Boolean searches to find market manipulation can now ask an agent questions in plain language and receive flagged conversations with risk scores, explained Rohit Khanna, chief customer officer of Smarsh. A context layer that maps identity hierarchies, for which Smarsh has filed a patent, helps prevent the AI from generating false positives. The company also builds compliance language models that are cheaper to run than large language models, including a multilingual model that tracks speakers switching between languages. Its S-Combinator innovation group of 11 volunteers built a model risk management agent that is now in limited availability. Governance must come first, Khanna added.
Check out the full segment on theCUBE.
3. Agentic automation scales with the risk of each workflow.
Organizations can combine Smarsh’s agents with their own models and agents, while the platform provides underlying governance, data access controls and explainability underneath, noted Kamesh Tumsi, chief product officer of Smarsh. The company has launched four or five agents in six months alongside its new MCP server. Because 70% to 80% of compliance spending still goes toward labor, the potential return from AI is significant, according to Tumsi. He described four levels of autonomy: assisting, recommending, executing under guardrails and fully autonomous. Each process is matched to a level by weighing whether it is reversible, how complex it is and how much observability it requires.
See theCUBE’s full coverage.
4. AWS and Caylent help build governance into the infrastructure layer.
Customer anxiety about AI a year ago has turned into excitement now that the infrastructure exists, according to Nadella, who appeared with Arym Diamond, head of data and AI go-to-market sales at Amazon Web Services Inc., and Peter Sankauskas (pictured, right), portfolio chief technology officer of Caylent Inc., during a panel interview. Through a multiyear strategic collaboration agreement with AWS, Smarsh is building governance and security in at the infrastructure layer, because customers now want to know who or what is accessing their data. Smarsh has shifted from a system of record to a system of engagement built on AWS, explained Diamond. AI needs a balance: authority without context produces slop, and context without authority leaves teams babysitting it, added Sankauskas.

articles.title: GALAX GeForce RTX 5080 HOF Extreme Comes with Dual 12V-2x6 Power Connectors
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
GALAX GeForce RTX 5080 HOF Extreme Comes with Dual 12V-2x6 Power Connectors
GALAX has unveiled the specifications for its GeForce RTX 5080 Hall Of Fame Extreme edition graphics card, the only RTX 5080 model featuring two 12V-2x6 power connectors. Interestingly, the card has a TGP of 400 W, and the official GALAX announcement states that the two power connectors are not required for simultaneous use. Instead, they are offered as alternatives to suit different PC builds and cable management preferences, so even if both connections are used, only one will be active. One standard connector is located on the top of the GPU, in the usual spot. The second 12V-2x6 power cable is positioned at the bottom of the card, concealed behind a GPU shroud near the PCIe x16 connector. This serves as an alternative power supply, allowing system builders to hide visible cables for a cleaner look.
For the GPU itself, GALAX has implemented a 20-phase power delivery system for the GPU and a 4-phase power delivery design for the GDDR7 memory, along with a digital PWM controller, eFuse, and HOF-branded inductors. All of this is mounted on a customized white PCB with gold plating on key connections. In OC Mode, which raises the TGP to 400 W, the GPU clock speed reaches 2,805 MHz. In regular Gaming Mode, the TGP is reduced to NVIDIA's reference 360 W, with clock speeds at 2,655 MHz. Since the 12V-2x6 connector is sufficient for these TGP designs, a second power source is unnecessary. GDDR7 memory is running at 30 Gbps on a 256-bit memory bus for a total of 960 GB/s memory bandwidth.Currently, the GALAX GeForce RTX 5080 Extreme is only available in China, and it's unclear if it will be sold in Western markets. However, the card is likely to attract enthusiasts worldwide, though it is expected to come with a hefty price tag. The current fixed price in China is 19,999 Yuan, which is approximately 2,995 US Dollars at the time of writing.

articles.title: De baterías a materiales del futuro: el MIT creó una IA que podría identificar compuestos prometedores
articles.text:
Encontrar el material ideal para una tecnología específica podría volverse tan sencillo como describirle a una inteligencia artificial qué propiedades debe tener. Investigadores del Instituto de Tecnología de Massachusetts (MIT) desarrollaron un modelo que no solo procesa texto, sino que puede “ver” cómo están organizados los átomos de un material en tres dimensiones y razonar sobre sus características y usos. El sistema, descrito en la revista Nature Communications, podría acelerar un proceso de descubrimiento que hoy puede llevar años de prueba y error, informó MIT News, el portal de noticias del instituto.
Los cristales poseen disposiciones atómicas altamente ordenadas y representan más del 90% de los materiales sólidos de la Tierra. Sin embargo, los modelos de inteligencia artificial actuales enfrentan dos limitaciones para trabajar con ellos: la literatura experimental se concentra en unas pocas clases de cristales, lo que sesga sus respuestas hacia esos materiales, y al estar entrenados solo con texto, no pueden interpretar las estructuras tridimensionales que definen el comportamiento de un cristal.
Para superar esas barreras, el modelo desarrollado combina las estructuras atómicas en 3D con descripciones en lenguaje natural obtenidas de publicaciones experimentales y bases de datos computacionales basadas en primeros principios. En lugar de depender exclusivamente de trabajos ya publicados, el equipo optó por generar narrativas sobre los materiales a partir de esas fuentes. “Descubrimos que, cuando usamos ese conjunto de datos narrativo, los modelos predicen mejor la función”, explicó Ju Li, profesor Carl Richard Soderberg de Ingeniería de Potencia en los departamentos de Ciencia e Ingeniería de Materiales y de Ciencia e Ingeniería Nuclear del MIT.
El resultado es una caracterización que reúne composición química, estructura, propiedades, consideraciones de procesamiento y aplicaciones potenciales.
La estructura atómica como vínculo con el desempeño
El equipo empleó aprendizaje contrastivo, un método que entrena al modelo mediante la comparación entre ejemplos similares y diferentes de estructuras y descripciones. Así buscó construir una comprensión compartida entre la disposición espacial de los átomos y el lenguaje utilizado para describirla.
“La estructura está realmente en el centro del campo de la ciencia de materiales”, afirmó Li. “Si se entiende la estructura, se puede inferir bastante sobre las propiedades y el desempeño de los materiales. Queríamos construir para el modelo la conexión entre la estructura atómica de un material y sus propiedades y procesamiento”.
Para validar el enfoque, la investigación comparó dos versiones del sistema: una entrenada con descripciones generadas por inteligencia artificial y otra alimentada únicamente con textos de artículos científicos. La primera logró relacionar las geometrías cristalinas con sus descripciones lingüísticas; la segunda no alcanzó esa asociación.
Búsqueda de electrolitos para baterías de estado sólido
Los investigadores mostraron que el modelo puede recibir una consulta en lenguaje natural que describa una propiedad y, a partir de ella, identificar materiales cristalinos con esa característica.
Cuando se le pidió encontrar materiales aptos para electrolitos de baterías de litio de estado sólido, los primeros resultados incluyeron compuestos que ya habían sido señalados de forma independiente como candidatos prometedores.
“A veces se producen estos saltos dentro de la ciencia de materiales en torno a la integración algorítmica hacia herramientas útiles, que la comunidad utiliza para seguir avanzando en el campo”, dijo Elsa Olivetti, profesora Jerry McAfee (1940) de Ingeniería en el Departamento de Ciencia e Ingeniería de Materiales del MIT.
“Este enfoque nos ayuda a observar con mayor profundidad las estructuras tridimensionales y a vincularlas con las propiedades y el procesamiento. Espero que pueda ser uno de esos saltos”, agregó.
Li comparó el potencial de esta herramienta con AlphaFold, el modelo de inteligencia artificial que relaciona las estructuras de las proteínas con sus funciones y que contribuyó a la investigación biológica y al desarrollo de fármacos. “Poder ver un cristal tridimensional y cómo están conectados sus átomos es algo fundamental. Creo que esto será útil para cualquiera que practique la ciencia de materiales”, sostuvo.

articles.title: Valve publicly mentions HLX, which might be Half-Life 3, for the first time
articles.text:
Crystal ball: Hype surrounding the possibility that Valve was putting the finishing touches on Half-Life 3 reached a fever pitch last year before fading. A fresh batch of data-mining results and comments from Valve this week has reignited anticipation, however. While it remains unclear what precisely the company is working on, it appears to be completely unlike its current stable of live-service games.
Valve hasn't offered substantial details about a new Half-Life project since launching Half-Life: Alyx in 2020, but a quick name-drop has revived debate over whether Half-Life 3 is in advanced development. Code recently added to Deadlock and other Valve games also sheds more light on the game's features, if it indeed exists.
The codename HLX has appeared in the company's code since early 2024, but Valve did not mention it publicly until a Q&A session at GameSoundCon 2026 on Wednesday. Composer and sound designer Mike Morasky confirmed that Deadlock and HLX each have custom HDR implementations.
 – Tyler "Hype Merchant" McVicker (@Tyler_McV) October 22, 2026
Fellow sound designer David Feise, seated next to him, could be heard whispering "nice work," and later quipped that Morasky had only said HLX once, suggesting the mention wasn't meant to be public. This isn't the first time Morasky has referenced future Half-Life projects.
Then, on Thursday, well-known Valve data miner Tyler McVicker released his latest video describing how recent Source 2 engine updates for Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, and Deadlock might relate to HLX.
Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, and Deadlock are multiplayer games, but several reports from McVicker last year outlined portions of code mentioning systems typically associated with single-player shooters, such as AI-controlled enemies and concepts from prior Half-Life games.
Other features that seem unique to HLX include procedural level alteration, ray tracing, and AMD FSR support. In this week's video, McVicker also described features related to the Combine gunship and other enemies, as well as dynamic rain audio and new cut-scene animation technology.
The data miner has also been tracking Valve's commit rate, which spiked after the recent Source 2 updates. While some observers might suspect AI coding tools are behind the uptick, prior reports lead McVicker to believe the company has been using AI tools since at least 2024. The nature and extent of AI use within Valve remains unclear, but it's possible that HLX or something else is behind the increased activity.

articles.title: GPUs from stolen $470,000 Nvidia RTX 5090 shipment at Brazil airport appear for sale online, identified by serial numbers — three employees identified by police helped steal equipment
articles.text:
GPUs from stolen $470,000 Nvidia RTX 5090 shipment at Brazil airport appear for sale online, identified by serial numbers — three employees identified by police helped steal equipment
The haul is thought to be worth nearly half a million dollars.
Following reports over the weekend that an Nvidia RTX 5090 shipment worth $470,000 was stolen from a Brazilian airport, a contraband graphics card linked to the shipment has shown up for sale online. Brazilian media also reports that the police and airport authorities have identified three employees thought to have been involved in the heist, according to GMC. (Machine translated)
According to the report, Guarulhos International Airport has issued a statement confirming that "The investigation of the facts is the responsibility of the competent authorities to clarify the circumstances of what happened." A Brazilian TV news network appears to have identified one of the cards, a Zotac Gaming RTX 5090 for sale on the online marketplace OLX for over $6,000. Quite unfortunately, the reseller uploaded clear pictures of the card's serial number, linking it to the missing haul of graphics cards. Per the report, there is no information to identify the seller, and the listing appears to have since been taken down.
However, police information reported by the outlet does reveal a chain of events and some possible suspects in the case. The shipment, imported from the United States and thought to be worth nearly $500,000, arrived in Brazil on September 20 and was registered with customs on September 24. The two pallets went missing after being authorized for release on September 25. Police believe "two outsourced forklift operators" removed the pallets from the warehouse on September 21, an act apparently recorded by CCTV.
Police state the equipment was loaded onto a truck and hasn't been seen since. A third "checker" employee is said to have released the merchandise from the system to pass through electronic controls.
The RTX 5090 is the world's best consumer gaming GPU, but high demand for AI compute has seen it all but disappear from conventional retail, with the card now fetching upwards of $10,000 in the few remaining marketplaces it can be found, nearly always offered by third-party sellers. articles.title: Durabook Introduces the R12 Rugged Tablet Active Edge AI Platform
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Durabook Introduces the R12 Rugged Tablet Active Edge AI Platform
Durabook, the global rugged mobile solutions brand owned by Twinhead International Corporation, today announced its new R12 Rugged Tablet active edge AI platform. With the Intel Core Ultra Series 3 CPU, the R12 Rugged Tablet delivers exceptional computing power with enhanced AI performance, energy efficiency, and multitasking capability. It is well-suited to teams from defense, public safety, and industrial operations working from vehicles or outdoors where connectivity is unreliable.
With the potential for up to 412 TOPS of combined AI compute the platform is built for demanding edge AI workloads. 180 TOPS of integrated AI performance can process data from cameras, sensors, and connected systems locally, helping teams analyze information and use it to make decisions on the spot. The R12's integrated AI power can be boosted by an optional 232 TOPS of discrete GPU delivering up to 412 TOPS. This scalable architecture gives users the flexibility to run advanced AI inference, computer vision, and mission-critical software-enabled AI applications directly at the edge.A unique and significant advantage of the R12 tablet is optional dedicated NVIDIA RTX 2000 Ada graphics, which brings energy efficient workstation-class graphics performance to this fully rugged tablet for demanding visual and compute-intensive applications such as architectural visualization and digital content creation.
The R12 Rugged Tablet provides a 12.2-inch, DynaVue sunlight readable display with brightness up to 1,200 nits so users experience the space and screen clarity to work with maps, imagery, sensor outputs, and multiple information layers. This resides within a chassis smaller than current 11.6-inch market tablets. When paired with a detachable backlit keyboard the R12 lets users move between touch-based field work and tasks that benefit from a keyboard, without changing devices.
"Rugged, powerful, and mission-ready, this Durabook tablet is taking its rightful place supporting AI at the edge for professionals in the field," said Twinhead CEO Fred Kao. "The R12 Rugged Tablet enables a clearer view of information in mobile, space-constrained, or disconnected environments."
Even when connectivity is unreliable the R12 tablet is designed to receive data including 4K video and 8K content from cameras, sensors, and connected systems, process it locally, and support making better decisions more quickly. The R12 is equipped with an array of connectivity options including high-speed 2.5GbE LAN, Thunderbolt 4, USB and 4G/5G, and offers the rare option of up to two RJ-45 ports, and expansion options for purpose-built configurations.
In an ever-evolving mobile work environment, the R12 is protected with advanced security support, such as TPM 2.0 as standard, as well as a 5.0 MP IR camera for Windows Hello with dynamic shutter design, 13 MP rear camera with dynamic shutter design, and Windows 11 Secured-core PC, quick-release SSD and a fingerprint scanner.
Another distinctive feature of the R12 is its dual easy-removable battery design with optional hot-swappable, high-capacity battery technology so users in the field avoid downtime. It has an extended battery life of up to 20 hours.
Wherever performance and durability must coexist such as in defense, public safety, field service, or manufacturing applications the R12 Rugged Tablet is engineered for the mission with proven resistance to drops, shocks, vibration, dust, and extreme temperatures. The tablet meets MIL-STD-810H, 6-foot drop, and IP66 standards, and MIL-STD-461G for electromagnetic compatibility. It is further certified with ANSI/UL C1D2 for use in specified hazardous locations across oil and gas, petrochemical manufacturing, industrial manufacturing, and other industries with potentially explosive atmospheres.
The new R12 Rugged Tablet is available for order now.
