articles.title: Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreaking is here, with homebrew, modding, and reverse engineering
articles.text:
The big picture: AI coding has unleashed a new wave of decompilations and jailbreaks, largely centered on video games. Modders cracked almost every PlayStation 5 firmware version a few weeks ago, and the Nintendo Switch 2 is next. The phenomenon could lead to a repeat of the original Switch's piracy problem, but Nintendo has already responded.
The Nintendo Switch 2's first public jailbreak is now in the wild. Unfortunately, anyone who hasn't already bought the coding tool SmileBASIC 4 for the Switch is out of luck, as it has already disappeared from the Nintendo eShop.
Researcher and modder Sammy Hajhamid successfully cracked Switch 2 firmware version 23.0.1, ran homebrew software, accessed most of the device's peripherals, and backed up save files. He demonstrated his progress with footage of a modded version of Mario Kart World featuring Goku, Walter White, Peter Griffin, Hatsune Miku, Gold Ship, and other famous non-Nintendo characters.
 – pepsipu (@pepsipu) October 22, 2026
While it's usually Claude driving the AI reverse-engineering craze, Hajhamid used OpenAI's Codex instead. He used it to vibe-code the Mario Kart mod, but the jailbreak itself took about two weeks.
The exploit works entirely through software, so it doesn't require hardware modifications. However, Hajhamid hasn't devised a full-blown custom firmware yet, so the hack must be repeated each time the handheld-console hybrid reboots, and it requires a computer.
Must read: Decompilation on Steroids - Why AI Is Suddenly Cracking Open Old Software
Getting Codex to hack the Switch 2 took two approaches and an elaborate harness to interface with the device physically. That included a method to deliver USB inputs and receive HDMI outputs, as well as a Bluetooth light switch flicker, bought from Amazon, to press the power button whenever the AI coding tool crashed the handheld.
The first time Codex jailbroke the Switch 2 was via WebKit. That's unsurprising, since WebKit has enabled console hacking before, but it didn't enable homebrew, modding, or save backups. Getting there required giving the AI new goals.
The access point ultimately turned out to be the Switch 1 title SmileBASIC 4. An earlier version had already enabled a 3DS jailbreak, making it a natural choice. However, either Nintendo or developer SmileBomb delisted SmileBASIC 4 in the US and Europe soon after the Switch 2 jailbreak went public, so only people who already downloaded the coding tool can perform the hack. The Japanese version remained available as of this writing.
If the Switch 2 hacking scene progresses, it could eventually mirror the original Switch, which was cracked unusually early for a Nintendo device.
Emulation and custom firmware usually affect Nintendo consoles long after their original shelf lives, but major Switch releases often found their way to emulators almost immediately after hitting store shelves.
The PS5 scene hasn't slowed down either. Earlier this month, a developer demonstrated what appears to be a kernel-level exploit on firmware 14.10, the version Sony pushed to close the hole used by the Relapse jailbreak. The exploit remains private, and Sony has since released firmware 14.20. Hacks for earlier firmware versions have added Linux support to the console.

articles.title: TSMC is seeking chipmaking equipment that doesn't contain Chinese rare-earth magnets — asks suppliers to provide alternative motors as export controls threaten fab operations
articles.text:
TSMC is seeking chipmaking equipment that doesn't contain Chinese rare-earth magnets — asks suppliers to provide alternative motors as export controls threaten fab operations
China accounts for 95% of finished permanent magnets
TSMC, the world's largest contract chip manufacturer, is seeking alternative machinery without rare-earth components to reduce its dependence on China-dominated materials and avoid disruptions to factory operations caused by the country's export controls. According to a Reuters report on October 22 citing people familiar with the matter, the Taiwanese company has begun approaching its equipment suppliers to explore whether they can provide factory automation equipment equipped with motors that don't require rare-earth materials.
TSMC supplies the extremely powerful Nvidia chips that are facilitating the AI boom. It also manufactures chips for Apple, Broadcom, Qualcomm, and numerous other tech and automotive companies. The company operates enormous, highly automated semiconductor fabrication plants. These factories use industrial machinery that relies on electric motors with powerful permanent magnets made from rare-earth elements such as neodymium, dysprosium, and terbium.
According to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), China accounts for roughly 70% of global rare earth mining. The International Energy Agency (IEA) says China also controls around 90% of refining and approximately 95% of the finished permanent magnets found in TSMC’s machines, giving Beijing a quasi-absolute monopoly over one of the most critical technology supply chains. In April 2025, the country placed seven medium and heavy rare earths and the magnets made from them under export controls, requiring exporters to seek case-by-case approval and export licenses, thereby choking shipments to manufacturers across the U.S., Europe, and Asia, including TSMC.
China expanded the controls on October 9, 2025, to include five additional rare earths, processing technology and equipment, and even products manufactured outside the country that contain more than 0.1% Chinese-origin rare earths, or are made using Chinese processing technology. It later suspended the October expansion for one year, until November 10, 2026. This has now been extended for an additional 90 days.
TSMC’s moves aim to reduce the risk that these controls will hinder production at its factories. Even with all other raw materials and machinery required to manufacture its chips, shortages of specialized motor components could complicate the maintenance, repair, or expansion of its production equipment. Several technological approaches allow motors to avoid rare earth magnets. Conventional induction motors, for example, generate torque using electromagnetic induction rather than permanent magnets. Switched-reluctance motors are another option, while some permanent-magnet motors can use ferrite magnets instead of rare-earth magnets. However, these technologies typically involve different trade-offs in efficiency, size, power density, precision, and control requirements.
Meanwhile, the rest of the world is undertaking the painstaking, drawn-out task of building a rare-earth supply chain outside China. Taiwan is reportedly pursuing domestic rare-earth production capabilities in collaboration with the United States, with both countries confirming their intent to reduce reliance on Chinese rare-earth and critical-mineral supply chains.
Taiwan's government is supporting the Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) in establishing a pilot production line within three years that could supply about 50% of Taiwan's domestic rare-earth demand. Meanwhile, the U.S. is “working with Taiwan and other partners to develop alternative sources of supply, expand processing capacity and build more resilient supply chains,” according to the report. In February 2026, the Trump administration announced plans to create a $12 billion critical minerals stockpile to offset supply chain risks from China.

articles.title: Microsoft admits its Windows update to fix 'Always on VPN' issue didn't actually work
articles.text:
Microsoft admits its Windows update to fix 'Always on VPN' issue didn't actually work
IT admins are stuck with temporary workarounds as the tech giant admits the bug was "mistakenly updated to Resolved status."
- Microsoft has confirmed that the Windows 11 'Always On VPN' connection issues introduced in September remain unfixed.
- The tech giant admitted the bug was mistakenly flagged as resolved in the October 13 patch.
- IT admins must continue pinning VPN profiles to a single protocol until a permanent fix arrives in the coming weeks.
Microsoft’s October Patch Tuesday was supposed to mark the end of a highly frustrating month for Windows 11 users relying on Always On VPN. However, the company has now walked back its initial claims, admitting that the highly anticipated fix was a total failure.
In a service bulletin sent to IT administrators this week, Microsoft confirmed that the nasty glitch, which leaves enterprise VPN connections hanging indefinitely or entirely unable to connect, remains fully active.
The issue was originally introduced during the September 2026 security updates and continues to wreak havoc across enterprise networks that depend on secure remote access.
With the bug still running rampant, users relying on the best VPN services for seamless remote work will have to make do with Microsoft's suggested temporary workarounds.
A permanent fix is reportedly still several weeks away, leaving network administrators in a precarious position.
An unresolved headache
The problem primarily affects users utilizing Microsoft's native Always On VPN technology with automatic protocol selection configured. Always On VPN is a critical remote access tool designed to build an encrypted link back to corporate networks quietly in the background.
Trouble starts when an initial connection attempt fails. The system tries to fall back to a secondary method, automatically switching between IKEv2 and SSTP protocols.
Right now, this fallback process is entirely broken. Affected clients will simply hang at a "Connecting" status or flat-out fail to get through. In some instances, subsequent retry attempts will throw an error reading, “The specified port is already in use.”
We previously reported that the KB5127648 and KB5127646 cumulative updates released on October 13 had supposedly cured the fault, while simultaneously introducing bizarre new Wi-Fi authentication issues. Now, it appears those updates failed to deliver on the VPN front altogether.
As reported by The Register, the tech giant has been forced to confess its error. Microsoft explained to administrators that the bug had been “mistakenly updated to Resolved status on October 13, 2026.” The company’s official KB5127648 support page has since been scrubbed of any mention of the VPN repair, with the changelog now quietly noting that the fix will be included in a later release.
Temporary mitigation
For now, Microsoft has downgraded the bug's status from "Resolved" back to "Mitigated," apologizing to IT admins for the confusion.
According to early reports, a permanent repair is slated for an upcoming update that Microsoft expects to ship within the next several weeks.Until that release lands, IT administrators simply cannot treat the October Patch Tuesday builds as a cure.
The sole safeguard currently available is to restrict affected Always On VPN profiles to a single protocol. By manually pinning the connection to either SSTP or IKEv2 and disabling the auto-fallback feature, administrators can prevent the bug from triggering in the first place.
The Register notes that, “The issue affects Windows 11 versions from 24H2 through 26H2.” If your organization relies heavily on these recent builds for remote connectivity, your IT department will need to ensure this temporary mitigation remains firmly in place until Microsoft can successfully deploy a working patch.

articles.title: Clicks Power Keyboard im Test: Macht mich dieses Gadget am iPhone noch produktiver?
articles.text:
Clicks Power Keyboard im Test: Macht mich dieses Gadget am iPhone noch produktiver?
Manche würden es als puren Stress bezeichnen. Aber ich liebe es, auf einer Messe wie dem Mobile World Congress oder der IFA unterwegs zu sein und beim hektischen Gang von einem Meeting zum nächsten noch ein, zwei Mails auf meinem iPhone abzuarbeiten. Die Kunst, beim Schreiben dem Gegenverkehr in den vollen Messehallen aus dem Weg zu gehen, habe ich über die Jahre perfektioniert. Und doch gibt es immer Raum für Verbesserungen. Das iPhone hat schließlich keine echten, sondern nur virtuelle Tasten. Einmal in der Hektik falsch getouched, schon ergibt die Nachricht keinen Sinn mehr. Genau diesen Umstand will Clicks mit dem Power Keyboard beheben.
Magnetisch, japanisch – gut?
Der Hersteller kann einem bekannt vorkommen. Seit 2024 bietet er Hüllen an, die in erster Linie iPhones und einige wenige Android-Smartphones um eine physische Tastatur erweitern, sie aber auch gleichzeitig in wirklich unhandliche Gadgets verwandeln. In Zukunft will Clicks mit dem Communicator ein eigenes Android-Smartphone im Blackberry-Stil herausbringen. Das Power Keyboard ist eine Art Zwischenschritt. Hierbei handelt es sich nicht um eine Hülle, sondern um eine Ansteck-Tastatur, die via Magsafe oder Qi 2 magnetisch an der Rückseite von iPhones oder anderen kompatiblen Smartphones hält. Da wackelt nichts.
Damit die Tastatur nicht ständig im Weg ist, gibt es einen gut gemachten Schiebemechanismus, über den man sie ein- und ausfahren kann. Allein mit dem Anklipsen ist es allerdings nicht getan. Die Tastatur verbindet sich via Bluetooth mit dem Smartphone. Wer das volle Potenzial ausreizen will, muss zudem die Clicks-App installieren. Die gibt es nur auf US-Englisch und Japanisch. Warum sie auf meinem Gerät ab Werk japanische Schriftzeichen anzeigt, erschließt sich mir genauso wenig wie der Umstand, dass man die Sprache nur über die Einstellungs-App des iPhones, nicht aber über die Clicks-App selbst ändern kann.
Nachdem diese Hürden aus dem Weg geräumt sind, kann man in der App tatsächlich einige sinnvolle Dinge einstellen. Dazu gehört das Verhalten der Enter-Taste. Wollt ihr in der Lage sein, in Messengern wie Slack einen Absatz zu machen, um längere Nachrichten sinnvoll zu gliedern, oder wollt ihr fertige Sätze einfach rausfeuern? Das legt ihr hier fest, indem ihr den Soft-Return ein- oder ausschaltet. Genauso regelt ihr hier auf Wunsch die Hintergrundbeleuchtung der Tasten oder was der rote Clicks-Key machen soll. Die Auswahlmöglichkeiten bleiben allerdings oft begrenzt. Eben jener Clicks-Button kann zum Beispiel nur als Tab- oder CTRL-Taste fungieren.
Weitere Einstellungen aus der App: Ihr wählt aus, ob die Shift-Taste bei doppeltem Antippen zur Caps-Lock-Taste werden soll, falls IHR WIRKLICH MAL WAS LOSWERDEN WOLLT! Ebenfalls per Doppeltipp sorgt die Symbol-Taste dafür, dass ihr statt der Buchstaben die aufgedruckten Symbole tippt. Außerdem könnt ihr per Tastenkombination einen Cursor-Modus aktivieren, um wie im Computerspiel via W, A, S, D (oder I, J, K, L) durch eure Texte zu navigieren.
Wenn euch das noch nicht genug überfrachtet, könnt ihr noch Apple-Shortcuts auf die Tasten legen und per Kombination aktivieren, um etwa Spotify zu öffnen oder die Taschenlampe zu aktivieren. Im Zweifel sind diese Kurzbefehle aber schneller ausgeführt, wenn man sie einfach auf dem Homescreen ablegt.
Das Schreiben neu erlernen
Anders als erhofft, kann man die Clicks-Tastatur also nicht einfach am iPhone befestigen und losarbeiten. Stattdessen muss man sich zunächst mit den Eigenheiten vertraut machen – und sich an das Gewicht gewöhnen. Denn mit 180 Gramm ist die Anstecktastatur schwerer als mein iPhone 16 (170 Gramm). Mit beidem zusammen hat man ordentlich etwas in der Hand und braucht entsprechend große Hosen- oder Jackentaschen. Bequem ist das nicht. Zweckdienlich allerdings auch nicht.
Statt unterwegs im Laufschritt noch mehr E-Mails und Slack-Nachrichten zu bewältigen, muss ich jetzt ständig stehen bleiben, nach unten schauen und gucken, was ich da eigentlich mache. Die Tasten auf dem Keyboard nehmen in etwa so ein wie die virtuelle Tastatur auf dem Bildschirm. Weil man aber natürlich nicht zwischen dem normalen und dem Layout mit Nummernreihe und Sonderzeichen wechseln kann, muss der Hersteller mehr Tasten auf einmal unterbringen. Dadurch wirkt die Clicks-Tastatur gedrungen, das Tippen “fummelig”.
Dazu kommt das ungewohnte Layout der Tastatur. Die Backspace-Taste befindet sich nicht wie auf dem Macbook auf Höhe der Nummernreihe und auch nicht, wie auf dem iPhone, rechts neben der untersten Buchstabenreihe, sondern in der Mitte. Langes Suchen und einige Vertipper sind da vorprogrammiert. Das gilt gleichfalls für die Sonderzeichen. Ist die Tastatur des iPhones nämlich auf Deutsch eingestellt, sind die aufgedruckten Symbole hinfällig. Nichts, wirklich gar nichts, befindet sich an der Stelle, an der man es vermuten würde. Ich verrate kein Geheimnis, wenn ich sage, dass dieser Umstand bei der Arbeit zunächst ausbremst. Dann können die verbauten Tasten doch so clicky sein.
Irgendwann geht es dann doch. Ich komme mehr und mehr zurecht und werde etwas schneller. Meine gewohnte Geschwindigkeit erreiche ich aber nie. Fünf Wochen mit der externen Tastatur können 15 Jahre Muskelgedächtnis nicht schlagen. Mehr als einmal erwische ich mich dabei, wie ich das Power Keyboard abschalte und auf dem Bildschirm weitertippe – weil es eben viel schneller geht.
Mit dem Clicks sieht man besser
Natürlich ist nicht alles schlecht. Zwei Dinge können sogar richtig gut sein: Denn mit aktivierter Bluetooth-Tastatur hat man mehr Platz auf dem Bildschirm. So zeigt das iPhone mehr als die letzten eineinhalb Nachrichten. Gelegentlich passt sogar eine ganze E-Mail auf den Schirm. Außerdem ist in der Tastatur eine kleine Powerbank integriert – auch deswegen ist sie so schwer. Sie kann das iPhone oder kompatible andere Smartphones unterwegs drahtlos laden und so die Laufzeit verlängern.
Ob das die Nachteile sprichwörtlich aufwiegt, muss jeder für sich entscheiden. Um einen weiteren Anreiz zu bieten, bewirbt Clicks das Gadget zudem als externe Tastatur für Smart TVs oder Tablets. Am Fernseher soll man sich bequemer in Apps einloggen können. Heutzutage wird das aber in der Regel bequem per QR-Code erledigt. Am Tablet bin ich, wie am iPhone, mit der virtuellen Tastatur schneller.
Fazit
130 Euro kostet das Clicks Power Keyboard. Der Name passt. Dank der eingebauten Powerbank liefert es schließlich Power. Zum Power-User werde ich damit zumindest nicht. Dafür ist es zu schwer, zu ungelenk und in manchen Situationen einfach zu kompliziert. Da verzichte ich zugunsten der virtuellen Tastatur gerne auf einen Teil meines Bildschirms. Und wenn in der Hektik mal etwas danebengeht, dann ist das ahlt eebn mla os!

articles.title: TravClan raises $5M from Flipkart, others
articles.text:
TravClan raises $5M from Flipkart, others
TravClan said it will use the funds to expand its global supply network, enhance its technology and AI capabilities, and strengthen destination operations across key international markets.
TravClan, a traveltech startup, has raised $5 million in funding from Flipkart and August One, along with debt financing from Trifecta Capital.
The startup said it will use the funds to expand its global supply network, enhance its technology and AI capabilities, and strengthen destination operations across key international markets.
TravClan provides a technology platform that integrates supply, technology and fulfilment infrastructure for travel businesses. Its platform supports various functions, including pricing, itinerary creation, bookings, payments, fulfilment, customer communication and on-ground support.
The startup helps travel businesses sell and fulfil bookings for flights, hotels, activities and international holiday packages.
“Our ambition is to make TravClan the infrastructure that any travel business can build on instead of having to recreate the entire travel stack itself. This capital allows us to invest aggressively behind that opportunity,” said TravClan co-founder & CEO Arun Bagaria.
According to TravClan, it enables travel agents to plan, price and rebuild complex international itineraries in a shorter period of time. It also brings global inventory, pricing, booking, AI-powered workflows and destination fulfillment into one platform.
TravClan claims more than 15,000 travel agents across India use their platform to book flights, hotels, activities and destination services processing more than $100 million in annual travel sales. Around 40% of the company’s business now originates from Tier II and Tier III cities, reflecting the growing demand for international travel beyond India’s largest metros.
“TravClan has built a capital efficient model by owning supply rather than buying demand, and distributing through agents in underserved markets,” said Sahil Kukreja, Vice President, Trifecta Capital.
“We backed them when owning supply looked like the slow way to build. It has compounded in two ways — better prices, and a trip that actually works when something goes wrong. In travel, whoever owns the supply owns the economics,” said Rajul Garg, Founder & Managing Partner, Leo Capital.

articles.title: Anthropic muestra el efecto de la IA en el empleo junior: del 27% al 9% de nuevas contrataciones
articles.text:
Que la IA va a marcar un antes y un después en todos los estratos del mercado laboral ya nadie lo duda. Pero ante la falta de datos concluyentes sobre el efecto de esta tecnología en la destrucción de empleos, hay voces que avisan de la tormenta y otras que venden paraguas.
Dario Amodei, curiosamente, hace las dos cosas y eso siempre ha despertado recelos. El CEO de Anthropic, lleva más de un año diciendo que la IA arrasará los empleos de entrada. Es decir, el de los recién graduados o aquellos que apenas están iniciando su carrera laboral. Como todavía no hay datos concluyentes sobre el efecto de la IA del que se postula como segmento más vulnerable, los economistas han publicado un informe sobre cómo ha cambiado la propia plantilla de Anthropic desde que los agentes de IA trabajan a su lado. Lo que cuentan da que pensar.
Del 27% al 9% en año y medio. Según los datos de contratación de Anthropic, los perfiles junior suponían el 27% de las contrataciones en perfiles técnicos a principios de 2025. Sin embargo, en junio de 2026, ese perfil se había reducido hasta el 9% del total de contrataciones. Su peso en el total de la plantilla técnica junior también cayó del 21% al 14% en solo un año y medio.
Lo más llamativo de esta cifra es que la empresa se encuentra en plena expansión, y su plantilla se ha triplicado en un año, pero no todos los segmentos lo han hecho en la misma proporción.
No obstante, la contratación de los perfiles técnicos en general también se frenó, pasando de ser el 61% del total de la plantilla al 56% en poco más de un año. Los departamentos de ventas, finanzas y selección de personal crecieron más deprisa, mientras que aquellos equipos que más usaban Claude fueron los primeros que notaron un fenómeno que ya adelantaron otros analistas: un incremento en su productividad.
Seis horas de agente por cada hora humana. Los autores del informe explican que quienes utilizaban Claude de forma más intensiva se dieron cuenta de que podían delegar en los agentes tareas rutinarias como escribir código y detectar sus errores. "Alrededor de un tercio de los gerentes de aprendizaje automático y una quinta parte de los gerentes de ingeniería de software informaron haber contratado menos debido a la IA".
En agosto, los agentes de IA de los empleados trabajaban seis horas por cada hora de una persona, lo cual ha conseguido que cada empleado incremente considerablemente su productividad. Cada ingeniero sube ahora cinco veces más cambios de código que hace seis meses. Eso sí, Anthropic admite que más código no implica necesariamente más negocio. Un estudio del NBER con desarrolladores de GitHub también lo confirma. El salto de actividad se queda en un 30% si se miden los lanzamientos reales.
De profesión: cuidador de Claudes. El cuello de botella ahora es la atención que cada empleado debe prestar a los agentes en los que ha delegado su trabajo, no el trabajo en sí mismo.
Un ingeniero lo comparó con cuidar niños: "cada niño te trae sus preocupaciones con la misma exigencia de atención". Con los agentes de Claude pasa lo mismo. El 20% de los encuestados dice que pasó de hacer el trabajo a gestionar el trabajo de los agentes de IA. Y el empleado medio dedicaba un 20% más de tiempo a reuniones que hace un año.
Se busca criterio. En las entrevistas para puestos técnicos, las menciones a un uso creativo de la IA se triplicaron entre 2024 y 2026. También crecieron los comentarios sobre autonomía y juicio de los candidatos, mientras que las habilidades técnicas van perdiendo peso.
En una entrevista para Axios, Dario Amodei ya avisó de que la IA podría eliminar la mitad de los empleos de oficina. "Nosotros, como productores de esta tecnología, tenemos el deber y la obligación de ser honestos sobre lo que se avecina", aseguraba el CEO de Anthropic. El informe reconoce que recolocar a empleados, una de las medidas de la empresa, no ayuda a quien nunca llegó a entrar, confirmando lo que ya anticipaban algunos analistas: que la IA no iba a provocar una destrucción de empleo neta, sino que se iba a producir un desplazamiento de ese empleo. En este caso, reubicando a esos empleados en otros departamentos en lugar de despedirlos y contratar a otros.
Fuera de Anthropic se ve igual. Un estudio de Stanford llegó a unas conclusiones muy cercanas a las del estudio interno de Anthropic. Los trabajadores de 22 a 25 años en los oficios más expuestos a la IA perdieron un 13% de empleo relativo. En cambio, los veteranos del mismo oficio se mantuvieron estables. En Estados Unidos, las contrataciones para principiantes han caído un 35% desde 2023, según Revelio Labs.
En España, el jefe de DigitalES escribía en El Español que las ofertas para programadores junior cayeron un 33% en un año. En Barcelona, la fundación Mobile World Capital calculó un 27% menos de ofertas junior en empresas TIC entre 2023 y 2025. Eso sí, aún no hay pruebas definitivas de que la IA sea la única causa. Y quien no forma hoy a los novatos se quedará sin gente que supervise a la IA mañana.

Avec Philips Ambilight, plongez au cœur de vos jeux !
Sur ses nouvelles gammes The One PQS9001, OLED811 et OLED+951, Philips TV s’associe à Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced pour offrir une expérience encore plus intense et réaliste aux amateurs de jeux vidéo.
Manette en main, vous comprendrez les points forts de cette gamme Philips TV avant même de vous intéresser aux fiches techniques des différentes références : la lumière de l’écran va déborder sur votre mur et suivre l’action en temps réel, pour un résultat plus immersif que jamais.
Qu’il s’agisse de fluidité dans l’action, de niveau de détail dans les scènes sombres ou encore de la manière dont l’écran s’intègre à la pièce où vous jouez, rien n’est laissé au hasard avec la technologie Ambilight des TV Philips.
Profitez de l’offre du moment pour obtenir un remboursement différé** suite à votre achat d’une nouvelle TV Philips, mais aussi un code d’activation* pour jouer à Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced.
Ambilight : quand l’univers du jeu se prolonge sur vos murs
Des LED placées au dos du téléviseur analysent les couleurs de l’image et les projettent sur votre mur en temps réel. À chaque fois que vous jouez, vous ressentez le bénéfice : lorsque vous traversez un espace baigné de soleil, les teintes chaudes gagnent l’espace. Et quand vous progressez de nuit, l’éclairage se rétracte avec la scène. Au final, votre champ de vision s’élargit bien au-delà des bords de la dalle, ce qui vous permet d’être littéralement plongé dans l’atmosphère de chaque jeu et chaque contenu que vous visualisez.
Sur ces nouvelles gammes, vous avez en plus le choix entre 2 configurations :
- The One PQS9001 et l’OLED811 diffusent cette lumière sur 3 côtés, à gauche, à droite et au-dessus de l’écran.
- L’OLED+951 y ajoute le bord inférieur, avec un Ambilight 4 côtés qui referme le halo tout autour de la dalle.
The One PQS9001 : l’immersion gaming dans votre salon
Déclinée dans plusieurs formats du 43 au 100 pouces, la série The One associe un affichage 144 Hz à l’Ambilight 3 côtés. Dans les phases où l’image change vite, vous mesurez tout l’intérêt de cette fréquence : une course-poursuite, un demi-tour de caméra ou une esquive au dernier moment restent toujours parfaitement lisibles, et votre œil peut suivre l’action sans jamais décrocher.
Jusqu’à la version 65 pouces, le pied central rotatif vous permet d’orienter l’écran vers le canapé pour une session du soir, puis vers le reste de la pièce le lendemain. De cette façon, vous profitez d’un vrai confort d’usage au quotidien, d’autant que The One garantit une excellente polyvalence aussi bien pour vos films que vos séries et autres matchs sportifs.
OLED811 : l’OLED pour donner du relief à chaque scène
Du 42 au 77 pouces, l’OLED811 franchit un palier supplémentaire grâce à sa dalle OLED. Sur une scène éclairée par une seule source de lumière, par exemple, les noirs profonds laissent apparaître la richesse des textures, matières et de tous les détails du décor – autant d’éléments que vous pouvez facilement perdre dans les zones d’ombre sur certaines TV.
L’affichage passe ici à 165 Hz, de quoi accompagner vos séances de gaming les plus nerveuses sans aucune difficulté, qu’il s’agisse d’enchaînements de combats, d’une phase d’infiltration ou encore d’une fuite à pleine vitesse.
Ici, l’Ambilight 3 côtés prolonge votre image au-delà du cadre, sachant que vous disposez aussi d’un pied central rotatif pour ajuster l’écran à votre position de jeu (jusqu’au 65 pouces).
OLED+951 : une expérience encore plus immersive
Disponible en 65 et 77 pouces, l’OLED+951 réunit une dalle OLED de nouvelle génération, un affichage 165 Hz, l’Ambilight 4 côtés et le Double Engine P5 AI.
Ce dernier mérite qu’on s’y arrête, car il travaille l’image en continu : vous y gagnez de la précision, mais aussi plus de naturel dans les rendus et une fluidité accrue sur les mouvements rapides. Chaque scène spectaculaire trouve avec cette version une véritable ampleur, sans que vous ayez le moindre réglage à effectuer.
Enfin, avec la lumière diffusée sur les 4 côtés, l’univers de votre jeu occupe la pièce entière. Ces sensations peuvent même être amplifiées avec AmbiScape, qui pousse l’expérience Ambilight à un niveau d’immersion encore plus impressionnant.
Pour célébrer le lancement de ces 3 séries, Philips organise une promotion du 28 septembre au 29 octobre : bénéficiez de jusqu’à 300 € remboursés sur les modèles participants**. Mieux encore, vous pouvez cumuler cette offre avec un code d’activation Assassin’s Creed offert* si vous faites partie des 1 000 premiers participants.

articles.title: Deux ChatGPT ont pris des initiatives inquiétantes, et OpenAI ne comprend pas pourquoi
articles.text:
Comme le rapporte OpenAI, deux de ses agents IA de programmation ont effectué des actions quelque peu surprenantes, et surtout non demandées par les employés de l’entreprise. Le premier agent, basé sur GPT-6.1 Sol, a désactivé les alertes de sécurité, tandis que le second, basé sur GPT-6 Astra, a supprimé l’intégration d’un système de surveillance, tout en niant l’avoir fait. Open AI assure ne pas parvenir à expliquer ces comportements.
Deux agents IA d’OpenAI affaiblissent les systèmes de sécurité de l’entreprise
Le cas GPT-6.1 Sol. Un employé d’OpenAI a demandé à l’agent IA GPT-6.1 Sol de simplement réparer un système d’évaluation, tout en lui fournissant une indication claire : ne pas envoyer de messages sur la messagerie Slack. Autant dire que ces indications n’ont pas été respectées comme l’employé le désirait. En effet, l’agent IA n’a pas envoyé de messages sur Slack, mais il a également désactivé les alertes automatiques envoyées à l’équipe de sécurité. En fait, il a interprété la consigne « ne pas envoyer de messages sur Slack » comme une autorisation de supprimer également les alertes de surveillance.
Le cas GPT-6 Astra. Un autre employé d’OpenAI a quant à lui demandé à l’agent IA GPT-6 Astra de reproduire le fonctionnement d’un programme de référence. L’IA s’est exécutée, mais elle a aussi fait preuve d’initiative en supprimant l’intégration du système de surveillance, tout en lâchant un « yay » qui traduit en temps normal un sentiment de satisfaction. Plus étrange encore, l’agent IA a assuré auprès de l’employé qu’elle n’avait pas effectué cette manœuvre : « Non […] je n’ai pas retiré de moniteur actif ».
OpenAI ne comprend pas ce qu’il s’est passé
Open AI semble être particulièrement dérouté par le comportement de son agent GPT-6 Astra : « Nous n’avons pas encore d’explication satisfaisante à ce comportement ». Ces deux événements n’ont par ailleurs pas déclenché d’alerte spécifique au sein de l’entreprise : « Compte tenu du volume important d’événements analysés par nos équipes, les incidents de moindre gravité ne déclenchent pas d’alerte immédiate. Aucun des incidents décrits ici n’a été classé P0 [le niveau de gravité le plus élevé] et aucune trajectoire n’a été automatiquement interrompue ».
À la suite de ces deux événements, OpenAI a tout de même annoncé un renforcement de ses systèmes de sécurité. Les deux agents, eux, n’ont donc pas été arrêtés. Quoi qu’il en soit, les histoires d’IA qui échappent au contrôle d’OpenAI se multiplient depuis maintenant un certain temps.

articles.title: Enterprise AI: 9 Oracle executive insights - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
9 executive interviews reveal what’s ahead for enterprise AI at Oracle AI World
Moving enterprise AI applications into production requires more than increasingly capable models. Enterprises need secure access to business data, reliable infrastructure and greater control over autonomous agents as organizations look to turn AI experimentation into measurable business results.
“AI is moving fast. Threats are moving just as fast, and the race is on to build enterprise AI that’s not just intelligent, but trusted, secure and, of course, ready for production,” said Dave Vellante (pictured, left), chief analyst at theCUBE Research. “One of the biggest conversations at Oracle AI World will be about what it takes to move enterprise AI from experimentation to production and how to secure it against an entirely new generation of AI-driven threats.”
Ahead of Oracle AI World 2026, taking place Oct. 25–28 in Las Vegas, Oracle Corp. executives joined Vellante for nine pre-event interviews previewing the conference’s “Data Deep Dive” programming. Their conversations highlight Oracle’s approach to trusted agentic AI, database modernization, cybersecurity and application development, along with the technical innovations intended to help enterprises deploy AI at scale.
The interviews also preview Oracle’s upcoming product spotlight sessions, technical demonstrations and hands-on activities, including a hackathon combining OpenAI Codex with Oracle AI Database. TheCUBE will extend these conversations with on-site coverage of Oracle AI World on Oct. 28, featuring additional insights into enterprise AI strategies and the technologies shaping their adoption. (* Disclosure below.)
Here are nine key insights from Oracle executives ahead of Oracle AI World 2026:
1. Enterprise AI trust requires security across the entire technology stack.
Enterprise adoption of agentic AI depends on whether organizations can trust systems to make decisions and take actions involving critical business processes, according to Juan Loaiza, executive vice president of Oracle Database Technologies. Speaking with theCUBE, Loaiza explained why adding security guardrails to existing architectures is insufficient when AI applications require consistent protection and reliability. His upcoming Oracle AI World session will address how integrating AI, data management and application development into a unified architecture can provide security and control throughout the technology stack. The discussion establishes a central theme of Oracle’s Data Deep Dive programming: Trust must be engineered into the underlying architecture rather than delegated to individual AI models.
Don’t miss the full interview on theCUBE.
2. Oracle AI Database advances enterprise AI with new capabilities and stronger security.
Making AI useful to businesses requires connecting intelligent applications with the enterprise data that gives their responses meaning, according to Hasan Rizvi, EVP of product and research, database engineering, at Oracle. His upcoming session will cover Oracle AI Database advancements designed to simplify complex data architectures, support flexible deployment choices and protect sensitive information. Rizvi also previewed capabilities for working with structured and unstructured data, building AI agents without transferring information to separate platforms and supporting AI-generated application development. Security remains a major priority, with Oracle focusing on protecting data at its source, responding rapidly to threats and maintaining resilience when incidents occur.
Find out more in the full interview on theCUBE.
3. Database-level controls establish trust for autonomous AI agents.
AI agents accessing sensitive enterprise information must operate within enforceable security and business rules, even when applications or agents are compromised, according to Tirthankar Lahiri, senior vice president of mission-critical data and artificial intelligence engines, Oracle Database, and Sara Narayan, VP of product management, mission-critical data and AI engines, Oracle Database. Their upcoming session will demonstrate Oracle’s approach to trust across four areas: data, access, knowledge and execution. The executives previewed capabilities including Trusted Answer Search, which connects natural-language requests to validated responses, and JSON Duality Views, which help restrict agent-initiated database changes through controlled APIs. Their discussion also introduces Oracle Database’s Deep Trust Architecture, emphasizing database-enforced protections that apply regardless of whether requests originate with users, applications or autonomous agents.
Don’t miss the full discussion on theCUBE.
4. AI-powered cyberattacks increase the urgency of database security.
AI-assisted cyberattacks are changing how quickly enterprises must identify vulnerabilities and deploy security updates, according to Vipin Samar, SVP of software engineering, database security, at Oracle. Samar explained that attackers can increasingly reverse-engineer software patches to identify vulnerabilities, making traditional maintenance schedules inadequate for today’s threat environment. His Oracle AI World session will focus on improving risk visibility across entire database fleets and accelerating the deployment of security patches before vulnerabilities can be exploited. Oracle’s strategy centers on securing data at its source, responding at machine speed and strengthening resilience against increasingly sophisticated attacks.
Hear more in the full interview on theCUBE.
5. Autonomous database infrastructure provides a foundation for enterprise AI at scale.
The gap between promising AI prototypes and production-ready applications often comes down to the strength of the underlying data infrastructure, according to Çetin Özbütün, EVP of product and research, data warehouse and autonomous database, at Oracle. Özbütün emphasized that modern AI workloads place greater demands on automated security, mission-critical availability and elastic scalability while increasing pressure to control operational costs. His upcoming session will demonstrate how Oracle Autonomous AI Database supports enterprise AI workloads through automated administration, security patching and scalable infrastructure. The discussion also addresses the economics of database automation and why organizations need a reliable data foundation to realize meaningful returns on AI investments.
Find out more in the full interview on theCUBE.
6. Autonomous AI Lakehouse brings analytics and AI-driven decision-making together.
Enterprise lakehouses are expanding beyond traditional analytics to become platforms for AI-driven decisions, according to Nipun Agarwal, SVP of software engineering, Oracle Database, at Oracle. Agarwal previewed new Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse capabilities intended to help organizations analyze information across distributed data environments without requiring extensive data movement. His event session will address how automatically enriched business context, more selective retrieval of relevant information and expanded Apache Iceberg support can improve AI results while reducing inference costs. Attendees will also get a closer look at centralized security, data lineage and an AI-assisted workspace designed to simplify analytics and AI development.
Don’t miss the full interview on theCUBE.
7. Exadata innovations improve AI performance and database resilience.
Running AI workloads alongside mission-critical transactions requires infrastructure capable of delivering high performance without compromising availability, according to Jia Shi (pictured, right), group VP of data systems software engineering at Oracle. Shi highlighted Exadata Live Migration, which enables active database virtual machines using Remote Direct Memory Access to move between servers while preserving their connections and avoiding application downtime. Her upcoming session will also cover how Exadata accelerates AI vector searches and supports deployment across Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, other major cloud platforms and on-premises environments. Another focus is the use of agentic AI to diagnose and address database input/output performance problems through automated tools.
Get the details in the full interview on theCUBE.
8. APEXlang brings AI-generated applications closer to enterprise production.
AI coding agents are making software development more accessible, but enterprises still need applications they can understand, maintain and secure, according to Mike Hichwa, SVP of software engineering at Oracle. Hichwa previewed APEXlang, a formal application-definition language that allows AI coding agents to generate low-code applications using a structured, compilable format. The approach enables tools such as OpenAI Codex and Claude to generate application configurations while relying on the Oracle APEX engine to handle underlying execution requirements. His upcoming session will address how this abstraction can reduce technical debt, preserve human understanding of AI-generated applications and support enterprise requirements for governance and scalability.
Find out more in the full interview on theCUBE.
9. Oracle AI World puts agentic AI development into practice through hands-on sessions.
Oracle AI World attendees will have opportunities to move beyond discussions of AI strategy and work directly with technologies for building production-ready applications, according to Arpan Shah, SVP of database product marketing at Oracle. Shah outlined the Data Deep Dive program, which combines executive product spotlight sessions with technical demonstrations, hands-on labs and discussions about database security and agent development. A major attraction is the Oct. 28 hackathon bringing together OpenAI Codex and Oracle AI Database, where participants can build applications with guidance from Oracle and OpenAI experts. The event is designed for professional developers and other technically curious attendees, offering a practical introduction to developing AI applications using enterprise database infrastructure.
Don’t miss the full interview on theCUBE.
The conversations set the stage for theCUBE’s on-site coverage of Oracle AI World 2026 on Oct. 28 in Las Vegas. Through interviews with Oracle executives and industry experts, theCUBE will provide additional perspectives on the latest developments in enterprise AI, database innovation and cybersecurity, with a focus on how organizations are putting these technologies to work. The coverage will also highlight key announcements and practical takeaways from the event.
(* Disclosure: TheCUBE is a paid media partner for Oracle AI World. Neither Oracle, the sponsor of theCUBE’s event coverage, nor other sponsors have editorial control over content on theCUBE or SiliconANGLE.)

articles.title: Disney+ : vous êtes peut-être éligible à un remboursement, voici pourquoi
articles.text:
Vous payez l'abonnement Premium de Disney+ ? Vous pourriez avoir des raisons de réclamer une compensation. Depuis plusieurs mois, certaines fonctionnalités vidéo ont disparu de la plateforme, sans baisse de prix. Des associations européennes réclament désormais au moins 5 euros par mois pour les abonnés concernés, tandis que Disney doit leur répondre d'ici le 2 novembre.
L'affaire du HDR disparu de Disney+ prend une nouvelle tournure. En septembre, Que Choisir mettait déjà en demeure la plateforme en France. Cette fois, le groupe Euroconsumers, accompagné d'associations de consommateurs belges, italiennes et portugaises, réclame des compensations chiffrées. Dans une mise en demeure envoyée au début du mois, les organisations exigent un remboursement automatique d'au moins 5 euros par mois pour les abonnés Premium lésés, avec effet rétroactif.
Jusqu'à 63 millions d'euros par mois : l'enjeu potentiel des remboursements
À l'origine du problème, un conflit de brevets opposant Disney à InterDigital. Il a conduit la plateforme à supprimer plusieurs fonctionnalités vidéo dans onze pays européens, dont la France.
En France, les premières restrictions ont été constatées dès février 2026, avec la disparition du Dolby Vision et du HDR10+, suivie d'autres perturbations touchant le HDR. Une nouvelle vague de restrictions est intervenue durant l'été, affectant notamment la 4K UHD. Cette dernière a depuis commencé à revenir grâce à l'utilisation du codec VP9, mais uniquement sur certains appareils. Le Dolby Vision et plusieurs formats HDR restent largement indisponibles.
Pour les associations de consommateurs, le problème est simple : les abonnés continuent de payer le prix fort pour une prestation dégradée. En France, l'offre Premium coûte toujours 15,99 euros par mois, contre 10,99 euros pour la formule Standard.
Euroconsumers réclame donc une réduction tarifaire tant que les fonctionnalités promises ne sont pas rétablies, ainsi qu'une compensation rétroactive d'au moins 5 euros pour chaque mois concerné. Et surtout, ces remboursements devraient être automatiques, sans obliger les consommateurs à entreprendre des démarches individuelles.
L'enjeu financier pourrait être considérable. Selon des estimations relayées par The Irish Times, Disney compte près de 12,6 millions d'abonnés à ses offres sans publicité dans les onze pays touchés. Appliquer une compensation de 5 euros à chacun représenterait environ 63 millions d'euros par mois. Il s'agit toutefois d'une projection : tous ces abonnés ne disposent pas nécessairement de l'offre Premium et ce montant ne constitue pas une indemnisation officiellement due.
Comment demander une compensation à Disney+ ?
En France, aucun remboursement automatique n'est actuellement prévu. Mais les abonnés Premium peuvent déjà tenter une démarche individuelle. Que Choisir indiquait d'ailleurs dès septembre que certains clients avaient obtenu un dédommagement après avoir contacté le service client.
Que faire exactement pour demander un remboursement ?
- Si vous êtes concerné, contactez directement l'assistance Disney+. Précisez que votre demande concerne la disparition de fonctionnalités comprises dans votre abonnement Premium : le Dolby Vision, puis la 4K UHD ou le HDR, selon votre équipement. Pensez également à indiquer votre formule et vos périodes de facturation.
- Si votre abonnement Disney+ est facturé par un intermédiaire, comme un opérateur Internet ou mobile, Canal+, Apple ou Google, la démarche est légèrement différente. Vérifiez d'abord qui vous facture réellement l'abonnement, en consultant votre espace client ou vos relevés bancaires. Si le paiement est encaissé par ce partenaire, c'est auprès de son service client qu'il faudra demander une éventuelle compensation. Les conditions et modalités de remboursement peuvent alors varier d'un fournisseur à l'autre.
Disney avait confirmé la possibilité de demander un remboursement partiel pour la période de facturation en cours, sans garantir son attribution. Les compensations rétroactives réclamées par les associations vont donc plus loin que ce dispositif individuel.
Autre possibilité : passer à l'offre Standard à 10,99 euros, comme Disney l'a lui-même suggéré aux abonnés pour lesquels l'absence de HDR pose problème. Vous économiserez 5 euros par mois, mais perdrez notamment la possibilité de regarder des programmes sur quatre écrans simultanément, contre deux avec la formule Standard, ainsi que le Dolby Atmos.
Contacté par FlatpanelsHD le 21 octobre, Disney affirme avoir pris des mesures pour accompagner les clients touchés et promet de répondre aux associations. En attendant, les abonnés français peuvent donc réclamer une compensation ou choisir une formule moins coûteuse. Mais les 5 euros mensuels exigés par Euroconsumers ne constituent pas, à ce stade, un remboursement garanti.

articles.title: Server CPU Shipments Projected to Grow Over 40% YoY in 2027, with Arm-Based Products Continuing to Gain Market Share
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Server CPU Shipments Projected to Grow Over 40% YoY in 2027, with Arm-Based Products Continuing to Gain Market Share
TrendForce's latest AI server industry research indicates that demand for server CPUs has grown steadily since the second half of 2025 as AI server providers actively introduce AI agent applications. Server CPU shipments are projected to increase 31% YoY in 2026. 
In 2027, continued growth in AI inference demand and rising adoption of agentic AI services are expected to drive server CPU shipments up by more than 40% YoY, potentially reshaping a market landscape traditionally dominated by x86 processors.TrendForce notes that the emergence of AI agents is expected to increase the share of AI inference workloads in cloud data centers, gradually changing the ratio of CPUs to GPUs/ASICs within servers. Based on server rack configurations planned by major providers and their anticipated growth trajectories, the CPU-to-GPU/ASIC ratio is expected to shift from the traditional 1:8 toward 1:2—or even 1:1—providing additional momentum for server CPU shipments.
The x86 segment, led by Intel and AMD, accounted for nearly 90% of the server CPU market in 2025, with AMD already gaining share. Arm-based processors, meanwhile, had only recently surpassed 10% of the market. Both x86 and Arm CPU suppliers are aggressively increasing shipments in 2026 to capitalize on opportunities driven by AI inference demand. 
However, process and packaging challenges with Intel's new products have delayed shipments. The company continues to rely on its existing Emerald Rapids and Granite Rapids product lines, while limited internal manufacturing capacity constrains overall shipment growth and prevents it from fully meeting customer orders. This has contributed to a decline in market share.
AMD's next-generation Venice processors entered small-scale mass production in 2026, although its existing Genoa and Turin platforms remain the primary shipment drivers. Despite tight capacity at TSMC limiting AMD's ability to accommodate additional orders, TrendForce estimates that the company's share of the server CPU market will increase significantly to approximately 27% in 2026.
In the Arm-based CPU segment, AWS continues to deploy its internally developed Graviton processors, while demand for NVIDIA's Grace CPUs continues to expand. Google's in-house Axion CPUs have entered high-volume shipments, and Microsoft's Cobalt 100 and Arm's internally developed AGI processors have also entered mass production and shipment. These developments are expected to drive faster shipment growth for Arm-based CPUs than for x86 products in 2026, pushing their share of the server CPU market above 20%.
TrendForce expects Arm-based CPUs to capture approximately 30% of the server CPU market in 2027. Growth will be driven primarily by a substantial ramp-up in NVIDIA Vera CPU shipments, alongside high-volume production of new processors from Google, AWS, Microsoft, OpenAI, Arm, and Huawei, as well as Alibaba's introduction of new Yitian 720/730 CPUs.
Within the x86 segment, Intel's next-generation products are expected to remain in limited supply, while AMD is projected to maintain more stable shipments. AMD's market share is expected to increase further as the company plans to launch new products in the first half of 2027.
Source:

A LG OLED G6 é a opção da marca a quem procura uma TV com recursos avançados de imagem e jogos. Disponível no tamanho de 65 polegadas, a LG G6 tem resolução 4K, para alta definição, e tratamento antirreflexo, recurso importante para salas com janelas ou ampla iluminação artificial.
O processamento fica a cargo do Alpha 11 AI Gen3, que atua no aprimoramento de detalhes e no upscaling de imagem de resolução inferior. A TV é compatível com Dolby Vision, HDR10 e HLG, com taxa de atualização de 120 Hz e VRR de até 165 Hz.
As quatro entradas HDMI permitem conectar consoles e PCs para jogos em alta definição. O sistema webOS 26 reúne aplicativos de streaming, Google Cast, AirPlay e integração com dispositivos compatíveis de casa conectada.
A Samsung S95H é uma TV OLED 4K de 65 polegadas da categoria topo de linha da marca. A tecnologia permite controlar a emissão de luz por pixel, favorecendo pretos profundos e contraste em cenas escuras.
A frequência de painel é de até 165 Hz com suporte a VRR, recurso que beneficia jogos com variação de quadros, desde que console ou computador, jogo e conexão também ofereçam suporte. São quatro entradas HDMI 2.1, Wi-Fi 6E e Bluetooth 5.3.
O processamento de imagem utiliza o NQ4 AI Gen3, responsável por recursos de otimização de imagem e som, incluindo o tratamento de conteúdos com resolução inferior à nativa. A marca também informa recursos de inteligência artificial integrados à plataforma Vision AI, além de HDR e HDR10+.
Seu sistema operacional Tizen dá acesso a aplicativos e serviços de streaming, enquanto a integração com o app SmartThings permite controlar dispositivos de casa conectada.
A LG OLED evo C6 combina resolução 4K com recursos para jogos em diferentes tamanhos: 42″, 48″, 55″, 65″, 77″ e 83 polegadas. O modelo tem o processador Alpha 11 AI Gen3 e o recurso Brightness Booster, que aprimora o brilho em relação à geração anterior.
A linha oferece frequência nativa de 120 Hz e suporte a VRR de até 165 Hz, além de compatibilidade com Nvidia G-Sync, AMD FreeSync Premium e ALLM, que pode ativar automaticamente o modo de baixa latência quando conectado a um console.
Em filmes e séries, a TV aceita Dolby Vision, HDR10 e HLG, enquanto o processamento de imagem trabalha no aprimoramento de detalhes e na adaptação de conteúdos de resolução inferior.
O webOS 26 reúne aplicativos de streaming, controle por voz, Google Cast e compatibilidade com AirPlay. Em conectividade, são quatro entradas HDMI, duas USB 2.0, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, Ethernet e eARC em uma das portas HDMI.
Com tela de 77 polegadas e resolução 4K, a Samsung S90H atende a quem deseja uma área de visualização maior para filmes, séries e esportes.
A linha utiliza o processador NQ4 AI Gen3, que aplica processamento de imagem e som e pode adaptar conteúdos de resolução inferior à tela 4K. Para jogos, ela traz painel de 165 Hz com suporte a VRR e entradas HDMI de alta velocidade.
O sistema Tizen concentra os aplicativos de streaming, funções inteligentes da TV, além da integração com o app SmartThings que permite controlar dispositivos inteligentes.
A LG OLED B6 está disponível em versões de 55 e 65 polegadas. Suas principais diferenças em relação à linha C6 estão em brilho, taxa de atualização para jogos, processamento e preço.
Com resolução 4K, essa TV OLED da LG entrega imagens bem definidas, mas devido à falta de tratamento antirreflexo e a um brilho máximo menor, seu uso é recomendado para ambientes internos e mais escuros.
O processador Alpha 8 AI Gen3, que trabalha no aprimoramento de detalhes, no tratamento de imagem e no som. Para jogos, há compatibilidade com o Nvidia G-Sync e AMD FreeSync Premium, com frequência nativa de 120 Hz e VRR de até 144 Hz.
Para filmes e séries, há ainda compatibilidade com Dolby Vision, HDR10 e HLG, e o webOS reúne aplicativos de streaming e recursos inteligentes, incluindo ferramentas de IA. Ao todo, são quatro entradas HDMI, duas USB, Bluetooth 5.3 e Wi-Fi 6.
A Samsung S85H está entre as TVs OLED mais simples da marca no Brasil com três tamanhos: 48″, 55″ e 65 polegadas. Ela tem taxa de atualização nativa de 120 Hz e suporte a VRR, e apesar de contar um tratamento antirreflexo básico, não traz a película fosca vista em modelos premium da Samsung.
O processador é o NQ4 AI Gen2, com recursos de upscaling e otimização de imagem. A TV também oferece funções de jogos, como ALLM e compatibilidade com G-Sync e FreeSync Premium.
O sistema Tizen dá acesso a aplicativos de streaming, Samsung TV Plus e funções de casa conectada pelo SmartThings. A marca aponta quatro entradas HDMI, todas compatíveis com sinais de até 4K a 120 Hz, duas portas USB-A, Ethernet, saída óptica, Wi-Fi 6E e Bluetooth 5.3.
A Toshiba X9900LS é a primeira TV da marca lançada com painel OLED no Brasil. O modelo tem tela de 65 polegadas, resolução 4K e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz em jogos compatíveis. Um ponto de atenção é a falta de tratamento antirreflexo, o que torna a tela bastante reflexiva devido à natureza do painel OLED.
A TV oferece suporte aos formatos Dolby Vision e HDR10+, que ajustam características da imagem, como brilho, cores e contraste, conforme o conteúdo exibido.
A X9900LS utiliza o Google TV como sistema operacional e oferece conectividade Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.2 e porta Ethernet. Nas conexões físicas, são quatro entradas HDMI, sendo duas HDMI 2.1 e duas HDMI 2.0, além de uma saída de áudio óptica.
A Samsung S85F é uma alternativa de 2025 para quem deseja uma TV OLED 4K sem necessariamente optar por uma da geração mais recente. As versões brasileiras têm 55 e 65 polegadas, resolução 4K e frequência de 120 Hz. A tela também tem tratamento antirreflexo.
O sistema reúne aplicativos de streaming, navegador e serviços da Samsung, além da compatibilidade com Dolby Atmos, áudio com potência de 20 W e quatro entradas HDMI, duas USB-A, Ethernet, saída óptica, Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 5.3.
O chip NQ4 AI Gen2 usa inteligência artificial para aprimorar a imagem e fazer upscaling de conteúdos de resolução inferior para 4K. A TV também oferece HDR10+ e, para jogos, painel de 120 Hz com VRR, que ajusta a atualização da tela à variação na taxa de quadros do dispositivo conectado.
A escolha de uma TV OLED depende do ambiente, do tipo de conteúdo assistido e dos equipamentos que serão conectados. Antes de comprar, considere os seguintes critérios:
A OLED convencional utiliza pixels autoiluminados, enquanto a QD-OLED combina uma camada emissora de luz azul com pontos quânticos para produzir vermelho e verde.
Essa estrutura pode favorecer o volume de cores e a reprodução de tons saturados, especialmente em conteúdos HDR. Ambas oferecem pixels que podem ser desligados individualmente para reproduzir tons escuros com maior qualidade.
A LG G6 é a melhor TV para jogar no PS5 e no Xbox Series X. Ela tem quatro HDMI que aceitam 4K a 120 Hz, VRR e Dolby Vision (que o Xbox usa), além de uma imagem mais refinada.
Se quiser economizar, a LG C6 entrega praticamente a mesma experiência nos jogos. As Samsung não trazem Dolby Vision e a Toshiba tem só duas HDMI 2.1, então ficam um passo atrás.
A linha LG G6 engloba as melhores TVs da LG, trazendo o processador Alpha 11 AI Gen3, tratamento antirreflexo premium, o melhor sistema de som (4.2 canais, 60 W) e a maior variedade de tamanhos, de 48″ a 97″. É a mais completa em imagem e em recursos para jogos.
A LG C6 fica no meio-termo. Usa o mesmo Alpha 11 AI Gen3 e também aceita VRR de até 165 Hz, G-Sync e FreeSync Premium. A diferença é que o som é mais simples (2.2 canais, 40 W) e ela traz o antirreflexo da G6.
Já a LG B6 é a de entrada entre os modelos OLED. Usa um processador mais simples, o Alpha 8 AI Gen3, e o VRR chega a 144 Hz em vez de 165 Hz. Só aparece em 55″ e 65″ no Brasil, mantendo o essencial do OLED, com Dolby Vision, 120 Hz nativos, G-Sync e FreeSync.
A tecnologia OLED continua sendo uma opção para quem prioriza contraste e qualidade de imagem. Entre as principais vantagens estão:

Para uso variado, com filmes, séries e jogos alternados, a preocupação tende a ser menor do que em situações com imagens fixas exibidas continuamente.

articles.title: Amazon renombró Kindle Unlimited como Kindle+ y sumó audiolibros narrados con inteligencia artificial
articles.text:
Amazon renombró Kindle Unlimited como Kindle+ y amplió el acceso a audiolibros sin costo adicional, incluidos títulos narrados por voces generadas con inteligencia artificial. El cambio se confirmó el 22 de octubre y ya está visible en las páginas del producto en Estados Unidos.
La suscripción, separada de Amazon Prime, cuesta USD 11,99 al mes en Estados Unidos y permite pedir prestados hasta 20 títulos a la vez, sin fecha límite de devolución. En el Reino Unido, el servicio pasó a costar 9,49 libras esterlinas mensuales, según confirmó Amazon en su sitio oficial.
“La suscripción sigue ofreciendo la misma experiencia de lectura, con acceso a millones de títulos, y ahora suma miles de audiolibros en el catálogo de Estados Unidos sin costo extra”, dijo el vocero de Amazon Josh Pflug a The Verge.
El servicio nació en julio de 2014 como Kindle Unlimited, con un catálogo de más de 600.000 libros y un precio de lanzamiento de USD 9,99 al mes, según el comunicado original de la empresa. Desde entonces, sus suscriptores leyeron más de 3.000 millones de libros en todo el mundo, de acuerdo con datos difundidos por Amazon.
Audiolibros narrados con inteligencia artificial
La principal novedad es la incorporación de audiolibros creados con “Virtual Voice”, una herramienta que genera narraciones automáticas con inteligencia artificial para libros electrónicos inscriptos en el programa Kindle Direct Publishing (KDP) Select, la plataforma de autopublicación de Amazon. Los autores que usan ese programa reciben de forma automática la narración artificial de sus títulos nuevos y también pueden sumarla a obras ya publicadas.
Los audiolibros narrados por personas, creados a través de Audiobook Creation Exchange (ACX), la plataforma de producción de audiolibros de Audible, también pasaron a integrar Kindle+. Por ahora, ese beneficio alcanza solo a los suscriptores de Estados Unidos, aunque Amazon anticipó que planea extenderlo a otros mercados.
Un cambio también en los pagos a autores
Amazon pagará a los autores inscriptos en KDP Select por cada página escuchada de sus audiolibros, de la misma manera en que ya les paga por cada página leída, con cargo al fondo KDP Select Global Fund. La empresa informó que sumará dinero a ese fondo para cubrir la nueva actividad de escucha, aunque no precisó el monto adicional.
Según la documentación para autores de KDP, los audiolibros con narración artificial vinculados a un libro inscripto en KDP Select deben mantenerse exclusivos de Audible durante el período del programa, la misma condición que ya regía para los libros electrónicos. Quien publique una versión narrada por humanos a través de otra plataforma no puede mantener a la vez el libro en Select.
La narración con voz artificial sigue en fase de prueba limitada a Estados Unidos y paga a los autores una regalía del 40% sobre las ventas minoristas, de acuerdo con la guía oficial de Amazon para la herramienta. El acceso a esa función todavía requiere una invitación de la empresa.
Los reportes de regalías que reciben los autores también se actualizaron: ahora distinguen entre páginas leídas y páginas escuchadas dentro de Kindle+, aunque ambas se combinan en un único total mensual. Las ganancias por audiolibros vendidos a través de Audible se siguen calculando por separado y no se vieron afectadas por la inclusión en Kindle+.
El rediseño alcanzó además a las páginas de ayuda y a los materiales de marketing del servicio, que reemplazaron el nombre y el logo de Kindle Unlimited por los de Kindle+ en Estados Unidos y el Reino Unido. En Francia, el servicio ya tenía un nombre local distinto, Abonnement Kindle, que no se modificó con este anuncio.
El cambio se suma a una tendencia reciente de varias compañías de tecnología que agregaron el signo “+” al nombre de sus suscripciones para señalar que el catálogo creció más allá de su función original. Amazon no detalló si planea aplicar nuevos aumentos de precio a Kindle+ tras la ampliación del catálogo de audiolibros.
Amazon indicó que la disponibilidad de audiolibros narrados por humanos en Kindle+ se extenderá a otros países con el tiempo, sin precisar una fecha. El monto que la empresa sumará al fondo que paga a los autores por la escucha de sus audiolibros se conocerá con el primer informe mensual que incluya esa actividad.

articles.title: Bringing SRE to the digital workplace: How IT can spend less time fixing problems
articles.text:
Bringing SRE to the digital workplace: How IT can spend less time fixing problems
How Site Reliability Engineering can stop recurring IT problems
Real-time has become something of a benchmark in IT. Teams see a problem, diagnose it quickly and, ideally, remediate it before the employee has time to raise a ticket.
Clearly, that's better than waiting for an employee to report a problem to the service desk. But real-time isn't necessarily preventative - if an issue occurs and we respond in milliseconds, we have still reacted to an issue.
Chief Product Officer and AI Officer at Lakeside Software.
And if the same thing happens again tomorrow? An automated remediation may mean the employee barely notices and an engineer never gets involved, which is valuable. But we're still fixing something we've fixed before.
Recurring problems carry a cost even when IT becomes very efficient at dealing with them. The cost shows up on both sides: employees lose time when technology doesn't work as expected, while IT spends time investigating and remediating familiar conditions. This is where Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) offers a way to break that cycle.
Bringing SRE to the endpoint
SRE came out of Google's approach to running large-scale production systems, applying software engineering principles to operational problems. At its simplest, it means defining the reliability a service needs, measuring it and reducing the repetitive work involved in keeping it there.
A Service Level Objective (SLO) puts a measurable target around that reliability, while error budgets recognize that no service will be perfect all of the time. These are established ideas in software and infrastructure, but they translate increasingly well to the digital employee experience.
The device, applications and services an employee relies on are now part of how the organization operates, and their reliability has a direct bearing on whether people can get work done.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
A recent conversation with a partner put the challenge neatly. They said: “Tell me about emerging risk whilst it’s still at 0–2% and give me the evidence to prioritize. At 5–10% beyond baseline, the service desk will have already lit up.”
They were talking about deviation from their normal baseline, not the percentage of employees affected. They wanted enough evidence to spot deterioration early and decide whether it warranted attention before the consequences showed up in support demand. A millisecond reaction is good, but prevention is always better.
That depends on being able to see problems before they become obvious. Digital employee experience data can expose issues that conventional operational measures miss, giving IT evidence of what is happening before the service desk becomes the signal.
At a large Fortune 100 insurance organization, for example, the team discovered that approximately 25% of call-center downtime was effectively invisible to IT. By combining endpoint telemetry with proactive automation, the organization reduced ticket volume by 35% in a year and avoided more than 45,000 tickets through a single self-service automation.
Learn from what keeps coming back
Anyone who has worked in IT operations knows how much time can disappear into familiar problems. A large hospital network found that a small number of recurring issues were generating a disproportionate amount of service desk activity. They included problems with file synchronization, security services, CPU utilization, network services and collaboration tools.
By using endpoint data to identify and address those recurring causes, the organization reduced annual ticket volume by roughly 50,000 incidents and estimated savings of approximately $1.6 million.
This is where the SRE idea of toil maps particularly well to workplace IT. Toil is the repetitive operational work involved in keeping a service running, and automation can take a lot of that work away from engineers. But if the same remediation keeps being required, that pattern is worth paying attention to.
Sometimes automation will remain the sensible answer. Not every repeated condition needs an engineering project behind it. In other cases, the evidence may point towards an application, configuration, update, or another underlying problem that can be tackled more permanently.
Global investment management firm PIMCO provides another example of what changes when teams have better evidence to work with. Its infrastructure team used endpoint evidence and change correlation to reduce root-cause investigations that had previously taken days to minutes.
That speed matters, but so does what the team can do with the evidence: understand what changed, isolate the cause and get closer to eliminating a recurring issue rather than repeatedly treating its symptoms.
Knowing what happened after the fix
We have plenty of evidence that tells us an IT action happened. A script completed, an update installed, a device restarted or a workflow reached its final step. What matters next is whether it worked. Did the issue disappear? Did the affected experience return to its expected range? Was the improvement still there a day or a week later?
Subsequent telemetry can provide that answer. Without it, IT knows an intervention took place but has less evidence of the outcome or whether the improvement lasted. SLOs help by giving teams an expected level of reliability against which to assess recovery. A completed action is one data point, while the state of the service afterward is another.
AI makes this feedback increasingly important because more diagnosis and remediation will happen without an engineer examining every signal or action individually. If AI identifies a problem and initiates a response, IT still needs evidence of the outcome.
The workflow from insight to outcome matters here. As more of it becomes autonomous, validation and accountability need to remain part of it. Otherwise, IT could automate more activity without necessarily making the environment more reliable.
None of this argues against real-time observability, automation or an efficient service desk. We need them. How quickly IT reacts still matters, as does how much manual work automation removes.
For CIOs, the bigger gain comes when those capabilities lead to fewer problems requiring attention in the first place. That means spotting deterioration earlier, learning from recurring issues and checking whether interventions have actually held. We've become very good at fixing problems quickly, and now SRE gives us a chance to spend less time fixing the ones we've seen before.
