articles.title: 1Password
articles.text:
Have you ever forgotten a password? We all have. Now you don't have to worry about that anymore. With 1Password you only ever need to memorize one password. All your other passwords and important information are protected by your Master Password, which only you know.
Is 1Password trustworthy?
Yes, 1Password is a well known and safe web security application. This password manager allows you to encrypt your passwords and other sensitive data with AES-256 encryption at rest and at transit. For better privacy, you can use two-factor authentication to unlock your vault.
Does 1Password save the database in the cloud?
1Password saves and encrypts a copy of your vault on your local computer first, then this data is sent to 1Password's servers using AES-256 encryption, so you can access it from other devices. It includes 1GB of cloud storage for your vault and sensitive information.
Can I access 1Password from an Android or iOS phone?
Yes, 1Password includes native apps for desktop and mobile operating systems like Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS. You can access your vault and store passwords on an unlimited number of devices.
Is 1Password free?
No, 1Password includes a 14-day trial, after that a paid 1Password plan must be purchased in order to continue using it. 1Password plans start at $2.99 per month with unlimited password storing and 1GB of cloud storage for saving sensitive documents.
Which are the best 1Password alternatives?
Bitwarden and KeePass are great free and open-source password managers. Dashlane and Keeper offer similar plans as 1Password with unlimited device access.
Features
Locked up tight
Your logins and private documents are securely stored in your password vault. This keeps your information locked away from thieves, hackers, and other unsavory types.
At the tip of your fingers
1Password can record your usernames and passwords when you sign in to apps and websites. Our automatic form filler allows you to sign in to your online accounts with a single click, look, or touch.
Keep your secrets safe
Your privacy is our top priority. A combination of policy, innovative thinking, and a deep respect for your right to privacy ensure that your data is always kept safe and secure.
Use 1Password, anywhere
Available for all devices, browsers, and operating systems. 1Password syncs your data seamlessly between devices so you always have your passwords with you.
Check for breaches
Watchtower keeps track of password breaches and other security problems so you can keep your accounts safe. It checks for weak, compromised, or duplicated passwords and lets you know which sites are missing two-factor authentication or using unsecured HTTP.
What's New
Windows version updated to 8.12.42
Give personal AI agents access without giving them your passwords
Personal AI agents should work for you without taking over your digital life. As agents become increasingly capable of automating tasks, prototyping apps, and making work and personal projects easier, control and convenience should go hand in hand. Today we are announcing the 1Password for Agents platform, which helps agents work while keeping the credentials they need secure and making access something every user can see, approve, and manage.
Planning a great event can be rewarding, but organizing one while juggling the rest of your responsibilities is not. Now you can ask an agent to handle the preparations, coordinate dates, and create and send invites, while you design an unforgettable experience.
The degree of usefulness of your agent depends on its ability to log in to the accounts and accomplish all of the tasks you've given it. When an agent reaches a sign-in page, the agent stops and asks for the credential that would allow it to sign in on your behalf. When this happens, you face a choice. You could take control of the agent session and manually enter your username and password into the website each time, which is slow and tedious. You could paste your password into a prompt, which means allowing the agent to have access to your credential, potentially beyond the task at hand. Neither of those are acceptable.
Now, with 1Password for Agents, your agent can request to use a credential from your vault, and if you approve the request, 1Password directly auto-fills the credentials in the destination site so the agent doesn't have access to the credentials.
1Password is the best option for keeping your agents working without letting them see your passwords. You control what agents access and when, all the way from the prompt to the party.
1Password for Agents secures sign-ins for personal AI agents
1Password for Agents makes secure sign-in standard for the personal AI agents people use today. With integrations for Muse, from Meta, Anthropic's Claude Duet, OpenAI ChatGPT Work and dots, SpaceXSI Grok Bot, and Town Townie, 1Password lets you choose the right agents for any task without handing over your credentials or managing passwords across multiple systems. Additional integrations with Instinct, Browserbase, Browser Use, Dana, KERNEL, Perplexity, Ramp, Tomo, and Wajo are coming soon.
1Password's integration with each agent unlocks that agent's potential in unique ways.
- Muse – integrations rolling out over the coming days across all platforms – turns goals into action plans and keeps working as circumstances change, requesting logins from 1Password when using the integration, so people stay in charge of what Muse can reach.
- Anthropic's Claude Duet – integrations coming soon – works inside the tools teams already use to proactively get work done on their behalf. The 1Password integration gives Claude approved access when needed, so users can accomplish tasks without handing over their passwords.
- OpenAI ChatGPT Work and dots – integrations coming soon – work with 1Password to sign into sites across the interest to help users get things done. Users approve sign-ins, and the passwords aren't exposed to the AI model.
- SpaceXSI Grok Bot – integrations rolling out over the coming days across all platforms – provides AI teammates that work across tools, inboxes, and websites. With 1Password, Grok Bot can use approved logins while credentials stay protected, helping you automate routine work more safely.
- Town Townie – web and iOS integrations coming soon – gives every user a Townie, an assistant that learns their people, projects, and voice from their email, calendar, and work tools. It drafts, schedules, and follows up for them, and works with teammates' Townies when a job involves other people. With 1Password, employees approve the logins a Townie needs and 1Password fills them in, so the Townie can keep working without ever seeing the password.
With 1Password for Agents, when an agent reaches a login, the agent app prompts you for the credential it needs from 1Password to continue. Review the requested credential and approve it in 1Password, all without exposing your password or one-time code to the agent.
1Password is the standard for trusting AI agents with passwords, secrets, and credentials. For anyone building a personal agent, 1Password gives users a seamless, secure way to approve sign-ins when an agent reaches a login prompt. You build the agent, 1Password secures the sign-in.
Release Notes:
- If you sign in with Unlock with SSO, you can now export your 1Password data when your administrator allows exports.
- 1Password Environments now support up to 25 local .env file destinations per computer.
- In 1Password Environments, you'll now be taken back to the Environments overview screen after you add an environment variable or import a .env file.
- When you try to delete a workload from a 1Password Environment, the Delete button is now always available. If the name you enter doesn't match the workload's name, you'll see an error.
- We've updated the phrasing and layout of the prompt for approving apps or AI agents to use credentials in 1Password, clarifying what's being used and how your credentials are protected.
- We've fixed an issue where you could sometimes see biometric unlock options on the lock screen that weren't available at that time.
- We've fixed a visual issue where every option in the sign-in address dropdown menu would show a checkmark beside it when you were signing in to a 1Password account manually.
- We've fixed an issue where a temporary connection problem could prompt you to set up a recovery code even if you already had one.
- We've fixed an issue where pressing the Home or End keys in the search field would select the first or last result instead of moving the cursor to the start or end of your search.
- We've fixed an issue where you could delete your only working recovery code if you have a 1Password account that signs in with a passkey and you also had an older, inactive recovery code.
- We've fixed an issue where 1Password could show the wrong account or collection when you opened the app after being away for a while.

- 1Password Environments now support up to 25 local .env file destinations per computer.
- In 1Password Environments, you'll now be taken back to the Environments overview screen after you add an environment variable or import a .env file.
- When you try to delete a workload from a 1Password Environment, the Delete button is now always available. If the name you enter doesn't match the workload's name, you'll see an error.
- We've updated the phrasing and layout of the prompt for approving apps or AI agents to use credentials in 1Password, clarifying what's being used and how your credentials are protected.
- We've fixed an issue where you could sometimes see biometric unlock options on the lock screen that weren't available at that time.
- We've fixed a visual issue where every option in the sign-in address dropdown menu would show a checkmark beside it when you were signing in to a 1Password account manually.
- We've fixed an issue where a temporary connection problem could prompt you to set up a recovery code even if you already had one.
- We've fixed an issue where pressing the Home or End keys in the search field would select the first or last result instead of moving the cursor to the start or end of your search.
- We've fixed an issue where you could delete your only working recovery code if you have a 1Password account that signs in with a passkey and you also had an older, inactive recovery code.
- We've fixed an issue where 1Password could fail to start if a damaged local cache couldn't be removed.
- We've fixed an issue where 1Password could show the wrong account or collection when you opened the app after being away for a while.
Android version updated to 8.10.32
Starting today, you can save and sign in with passkeys using the desktop version of 1Password in the browser, as well as your iOS and iPadOS devices. You can also use 1Password on any device to view, organize, and share your saved passkeys.
It's the most convenient and complete passkey experience.
There's no better time to get started with Google, Nintendo, GitHub, and others turning on capabilities for passkeys this summer.
Visit our online passkey directory or open Watchtower in 1Password to discover which of your logins can be upgraded with a passkey.
Passkeys are here
Need a refresher on what passkeys are, and how they work? No problem. Passkeys are the future of account security and how we protect our private data. And they're here to stay.
You can use passkeys to sign in to compatible websites and apps without entering a password. No magic links. No two-factor authentication codes. Just passwordless bliss.
Passkeys are secure, convenient to use, and backed by the largest companies in the world. Here are just a few reasons why you should start using passkeys in 1Password:
Signing in with passkeys is quick and hassle-free. You don't have to memorize or type out anything when you sign in with a passkey. Find the login page or button and, if prompted, choose the passkey option. 1Password will then handle the rest.
Passkeys are secure. Unlike passwords, every passkey has two parts: a public key and private key. The private key isn't shared with the service you're signing in to. That's why passkeys are resistant to phishing and can't be stolen in data breaches.
You can sync your passkeys between devices. Passkeys are synced just like any other item saved in your password manager. You can access them on any device and any major web browser, and organize them using tags and vaults.
Save and sign in using passkeys in the browser
Ready to start using passkeys? Download the 1Password extension for one of the following browsers:
- Chrome (macOS, Windows, and Linux)
- Edge (macOS, Windows, and Linux)
- Brave (macOS, Windows, and Linux)
- Safari (macOS, iOS, and iPadOS)
- Firefox (the ability to save and sign in with passkeys is coming soon)
Next, find a site that supports passkeys. You can do this by browsing our passkey directory, or by opening Watchtower in 1Password, which now flags all of your existing logins that could be updated with a passkey.
Locate the site's sign in page or button and follow the prompts to create a passkey. 1Password will ask which account and vault you'd like to save it in.
Previous Release Notes:
I'm so excited to share 1Password 8 for Windows with you today. We went back to the drawing board and recreated every bit and every pixel to bring you the most modern, productive, and secure version of 1Password yet!
Before jumping in, if Dark Mode is your jam, hop on over to our 1Password 8 for Windows: Dark Mode Edition announcement post to see every screenshot in glorious dark mode. That's right, 1Password 8 fully supports dark mode!
Modern Design
- We set out to create a modern, first-class experience that feels right at home on Windows 11. To make this possible we created an entirely new 1Password design language, code-named Knox.
- Let's open things up to see the beautiful design in its full glory.
- Despite its simplicity, 1Password 8 is packed with features to help you organize your digital life. Create vaults directly from the sidebar, find recently deleted items, and focus in on the vaults and items you need with Collections.
- The new design carries throughout every aspect of the app and flows into the browser experience as well.
- With 1Password 8, you can enjoy a fluid, consistent experience no matter where you go or which theme (dark mode or light mode) you enjoy.
Productivity
- One of the places where the power of our new design language really shines is search. Press Ctrl + Shift + Space from anywhere on your PC to bring up Quick Access.
- With Quick Access you can find any item you need, without leaving the app you're working in. It supports all the advanced search options and is fully optimized for keyboard warriors.
- Quick Access is smart, too. It detects open apps and remembers items you use most frequently so you always get the most relevant suggestions. You'll be more productive than ever when logging into your Steam games.
- Finding your items has never been quicker, and now creating them has never been easier. It all starts with a smart catalogue of suggested items to choose from, making it a snap to create what you need.
- The catalogue will help you find what you're looking for and pre-fill details like the website address and title, so your newly created item is ready to autofill in your browser.
- Speaking of which, the new 1Password experience in your browser takes productivity to the next level.
- The new browser experience integrates seamlessly with the desktop app, using a secure connection to ensure a consistent lock state. It also brings support for passwordless to the browser with Windows Hello.
- And perhaps the biggest productivity booster of all: 1Password 8 is incredibly fast.
- It's hard to be productive when waiting for things to load, so we tuned 1Password 8 to be super efficient using our Rust-powered core. Everything is instant so you're never waiting on a spinner.
Security & Privacy
- 1Password 8 comes with the security and privacy guarantees you've come to expect from 1Password and provides new tools to keep you safe online.
- The new Watchtower Dashboard makes it super simple to get a pulse on your security and see where you need to improve.
- Using on-device analysis to calculate password strength and detection of vulnerable passwords, Watchtower gives you actionable advice while preserving your privacy and security.
- Securely sharing items with others in your 1Password Families and 1Password Business accounts is super easy, too. With shared vaults, items magically appear for everyone you grant access to and everything shared in this way will prominently show who has access.
- Windows Hello is integrated directly into the lock screen to provide a passwordless unlock experience. And those with a TPM 2.0-enabled PC are in for a treat later this year when our enhanced support for Windows Hello will allow unlocking 1Password, even after app restarts and system reboots (join our beta family to be the first to enjoy this once available). ð¥³
- Last but not least, 1Password 8 stands upon the most secure security design we've ever had. And all the critical bits are done in Rust, a systems programming language renowned for its security and safety.

articles.title: Oura sues rival Ultrahuman again, threatening its U.S. smart ring comeback | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Smart ring maker Oura has sued Indian rival Ultrahuman again, seeking to block U.S. sales of its Ring Pro (pictured above) just months after the redesign helped the Bengaluru-based startup return to the American market following an import ban. The case is the latest in a string of patent disputes Oura has brought against competing smart-ring makers, including Samsung and RingConn.
In a complaint filed Thursday in a federal court in Texas, Oura alleged that Ultrahuman’s Ring Pro infringes two of its patents covering the ring’s design and internal components, including its battery and sensors. Oura is seeking monetary damages and a permanent injunction that would stop Ultrahuman from selling the ring.
Ultrahuman’s redesigned Ring Pro, launched in February, received a favorable ruling from U.S. Customs and Border Protection in March, paving the way for the startup’s return to the U.S. market. The decision followed an import ban on Ultrahuman’s earlier Ring Air, which took effect after Oura secured a patent infringement ruling from the International Trade Commission in August last year.
“Ultrahuman has a history of copying Oura’s innovations, as demonstrated by the 2025 ITC ruling against the company,” an Oura spokesperson said in a statement to TechCrunch. “Ultrahuman introduced a redesigned ring but failed to address continued infringement of Oura’s patents, seeking instead to capitalize on our innovation and the market leadership we have built.”
Oura argues that the Customs ruling covered only the patent involved in the earlier dispute, not the two patents cited in its latest lawsuit: D804,471 and 12,769,363. “To protect its patent rights, Oura is now forced to file this complaint of patent infringement,” the company said in its filing.
One of those patents, 12,769,363, is also very new. It was issued to Oura on October 20, just two days before it filed the lawsuit. It covers a smart-ring design incorporating internal components such as a curved battery, circuit board, magnets, and sensors.
Oura has also named Texas-based electronics manufacturer SVTronics as a defendant in the lawsuit. The complaint says SVTronics manufactures the Ring Pro at a facility in Plano, Texas, allegedly under Ultrahuman’s direction and control. It also alleges that both companies infringe Oura’s patents through the manufacture, importation, and sale of the device in the U.S.
Ultrahuman co-founder and CEO Mohit Kumar told TechCrunch the startup was confident in the Ring Pro and would fight the new allegations.
“Oura has now chosen to assert different patents, including one that issued just two days before this lawsuit was filed,” Kumar said. “We will address these claims through the appropriate legal process and will defend our position vigorously. There is no court order affecting Ring Pro, and it remains available to customers in the U.S.”
Oura and Ultrahuman have been fighting over patents since 2023, when Oura sued the Indian startup over its Ring Air, which had helped Ultrahuman make a name for itself in the U.S. Oura brought a separate case before the U.S. International Trade Commission in 2024 that helped it secure a ruling last year, leading to the import ban on the Ring Air.
Ultrahuman is not the only rival facing legal pressure from Oura. The company has also pursued patent infringement claims against smart-ring makers including Samsung, RingConn, Circular, and Zepp Health. Some of those disputes have ended in licensing agreements, with RingConn and Circular agreeing to pay royalties to Oura to continue selling their products.
The dispute emerges as the smart-ring market continues to grow. Research firm IDC expects global shipments to rise 12.8% this year to 4.9 million units and reach about 6.3 million by 2030. While Oura remains a leading player in the category, Ultrahuman is among the growing competitors.
The lawsuit also comes just weeks after Oura shelved its $2.2 billion IPO, citing “uncertainty” in the market. The company has continued to add features to its smart rings, introducing new fitness metrics earlier this week that help users track how workouts affect their cardiovascular health.
In September, Ultrahuman raised $70 million from investors including Qualcomm Ventures and Labcorp, valuing the startup at about $365 million. The startup is also working with Qualcomm on a new smart ring that could run more software directly on the device, as it looks to expand beyond health and fitness tracking into areas such as AI interactions and gaming.
The article has been updated to include comments from Ultrahuman co-founder and CEO Mohit Kumar.

articles.title: The iPhone Duo 2 should skip out on the under-display camera
articles.text:
I’ve been using the iPhone Duo for about a week, and I’ve been pretty impressed by the foldable.
The iPhone Duo, like many folding phones, has multiple cameras: two rear-facing, one on the front and one on the larger, internal display.
I love taking selfies, but with a folding phone, I typically don’t need to use the internal selfie cameras because of the multiple screens. With folding phones, I can open up the handset and use the cover screen as a viewfinder and take selfies with the rear-facing cameras. The iPhone Duo has two capable rear-facing cameras that are able to take stellar selfies, so I end up forgetting about the camera on the inside display. Unfortunately, on the iPhone Duo, it isn’t that great.
Apple doesn’t list the camera specs anywhere for this lens in particular, which I found a little suspicious. And Apple specifically calls it an under-display FaceTime camera, which is very nondescript. And well, the camera was pretty disappointing.
Check out the differences between taking a selfie with the under-display camera, the cover display shooter and the primary sensor.
Samsung used under-display camera technology for the Galaxy Z Fold 4 through Galaxy Z Fold 6. They all had a 4MP sensor and were the reason why I got used to never using the selfie camera on the inside screen. I like the idea of an under-display camera (UDC), so you don’t have something obstructing your view when you’re watching content.
But on those three devices and the iPhone Duo, you can pretty much always see the UDC, so it’s not even worth it. The Z Fold 7, 8 and 8 Ultra got rid of the under-display camera and now use a regular hole-punch camera with a 10MP sensor, which I think is a better alternative. I’m also a fan of just getting rid of the camera on that display; use the main shooters or the one on the cover display if you want to use the camera hands-free.
Either way, I hope Apple does something different with the iPhone Duo 2; however, as someone who doesn’t use this camera ever, it hasn’t impacted my iPhone Duo experience at all.

articles.title: One easy change makes Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark a better gaming system
articles.text:
One easy change makes Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark a better gaming system — custom resolutions make DLSS easier on the device
We define custom 3:2 resolutions to give DLSS an easier time
Nvidia's RTX Spark platform puts local AI inference and content creation first, but Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra really wants to game, too. The vented keyboard keeps the critical WASD keys cool under load by design, the smooth 120Hz screen can get as bright as 2000 nits with HDR games, and the built-in speakers may be the best I've ever heard on a laptop, period.
There's just one problem: that 3270x2180 screen asks a lot of DLSS upscaling. The computation that DLSS performs doesn't come for free, and the load increases with higher output resolutions. This is especially relevant with the Surface Laptop Ultra's high-density panel, which has just 14% fewer pixels than a 16:9 4K display.
The Surface's unusual 3:2 aspect ratio (at least compared to the average gaming laptop) also means that scaling content up to fill the screen isn't straightforward in many games. 16:9 and 16:10 content gets stretched vertically, causing obvious distortion of character models and objects like tires. And if you use windowed mode instead, playing in a 16:9 or 16:10 window on a relatively small screen like this quickly tires the eyes.
The thing is, all this is easy to solve—easy enough, in fact, that I'm surprised I had to do it myself at all.
Microsoft seems aware that lower 3:2 resolutions are useful for this system, as it put a 1600x1024 custom resolution in the list of display modes that's slightly less than half of native on both axes. But at roughly 1.6 megapixels in total, that image offers less resolution than even a 1920x1080 display does. Scaling up from such a low-res baseline on the Surface screen results in a noticeably soft image even before we dial in DLSS.
What we really want, for reasons of both performance and adequate sharpness, is a 3:2 resolution that comes close to the 2.07 megapixels that 1920x1080 yields. Some quick math and rounding to whole numbers gives us 1764x1176 as an optimal target.
With those ideal dimensions in hand, the next step was to create a custom resolution to match. The Nvidia Control Panel doesn't work on Windows on Arm, but we can still use the Nvidia App to set custom resolutions.
After diving into the System tab and expanding the Display Properties pane, I found the "Customize Resolution" button to open an editor to that end and added 1764x1176 at 120Hz. I then tested it and confirmed that it worked as a supported display mode. (If you want to match the 3.7 MP of 2560x1440, set up a 2352x1568 resolution while you’re at it.)
If for some reason you don't want non-3:2 content to fit the entire Surface Laptop Ultra screen, there is a Scaling pane in the Nvidia App that lets you control that behavior. The "Aspect Ratio" scaling mode will letterbox 16:9 and 16:10 material if you set the display resolution accordingly. But if you're paying $5899 for this system, I presume you want to use every one of its pricey pixels rather than leaving some of them dark.
So what does that bit of tweaking buy us compared to our initial gaming results with Control Resonant?
As someone who primarily games on our Ryzen 7 9800X3D GPU testing system and not a laptop, I wanted to make sure I wasn't setting unreasonable expectations for the Surface Laptop for input latency or CPU performance. So I hauled out an older 17" gaming laptop with a Core i9-11980HK and an RTX 3080 Mobile 16GB inside to get some perspective.
To level the playing field with the Surface Laptop Ultra and its native support for frame generation, I modded Optiscaler into Control Resonant on that system to enable Intel's Xe Frame Generation and Xe Low Latency features.
I conducted my testing with Control Resonant's High raster preset and medium RT preset, which gets you a noticeable boost in image quality thanks in part to DLSS Ray Reconstruction.
| Control Resonant performance - High raster, Medium RT, DLSS Ultra Performance, FG 2X |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Average FPS | 1% Low FPS | Average input latency (ms) | 
| Surface Laptop Ultra - 3270x2180 | 63.5 | 38.1 | 87. 9 | 
You can see that with these settings, trying to upscale Control Resonant to the Surface Laptop Ultra's native resolution is too much to ask for a smooth or responsive gaming experience. Even with DLSS Ultra Performance (an input resolution of 1090x727) and 2X frame generation, we only just break 60 FPS, and latency is at an unacceptable 87 ms average. There's no latency budget left to turn up MFG without turning down other image quality settings.
| Control Resonant performance - High raster, Medium RT, DLSS Quality, FG 2X |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Average FPS | 1% Low FPS | Average input latency (ms) | 
| Surface Laptop Ultra - 1764x1176 | 83.4 | 42.9 | 67.8 | 
| RTX 3080 Mobile + 11900HK - 1920x1080 | 87.1 | 53 | 69 | 
With our 1764x1176 custom resolution, however, we're off to a great start with DLSS Quality upscaling (an input resolution of 1176x874). The resulting 83.4 FPS average, 42.9 1% low FPS, and an average input latency of 67.8 ms is a fine experience. We still have room to dial in MFG 3X, leading to a 123 FPS average and 55 FPS 1% lows while keeping latency a reasonable 71 ms.
The RTX 3080 Mobile system with XeFG and XeLL, meanwhile, turns in an 87.1 FPS average, 53 FPS 1% lows, and a 69 ms average input latency at 1920x1080 with the same image quality settings. Its key advantage is in 1% lows, but that win comes with significant trade-offs.
Plugged into our Watts Up meter, the RTX 3080 system draws 250 W from the wall to deliver the experience it does, but according to a USB-C power meter, the Surface Laptop Ultra pulls between 110 W and 120 W under load. Silicon has come a long way since Tiger Lake and Ampere.
The RTX 3080 system and its enormous power adapter together also weigh over nine pounds (4.1 kg). It's technically portable but practically a pain to haul around. The Surface Laptop Ultra and its 140W adapter weigh just 5.3 lb (2.39 kg), which isn't featherweight but won't break your back.
And the Surface will actually fit on a tray table or your lap, with enough battery life that you can use it through a transcontinental U.S. flight, say, and still have plenty of juice left for either side of the trip.
So at least in Control Resonant, the Surface Laptop Ultra is delivering largely the same gaming experience as that high-end RTX 3080 Mobile system, but in a much smaller and lighter total package that draws less than half the wall power. And if you want to stretch frame rates further with MFG 3X, the Surface has MFG support that the older system doesn't. Just add in the 1764x1176 intermediate resolution that Microsoft forgot, and you’ll be well on your way to a better gaming experience.
As the Senior Analyst, Graphics at Tom's Hardware, Jeff Kampman covers everything that has to do with graphics cards, gaming performance, and more. From integrated graphics processors to discrete graphics cards to the hyperscale installations powering our AI future, if it's got a GPU in it, Jeff is on it.

articles.title: El thriller de espías que tiene un 100% de críticas positivas en Rotten Tomatoes ya tiene su sexta temporada completa en Apple TV+
articles.text:
Las historias de espías suelen estar protagonizadas por agentes impecables, capaces de llevar a cabo las misiones de más alto nivel con la tecnología más asombrosa. Hay una serie de ficción que lleva años cosechando éxitos mientras apuesta por justo lo contrario. Se trata de 'Slow Horses', de Apple TV+ y acaba de concluir su sexta temporada con un 100% de críticas positivas en Rotten Tomatoes.
El purgatorio del servicio secreto. La trama sigue a varios agentes que han sido descartados por el MI5 tras cometer fallos graves; nada que ver con los agentes infalibles habituales. En lugar de despedirlos, la agencia los confina en una oficina en Slough House para que se ocupen de tareas burocráticas rutinarias.
El jefe es Jackson Lamb (Gary Oldman), un veterano de la Guerra Fría desaliñado y muy maleducado. A su lado está River Cartwright (Jack Lowden), un prometedor agente que acaba relegado a Slough House tras cometer un error durante un ejercicio de entrenamiento. Aunque todo parece indicar que sus carreras están acabadas, siempre acaban involucrados en operaciones que ponen en jaque la seguridad del país.
El entusiasmo crece en cada entrega. La sexta temporada de 'Slow Horses' acaba de terminar y la crítica ha vuelto a rendirse a ella. Como decíamos, ha logrado un 100% de la crítica en Rotten Tomatoes y la serie completa una media de un 98 %. El sentimiento se extiende en otras plataformas como IMDB, donde tiene una puntuación de 8,4.
El anti-James Bond. Parte de su atractivo está precisamente en cómo huye de los tópicos del espionaje. Aquí no hay espías atractivos con cochazos ni tecnología futurista, sino dos agentes repudiados que tienen que demostrar que aún sirven para algo. Las interpretaciones de Gary Oldman y Jack Lowden son uno de sus grandes reclamos, además de una combinación de intrigas políticas, humor negro y escenas de acción que evita tomarse demasiado en serio a sus protagonistas.
Habrá más misiones en camino. La sexta temporada comenzó su emisión en Apple TV+ el 16 de septiembre de 2026 y emitió su sexto episodio el 21 de octubre de 2026. Si ya has visto todos los capítulos disponibles, hay buenas noticias porque ya están confirmadas dos temporadas más. Eso sí, tendrás que esperar para saber cómo continúa después de ese cliffhanger.

articles.title: Après Muse de Meta et ChatGPT Dot, Anthropic s'aligne et dévoile Claude Duet
articles.text:
Anthropic a ouvert le 21 octobre une liste d’attente pour Claude Duet, un « aperçu de recherche » réservé aux abonnés Pro et Max américains, les formules Team et Enterprise restant pour l’instant à l’écart. L’application, déclinée sur iOS, Android et le web, inverse le rapport habituel au chatbot, puisque l’agent surveille les comptes connectés et signale de sa propre initiative ce qui mérite votre attention. Avec Muse chez Meta et Dots chez OpenAI, le secteur aura lancé trois agents de ce genre en six semaines.
Un assistant qui n’attend plus vos questions
Chaque matin, Duet envoie un résumé des éléments importants repérés dans les applications reliées au compte, agendas, boîtes mail ou outils de travail, piochés parmi plus de 6 000 connecteurs. Le reste de la journée, l’agent repasse sur ces comptes toutes les quelques heures et n’écrit que lorsqu’un sujet réclame une décision. Anthropic destine l’outil « aux professionnels et aux patrons de petites entreprises qui ont plus sur les bras qu’ils ne peuvent en suivre ».
Les tâches confiées vont de la prise de rendez-vous à la construction de tableaux de bord, de prévisions financières ou de petites applications web. Propulsé par le modèle Opus 5.5, l’agent hérite de la mémoire, des compétences et des connexions déjà configurées dans le compte Claude, et se pilote à la voix comme à l’écrit.
Des garde-fous encadrent cette autonomie : Duet demande une validation avant d’envoyer un message, de payer, de signer un document ou de supprimer un fichier, tandis que les ordres de Bourse et les virements lui seraient interdits d’office. L’activité de fond se paie en revanche sur le quota de l’abonnement, l’entreprise expliquant qu’« une vérification permanente épuiserait les limites de votre forfait bien plus vite ». Elle admet aussi que son agent « peut encore mal juger ce qui est urgent ».
Trois agents en six semaines, aucun en Europe
La séquence s’est ouverte le 8 septembre avec Muse, l’agent de Meta lancé aux États-Unis puis étendu au Canada, gratuit pour l’essentiel et rémunéré par une commission sur les transactions qu’il mène à bien. OpenAI a suivi le 29 septembre en dévoilant Dots lors de sa conférence développeurs, des agents permanents qui travaillent sur leur propre machine dans le cloud.
Comme à l’accoutumé avec les nouveautés IA, aucun des trois ne fonctionne en France. Dots est explicitement exclu de l’Espace économique européen, de la Suisse et du Royaume-Uni pour les abonnés Pro, sans qu’OpenAI avance la moindre raison. Muse se cantonne à l’Amérique du Nord, et la liste d’attente de Duet exige un compte américain. Le précédent de Sora, lancé fin 2024 sans l’Union européenne, ou celui d’Operator, arrivé sur le continent avec des semaines de retard, laisse espérer des arrivées décalées plutôt qu’un renoncement durable.
Pour l’Hexagone, l’échéance reste donc floue, et l’addition se devine déjà, puisque ces agents consomment le quota de l’abonnement même quand vous ne demandez rien. Trois des plus gros acteurs du secteur misent pourtant désormais sur le même pari, celui d’une IA qui vient vous chercher au lieu d’attendre vos ordres.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (October22, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (October22, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, October 22, 2026.
YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Meet the ‘Flower Lady of Manipur’
Chokhone Krichena, founder of Manipur-based social enterprise Dianthe, is helping over 300 women farmers turn their love of flowers into income. Founded in 2021, Dianthe works with women in Mao, Senapati district, to source locally grown flowers, preserve them through natural drying techniques, and sell them to customers across India. What began during the Covid-19 pandemic as an effort to find buyers for surplus flowers has grown into a business supplying home décor products to customers in 20 states.
Funding news
Karta AI raises $3 million to scale voice AI for financial services
Karta AI, a voice AI platform that automates inbound customer operations for banks, financial services and insurance companies, has raised $3 million in a funding round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill Capital. Wyser VC, CDM Capital and Seedstars also participated. The company says it handles around two million customer conversations every month across more than 25 languages and is already deployed with financial institutions.
The platform uses AI agents to understand customer requests and resolve issues such as failed payments, blocked cards, loan queries and insurance claims by coordinating actions across enterprise systems. Unlike conventional voice bots that primarily answer questions, Karta AI aims to complete customer service workflows autonomously, escalating cases to human agents when needed. Its technology also learns from past interactions to improve resolution over time.
CureBay raises Rs 100 crore in Pre-Series C round
Rural healthcare platform CureBay has raised Rs 100 crore in a Pre-Series C funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. The round includes Rs 69 crore in equity from IvyCap Ventures and existing investors, along with over Rs 30 crore in debt from Trifecta Capital, Alteria Capital and VentureSoul Partners.
Founded in 2021 by Priyadarshi Mohapatra, Shobhan Mahapatra and Sanjay Swain, CureBay operates over 250 technology-enabled clinics across seven states. The company will use the funds to expand its operations, strengthen its healthcare delivery network and develop its technology and AI capabilities, including tools for patient screening, health insights and clinical decision-making. CureBay says it has served over 17 lakh patients and conducts more than 400 health camps every month.
Other news
Uroionpro Transit, Mastercard partner to simplify transit payments
Uroionpro Transit is expanding its partnership with Mastercard to help public transport agencies and government authorities across North America modernise transit payment systems and improve passenger experience. The collaboration focuses on making contactless payment solutions easier to assess, procure and deploy across public transportation networks.
The partnership will support transit agencies through practical procurement frameworks, repeatable implementation methods and deployment models that can be adapted to local operational and policy requirements. The aim is to reduce the complexity of introducing contactless payments while enabling secure, seamless and convenient transactions for passengers.
Maasi launches on-demand nanny platform in Bengaluru
Maasi, a childcare platform offering trained, background-verified nannies on demand and through subscription plans, has launched in Bengaluru. During its invite-only beta, the platform served 1,200 families and built a waitlist of over 5,000 parents. Instant Nanny visits start at Rs 660, while subscription plans begin at Rs 15,660 a month.
Founded by Gargi Pandey, Aashu Manchali and Reshov Roy, Maasi offers short-notice childcare and part-time, full-time, live-in, governess and postpartum care. The startup aims to address the shortage of reliable childcare, which can force parents, particularly women, to step away from their careers. Its caregivers undergo background verification and training, with replacement support if a caregiver leaves
Pine Labs partners WEBXPAY to enable UPI payments in Sri Lanka
Pine Labs has partnered with Sri Lankan payment aggregator WEBXPAY to enable Indian payment methods across its merchant network in Sri Lanka. The collaboration is the country's first Payment Aggregator-to-Payment Aggregator partnership under India’s RBI-authorised PA-CB framework.
Through the partnership, merchants can accept UPI, UPI AutoPay, cards from major Indian issuers, net banking across more than 100 banks, EMI conversions and Credit on UPI. The solution offers T+1 settlement and integrates with existing merchant systems, enabling Indian travellers to pay in Sri Lanka using familiar methods.
Vultr announces Chennai cloud data centre region with 20 MW AI supercluster
Cloud infrastructure provider Vultr has announced Chennai as its 34th global cloud data centre region, featuring an AI supercluster powered by AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, starting at 20 MW. The facility aims to give Indian enterprises and developers access to high-performance computing infrastructure closer to where they build and deploy AI applications.
Vultr plans to expand the supercluster in 2027 with next-generation AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs and AMD Helios rack-scale technology. The company said the infrastructure will help enterprises scale AI projects from pilots to production while offering greater control over workloads through an open software foundation.
Binny Bansal-backed ShopOS launches AI creative platform Sloosh
ShopOS, a Bengaluru-based AI company backed by Flipkart co-founder Binny Bansal’s 3STATE Ventures, has launched Sloosh.ai, an AI creative platform that converts ideas, photos and videos into product imagery, visual scenes, reels and creator-style clips. The platform is now available globally, giving creators and businesses access to ShopOS’ creative engine.
ShopOS has raised $20 million and uses AI agents, reusable workflows and human experts to produce content for global and Indian brands. With Sloosh, the company aims to make AI-powered creative production more accessible and lower-cost for agency teams, brands, founders, small businesses, and independent creators.
Sirona launches ‘Unpause Menopause’ campaign to break stigma
Women’s period care and wellness brand Sirona has launched ‘Unpause Menopause’, a campaign aimed at breaking the silence around menopause and challenging the stigma and ageism associated with this stage of women’s health. Built around the message “Cut the noise. Start the conversation,” the initiative encourages women to speak openly about their experiences without embarrassment.
The campaign highlights lesser-discussed menopause symptoms, including joint aches, itchy ears, dizziness, heart palpitations, changes in body odour, and dry eyes. While conversations around periods and reproductive health have gained visibility, menopause often remains a private struggle.
Beginning October 18, the brand has mobilised some of India's most influential voices to speak openly about menopause, their experiences, their symptoms, and why the silence has gone on too long. On October 21, Sirona released the Unpause Menopause brand film alongside a curated series of expert conversations, bringing together doctors, specialists and women who have lived through this transition to address the questions most women have never had the space to ask. The film and expert series are available on Sirona's YouTube channel and Instagram page.

articles.title: Der Auslöser lag im Norden, die CO2-Falle am Südpol – wie 13 Prozent kalter Ozean für eine Eiszeit reichten
articles.text:
13 Prozent kalter Ozean reichen für eine Eiszeit: Wie der hohe Norden über die Tiefsee das Erdklima kippte
Forscher:innen um die Geowissenschaftlerin Madison Shankle von der schottischen University of St Andrews haben nun in Computersimulationen nachgewiesen, wie wachsende Eisschilde auf der Nordhalbkugel den Entzug von Kohlendioxid (CO2) im weit entfernten Südpolarmeer auslösen konnten. Wie in einer im Fachmagazin Journal of Climate veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, reicht eine Abkühlung der hohen nördlichen Breiten allein aus, um 74 Prozent jenes temperaturbedingten CO2-Rückgangs zu erzeugen, der bei einer Abkühlung des gesamten Planeten entsteht.
Simulation mit dem MIT-Zirkulationsmodell verbindet Arktis und Antarktis
Dass periodische Schwankungen der Erdbahn und der Erdachsenneigung – die sogenannten Milanković-Zyklen – den Takt vergangener Eiszeiten vorgaben, ist in der Geologie seit Jahrzehnten bekannt. Diese veränderten Einstrahlungswerte kühlten allerdings vor allem die Sommer auf der Nordhalbkugel ab und ließen dort kilometerdicke Eisschilde wachsen, während der eigentliche Treiber für den globalen Temperatursturz im Südlichen Ozean rund um die Antarktis lag, wo das Meer der Atmosphäre große Mengen CO2 entzog.
Um zu prüfen, ob ein lokaler Kälteimpuls im Norden über rund 15.000 Kilometer hinweg das Südpolarmeer verändern kann, nutzte Shankle gemeinsam mit Kolleg:innen vom britischen National Oceanography Centre in Southampton sowie der University of Chicago im US-Bundesstaat Illinois ein am Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) entwickeltes Ozean-Zirkulationsmodell. In vier Versuchsreihen über jeweils 15.000 Simulationsjahre kühlten die Wissenschaftler:innen lediglich die Lufttemperaturen nördlich des 40. Breitengrades, und damit nur 13 Prozent der Modelloberfläche, auf eiszeitliche Werte ab und hielten den gesamten Rest der Welt künstlich auf einem vorindustriellen Warmzeit-Niveau.
Kälte aus dem Nordatlantik lässt Meereis im Südpolarmeer wachsen
Das Modell zeigt eine mehrstufige physikalische Kettenreaktion quer durch die Weltmeere. Die kalte Luft über dem Norden kühlt das Oberflächenwasser ab, das als sogenanntes Nordatlantisches Tiefenwasser absinkt und in 1.000 bis 2.000 Metern Tiefe nach Süden strömt. Zwar schwächt sich diese obere Umwälzzirkulation, das Pendant zur heutigen Atlantischen Meridionalen Umwälzzirkulation (AMOC), durch die Kälte im Norden um 33 Prozent ab, doch die verbleibende Strömung reicht aus, um das abgekühlte Wasser bis in die Antarktis zu transportieren.
Dass diese ozeanische Transportverbindung auch während realer Kaltzeiten Bestand hatte, stützen Analysen von Meeressedimenten in einer in Nature Geoscience veröffentlichten Studie, an der unter anderem Forscher:innen des Kieler Helmholtz-Zentrums für Ozeanforschung (Geomar) beteiligt waren. Wenn dieses kalte Tiefenwasser im Südlichen Ozean wieder zur Oberfläche aufsteigt, bremst es dort die Wärmezufuhr ab und lässt das antarktische Meereis in der Simulation auf die dreifache Dicke anwachsen, obwohl die Luft darüber weiterhin warmzeitliche Werte aufweist.
Wenn Meerwasser rund um die Antarktis gefriert, bleibt das gelöste Salz im umliegenden Wasser zurück. Dieses salzige Wasser ist schwerer als das Oberflächenwasser, sinkt bis auf den Meeresgrund ab und schirmt die Tiefsee dadurch vom Austausch mit den oberen Wasserschichten ab.
Kaltes Wasser und dickes Meereis sperren Kohlendioxid in der Tiefsee ein
Durch diesen Effekt schluckt der Ozean im Modell 18,8 Milliarden Tonnen zusätzlichen Kohlenstoff, sobald allein der hohe Norden abkühlt. Das entspricht bereits knapp drei Vierteln jener Menge, die das Meer bei einer Abkühlung der gesamten Erde aufnehmen würde.
Dahinter stecken zwei einfache physikalische Prinzipien: Zum einen kühlt das Wasser aus dem Norden nach und nach die gesamte Tiefsee um durchschnittlich 2,5 Grad Celsius ab, und kaltes Wasser kann grundsätzlich mehr Kohlendioxid binden als warmes. Zum anderen wirkt das dickere Meereis im Süden wie ein fester Deckel auf dem Ozean, sodass aufsteigendes Tiefenwasser sein gespeichertes CO2 nicht mehr an die Luft abgeben kann.
Ein gegenläufiger Effekt bremst diese Aufnahme im Modell allerdings etwas ab. Weil die veränderte Strömung im Süden mehr Nährstoffe ungenutzt in die Tiefe zieht, fehlt an der Wasseroberfläche Nahrung für Algen, die normalerweise per Fotosynthese weiteres CO2 aus der Luft binden.
Grenzen des Computermodells und Bedeutung für die Klimaforschung
„Im Wesentlichen haben wir Belege für einen plausiblen Mechanismus geliefert, der diese beiden weit voneinander entfernten Puzzleteile miteinander verbindet – die Eisschilde der Nordhalbkugel und die Veränderungen der Ozeanzirkulation auf der Südhalbkugel, die zum CO2-Entzug aus der Atmosphäre führen“, wird die Hauptautorin Madison Shankle von Phys.org zitiert. Zu einem ähnlichen Ergebnis kamen kürzlich auch Forscher:innen des Max-Planck-Instituts für Meteorologie in Hamburg und der Schweizer Universität Bern: In einer in den Geophysical Research Letters veröffentlichten Studie zeigten sie ebenfalls, dass die Eisschilde im Norden und in der Antarktis über weite Distanzen hinweg voneinander abhängen.
Dennoch hat das Computermodell aus St Andrews Grenzen, auf die die Autor:innen selbst hinweisen. Um den Kälteeffekt aus dem Norden im veröffentlichten Quellcode der Simulation isoliert zu untersuchen, rechnet das Programm mit einem stark vereinfachten Ozean, der nur aus einem einzigen, vier Kilometer tiefen Becken mit flachem Boden und ohne Jahreszeiten besteht. Zudem blendet die Simulation weitere Einflüsse wie eisenhaltigen Wüstenstaub aus, der in realen Eiszeiten das Algenwachstum im Meer als natürlicher Dünger angekurbelt hat. Deshalb erklärt das Modell insgesamt knapp die Hälfte des tatsächlichen CO2-Rückgangs früherer Kaltzeiten.
Wie stark solche Berechnungen von den gewählten Startwerten abhängen, zeigt der Vergleich mit einer ähnlichen Studie aus dem Jahr 2022. Damals hatten andere Forscher:innen das gleiche Simulationsprogramm mit zwei Ozeanbecken und wärmeren Ausgangstemperaturen gefüttert. Ihre Ergebnisse zeigten, dass eine Abkühlung im Norden das Meerwasser stärker durchmischte und sogar etwas mehr CO2 in die Luft entweichen ließ. Für aktuelle Klimamodelle, die berechnen, wie viel menschengemachtes Treibhausgas die Weltmeere künftig noch aufnehmen können, liefert die neue Arbeit dennoch einen wichtigen Hinweis. Veränderungen im Nordatlantik und im Südpolarmeer lassen sich demnach nicht getrennt voneinander betrachten.

articles.title: Sportifs et voyageurs : la DJI Osmo 360 passe à 313,14€ sur AliExpress
articles.text:
Depuis l’arrivée en France de l’Osmo 360 II, vendue 589 €, la première caméra 360° de DJI devient la porte d’entrée raisonnable pour filmer en 8K. AliExpress affiche la DJI Osmo 360 à 313,14 €, sous son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, pour un modèle que notre comparatif classe meilleur rapport qualité-prix, avec une limite à connaître : ses objectifs ne se remplacent pas.
Sortie à l’été 2025 à 479,99 € dans son pack standard, la DJI Osmo 360 est la première caméra 360° de la marque, pensée pour concurrencer Insta360. AliExpress la propose aujourd’hui à 313,14 €, contre 366,12 € pour son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours avant cette réduction, soit 52,98 € d’écart (-14 %). La fiche du vendeur mérite une lecture attentive : vérifiez ce qui accompagne la caméra dans le colis avant de valider.
L’offre s’adresse surtout à ceux qui veulent filmer une sortie à vélo, un voyage ou une session de glisse sans se soucier du cadrage au moment de tourner, puis choisir l’angle au montage.
La DJI Osmo 360, caméra 360° 8K à double capteur carré, passe à 313,14 € au lieu de 366,12 € sur AliExpress.
Pourquoi choisir la DJI Osmo 360 ?
- De la 8K à 360° : La caméra filme jusqu’en 8K à 50 images par seconde sur 360°, ce qui laisse de la marge pour recadrer après coup. Les photos panoramiques montent jusqu’à 120 mégapixels.
- 105 Go déjà embarqués : Ses 128 Go de stockage interne, dont 105 Go utilisables, permettent de partir filmer sans carte microSD.
- Une action cam en prime : Le mode mono-objectif filme en 4K à 120 images par seconde avec un champ de 170°. La même caméra sert donc aussi de grand-angle classique, ralentis compris.
Vélo, voyage, vlog : ce que la 360° change au tournage
Sur un parcours VTT ou une descente à ski, la stabilisation HorizonSteady 360° garde l’horizon droit, que notre guide d’achat juge efficace sur terrain accidenté. L’étanchéité IP68 jusqu’à 10 mètres, sans caisson, couvre la pluie, la baignade ou une sortie en kayak. Pour le vlog, la caméra accepte jusqu’à deux micros DJI Mic, utiles pour capter une voix loin de l’appareil, et son écran tactile de 2 pouces simplifie les réglages caméra en main.
Le profil idéal est celui d’un sportif ou d’un voyageur qui filme beaucoup et préfère décider du cadrage au montage, ou d’un créateur déjà équipé en micros DJI. L’enregistrement en D-Log M 10 bits intéressera aussi ceux qui étalonnent leurs images. En revanche, si vous filmez surtout en intérieur ou à la tombée de la nuit, l’Insta360 X5 garde une avance nette en basse lumière. Comptez enfin environ 100 minutes d’enregistrement en 8K à 30 images par seconde.
Osmo 360 II, Insta360 X5 : où se situe cette première génération
Le principal défaut de l’Osmo 360 tient à ses objectifs fixes : une lentille rayée pose un vrai problème, là où l’Osmo 360 II, vendue 589 € en pack Standard, adopte des lentilles remplaçables et monte à la 8K à 60 images par seconde. Face à l’Insta360 X5, choix de la rédaction dans notre comparatif des meilleures caméras 360, la DJI se défend avec son stockage intégré et sa fiche technique, mais son application et son écosystème logiciel restent en retrait. Elle y décroche la place du meilleur rapport qualité-prix, un statut que ce tarif renforce encore.
✅ Les points forts
- Vidéo 8K à 360° et photos jusqu’à 120 mégapixels
- 105 Go de stockage interne utilisables
- Étanche IP68 jusqu’à 10 mètres sans caisson
- Mode 4K à 120 images par seconde sur un seul objectif
- Compatible avec deux micros DJI Mic
❌ Les limites
- Objectifs non remplaçables en cas de rayure
- Basse lumière en retrait face à l’Insta360 X5
- Pas de photo 360° en RAW
- Autonomie d’environ 100 minutes en 8K à 30 i/s
Avant de commander la DJI Osmo 360 à 313,14 € chez AliExpress, vérifiez le contenu du pack et les délais de livraison annoncés.
À 313,14 €, la DJI Osmo 360 coûte près de 276 € de moins que l’Osmo 360 II dans son pack Standard, pour une fiche technique qui reste solide : 8K à 360°, double capteur carré, stockage intégré et étanchéité à 10 mètres. Les apports de la seconde génération, lentilles remplaçables et 8K à 60 images par seconde, comptent surtout pour les tournages exigeants ou les usages qui exposent les optiques. Pour les vacances, le sport ou le vlog, cette première génération couvre déjà l’essentiel.
Elle convient moins à ceux qui tournent souvent dans la pénombre, où l’Insta360 X5 fait mieux, ou à ceux qui malmènent leur matériel et préféreront des lentilles faciles à changer. L’achat sur AliExpress demande aussi de lire la fiche avec attention, notamment le contenu du pack et la livraison. Si ces points vous conviennent, la DJI Osmo 360 reste une base sérieuse pour apprendre à filmer en 360° et à recadrer vos plans au montage.

articles.title: Anthropic introduces Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent for professionals - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Anthropic introduces Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent for professionals
Anthropic PBC Wednesday introduced Claude Duet, a proactive artificial intelligence agent for professionals and small business owners in research preview, which completes tasks when asked, keeps working behind the scenes and checks in.
Duet is available as a standalone app on the web, iOS and Android for Pro and Max subscribers.
The company said the new assistant will send a short brief each morning of the most important items across connected apps and keep tabs on messages only when something needs attention. It can also handle numerous different administrative tasks, like a digital secretary. These include scheduling meetings and more complex tasks, such as building dashboards with interactive tools, creating financial or sales forecasts and prototyping and building web apps.
Users will message Duet like another teammate, by text or voice, with no prompts or setup. The idea is to use it like a secretary who can access apps, calendar, email and other connected information. It’s part of Claude, so it also has a running history in one thread. It remembers what a user said before, and returns finished work like a doc, sheet or deck for review.
Duet is part of the Claude that users already participate with. It can access memory, skills and apps from Claude – so there is no additional setup.
Anthropic stressed that Duet is built on the company’s framework for trustworthy agents, which also guides the company’s existing agentic systems such as Claude Code and Claude in Chrome. An automatic classifier approves any actions the agent takes by checking messages for sensitive information leaks and double-checking with the user before taking important actions.
The company added that people at Anthropic are using Duet themselves. Claude Code’s own Boris Cherny uses it on walks to talk through to-dos and save time at his desk, and the team behind Duet uses it to build the product. Karan Ahuja, who leads the team, works with it to schedule user interviews and even ship code.
The research preview will help Anthropic better understand Duet’s use cases and failure modes. Right now, it is an early, experimental version. It still might misread a thread or miscalibrate what is urgent: The agent is designed around work, so personal errands, such as booking tickets, won’t be treated as urgently and it can’t show its browser. The company will use what it learns from early users to fine-tune how it works.

articles.title: El empleo de los jóvenes británicos en tecnología y finanzas cayó 22% en tres años
articles.text:
El empleo de los jóvenes de entre 18 y 24 años en los sectores de tecnología y finanzas del Reino Unido cayó 22% entre fines de 2022 y fines de 2025, según un análisis del Centro para el Crecimiento de Boston Consulting Group (BCG) difundido esta semana por la agencia Bloomberg.
El informe, elaborado a partir de datos oficiales de empleo, encontró que la cantidad total de jóvenes que trabajan en esas dos industrias pasó de unos 208.000 a 163.000 en tres años, una pérdida de 45.000 puestos en los rubros mejor pagos del país.
La caída no fue pareja entre los dos sectores. El empleo juvenil en el rubro de información y comunicación, que incluye a la mayoría de los trabajos tecnológicos, se redujo 30% desde fines de 2022. En finanzas, la caída fue del 10% en el mismo período.
Mientras tanto, el empleo general de ese mismo grupo etario en el resto de la economía británica se mantuvo prácticamente estable, un contraste que, según BCG, confirma que el fenómeno está concentrado en las industrias de mayor productividad y mejores salarios.
Un problema que excede a la inteligencia artificial
Raoul Ruparel, director sénior del Centro para el Crecimiento de BCG, dijo que las empresas se volvieron menos propensas a contratar personal sin experiencia, pero aclaró que la reducción del empleo juvenil “no puede explicarse solo” por la adopción de inteligencia artificial.
Según Ruparel, buena parte de la pérdida de puestos ocurrió en 2023 y 2024, cuando las aplicaciones avanzadas de inteligencia artificial todavía no estaban tan extendidas como ahora. El informe también atribuye parte de la caída a la desaceleración poscovid del sector tecnológico y a las dificultades para capacitar personal nuevo con el trabajo remoto.
Finanzas y tecnología concentran algunos de los empleos mejor pagos del Reino Unido: según el informe, el trabajador promedio del sector financiero gana unas 52.000 libras al año, mientras que en tecnología el salario promedio ronda las 50.000 libras.
El desempleo juvenil llegó a su peor nivel desde 2014
De acuerdo con datos oficiales citados en el informe, la tasa de desempleo juvenil en el Reino Unido superó el 16% durante el invierno boreal, su nivel más alto desde 2014. A eso se suma una creciente preocupación por las dificultades de los recién graduados universitarios para conseguir trabajo.
El reporte advierte que la pérdida de puestos de entrada en sectores de alta productividad como tecnología y finanzas puede tener un efecto a largo plazo: esas posiciones son las que tradicionalmente forman a los trabajadores con experiencia que las empresas necesitarán en el futuro.
BCG identificó qué sectores sí sumaron empleo joven desde 2019: construcción, transporte y almacenamiento, y artes y entretenimiento tuvieron el mejor desempeño en la contratación de trabajadores de entre 18 y 24 años, en contraste con la caída de tecnología y finanzas.
El mismo fenómeno se repite en Estados Unidos
El fenómeno no se limita al Reino Unido. Un informe publicado el 21 de octubre por el Canaries Dashboard, un proyecto conjunto del Laboratorio de Economía Digital de Stanford y ADP Research, analiza el empleo de trabajadores estadounidenses de entre 22 y 25 años.
Ese informe encontró que el empleo de ese grupo etario cae de forma interanual desde hace 36 meses consecutivos en las ocupaciones más expuestas a la inteligencia artificial, con una contracción del 3,7% en septiembre frente al mismo mes del año anterior.
La publicación del informe de BCG coincide con el anuncio del banco Barclays de recortar 5.000 empleos este año, una decisión que la entidad vinculó directamente con la expansión del uso de inteligencia artificial en sus operaciones.
El Centro para el Crecimiento de BCG planteó la necesidad de que universidades, empleadores y el gobierno británico acuerden nuevas formas de capacitar a los jóvenes si la automatización sigue reduciendo los puestos de entrada que históricamente cumplieron esa función.

articles.title: Spotify aperta cerco contra o compartilhamento e adota QR Code • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Spotify aperta cerco contra o compartilhamento e adota QR Code
Membros selecionados do plano Família têm prazo de sete dias e podem ficar um ano fora de outros planos compartilhados.
O Spotify começou a usar uma nova verificação por QR Code para conferir se integrantes do Premium Família realmente moram no mesmo endereço. A checagem exige que as duas pessoas estejam no mesmo local no momento da leitura do código.
A empresa de streaming afirma que pode solicitar o procedimento a alguns membros, sem informar quantas contas serão verificadas.
A orientação já aparece na página de suporte brasileira do Spotify. Quando recebe a solicitação, o integrante tem sete dias para concluir a checagem.
O administrador deve abrir o Spotify no celular, tocar na foto de perfil e acessar “Seu Premium” e “Administrar” para exibir o QR Code. O outro membro precisa escanear o código com a câmera do próprio celular. Segundo o Spotify, os dois aparelhos devem estar no mesmo local e com a versão mais recente do aplicativo instalada.
O código muda a cada poucos segundos, o que dificulta o envio de uma captura de tela para alguém que esteja em outro local. A verificação só funciona pelo aplicativo para celular. O Spotify também recomenda conferir data e hora dos dois aparelhos ou reiniciar o app caso a leitura apresente problemas.
Quem não fizer a leitura dentro dos sete dias perde o acesso ao plano Família e passa para a modalidade gratuita. O integrante continua podendo assinar outro plano Premium individualmente. Quem não concluir a checagem pode ficar impedido de entrar em outro Premium Família ou Duo durante 12 meses, segundo o Spotify.
A exigência de morar no mesmo endereço não é nova. Desde 2019, o Spotify já exigia que integrantes do plano confirmassem o mesmo endereço. Na época, a empresa também previa verificações periódicas e chegou a testar o uso da localização do celular em alguns mercados. Mais tarde, o serviço passou a permitir a confirmação pelo endereço residencial.

articles.title: Nvidia driver update should greatly speed up PC games
articles.text:
Nvidia has rolled out a new GPU driver that should significantly speed up game launches.
The update, 621.01, adds Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery tech to reduce the load on CPUs by offloading the heavy lifting to the cloud. As Nvidia notes, modern games rely on tens of thousands of complex shaders as well as generic shader files that result in a slow, CPU-heavy process that can take up to 30 minutes.
But with Microsoft’s latest tech, the cloud network can greatly cut down these wait times by precompiling shaders for hundreds of thousands of hardware and driver combinations. It also removes mid-game “just-in-time” shader compilation that can cause CPU spikes and frame stutters.
For now, this week’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and the recently released Gears of War: E-Day from Vancouver’s The Coalition support Advanced Shader Delivery. You’ll need to download these games via the Xbox PC app, but from there, you’ll benefit from the new shader system even when playing Steam games as long as the Xbox app remains installed.
The 621.01 update can be downloaded here. The new GPU driver comes as part of a larger series of updates to improve gaming on Nvidia GeForce. The full breakdown can be found on Nvidia’s blog.

articles.title: Cherry Launches MX ILLUMA and MX EMERALD REEF Mechanic Keyboard Switches
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Cherry Launches MX ILLUMA and MX EMERALD REEF Mechanic Keyboard Switches
CHERRY has expanded its range of mechanical keyboard switches with the launch of the MX ILLUMA RED, MX ILLUMA BROWN and MX EMERALD REEF. Designed for different typing preferences, the new switches focus on improved stability, enhanced RGB lighting and quieter operation. The new launches are also included in CHERRY's MX EXPERIENCE BOX 2ND EDITION, which gives users the opportunity to test 10 different MX switches and compare typing feel, responsiveness and sound levels.MX ILLUMA: Greater Stability and Improved RGB Lighting
The new MX ILLUMA range has been developed to deliver a more stable and precise typing experience.
The MX ILLUMA RED is a linear switch designed for smooth, consistent keystrokes, while the MX ILLUMA BROWN provides gentle tactile feedback without compromising stability. Both switches are built on CHERRY's Gold Crosspoint technology and are engineered to withstand more than 100 million keystrokes. 
A redesigned housing and refined internal guidance system help reduce unwanted movement and noise, resulting in a more controlled typing experience. The switches also feature integrated lenses that improve light distribution, creating brighter and more even RGB illumination across compatible keyboards.
The MX ILLUMA RED has an actuation force of 45 cN, while the MX ILLUMA BROWN offers a tactile force of 55 cN. Both are available in packs of 36 switches.
MX EMERALD REEF: Tactile Feedback Without the Noise
Built on the MX ILLUMA platform, the MX EMERALD REEF has been designed for users who enjoy tactile feedback but prefer a quieter typing experience.
Developed with input from the keyboard enthusiast community, the switch delivers a distinct tactile bump while incorporating noise-dampening features that reduce sound when keys are pressed and released. An enhanced stem guidance system also helps minimise wobble, improving overall stability and accuracy.
The MX EMERALD REEF also stands out visually, with a turquoise to housing, light blue base and neon green stem inspired by the colours of coral reef.
The switch has an actuation force of 41 cN, actuates at 2.0 mm and is rated for more than 50 million keystrokes. It also supports full RGB lighting and is available in packs of 36 switches.
Try Before You Buy with the MX EXPERIENCE BOX
Choosing the right keyboard switch typically comes down to personal preference. To help users find the right option that suits them best, CHERRY's MX EXPERIENCE BOX 2ND EDITION includes sample versions of 10 MX switches:
- MX EMERALD REEF
- MX ILLUMA RED
- MX ILLUMA BROWN
- MX PETAL
- MX BLOSSOM
- MX2A HONEY
- MX FALCON
- MX NORTHERN LIGHT
- MX2A BLACK
- MX2A SILENT RED
The MX EXPERIENCE BOX brings together a broad range of switch characteristics and sound profiles, allowing users to directly compare typing feel, feedback and noise levels. All included switches feature a 5-pin design and are compatible with hot-swap keyboards. The switches are supplied in plastic-free cardboard packaging, which also protects the contact pins during transport.
The switches can be tested side-by-side in compatible hot-swappable keyboards, making it easier to compare feel, sound and performance before committing to a full set.
Gunnar Schreck, Head of Product Management at CHERRY said: "The keyboard community is paying closer attention than ever to how a switch feels, sounds and looks. With MX ILLUMA AND MX EMERALD REEF, CHERRY has introduced switches that deliver a refined typing experience, whether that's smoother keystrokes, quieter tactility or enhanced RGB effects.
"Combined with the MX EXPERIENCE BOX, we're also making it easier for people to discover the switch that matches their preferred typing feel."

articles.title: Leaked private keys for eight CA certificates let any attacker impersonate any domain — billions of older devices and software installations may be vulnerable after round of fixes, patch yours immediately
articles.text:
Leaked private keys for eight CA certificates let any attacker impersonate any domain — billions of older devices and software installations may be vulnerable after round of fixes, patch yours immediately
Stop everything and update your browsers, OSes, development tools, and routers.
Most everyone in the tech space has been living in interesting times, but this week isn't done yet, and it's already quite special for systems administrators worldwide. They already had to deal with the critical PHP RCE vulnerability, but they also have to update untold amounts of machines and software, thanks to eight insecure intermediate CA certificates that can allow attackers to impersonate any domain and/or pretend their malware is from a legitimate source.
An attacker anywhere in the path of your network traffic, like, say, in a company or government network, public Wi-Fi, your ISP, or one of any number of government entities, can intercept your connection and pretend that they're any website, like apple.com, amazon.com, or bankofamerica.com. If not updated, your operating system and installed software would be none the wiser. Additionally, with the code signing certificates, an application you download can be shown as completely legitimate from, say, Microsoft or Google.
The way that software checks a certificate is legitimate is by verifying its "chain." For example, a website like tomshardware.com has a certificate, issued and signed by an intermediate Certification Authority (or CA, a certificate-selling company), and whose certificate, in turn, is trusted and signed by root certificates — whose exceedingly precious keys are kept offline in safes. In this week's event, Indian CA firm eMudhra issued six TLS and two code-signing intermediate certificates with easily guessable keys.
Your operating system and potentially tens of different applications on your machine all keep a list of which root certificates and CAs are trusted. Browsers also keep a list of those not to trust, called a revocation list. These lists are updated periodically as screw-ups happen, just like the one that took place this week. And now they all need to be updated again, by revoking the eight CAs, removing the one affected root certificate, or just hard-coding a rejection of all eight affected keys.
There's a silver lining: recent versions of Chrome, Brave, Firefox, and Safari all enforce a feature called Certificate Transparency that consults a public read-only log of certificate issuances, and blocks any that aren't mentioned. Google reports that no certificates signed by the six affected intermediate CAs were logged, so if regular web browsing is all you did, you should be safe — but still check all your software for updates nonetheless.
The problem here is the sheer amount of machines and software that needs updating: PCs, servers, operating systems, phones, tablets, routers, web browsers, web browsers wrapped in apps, virtual servers, virtual machines, Docker and other containers, programming languages like Python, Go, Node.js, Rust, standalone download utilities like curl, and probably tens or hundreds of other categories. Additionally, we discussed things that are expected and likely to get updates. Old routers, smart and IoT appliances, and old computers could eventually present a problem.
As for the technical details, eMudhra issued six intermediate CA certificates and two intermediate code-signing certs with rather unadvisable private keys. The private key is the secret half of the two parts of a certificate, and for some reason, those of the aforementioned certs were only 1 byte long — thus a number from 0 to 255, trivial to brute-force in a split second. How the heck that happened is still under investigation.

articles.title: Seagate’s 8TB IronWolf drops further at Newegg than Best Buy
articles.text:
Seagate's IronWolf 8TB NAS drive is a 4-star HDD — it's on sale at Best Buy, but buy it from Newegg now to save even more
The CMR hard drive suits NAS systems, RAID arrays and multi-user environments
Seagate's IronWolf HDD scored it 4 stars after testing. And right now the Seagate IronWolf 8TB is down to $330 at Newegg, in a 'shell shocker' deal.
Now, I spend a lot of time hunting down the best tech deals. Originally, I spotted this hard drive for $350 (was $480) at Best Buy. Then I stumbled on the Newegg pricing, so I'd skip Best Buy and pocket the extra $20.
• Best for: Anyone for expanding a home NAS, small business server, or RAID array.
• What we like: The 8TB Seagate IronWolf is an excellent all-rounder. It's built for continuous 24/7 operation in multi-drive systems, with CMR recording technology, a 7200 RPM spindle speed, and a 256MB cache. Seagate also rates it for workloads of up to 180TB annually, with a mean time between failures (MTBF) of 1 million hours.
• What you need to know: I'd look elsewhere if silence and low power consumption are priorities. A 7200 RPM mechanical drive is designed with performance in mind and won't offer the near-silent operation of an SSD.
The 8TB IronWolf ST8000VN004 HDD offers 7200 RPM performance, 256MB cache and SATA 6.0Gb/s connectivity, with a 180TB/year workload rating and rotational vibration sensors.
It's the same drive, and although Best Buy has knocked $167.66 off its list price, you'll still pay $20 more than you would at Newegg.
Why we recommend it
The 8TB Ironwolf NAS drive's 7200 RPM spindle speed and 256MB cache and SATA 6.0Gb/s interface makes this a performance-focused mechanical drive rather than somewhere to store your rarely accessed files.
AgileArray provides RAID optimization and dual-plane balancing. Rotational vibration sensors can maintain consistent performance when several drives are running together.
In his 4-star review of the 8TB NAS drive, our expert Mark said: "IronWolf drives feature CMR technology and AgileArray firmware, ensuring smooth RAID performance, reduced vibration, and efficient power management. The 180TB per year workload rating, the RV sensors, the three-year warranty, and the bundled Rescue Data Recovery Services have all persisted as defining features of the consumer tier."
For more options, take a look at our roundups of the best desktop and laptop hard drives and best NAS hard drives.
Price context & historical value
Best Buy is currently selling the 8TB Seagate IronWolf for $349.99, which is a massive $167.66 reduction off the usual $517.65 asking price.
While that looks like a brilliant deal on paper, the exact same drive is $329.99 at Newegg, a saving of $187.66 against Best Buy's usual asking price. I've seen this price before back in August, and also previously suggested heading to Newegg. My advice hasn't changed.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the 8TB Seagate IronWolf NAS drive if...
You need a high-capacity drive to cope with the demands of an always-on NAS. The combination of 8TB capacity, CMR recording and 7200 RPM makes this a strong option for backups, media libraries, and shared files.
It's particularly well suited to multi-bay and RAID setups. AgileArray is designed to optimize RAID performance, while the built-in rotational vibration sensors help the drive maintain consistent operation when it's surrounded by other spinning hard drives.
❌ Skip the 8TB Seagate IronWolf NAS drive if...
You only need additional storage for an ordinary desktop PC. Although you can use an IronWolf as a conventional SATA hard drive, much of what you're paying for is specifically intended for NAS environments, including 24/7 operation, RAID optimization and vibration management.
Also consider
The larger 12TB IronWolf model combines 7200 RPM performance with a 256MB cache, up to 210MB/s read and write speeds, IronWolf Health Management, and included Data Recovery Services.
This Seagate IronWolf HDD provides 4TB of CMR storage, a 5400 RPM spindle speed, 256MB cache, SATA 6Gb/s connectivity, 24/7 operation, and a 180TB/year workload rating.
