articles.title: Discord
articles.text:
Discord is a cross-platform voice and text chat app originally designed for gamers, but since finding mainstream popularity, all kind of communities have migrated to it. Even TechSpot staff have moved away from Slack to use Discord full-time for team collaboration and communication.
Is Discord better than Zoom?
Zoom and Discord serve two different purposes. Discord is great for small and big team communication and collaboration via text or voice. Zoom is better suited for real-time online meetings and presentations.
Is Discord only for gamers?
Discord is great for gaming and voice chat. That's how Discord got started but today all kinds of communities have migrated to it. Just like Microsoft Teams or Slack, Discord offers public and private servers that anyone can create and join for free, and today it's widely used for team communication and collaboration.
Is Discord encrypted?
Discord uses basic encryption methods like TLS to protect text and images in transit but does not offer end-to-end encryption like WhatsApp or Telegram. Other community oriented platforms offer similar safety features for written messages, but some like Microsoft Teams do offer end-to-end encryption for VoIP calls.
Is Discord free?
Discord is free for voice, text, and video chat options with no restrictions. There is an optional "Nitro" paid membership that offers extra benefits, but even setting up a private server for your business can be done with no additional cost.
Is Discord safe?
Although Discord is a great messaging app, the platform does not offer end-to-end encryption for text or audio/video communication. While your data is encrypted in transit to Discord servers, it is stored on said servers. Even when you use the app's privacy settings to disable their ability to "Use data to improve Discord," they still collect this data and store it in their database.
Discord Nitro Basic and Nitro: What's the Difference?
Our most-popular Nitro plan unlocks access to all the available Nitro perks, including custom emoji and stickers anywhere, HD video streaming, and an expanded selection of our newly-released Activities, just to name a few.
Nitro Basic includes a selection of some of the most-loved Nitro features that help you better express yourself on Discord, including custom emoji anywhere, bigger file uploads, and more.
We're excited to continue growing Nitro and give users more ways to have fun and create lasting memories on Discord. In the United States, Nitro Basic will be available for $2.99 per month. For those living outside the United States, pricing is viewable within your User Settings > Nitro page once it's rolled out.
Features
Discord was created to bring people together around games. You've taught us that it can be used for so much more. People use Discord for all kinds of hanging out: from live karaoke nights, to screenshare group painting, to virtual wedding parties. People create Discord servers for gaming, yoga classes, comedy fan clubs, and even run entire podcasting businesses. Discord is for anyone who could use a place to talk with their friends and communities.
Download Discord and experience modern chat:
- Voice chat: Join voice channels and chat with your group
- Real-time messaging: Share video, images, and text in rich chat
- Push notifications: Never miss a thing with @mentions and direct messages
- Instant Invite: Easily add friends to your voice server by sharing the Instant Invite link
- Direct messages: Send one-to-one private messages
- Multiple server support: Manage all your game chat groups in one client
- Organizable channels: Keep discussions on topic through structured communication
What's New
It's October, which means we have entered the scariest part of the year. Not because 2026 is already 75% over, but because of ghosts, skeletons, and little green ghouls, buddy! We have some fresh, new spooky stuff we sent your way, like a special ringtone by The Living Tombstone and a positively ghastly loading animation. Make sure you read it because it will be on the exam.
Make Servers and Channels "Move To…" Easier
You just joined an emoji server that specializes in a mysterious puffer fish, and down it goes, immediately thrown in a server folder with the others. Now, instead of holding-and-dragging it allllll the way to your emoji server folder, you can right-click that bad boy and "Move to…" any folder you want! And it's not limited to just servers – you can also right-click channels to "Move to…" the category they belong to. You can even reorder entire folders with it!
Better Markdown Previews
When you upload a Markdown (.md) file, you'll now see the file rendered all nice and neat and pretty instead of with a bunch of symbols. This includes tables, formatting, all that good stuff. Totally great for when you're doing a casual Sunday-night sharing READMEs with your friends.
New Nitro Morsels + 1GB uploads
If you're a fancy Nitro member, you get two new perks: 20% off YouTube Premium for 6 months (Current and new subscribers, Terms apply.), and you can now upload files up to 1GB in size! Upload the entirety of your photos from your recent trip to Dinosaur, Colorado, or your sick skate videos of you doing an inward heelflip over the brontosaurus. 
Prettier Media Attachments
We recently rewrote our entire image and video-sharing media engine! The Engineers said they replaced the old C++ codebase with Rust, resulting in more accurate results, better-preserved colors, and improved reliability.
Previous Release Notes:
Make a BOLD first impression with new formatting tools on desktop to help put the finishing touches on your bio without having to memorize Markdown. Apparently, it's called a "WYSIWYG" editor, which is really fun to say. WYSIWYSIWYSIWIG.
We've shipped another portion of our User Settings redesign:
- Activity is now Games & Apps
- Content & Social is now Messaging Permissions
- Related settings, such as Authorized Apps/Connections and OS-specific pages/keybinds, have been consolidated for clarity.
- We've made language and style updates across several settings pages, including Data & Privacy and Activity Privacy.
We upgraded our Desktop client to using Electron 42, which aside from general maintenance best practices on our end, yielded some incremental improvements to CPU usage of our app.
Now it's time for a LOITWAODL, or: a List Of Improvements That Were Added On Discord Lately:
You can now set your profile as "Private." Blind others with the majesty of your bio with everyone, just smaller servers, or just those you actually have added as a friend.
Attach a note when sending a friend request so your future buddy knows why you're adding them, that way they won't ask "who the hell is this again??"
New spoiler channels make server members say "yeah man i wanna see it" before viewing a text channel, without moderators having to mark the entire channel as Age Restricted as a workaround.
On desktop, share a game by mentioning it. By typing @game, you can search for any game with a Discord profile and embed it in your message, like <@game Palworld> or <@game Sunderfolk>. Mobile support in the works!
Goggle-wearers rejoice: Discord's on Meta Quest! Keep the app pinned in your virtual environment while playing a VR game, or like, boiling eggs. With your headset on.
Frame your picture-perfect profile by adding one of the newest profile customization options in the Shop: Frames!

articles.title: Uber rival inDrive eyes 2027 robotaxi tests in Central Asia with Pony.ai and Nvidia | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ride-hailing company inDrive, known for letting passengers and drivers negotiate fares, is working with Chinese autonomous driving firm Pony.ai and Nvidia to begin testing robotaxis in Kazakhstan in 2027.
The companies said Friday that they had signed a memorandum of understanding to explore bringing Pony.ai’s robotaxis to inDrive’s platform — a reflection of the growing interest in self-driving technology beyond the U.S. and China.
Testing will begin in Kazakhstan’s capital, Astana, in the first half of 2027, inDrive CTO Yuri Misnik told TechCrunch. The tests will initially involve a safety operator, with fully driverless rides as the eventual goal.
Under the proposed plan, Pony.ai would provide its Gen-7 robotaxis, which inDrive would offer through its ride-hailing app and operate in Kazakhstan. Nvidia, on the other hand, would supply the AI technology, including its Hyperion platform and Halos safety system.
The move comes as ride-hailing companies expand their push into robotaxis. Earlier this month, Uber announced plans to test Pony.ai’s robotaxis in London, where it has also started offering supervised autonomous rides with British startup Wayve, an investor-backed partner. Uber is also working with multiple robotaxi companies in other markets, including the Middle East.
inDrive, which has built its business around affordable rides, is looking to bring a similar focus to autonomous ride-hailing as it explores a market where Uber and other rivals are already making moves.
“Our approach is capital-light by design,” said Misnik. “We work with a range of partners in different markets, combining their expertise with ours to deliver a better customer experience.”
Nvidia says its Hyperion platform could lower the cost of developing robotaxis by giving companies a ready-made foundation of sensors and computing technology, rather than requiring them to build and integrate everything themselves. The company also offers its Alpamayo model and tools to generate synthetic data and test autonomous driving systems across different driving scenarios.
“Those savings are particularly relevant in emerging markets, where ride-hailing is already relatively affordable and autonomous services need to compete on cost,” Ali Kani, Nvidia’s vice president of automotive, told TechCrunch.
The announcement coincides with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s first visit to Kazakhstan on Friday.
The Kazakhstan proposal would also add to Pony.ai’s ongoing push beyond China. The company aims to have more than 3,500 robotaxis operating in over 20 cities worldwide by the end of 2026, up from a fleet of 1,975 vehicles at the end of June.
Last month, Kazakhstan announced plans to launch autonomous taxi services in 2027, with initial trials planned in Astana and two other cities. It has also introduced rules for autonomous vehicles to be tested on certain public roads.
Astana’s harsh winters could make it a useful testing ground for robotaxis. The city, with a population of around 1.7 million, faces months of snow and ice, posing challenges for autonomous driving systems.
“Launching here will provide an important opportunity to evaluate autonomous driving technology in challenging winter conditions,” inDrive founder and CEO Arsen Tomsky said. “Success in Astana could offer valuable insights for expanding autonomous mobility to other locations facing similar challenges.”
Kazakhstan is not the only market where inDrive is exploring robotaxis. In December, the company signed a separate agreement with Saudi Arabia’s AI Driver to explore deploying autonomous vehicles powered by Chinese self-driving firm WeRide, starting with Riyadh. The companies had targeted a pilot in the first half of 2026, though it remains unclear whether testing has begun.
“We are also looking at a number of other markets for future deployments,” said Misnik. “One of the main requisites for successful launch in our view is a favorable and collaborative regulatory environment to facilitate safe and sustainable testing on the roads.”
inDrive operates in more than 1,200 cities across 47 countries. The company has also expanded beyond ride-hailing into delivery, intercity transportation, and financial services.

articles.title: Shiprocket’s fastrr taps food commerce with new restaurant partnerships
articles.text:
Shiprocket’s fastrr taps food commerce with new restaurant partnerships
Shiprocket’s fastrr has partnered with Punjabi Angithi operator Vegorama Group and Bikkgane Biryani to expand into food commerce, helping the brands manage direct orders, customer engagement and hyperlocal deliveries.
Shiprocket’s AI-native commerce platform, fastrr, has entered the food commerce segment through partnerships with Vegorama Group, which operates Punjabi Angithi, and Bikkgane Biryani.
The partnerships come as restaurant brands explore ways to drive orders through their own digital channels rather than relying solely on third-party food aggregators. Direct channels can also give restaurants greater access to customer data and more opportunities to engage with diners after a purchase.
Under the partnerships, the brands will use fastrr’s tools for customer identification, order management and marketing. Fastrr Identity and fastrr Signals will help identify high-intent and returning customers and flag potential return-to-origin (RTO) and cash-on-delivery (COD) risks before an order is placed, the company said in a statement.
Fastrr Ads will support performance campaigns measured against delivered orders, while its WhatsApp tools will be used to follow up on abandoned orders and send offers and reorder reminders, it added.
Shiprocket Quick’s multi-partner rider network will handle hyperlocal deliveries from individual outlets, with live tracking for orders placed through the brands’ direct channels. The partnership also covers influencer-led campaigns for Vegorama Group and packaging and design support for both brands.
The companies also plan to explore selling direct-to-consumer food products through their websites and quick-commerce platforms.
“The next phase of growth in food commerce lies in building lasting customer relationships that translate into repeat business for them. For restaurants, every order is an opportunity to build familiarity, understand what customers value and give them a reason to return. We believe brands should have the ability to build that relationship directly, rather than have it mediated entirely by third-party platforms,” said Gaurav Mangla, CEO, Ads and Checkout, Shiprocket.
“This is the opportunity we see in food commerce, and one we are working with our partners to unlock. Fastrr by Shiprocket brings together the capabilities needed to support this journey, while helping restaurant businesses strengthen their digital presence and explore new avenues for growth.”
For customers, the brands’ direct ordering channels will offer access to menus, offers and reorder reminders through WhatsApp. The brands also plan to introduce direct-to-consumer (D2C) food products through their own channels.
Shiprocket said it plans to extend its food-commerce offering to more restaurant chains, quick-service restaurants and cloud kitchens. It is also exploring categories such as bakeries, desserts, beverages and packaged foods. Some of the planned features include menu-based checkout, loyalty programmes, reorder reminders and delivery allocation during peak hours.

articles.title: Après la panne, Orange doit gérer un autre problème : plusieurs services sont suspendus à cause des failles PHP
articles.text:
Orange traverse actuellement une forte période de turbulence. Ce mercredi 21 octobre, l’opérateur a été victime d’une panne majeure, privant une partie conséquente de ses clients de réseau. Contacté par nos soins, l’entreprise a expliqué que l’« incident technique a eu lieu sur un équipement de [son] nouveau cœur de réseau ». Orange a d’ailleurs annoncé faire un geste de dédommagement pour les clients touchés par la panne. À cette panne s’ajoutent deux failles PHP critiques qui touchent des centaines de millions de sites web à travers le monde. Une situation qui se révèle être un véritable casse-tête pour tout le monde, y compris Orange. En effet, l’opérateur a annoncé suspendre l’accès à certains de ses sites et à certaines applications utilisant PHP.
Orange annonce suspendre l’accès à certains de ses sites et applications
Dans un communiqué, Orange annonce « suspendre temporairement l’accès à certains sites et applications utilisant PHP ». L’objectif : éviter toute tentative de cyberattaque en coupant purement et simplement l’accès aux services concernés. L’opérateur explique que « cette décision a permis de déployer les correctifs de sécurité nécessaires et de réaliser les vérifications associées avant la remise en service progressive des sites et applications ». Les correctifs auraient déjà été déployés sur une grande partie des sites concernés.
Orange ne précise toutefois pas les services et applications qui sont concernés par cette suspension temporaire. Nous savons seulement que « cette mesure préventive concerne quelques sites web, services et applications au sein de plusieurs filiales et entités du Groupe Orange ».
Combien de temps va durer cette suspension de certains services d’Orange ?
Autant le dire tout de suite, nous ne savons pas combien de temps durera cette suspension. L’opérateur prendra sans aucun doute le temps qu’il faut pour empêcher toute intrusion malveillante qui pourrait lui être particulièrement préjudiciable. Quelques heures de services hors ligne doivent certainement valoir mieux que de risquer une cyberattaque.
Orange assure que ses équipes sont mobilisées « pour rétablir les services concernés dans les meilleurs délais et en toute sécurité ». Enfin, notons qu’Orange présente ses excuses aux clients et utilisateurs impactés. La panne dont a été victime Orange ce 21 octobre est désormais résolue. Il va falloir maintenant attendre que l’opérateur sécurise ses services et applications utilisant PHP. Patience donc.

articles.title: Weltraumteleskop Euclid entdeckt ganz nebenbei einen unbekannten Kometen
articles.text:
Per Zufall: Weltraumteleskop Euclid entdeckt unbekannten Kometen
Euclids eigentliche Aufgabe ist ambitioniert: Das Weltraumteleskop der Europäischen Raumfahrtbehörde ESA soll eine dreidimensionale Karte des Universums erstellen. Die Daten sollen auch dabei helfen, Dunkle Materie und Dunkle Energie besser zu verstehen.
Seit dem Missionsstart des Teleskops im Juli 2023 hat Euclid bereits beeindruckende Aufnahmen geliefert. Erst im Juni 2026 veröffentlichte die ESA etwa eine Aufnahme des Zentrums der Milchstraße, auf der mehr als 60 Millionen Sterne zu sehen sind.
Die Entdeckung eines Kometen durch das Weltraumteleskop kommt dagegen unerwartet. Zu verdanken ist der Zufallsfund einer Software, die gezielt nach beweglichen Objekten in astronomischen Aufnahmen sucht.
Euclid beobachtet eigentlich Galaxien – so gelang jetzt der Kometenfund
Für die Kartierung von Galaxien nimmt Euclid große Himmelsbereiche auf und nutzt dafür die sogenannte „Step-and-stare“-Methode. Dabei wird der „Blick“ des Teleskops für einige Zeit auf einen Himmelsausschnitt gerichtet, um eine längere Belichtung zu ermöglichen. Dann ist der nächste Ausschnitt dran. Jeder Bereich wird dabei in der Regel nur einmal erfasst.
Durch diese Art der Aufnahme sind bewegliche Objekte wie Kometen in den Bildern meist schwer zu erkennen. Sie „huschen“ durchs Bild und sind nur als Lichtspur zu sehen. Mikko Pöntinen von der Universität Helsinki hat deshalb eine spezielle Software zum Erkennen beweglicher Objekte entwickelt – und im September 2026 direkt einen großen Fang gemacht: einen bislang unbekannten Kometen.
„Ich war begeistert, als meine Software einen über mehrere Bilder verschmierten Streifen markierte – das Ergebnis eines sich schnell bewegenden Objekts. Durch die Vorhersage seiner Position konnte ich es in weiteren Bildern identifizieren und fand es insgesamt in fünf Bildsätzen“, sagt Pöntinen in der Pressemitteilung der ESA.
Der neu entdeckte Komet erhielt den Namen C/2026 S1 (Euclid). Er ist derzeit rund 1,3 Milliarden Kilometer von der Erde entfernt und bewegt sich nicht auf der gleichen „horizontalen“ Ebene wie die Planeten unseres Sonnensystems, sondern von der Sonne aus gesehen „nach oben“. Seine steile Bahn könnte bedeuten, dass der Komet Tausende Jahre brauchen wird, um die Sonne zu umrunden.
Entdeckung könnte zukünftigen ESA-Missionen helfen
Der Fund ist mehr als eine astronomische Randnotiz. Er zeigt, dass sich große wissenschaftliche Datensätze mithilfe spezialisierter Algorithmen auch für Entdeckungen nutzen lassen, die über die ursprünglichen Ziele einer Mission hinausgehen.
Pöntinens Software wurde entwickelt, um bewegliche Objekte im Sonnensystem in Euclids Aufnahmen zu erkennen. Das hilft nicht nur bei der Suche nach bislang unbekannten Himmelskörpern, sondern kann auch die Auswertung der Galaxienbilder unterstützen: Bewegliche Objekte lassen sich so besser identifizieren und von den übrigen Bilddaten unterscheiden.
Auch für künftige Missionen könnte die Methode wertvoll sein. Die ESA sieht in der Entdeckung einen Testfall für das Zusammenspiel mit dem geplanten Projekt „Comet Interceptor“. Die Mission soll einen geeigneten Kometen möglichst früh nach seiner Entdeckung ansteuern und untersuchen. Dafür müssen solche Objekte rechtzeitig gefunden und ihre Flugbahnen bestimmt werden.

articles.title: L’éditeur de Norton et Avast retrouve vos chatbots IA et note leur confidentialité
articles.text:
Gen, la maison mère de Norton et d’Avast, a lancé en bêta l’AI Data Checker. À partir d’une adresse e-mail, l’outil retrouve les services d’IA que vous utilisez et note la façon dont ils traitent vos données.
L’éditeur des solutions antivirus explique que près d’un utilisateur d’ordinateur sur trois interagit déjà avec des services d’IA agentique, des assistants capables d’agir à notre place pour acheter, préparer un voyage ou gérer ses finances. Reste à savoir ce que ces outils font des données auxquelles ils ont accès.
15 questions, une lettre : comment Gen note la confidentialité des IA
Il suffit de saisir son adresse e-mail ou son nom d’utilisateur. L'outil affiche alors les applications d’IA liées à cet identifiant, ainsi que des comptes hors IA où des informations personnelles ont pu être partagées. Chaque service a son rapport sur la collecte des données, l’usage pour l'entraînement des LLM, le temps de conservation de ces données et la présence de réglages de confidentialité. Notons que pour lancer la recherche, il est nécessaire de confirmer avoir 18 ans ou plus et prendre connaissance de la notice de confidentialité de Gen.
Gen explique vouloir simplifier les recherches pour les utilisateurs et notamment leur éviter d’avoir à lire de longues politiques de confidentialité. Pour établir ses notes, l’entreprise analyse la politique de confidentialité et les conditions d’utilisation de chaque application. Elle répond ensuite à 15 questions. Chacune des réponses cite précisément le texte, que Gen dit vérifier mot pour mot. Il en résulte une lettre de A+ à F. Une application sans politique de confidentialité reçoit d’office un F. Pour les assistants capables d’acheter, de réserver ou d’envoyer des messages, 10 % de la note porte sur la sécurité, et notamment le comportement du chatbot face aux sites potentiellement dangereux.
Sur la page d’accueil, chaque application affiche aussi un niveau de risque. ChatGPT est en risque moyen, avec la mention d’une publicité personnalisée possible sur les offres Free et Go. Claude et Gemini sont en risque faible, même si l’outil précise qu’ils s’entraînent par défaut sur les données des utilisateurs. L’entraînement n’est donc pas le seul critère retenu. Notons qu’ironiquement l'outil de Gen s’appuie lui-même sur l’IA, qu’il peut se tromper et que ses rapports sont à vérifier.
L’AI Data Checker est le dernier outil de l’Agent Trust Hub, lancé en février par Gen. Celui-ci compte aussi un VPN pour agents et Sage, une couche de sécurité accessible via Norton AI Agent Protection. Cette dernière a été lancée en bêta dans Norton 360. Elle s’intercale entre l'agent et ce qu’il veut faire, laisse passer une action normale, bloque une action dangereuse et demande une validation humaine en cas de doute.
Reste que dans les faits, Gen nous demande de saisir notre adresse email pour opérer une vérification. Côté confidentialité, l’éditeur antivirus affirme ne pas vendre les données personnelles. L’adresse e-mail saisie est conservée en clair sur les serveurs, séparément des données de l’analyse. En revanche, les durées de conservation restent vagues. Les résultats sont supprimés après une durée limitée, sans délai précis. Une connexion Gmail facultative permet de chercher, sur deux ans, les e-mails envoyés par des applications connues. Gen n’en lit que les métadonnées (expéditeur, objet, date), mais Google demande la permission gmail.modify, qui autorise la modification de la boîte. Gen dit ne pas pouvoir demander une lecture seule et compte s’en servir plus tard pour effectuer des demandes de retrait ou de suppression au nom des utilisateurs. L’adresse Gmail connectée est enregistrée sur les serveurs, et l’accès est révoqué à la fin du scan. La politique de confidentialité cite aussi plusieurs prestataires, dont xAI pour analyser les politiques des applications. La politique de confidentialité ne précise pas si des données quittent l’Union européenne.

articles.title: Thomson Reuters folds AI into its professional tax and audit software - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Thomson Reuters folds AI into its professional tax and audit software
Thomson Reuters Corp. today is launching a rebuilt version of its CoCounsel Tax, Audit & Accounting platform designed to move beyond answering questions to planning assignments, performing calculations and producing documents for professional review.
The enhanced platform combines artificial intelligence agents with client information, tax research and code execution to complete complex tasks such as building amortization schedules, preparing spreadsheets and drafting memos. The company said the new platform is available to all U.S. customers.
The release targets a challenge in applying generative AI to professional services: A mathematically correct answer can still be wrong if the system uses the wrong tax rule, overlooks client circumstances or fails to explain its reasoning.
“They expect close to perfection with any tool that they use,” Chief Product Officer David Wong said of tax accountants during a briefing.
Unlike its predecessor, which was designed around individual tasks, the rebuilt system can break complex requests into steps and select tools and information needed to execute them, Wong said. Professionals still must review and verify the results. The system provides citations, assumptions and calculations to help them assess its conclusions before approving work.
The research database is Checkpoint, Thomson Reuters’ collection of more than 12 million primary-source and analytical documents, maintained by hundreds of experts. The platform supports multiple AI models.
In a demonstration, David Ragones, head of product for direct tax and audit, showed how CoCounsel could use a commercial loan agreement and a firm’s spreadsheet template to produce an amortization schedule for a $5 million loan. The example included changing interest rates, a lump-sum payment and a balloon payment at maturity.
The resulting workbook contained live formulas, supporting assumptions and references. Users can select individual cells and ask CoCounsel to explain the calculations and their sources.
The demo also showed the system recalculating spreadsheet results using Python routines as a check on their accuracy. “A lot of times showing the work is actually doing the work,” said Lucas Adams, Thomson Reuters’ vice president of engineering.
Security controls limit agents to files permitted by the user’s access and the relevant workspace. Adams said those restrictions extend into the underlying infrastructure. Internet access is limited to approved government websites alongside Checkpoint.
A shared client context layer preserves uploaded documents and completed work across conversations, reducing the need to repeatedly supply background information. Integrations include Thomson Reuters’ UltraTax, Engagement Manager and Guided Assurance.
Support for Model Context Protocol allows connections with other systems and access to cited tax and accounting answers through third-party AI tools, including Anthropic PBC’s Claude and Microsoft Corp.’s Copilot.
Wong said staffing shortages are helping drive demand as firms seek to handle workloads without expanding seasonal hiring. Thomson Reuters also sees an opportunity to free professionals for advisory work.
Executives acknowledged that the practical test is whether reviewing AI output takes less effort than producing it manually. “If it takes just as much time to verify the work than it takes to do the work, AI is not really helpful,” Adams said.

articles.title: Vender ropa usada de famosos en internet, se volvió el negocio de influencers: Amara que linda, Paola Turbay y Laura Acuña
articles.text:
Seguir a una celebridad en redes sociales dejó de ser la única forma de sentirse cerca de ella: hoy es posible comprar la ropa que esa persona usó en un evento, un video o una aparición en televisión.
Figuras públicas colombianas como Amara Qué Linda, Paola Turbay y Laura Acuña abrieron sus clósets para vender prendas que formaron parte de su vida pública y cotidiana, en un modelo que combina la cercanía con el fanático y el consumo responsable de moda.
La posibilidad resulta llamativa porque invierte la lógica habitual del mercado de segunda mano. En GoTrendier, en lugar de comprar una prenda genérica usada, el comprador puede elegir una pieza con una historia concreta: la chaqueta que una influenciadora llevó en un video, el vestido que una presentadora usó en un evento de gala o el vestuario que una cantante lució en un concierto.
Esa trazabilidad convierte la compra en algo más cercano a adquirir un recuerdo que a renovar el armario.
Qué celebridades venden ropa usada en Colombia
Amara Qué Linda, creadora de contenido nacida en Bogotá en 2003 y con más de cuatro millones de seguidores en TikTok, comparte en su espacio prendas de estilo urbano y juvenil, acordes con el público que sigue su contenido sobre moda y estilo de vida. Su inventario cambia con frecuencia, lo que permite encontrar piezas asociadas a producciones recientes.
La presentadora, Paola Turbay, exvirreina universal de la belleza y recordada por su protagónico en Ana de nadie, ofrece prendas de diseñador y piezas de alta gama que han formado parte de su trayectoria en la vida pública.
La presentadora Laura Acuña, conocida por su formato digital La Sala de Laura Acuña, dispone de una sección especial dedicada a vestuario de diseñador, con piezas utilizadas en programas de televisión y eventos de gala.
A esta lista se suman otras figuras colombianas que también venden sus prendas, entre ellas Fanny Lu, Alejandra Azcárate, Sara Uribe, Kimberly Reyes, Marcela Mar, Sebastián Villalobos, Raúl Ocampo, Flavia Dos Santos, Angélica Blandón y Marcela Carvajal. En varios casos, parte de lo recaudado se destina a fundaciones y causas sociales, lo que añade un componente solidario a la transacción.
Desde un vestido de novia hasta prendas de uso diario
El catálogo de artículos disponibles no se limita a ropa casual. Ana Jiménez, country manager de GoTrendier en Colombia y cofundadora, relató uno de los casos más llamativos registrados hasta ahora.
“Se compran y se venden hasta vestidos de novia. Hace aproximadamente un mes, Marcela Carvajal vendió su vestido de novia vintage Carolina Herrera a una usuaria que estaba feliz de estrenarlo el día de su boda”, explicó.
“Así que sí, se vende absolutamente de todo. Incluso las cosas que uno pensaría imposible, eso se está comprando y vendiendo”, agregó Jiménez. El testimonio ilustra hasta qué punto la demanda por adquirir una prenda con historia propia puede extenderse a objetos que, en otro contexto, permanecerían guardados como recuerdo personal.
La compra de ropa usada por figuras públicas plantea un desafío distinto al de una tienda convencional: la verificación de que la prenda realmente perteneció a esa persona. Por eso, cada publicación suele incluir fotografías o referencias de la pieza, un detalle que funciona como respaldo frente a los compradores.
Este tipo de transacción también depende de que el proceso completo, desde la publicación hasta el envío, ocurra dentro de un mismo sistema, sin que comprador y vendedor deban coordinar un encuentro presencial. Esa estructura permite que una persona en otra ciudad pueda adquirir con tranquilidad una prenda que vio en televisión o en redes sociales, sin más contacto que el de la plataforma donde se concreta la compra.
La ropa que antes solo era visible en una pantalla ahora puede formar parte del armario de cualquier persona, un giro que redefine la manera en que el público se relaciona con sus referentes. Más allá de la transacción comercial, esta modalidad plantea una forma distinta de admiración, donde el acercamiento a una celebridad ya no depende únicamente de una fotografía o un comentario en redes, sino de un objeto físico con una historia compartida.

articles.title: Android 17 pourrait faire disparaitre votre angoisse des notifications sur les Pixel
articles.text:
La dernière bêta d’Android 17 pourrait bien ravir les angoissés de la notification. Google préparerait une nouveauté permettant enfin de personnaliser l’affichage des notifications sur l’écran d’accueil des Google Pixel. Depuis Android 8, les smartphones dépourvus de surcouche affichent généralement les notifications non lues sous la forme d’un simple point sur les icônes des applications. Un choix qui rassure ceux qui préfèrent ne pas compter les messages en attente, mais qui frustre les adeptes des compteurs numériques. Avec Android 17, ces deux mondes pourraient enfin trouver un terrain d’entente.
Trois options à venir
Dans la version d’Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2, les équipes d’Android Authority ont réussi à activer un nouveau menu dans le code des paramètres du Launcher. Situé dans la section notification, ce dernier s’intitule sobrement « Badges de notifications ».
Une fois activé, celui-ci permettrait de choisir entre trois modes d’affichage : un compteur numérique indiquant le nombre de notifications, le traditionnel point de notification ou bien une désactivation complète des indicateurs.
Pour le moment, cette fonction est encore en développement. Il faudra patienter avant de pouvoir la tester officiellement lors d’une prochaine bêta d’Android.

articles.title: Los agentes de IA ya se mueven por cuentas bancarias y algunas entidades de EEUU se preparan para lo peor
articles.text:
Agentes, agentes y más agentes. Estos sistemas de inteligencia artificial capaces de ejecutar tareas con cierto grado de autonomía están apareciendo en servicios, aplicaciones y herramientas que utilizamos cada día. Y ahora también están entrando en cuentas bancarias. Algunos clientes ya les están permitiendo acceder para que actúen en su nombre, justo cuando todavía estamos aprendiendo hasta dónde pueden llegar, cómo interpretan nuestras instrucciones y qué ocurre cuando se equivocan. Para las entidades estadounidenses, esa combinación ha empezado a convertirse en un problema difícil de ignorar.
La puerta la abre el cliente. Aquí no estamos hablando, al menos principalmente, de bots que irrumpen en una cuenta bancaria tras vulnerar los sistemas de una entidad. Axios describe sobre todo otro escenario: usuarios que permiten a un agente acceder con sus credenciales para que opere por ellos. El matiz es importante porque una cosa es contar con el permiso del titular y otra muy distinta cumplir las reglas de acceso de su banco. JPMorgan ya ha explicado que bloquea, cuando puede, servicios que funcionan mediante este tipo de intercambio de credenciales, una práctica que considera insegura.
El problema empieza después. Tener acceso no significa únicamente poder consultar un saldo. Según Axios, los ejecutivos bancarios temen especialmente qué puede ocurrir cuando un agente cuenta también con autoridad para realizar compras o mover fondos, porque entonces una instrucción mal interpretada puede convertirse en una acción financiera real. Y hay una segunda inquietud: las fuentes consultadas aseguran que algunas entidades han observado agentes contactando con centros de atención o realizando acciones que parecen independientes de las instrucciones del usuario. La palabra importante es "parecen": todavía no sabemos si esos sistemas actuaron realmente por su cuenta.
Distinguir humanos ya no basta. Unos datos de acceso válidos ya no bastan para resolver una cuestión mucho más compleja: quién está actuando realmente detrás de ellos. Los agentes complican todavía más esa ecuación. Varias fuentes bancarias consultadas para la investigación explicaron que sus sistemas no siempre pueden distinguir la actividad de una persona de la ejecutada por una herramienta de IA, ni determinar con certeza si esta última está siguiendo una orden legítima del titular. Eso obliga al sector a enfrentarse a una pregunta nueva: no solo quién tiene acceso, sino quién está tomando realmente cada decisión.
Prepararse para el día después. La preocupación ha llegado al punto de que varias entidades ya trabajan no solo para restringir estos accesos, sino también para responder si algo sale mal. Las fuentes de la investigación hablan de los "peores escenarios" y de planes para el "día después", pensados para asegurar o restaurar rápidamente el acceso de un cliente a su cuenta. Según Axios, Morgan Stanley ha empezado a bloquear agentes de terceros, mientras que JPMorgan, Bank of America y Citi también están imponiendo restricciones.Wells Fargo, por su parte, ya ha incorporado los agentes de IA a las condiciones que entrarán en vigor el 24 de noviembre: contempla expresamente acciones no deseadas, errores en la interpretación de instrucciones y casos en los que un agente exceda la autoridad concedida por el cliente.
Los atacantes también tienen agentes. Mientras los bancos intentan gestionar las herramientas que sus propios clientes dejan entrar, existe otro problema completamente diferente. Una investigación publicada por The Information revela que CyberCartel recurrió a varios agentes de IA para automatizar operaciones contra más de 400 objetivos financieros latinoamericanos. Straiker, la firma que reconstruyó su infraestructura, encontró modelos de Claude coordinando tareas y agentes basados en Grok participando en la recopilación de información. Aquí no hay clientes concediendo permisos: hablamos directamente de una operación ofensiva organizada por ciberdelincuentes.
Los agentes no van a desaparecer. El propio sector asume que los clientes querrán seguir utilizando estas herramientas, así que el debate no parece encaminado a expulsarlas por completo de la banca. Muchas entidades ya permiten o avanzan hacia accesos de solo lectura, una fórmula que deja consultar información sin conceder capacidad para actuar sobre ella. La cuestión será decidir hasta dónde queremos delegar. Porque cuanto más poder demos a estos sistemas, más importante será saber qué pueden hacer, cómo comprobar que siguen nuestras instrucciones y quién responde cuando el resultado no es el que esperábamos.

articles.title: “Pirate la Switch 2, ne fais aucune erreur” : un chercheur confie la mission à une IA, la console de Nintendo cède
articles.text:
“Pirate la Switch 2, ne fais aucune erreur” : un chercheur confie la mission à une IA, la console de Nintendo cède
Seize mois après son lancement, la Switch 2 vient de tomber, à jour, sans la moindre puce soudée. Derrière ce premier jailbreak logiciel, on trouve un chercheur en sécurité et un obscur logiciel de programmation venu de la Switch 1. Il y a aussi une intelligence artificielle, lâchée sur la console avec une consigne aussi brève que culottée.
Le 22 octobre 2026, le chercheur en sécurité Sammy Hajhamid, alias pepsipu, a publié ns2jb, qu'il présente comme le premier jailbreak purement logiciel de la Switch 2. Il fonctionne sur le firmware 23.0.1, déployé par Nintendo le 30 septembre. Il autorise les homebrews, la modification des jeux et l'extraction des sauvegardes. Démonstration à l'appui : Mario Kart World accueille désormais Peter Griffin, Hatsune Miku, Red d'Angry Birds et Walter White.
i jailbroke the nintendo switch 2
so i modded cinnamoroll, peter griffin, hatsune miku, and more into Mario Kart World, a switch 2 exclusive
now watch my friends and i get cooked by bots
learn more and get the exploit https://t.co/ykjgyfrFRppic.twitter.com/BOcFhejRz1
— pepsipu (@pepsipu) October 22, 2026
Comment l'IA d'OpenAI a trouvé la faille de la Switch 2
Le chercheur a d'abord bâti un banc d'essai autour d'une Switch et d'une Switch 2. Deux boîtiers JetKVM donnent à Codex, l'agent de programmation d'OpenAI, des yeux sur l'écran et des doigts sur la manette. Un petit robot Bluetooth enfonce le bouton d'alimentation à chaque plantage.
	
Fixe-toi pour objectif de jailbreaker la Switch 2. Ne fais aucune erreur.
L'IA a commencé par s'attaquer au navigateur WebKit, sans succès. Le chercheur a alors misé sur la rétrocompatibilité, car les jeux Switch 1 ont été compilés pour une machine dépourvue de la protection PAC. Dans SmileBASIC 4, l'atelier de programmation de SmileBoom, Codex a déniché un dépassement d'entier dans la commande REMOVE. Hajhamid a ensuite repéré une seconde brèche dans le module qui gère les fichiers. Elle lui a ouvert l'exécution de code avec les droits des services système.
Switch 2 piratée : un jailbreak fragile que Nintendo peut vite refermer
L'exploit est "tethered" : il s'évapore à chaque redémarrage. D'après GBAtemp, il réclame SmileBASIC 4 en version 4.4.9 et un PC branché sur le même réseau local. Aucun firmware modifié permanent, façon Atmosphère sur Switch 1, n'existe encore.
Gezine, auteur d'un exploit distinct dévoilé en juillet, dit avoir échangé avec pepsipu et juge ses travaux "légitimes, en apparence".
Talked with this guy.
Seems legit.
Also he knew what was my userland exploit 
(different with what he posted)
So I will post it in github in few days. https://t.co/ExxGnODnsZ
— Gezine (@gezine_dev) October 22, 2026
Nintendo connaît la parade. En 2016, le SmileBASIC de la 3DS avait disparu près d'un mois de l'eShop nord-américain pour une faille similaire. Hajhamid l'anticipe et songe déjà à porter son attaque vers le navigateur intégré, que Kyoto ne peut pas retirer de la vente.

articles.title: Ryzen 5800X3D Revival was Lisa Su's Initiative, and Other Interesting Details in AMD Interview with MyNavi Tech+
articles.text:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Ryzen 5800X3D Revival was Lisa Su's Initiative, and Other Interesting Details in AMD Interview with MyNavi Tech+
Japanese tech publication MyNavi Tech+ interviewed Travis Kirsch, the client-segment product manager for AMD, and there are some interesting excerpts from the conversation. It turns out that reviving Ryzen 7 5800X3D for the Socket AM4 market earlier this year, was an initiative going as far up as CEO Lisa Su. The effort required certain manufacturing process updates with TSMC to ensure they can build new 5800X3D chips that are identical in specs to the original ones, without having to revive deprecated manufacturing processes. 
AMD says that 5800X3D AM4 Anniversary Edition was released as a parting gift to the loyal Socket AM4 crowd that's holding on to DDR4 memory in the wake of brutal overpricing of DDR5. It was planned to help users better plan their transition to AM5 and DDR5 memory. The 5800X3D offers contemporary levels of performance with games, and its re-launch triggered a new wave of product launches from motherboard vendors.Next up, AMD was quizzed on why it decided to launch the Ryzen 7 7700X3D based on the slightly older "Zen 4" microarchitecture instead of the "Ryzen 7 9700X3D" positioned below the 9800X3D and 9850X3D. The company said that it wanted to use up its volumes of "Raphael" chips. Launching a "9700X3D" would've meant eating into the common stock of "Granite Ridge" chips meant for higher 9850X3D SKUs.
When asked to comment on the state of the memory market, Kirsch said that the current situation with the memory pricing is beyond anyone's control, and AMD has to respond to market realities ensuring consumers get an AMD-powered PC regardless of the price-point. The company still has an active Socket AM4 product line, including the top performing 5800X3D. 
Tech+ then steered towards the juicy topic of why AMD isn't offering entry-level Ryzen 3 SKUs, leaving Intel uncontested in that segment, to which AMD responded that the component market for Ryzen 3 is "small," and that the focus for the company is premium gaming. 
Lastly, AMD confirmed that the upcoming "Zen 6" microarchitecture will continue to see a common CCD being shared between consumer and enterprise products, and the company's strategy remains unchanged in this regard. Having a common CCD lets AMD build these chiplets at scale and dynamically allocate them between vastly diverse product lines.

articles.title: iPhone Duo: segunda geração pode receber Face ID sob a tela • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
iPhone Duo: segunda geração pode receber Face ID sob a tela
Apple já testa protótipos com biometria facial. Primeiro modelo usa Touch ID e chegou ao Brasil por R$ 21.999.
A Apple já estaria testando protótipos do iPhone Duo 2 com o sistema Face ID escondido sob a tela externa. A mudança permitiria que a segunda geração do dobrável recuperasse a biometria facial presente nos iPhones tradicionais sem precisar criar um recorte maior no display.
A informação foi divulgada nesta quinta-feria (22/10) pelo jornalista Mark Gurman, da Bloomberg. Segundo ele, o modelo é previsto para chegar entre setembro e dezembro de 2027.
O primeiro iPhone Duo usa Touch ID integrado ao botão lateral, em uma solução parecida com a do iPad Air e do iPad mini. A Apple optou pelo leitor de digitais porque o formato fino do dobrável deixa pouco espaço interno para os componentes do sistema.
A decisão se tornou uma das principais críticas ao aparelho nas primeiras análises publicadas nos Estados Unidos. O 9to5Mac afirmou que voltar a tocar no botão lateral parece um retrocesso depois de anos usando o reconhecimento facial.
Nos protótipos citados por Gurman, os componentes de autenticação facial estariam posicionados sob a tela externa. Isso permitiria que a Apple adotasse o Face ID sem acrescentar um grande recorte no painel. Os testes indicam ainda que a Apple pode tentar antecipar seus planos. Em setembro, Gurman estimava que o Face ID e uma câmera teleobjetiva poderiam aparecer apenas na terceira geração do Duo.
Vale destacar que a Apple trabalha há anos para tentar esconder componentes do Face ID. Os iPhones 18 Pro, por exemplo, usam uma câmera infravermelha posicionada sob o display, tecnologia que ajudou a reduzir o tamanho da Ilha Dinâmica.
Enquanto a Apple testa a suposta próxima geração, o primeiro iPhone Duo começa a chegar oficialmente aos consumidores nesta sexta-feira (23/10). No Brasil, o dobrável parte de R$ 21.999 na versão com 256 GB. Os modelos de 512 GB, 1 TB e 2 TB custam R$ 23.499, R$ 26.499 e R$ 30.999, respectivamente.
A procura alongou bastante os prazos. Alguns pedidos podem ter entrega prevista apenas para janeiro de 2027. A Apple abriu as reservas no país em 16 de outubro, uma semana antes da estreia oficial.
O primeiro Duo traz telas de 5,4 e 7,6 polegadas, chip A20 Pro e duas câmeras traseiras de 48 megapixels. A segunda geração é esperada para 2027.

articles.title: AMD Ryzen 5 5500F review: Vermeer rides again for budget gaming PCs
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
A necessary update for PC builders on a budget, improving gaming performance by 8% over the 5500 and adding in PCIe 4.0 support.
Reasons to buy
- + Bundled Wraith Stealth cooler
- + PCIe 4.0
- + 8-10% faster than 5500
- + Slots into existing AM4 motherboards
Reasons to avoid
- - Core i3-14100F is still 2.9% faster in games at 1080p
- - Pricing has risen to ~$120
- - Limited to 16 MB L3, like Cezanne APUs
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
We often criticise companies for misleading marketing, which typically falls in the direction of deceitful overpromising. With the Ryzen 5 5500F, we have the opposite problem. Its name and branding undersell what AMD is offering here. It’s a marked improvement over the base Ryzen 5 5500, giving AMD better standing among the best budget CPUs.
The 5500F is a Zen 3 CPU from the Vermeer family of chips, packing six cores, 12 threads, and a boost clock of 4.4 GHz. It’s modest by the standards of the best CPUs for gaming, but it also comes in at a suggested retail price of just $100. Those prices have drifted up toward $120, though hopefully they’ll settle down around list price before long.
Along with a 200 MHz jump in boost clock speeds over the 5500, the 5500F critically comes with access to PCIe 4.0. The original 5500 came from the Cezanne family of APUs, which all use monolithic dies and are limited to PCIe 3.0. Although the 5500F lives in the Vermeer family alongside the main Zen 3 stack, it’s still limited to the 16 MB of L3 cache that characterizes Cezanne (Vermeer chips have access to 32 MB of L3 otherwise).
The chip squarely targets Intel’s Core i3-14100F, a quad-core CPU available for around $100 that offers 11% better gaming performance at 1080p on average compared to the base 5500. The new 5500F tightens that gap to just 2.9%, and it manages to outclass Intel in multithreaded performance while offering a 10% average jump over the base 5500.
AMD Ryzen 5 5500F specifications and pricing
AMD gave the Ryzen 5 5500F a bad name. The “F” suffix across both AMD and Intel is typically used to note chips that lack integrated graphics. And indeed, the Ryzen 5 5500F does lack integrated graphics. But so does the Ryzen 5 5500. In reality, the Ryzen 5 5500F isn’t a re-released CPU with the iGPU sliced off, as F-series processors usually are, but rather an updated Ryzen 5 5500 that comes with better specs and, in turn, better performance.
If there’s any chip that falls in the bucket of a re-released CPU with the iGPU cut off, it’s the original Ryzen 5 5500, not this new F-suffix variant. The Ryzen 5 5500 comes from the Cezanne family of Zen 3 CPUs. These chips use the Zen 3 microarchitecture, but they have only 16MB of L3 cache and are limited to PCIe 3.0. Out of the full Cezanne family, the Ryzen 5 5500 is the only chip that isn’t either an APU like the Ryzen 5 5600G, or a laptop chip.
The newer Ryzen 5 5500F is from the Vermeer family, the same as other Zen 3-based desktop CPUs like the Ryzen 5 5600X. That brings with it an update to PCIe 4.0, which is a huge boon for GPU and storage performance, as well as a bump from a maximum boost of 4.2 GHz on the 5500 to 4.4 GHz on the 5500F.

| Ryzen 5 5500 ($159) | ~$90 | Zen 3 (Cezanne) | 6 / 12 | 3.6 / 4.2 | 19 MB | 65W / 88W | 
Although the Ryzen 5 5500F falls in the Vermeer family, it still carries some Cezanne DNA. It’s the only Vermeer chip to have 16 MB of shared L3; all other Vermeer chips have 32 MB of L3, at least, with X3D options scaling higher. Both families retain the same L1/L2 setup, naturally, as they share the Zen 3 microarchitecture.
Otherwise, the Ryzen 5 5500F retains the 65W TDP, and 88W platform maximum, and it comes bundled with AMD’s Wraith Stealth cooler. The Wraith Stealth cooler is plenty to keep the Ryzen 5 5500F cool under load, saving you some money on an aftermarket CPU cooler.

articles.title: Sony discontinues its last standalone Blu-ray player, leaving the PS5 as the sole remaining option
articles.text:
Bottom line: Sony has reportedly discontinued its last standalone UHD Blu-ray player in its home country, meaning the PlayStation 5 is now the company's only device capable of playing the format. Of course, for anyone that's been closely following Sony or physical media as of late, this isn't a surprisingly outcome.
Back in February, Sony halted sales of Blu-ray recorders worldwide – but the move didn't impact sales of standard Blu-ray players. Over the summer, the company dropped the bombshell that it would stop making physical PlayStation games starting in 2028. At that point, the writing was pretty much on the wall.
Now, Japanese blog Kunkoku – a Sony retailer – is reporting the company has discontinued its UBP-X700/K UHD Blu-ray player, the outfit's last standalone player. Indeed, a quick check of the machine on Sony's website shows it as out of stock with no return date mentioned.
As FlatpanelsHD highlights, the PS5 is first and foremost a game console which makes it an expensive option if you just want it for Blu-ray watching (and recent price hikes don't help matters). It also doesn't support Dolby Vision, so there is that. And looking ahead, it is unlikely that Sony's next-gen game console, tentatively named the PS6, will have an optical drive at all.
That said, if you're a fan of Blu-ray or want to ensure you have a way to keep watching your existing disc collection, now might be a good time to come up with some sort of hardware-based plan for the future. Depending on what you already have, that could involve buying a backup machine to unbox when your current solution eventually fails or picking up a PS5 now while they are still around.
Of course, Sony isn't the only player in the space. A handful of other reputable brands are still making Blu-ray players, but when a major industry influencer like Sony pulls out of the market, it's usually a sign that others aren't going to be far behind.

articles.title: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing | TechCrunch
articles.text:
AI agents left to explore a virtual island without a specific task began inventing challenges of their own. MIT researchers say the behavior bears the hallmarks of play.
The researchers put 13 AI agents called Eko, each running on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. They describe the experiment in a paper posted on arXiv, a site where researchers share studies before peer review. Afterward, they gave the agents specific challenges, like getting as many objects as possible onto the island’s tallest rock spire. The Eko agents that had spent those 30 hours playing generally beat identical agents that had never set foot on the island.
Today, developers decide in advance what AI should practice and what counts as success. The researchers see this technique — exploring without a goal — as a different way for AI agents to learn skills, especially skills that could one day be used to control robots.
“We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress,” the researchers write in their report. “Play suggests another regime: give an agent a sufficiently rich and safe world, let it choose what is interesting, and allow useful knowledge to accumulate from the history that follows.”
“Let me observe my surroundings,” one Eko wrote in its first hour on the island. Ambitiously, it set out to conquer the island’s tallest spire. But an hour later, after failing, it came back with a backup plan: it hauled the rock up a neighboring summit, stacked two blocks on top of it, and leapt.
“I’M ON THE SPIRE,” it wrote.
The agent’s next big moment went worse. Testing how far it could throw a golden ring, it wound up and sent it straight into the ocean. “Ouch. Lost the Ring.” it wrote, before deciding to “pivot to something achievable and meaningful” — building a heart made of stones, “a memorial to the lost Ring.”
When the game reset and ring reappeared, Eko put it straight to work as a basketball hoop, a target and, eventually, an accessory. When the game wouldn’t let Eko put the ring around its own body, Eko figured out a workaround, that falling off the edge of the cliff would make it respawn in the same area as the ring. It stepped off the edge and dropped back in, right through the middle of the ring.
“I’m wearing the Ring,” it announced.
Stunts like these weren’t just party tricks. Six of the 13 agents also learned they could throw a block farther by letting go of it mid-jump, something the researchers hadn’t meant to make possible. The exploration produced “knowledge of the world that its designers lacked,” the researchers wrote.
The setup did a lot to nudge the agents toward humanlike behavior. Eko was never told to invent games, but its master prompt, a “soul” file, described it as “naturally curious.”
Eunice Yiu, a cognitive scientist at UC Berkeley, told MIT Tech Review she was impressed but wants more evidence of the cognition behind the behavior. “It could be the case that the models are genuinely playing, but we don’t know based on the paper,” she said.
The researchers frame it as a different way to build agents. “Perhaps some capabilities are best taught by tasks,” their report concludes. “Others may need something closer to a childhood.”

articles.title: GM boasts 20% range boost from new EV platform at Forward event
articles.text:
General Motors recently hosted its second annual GM Forward event in New York, where the company revealed details on its fourth-generation EV powertrains, AI officially coming to OnStar, and its pathway to autonomy.
An all-new EV powertrain
To start things off, GM showed off its fourth-generation EV platform, which GM says sports a “world’s first” production lithium manganese-rich (LMR) battery, alongside more efficient electric propulsion and centralized computing. The company says the platform delivers 20 per cent more range.
According to GM, the LMR cells were produced by its Ultium Cells joint venture with LG Energy Solutions. The company plans to use it in its “highest-volume” EV segments, citing range, durability, and affordability, so expect GM’s mainline EVs to get it in the near future.
Interestingly, the company also noted that it is simplifying the powertrain, and that the new family of motors and electronics reduces the number of parts inside each unit by 40 per cent; a move that the company says will improve the interior space and lower production costs (yay).
OnStar now has AI
Second, GM announced it is expanding its OnStar service into an AI assistant. The automotive giant says the assistant will combine “conversation with vehicle understanding” to deliver personalized assistance and deeper insights, guided by permissions and privacy controls.
With the new OnStar AI Assistant, users can adjust the car (including opening some hatches, compartments, and ports), get real-time updates, get answers specific to their vehicle, and get helpful answers within the OnStar app. The good news, though, is that OnStar’s human advisors aren’t going away; GM says that if you need assistance, the OnStar AI assistant can connect you with an OnStar Advisor.
The feature will debut with the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq in the coming months through over-the-air updates, with other GM vehicles following soon after.
Intelligence and automation
Shifting from that, GM also shared more insight into personal autonomy and how it is expanding the tech. Mainly, GM will expand autonomous highway driving to its top-selling vehicles, including full-size SUVs and light-duty pickups.
Alongside this, the company also debuted a new centralized computing and electrical architecture that, in addition to being liquid-cooled, will roll out across both gas and EV models.

articles.title: AI chatbots hurt Canadian teens' education, says McGill prof
articles.text:
A McGill University teacher is warning Canadians of the negative impact of chatbots on teen education.
In a piece published on The Conversation, Adam Kenneth Dubé, associate professor of Learning Sciences at McGill’s Faculty of Education, wrote about some of the harmful effects that he’s been studying.
As he explains, new worldwide data on 15-year-olds’ science, math and reading ability was released last month by OECD’s Program for International Student Assessment (PISA). In Canada, 24,600 students from 897 schools took part, with this year’s report focusing on their use of AI in learning.
Notably, the report found that 86 per cent of teens globally use AI for school, and Canadian teens who use AI every week for school scored two years behind those who never use it. Dubé adds that scores have overall been declining for years, coinciding with the 2022 release of ChatGPT, although he stresses that this in itself isn’t evidence of causality.
Instead, he looked further into how and why Canadian students are turning to AI. Here were some of the biggest use cases:
- “To help me learn” (38 per cent in Canada, 46 per cent globally)
- To research new topics (23 per cent in Canada, 31 per cent globally)
- To summarize a reading (23 per cent in Canada, 30 per cent globally)
- To generate texts for assignments (18 per cent in Canada, 29 per cent globally)
Given that AI is notorious for making mistakes, also known as “hallucinations,” these findings are unfortunate, to say the least. It’s particularly concerning that roughly one-fifth of Canadian teens are effectively using AI to do their homework for them, too. Naturally, relying more and more on AI will also reduce critical-thinking skills in general, as we saw in a study earlier this year by Carnegie Mellon, MIT, Oxford and UCLA.
Overall, Dubé says the data shows that teens are using AI to “help them learn, not cheat, and are driven by curiosity.” But he also noted that the data “suggests using AI doesn’t help most teens with their learning, particularly Canadians.”
For instance, students who use AI daily to summarize text showed a 38-point lower score in science versus those who never use it. Worse, those who used it to draft text demonstrated a 42-point lower score. Dubé says these gaps are equivalent to two years of learning loss. He also noted that even results for those who were “trained” in AI use didn’t differ much from those who never used AI (two points lower in Canada, five points higher globally).
Going forward, he says it’s important to design “teen-ready AI” instead of training teens to be “AI-ready.” This includes an overhaul of Canada’s Safe Social Media Act to introduce greater restrictions, rather than features that encourage repeated use.
“If AI is reading and writing for you, then you’re not learning,” writes Dubé.
Via: The Conversation

articles.title: Astronomische Spurensuche: Was fünf Sterne im Zentrum über Van Goghs „Sternennacht“ verraten
articles.text:
Astronomische Spurensuche: Was die 5 Sterne im Zentrum über van Goghs „Sternennacht“ verraten
Schon in den 1980er-Jahren suchten zwei Forscher am Himmel nach Vorbildern für van Goghs Sternennacht: Albert Boime 1984 und Charles Whitney 1986. Doch ihre Ergebnisse widersprachen sich und führten zu keinem stichfesten Beweis. Ihre astronomischen Erklärungsversuche setzten sich daher nicht gegen die verbreitete Deutung durch, das Bild sei vor allem religiös oder symbolisch zu verstehen. Ein Brief an van Goghs Bruder Theo hatte das Bild bislang mit der Zeit um den 18. Juni 1889 in Verbindung gebracht.
Nach Angaben des koreanischen Forschungsteams hat seither niemand mehr untersucht, ob die Anordnung der gemalten Sterne nicht doch zu einem Himmel passt, den der Künstler tatsächlich vor Augen hatte. Die Ergebnisse wurden in Scientific Reports, einer Zeitschrift des Nature-Portfolios, veröffentlicht.
Nicht das Sternbild Widder, sondern Stier
Als der Astronom Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim frühere Deutungen von Vincent van Goghs „Sternennacht“ las, stutzte er: Andere Forschende hatten die Sterne im Bild dem Sternbild Widder zugeordnet. Kim und sein Team erkannten darin stattdessen den Sternhaufen der Hyaden im Stier. „Da das Team bereits viele Teleskope gebaut und jahrelang den Nachthimmel beobachtet hatte, hielt es das Sternbild Widder für eine unwahrscheinliche Inspirationsquelle des Malers“, heißt es in einer Pressemitteilung.
Um ihre Vermutung zu prüfen, reisten sie schon 2019 nach Frankreich und verglichen das Gemälde mit dem Himmel über Saint-Rémy. Zusätzlich baut die Forschung auf einem 2025 erschienenen populärwissenschaftlichen Buch von Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim auf, in welchem zusätzliche Belege gesammelt und durch quantitative Daten ergänzt wurden.
Sternbild, Mondphase und Venus sprechen für den 22. Juli 1889
Nach der Analyse ähneln fünf Sterne im Zentrum des Bildes dem Hyaden-Sternhaufen im Sternbild Stier. Dabei rückte auch der Mond in den Blick der Untersuchung. Nach Berechnungen des Teams passt die damalige Mondphase um den 18. Juni nicht zu der schmalen Sichel auf der Leinwand. Um den 22. Juli hingegen gingen die Hyaden zusammen mit der Venus im Osten auf, und die Form des Mondes entsprach in etwa dem Halbmond auf der Leinwand.
Gegen dieses Datum sprach bisher die Annahme, der Künstler habe innerhalb dieses Zeitraums einen Anfall erlitten. Kim und seine Mitautoren sichteten deshalb niederländische und französische Originalbriefe, zeitgenössische Wetteraufzeichnungen und darin enthaltene Bemerkungen zu Zikaden. Die zirpenden Insekten leben zwar den ganzen Sommer über, sind aber erst ab Ende Juni vermehrt aktiv. Das würde gegen den 18. Juni sprechen. Aus der Kombination aller Informationen haben die Forschenden geschlossen, dass van Gogh erst Ende Juli an gesundheitlichen Problemen gelitten hat.
Auf den Spuren von van Goghs Blick
In Arles verglich das Team „Sternennacht über der Rhône“ (1888) mit Fotos vom Schauplatz und zeichnete so van Goghs möglichen Blick auf den Fluss nach. Dasselbe Prinzip wandten die Forschenden auf die „Sternennacht“ an: In Saint-Rémy spürten sie den Ort auf, von dem aus van Gogh die Landschaft unter dem Sternenhimmel skizziert haben könnte, und rekonstruierten seine Blickrichtung.
Zusammen mit dem Vergleich der gemalten Sterne mit den Hyaden stützt das aus Sicht des Teams die Annahme, dass van Gogh eigene Beobachtungen in das Bild einfließen ließ. Sicher belegen lässt sich damit weder, dass er es am 22. Juli malte, noch, dass der Künstler den Himmel so gemalt hat, wie er ihn tatsächlich gesehen hat. „Ich hoffe, dass diese Arbeit einen neuen, interdisziplinären Blick auf die Entstehungsreihenfolge und die Arbeitsmethoden der Saint-Rémy-Gemälde sowie auf van Goghs Wege in jenem Sommer anregt“, sagt Kim.

articles.title: Google Maps accueille enfin Gemini sur CarPlay, et votre GPS devient bien plus bavard
articles.text:
Google commence à déployer Gemini directement dans Google Maps sur Apple CarPlay, permettant aux conducteurs de discuter avec leur GPS pendant leurs trajets. Une nouveauté déjà accessible aux États-Unis, dont l’arrivée en France reste à confirmer.
Les automobilistes équipés d’un iPhone et adeptes de Google Maps vont enfin pouvoir discuter avec leur GPS. Après avoir intégré Gemini à son application mobile et à Android Auto, Google s’attaque désormais à Apple CarPlay. L’objectif reste le même : remplacer les commandes vocales parfois un peu rigides par de véritables conversations avec l’intelligence artificielle. Une question sur un restaurant, une envie de détour ou un changement d’itinéraire ? Plus besoin de multiplier les recherches sur l’écran de la voiture. Gemini promet de s’en charger à votre place, sans vous faire perdre le fil de votre trajet.
Gemini s’installe directement dans Google Maps sur CarPlay
Comme le rapporte Android Authority, Google a commencé à déployer son assistant conversationnel au sein de Google Maps sur CarPlay.
La nouveauté prend la forme d’une icône Gemini, affichée sur le côté droit de l’écran pendant la navigation. Il suffit d’appuyer dessus pour lancer une conversation avec l’assistant, qui peut ensuite répondre aux questions et exécuter certaines commandes vocales.
L'intérêt est surtout de pouvoir enchaîner plusieurs demandes sans repartir de zéro. Google donne notamment l’exemple d’un conducteur qui cherche un parc offrant une belle vue sur la ville. Il peut ensuite demander si la météo sera favorable, vérifier les horaires les moins fréquentés, puis lancer le guidage en évitant les péages.
Gemini peut également rechercher une station-service, suggérer une étape pour déjeuner ou fournir des renseignements sur les lieux situés à proximité de l'itinéraire.
Autre possibilité : signaler vocalement un accident ou une perturbation de circulation, sans devoir manipuler les menus de Google Maps.
Ces fonctions existaient déjà dans l’application mobile. La véritable nouveauté est leur intégration à l’interface CarPlay, qui permet d’en profiter directement sur l'écran du véhicule.
Un déploiement mondial engagé, mais pas encore de confirmation pour la France
Gemini est disponible dans Google Maps sur CarPlay aux États-Unis depuis le 21 octobre. Google indique qu’un déploiement mondial est également en cours, sans préciser de calendrier pour chaque pays.
Les conducteurs français devront donc vérifier l’apparition de la nouvelle icône dans Google Maps. Pour le moment, rien ne garantit que tous les utilisateurs de CarPlay dans l’Hexagone puissent déjà en profiter.
Cette arrivée intervient alors que Google renforce également les capacités de Gemini sur Android Auto, notamment grâce à Personal Intelligence, une nouvelle fonction de l’assistant qui peut désormais exploiter certaines informations issues de Gmail, Google Agenda ou Google Photos pour personnaliser ses réponses.
Mais attention à ne pas confondre les deux nouveautés. Cette personnalisation avancée n’est pas annoncée sur CarPlay, et son déploiement sur Android Auto exclut actuellement l’Espace économique européen, dont la France.
Sur CarPlay, Gemini se concentre donc pour l’instant sur la navigation et les recherches liées au trajet. Un premier pas qui devrait déjà rendre Google Maps plus agréable à utiliser, à condition que l'assistant comprenne correctement les demandes et ne transforme pas chaque trajet en conversation interminable.

articles.title: Can AI Make Debt Collections Less About Chasing and More About Predicting?
articles.text:
Can AI make debt collections less about chasing and more about predicting?
The future lies in using data to understand portfolios, AI to prioritise decisions, and human judgement where individual circumstances matter most.
Defaults are inevitable.
For the past few years, we have been hearing about predictive analytics that can identify a borrower who is going to default before the default actually happens.
Time and again, we have seen the limits of this idea.
Defaults aren't a prediction problem that technology will eventually eliminate. Defaults are an uncertainty that lending produces, by design. What lenders need is not machinery that assumes this uncertainty can be removed, but machinery designed to operate effectively under it.
You cannot predict at an individual borrower level who is going to default. You can, at best, predict, over a sufficiently large cohort of borrowers, what the default rate might be.
The behaviour of large groups can be predicted statistically. The behaviour of a particular individual cannot.
If you have one million borrowers, you can make remarkably good statements about what will happen to the portfolio. Narrow it to 100,000 borrowers in Karnataka, and you can still make useful predictions. Narrow it further by repayment history, geography, employment, credit score and other risk characteristics, and you can create increasingly meaningful cohorts.
But as the cohorts get smaller, the certainty of those predictions starts decreasing.
Eventually, you arrive at an individual borrower, say Ashok.Ashok's salary didn't arrive yesterday because his employer had a cash-flow problem. Your model cannot know that. It cannot know that unless you invade the privacy of Ashok and everyone he interacts with. Which you absolutely should not do.
This is the fundamental limitation of trying to predict defaults at an individual level.
For example, if we look at borrowers onboarded in Karnataka who have paid 60% of their EMIs on time and have a credit score of 650 or above, we may be able to say with reasonable confidence that 90% of them will repay on time in April.
But we cannot tell you which 90%.
And lenders have to operate with this uncertainty.
Borrowers do not fit into a neat Excel formula. Even if they did, you would not know all the variables that go into calculating it.
Some of these variables are macro.
In the western region, for instance, collections can soften during August and September around Ganesh Chaturthi. We also see periods where household cash flows come under pressure around the start of the school year, when families are managing school fees, admissions, books and other education-related expenses.
This information is useful.
It can tell us that collections might be lower during a particular period and help us anticipate how a portfolio could perform.
But it still does not tell us who is going to miss their EMI.
Then there are micro circumstances.
A salary gets delayed. A business has a bad month. There is an unexpected expense. A school fee needs to be prioritised. Something happens in the family. Or someone simply forgets to maintain enough balance in their account.
It is impossible for a lender to know every individual's circumstances at every point in time. This is why lending is ultimately a game of large numbers.
Risk models can be extremely effective at estimating how a sufficiently large cohort will behave. But every individual in that cohort is a different person, going through a different set of circumstances.
None of this is to say that predictive analytics is not useful. In fact, it is the opposite.
Predictive analytics is a powerful tool when used for the problem it is actually capable of solving. It can tell you where a portfolio might end up. It can tell you where to focus effort. It can identify groups of borrowers that are more likely to need intervention than others. It can help lenders allocate their collection resources more intelligently and set realistic expectations for portfolio performance.
The mistake is in assuming that this translates into certainty at the individual level. It doesn't.
There will always be uncertainty at that level. And that means defaults will always exist.
The more interesting opportunity for AI, therefore, is not to predict every default before it happens. It is to make lenders better at responding to defaults when they do happen.
When a borrower misses an EMI, the system should be able to help determine what happens next. Who needs an immediate intervention? Who is likely to self-cure? Which borrowers require a human conversation? What is the appropriate channel and timing? How should collection teams prioritise their limited resources?
This is where predictive analytics, combined with AI-led decisioning and communication, can make a meaningful difference.
The objective should not be to chase every borrower harder. It should be to make every intervention more relevant.
That distinction matters, particularly as credit expands to millions of new borrowers across India. At that scale, collections cannot rely entirely on manual follow-ups, nor can it rely on the assumption that an algorithm will perfectly predict human behaviour.
The future lies somewhere more practical: using data to understand portfolios, AI to prioritise decisions, and human judgement where individual circumstances matter most.
Trying to predict every default before it happens is a game you cannot win. And it is a game you should not play.
The real competitive advantage will come from building a system that accepts uncertainty, and is intelligent enough to deal with it.
The author is Co-founder & CTO, DPDzero, an AI-led debt collection platform.

articles.title: Ces 2 panneaux de signalisation routière indiquent une obligation dans 34 départements dès le 1er novembre
articles.text:
Instaurée pour sécuriser les déplacements en hiver et fluidifier le trafic, cette mesure concerne les automobilistes qui circulent dans les communes désignées par les préfets au sein de 34 départements. Les massifs des Alpes, de Corse, du Massif central, du Jura, des Pyrénées et des Vosges sont concernés par ces arrêtés locaux pris en concertation avec les élus. Des panneaux de signalisation marquent également l’entrée et la sortie des zones d’obligation d’équipements en période hivernale, accompagnés d’un panonceau indiquant la période d’application.
Les équipements obligatoires pour votre véhicule
Posséder le bon matériel dans son coffre ou sur ses roues devient obligatoire sous peine d’infraction dans les communes concernées. Deux options s’offrent à vous si vous conduisez une voiture, un utilitaire ou un camping-car : installer quatre pneumatiques adaptés à la conduite hivernale ou garder des dispositifs antidérapants amovibles pour équiper au moins deux roues motrices. Les chaînes métalliques conviennent mieux à un usage fréquent et les chaussettes à neige textiles sont plutôt conseillées pour un usage occasionnel.
Chaque équipement amovible doit évidemment correspondre à la taille des roues et respecter l’espace disponible entre le pneu et la carrosserie. Si vos pneus hiver ont le symbole 3PMSF, qui représente une montagne à trois pics avec un flocon de neige, vous pouvez vous passer des dispositifs amovibles. Les véhicules équipés de pneus à clous n’ont également pas besoin d’accessoires. En revanche, si vous avez des pneus neige classiques (sans le symbole 3PMSF), des chaînes ou des chaussettes en complément sont obligatoires.
Un dispositif élargi à tous les usagers de la route
Les voitures et les utilitaires ne sont pas les seuls ciblés par cette réglementation hivernale en vigueur du 1er novembre 2026 au 31 mars 2027. Les autobus, les autocars et les poids lourds doivent également s’y conformer. Les poids lourds sans remorque ont le choix entre les pneus adaptés ou les dispositifs antidérapants amovibles, exactement comme les véhicules légers.
À lire : Deux nouveaux panneaux de signalisation apparaissent sur les routes : voici ce qu’ils signifient
Les poids lourds circulant avec une remorque ou une semi-remorque ont cependant une contrainte supplémentaire : ils ont l’obligation de détenir des chaînes ou des chaussettes pour équiper au moins deux roues motrices, même si leurs roues possèdent déjà des pneus hiver. Avant de prendre la route en zone de montagne, on vous conseille donc de consulter les listes de communes et les arrêtés préfectoraux disponibles sur le site de la Sécurité routière pour vérifier votre trajet.
