articles.title: Segundo bissexto será aposentado após alerta sobre riscos digitais • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Segundo bissexto será aposentado após alerta sobre riscos digitais
Conferência internacional aprovou mudança no horário mundial para reduzir riscos de sincronização em servidores, redes elétricas e dispositivos.
A Conferência Geral de Pesos e Medidas (CGPM) aprovou o fim dos segundos bissextos nos relógios mundiais. A mudança ocorre para evitar problemas de sincronização em sistemas digitais diante da possibilidade de precisarem de um segundo bissexto negativo, que retiraria um segundo do horário oficial.
A CGPM, que é responsável pela atualização do Sistema Internacional de Unidades (SI), acredita que esse tipo de ajuste representa um risco elevado para infraestruturas críticas e poderia exigir investimentos comparáveis aos realizados na preparação para o Bug do Milênio, segundo o The Register.
O segundo bissexto é usado para manter dois padrões de tempo próximos:
Como a velocidade da rotação do planeta varia ao longo do tempo, os dois padrões podem começar a se afastar. Quando essa diferença aumenta, segundos extras são adicionados ao UTC para compensar a diferença.
Nos últimos anos, porém, a Terra registrou períodos de rotação mais rápida e levantou a possibilidade de um segundo bissexto negativo, ou seja, que retiraria um segundo do relógio. Isso, no entanto, “é considerado de alto risco por causar anomalias e interrupções em infraestruturas críticas que estão amplamente despreparadas”, afirmou a organização.
A preocupação aumentou com a expansão de sistemas conectados que dependem da precisão de data e hora, incluindo redes elétricas, servidores e até dispositivos de Internet das Coisas (IoT).
No entanto, nem todos os equipamentos lidam da mesma forma com segundo bissextos, assim como há aqueles que recebem poucas atualizações ou não foram desenvolvidos considerando esse tipo de correção.
De acordo com o The Register, grandes empresas de tecnologia já adotam métodos próprios para suavizar a inclusão de segundo bissextos. As soluções, porém, não são padronizadas entre os diferentes serviços.
Com a decisão, a CGPM pretende substituir os ajustes frequentes de um segundo por uma tolerância maior entre o UTC e o UT1. O novo modelo, chamado de UTC Contínuo, permitirá que os dois padrões acumulem uma diferença maior antes que seja necessária uma nova correção. A previsão é que a implementação comece já no ano que vem.
A proposta admite uma defasagem de até 3.600 segundos, equivalente a uma hora. Dessa forma, a frequência de intervenções no horário utilizado por computadores e redes é reduzida.
A mudança também evita que desenvolvedores precisem preparar softwares especificamente para a inclusão ou remoção ocasional de um único segundo, operação que pode ser tratada de maneiras diferentes por cada sistema.

articles.title: Idéal en ce mois frisquet, ce chauffage d'appoint silencieux signé Dreo chute sous les 100 € — Frandroid
articles.text:
Si vous ne souhaitez pas encore rallumer tous les radiateurs de votre logement, mais que vous ne voulez pas non plus frissonner le soir dans votre chambre ou en journée dans votre bureau, un chauffage d’appoint électrique peut être une bonne solution. Dreo propose par exemple son Solaris Max, un modèle en forme de tour conçu pour réchauffer rapidement une petite pièce sans être trop bruyant. Compact et plus abordable que les nouveaux appareils que la marque a récemment annoncés, ce Solaris Max est actuellement proposé à moins de 100 euros.
Ce qu’il faut savoir sur le Dreo Solaris Max
- Un modèle assez discret et facile à porter
- Une puissance de 1 500 W et un thermostat réglable de 5 à 35°C
- Une minuterie intégrée
Auparavant affiché à 109,99 euros, le chauffage Dreo Solaris Max est aujourd’hui disponible en promotion à 99,99 euros sur Amazon. Et ce, jusqu’au 26 octobre 2026.
Un chauffage d’appoint pour une chambre ou un bureau
Le Dreo Solaris Max adopte un format colonne et demeure assez discret : haut de 63,5 cm, ce radiateur céramique n’est pas très encombrant et peut s’installer sans problème dans une chambre, un bureau ou une autre petite pièce. La marque indique qu’il couvre une surface de 9 à 25 m² selon le niveau de chauffage utilisé. Vous l’aurez compris, il n’est pas adapté aux grandes salles, qu’il aura du mal à réchauffer entièrement. Par ailleurs, l’appareil dispose d’une poignée de transport, qui permet de le déplacer facilement d’une pièce à l’autre.
Il est également fourni avec une télécommande, qui permet de le régler sans avoir à se déplacer jusqu’à lui. Le chauffage embarque aussi un panneau de commande et un écran, qui peut s’éteindre automatiquement. En revanche, sachez que le Solaris Max n’est pas connecté, contrairement à d’autres chauffages Dreo qui disposent du Wi-Fi et peuvent être contrôlés à distance depuis un smartphone. Côté sécurité, la marque n’a pas oublié la protection contre la surchauffe et le basculement. Un verrouillage pour les enfants peut également être activé.
Un réchauffement suffisamment rapide
Avec sa puissance de 1 500 W, le Solaris Max est capable de chauffer rapidement une pièce en diffusant de l’air chaud à une vitesse annoncée de 3,5 mètres par seconde. Son thermostat électronique est réglable de 5 à 35 °C. La tour oscille aussi sur 70° pour diffuser l’air chaud dans plusieurs directions, plutôt que de le diriger en permanence vers vous. Elle propose en prime quatre modes : silencieux (900 W), 1 300 W et Max (1 500 W), ainsi qu’un mode Éco, qui ajuste la puissance du chauffage en fonction de la température ambiante, afin de limiter la consommation d’énergie.
Côté bruit, Dreo annonce 32 dB au maximum ; son fonctionnement devrait donc rester assez silencieux, même si ça peut gêner pour dormir. Enfin, une minuterie permet de programmer le radiateur pour qu’il s’éteigne automatiquement après une durée déterminée, allant de 1 à 12 heures.

articles.title: Hay una buena razón por la que Elon Musk quiere juntar Tesla y SpaceX en una empresa de 3,5 billones de dólares: mas control
articles.text:
El martes, durante la conferencia de resultados de SpaceX, Elon Musk confirmaba que ambas empresas han formado comités especiales para estudiar una fusión. Esta idea de unir SpaceX y Tesla lleva un tiempo pululando y tras la unión entre la firma espacial de Musk y xAI, es un paso que al magnate le interesa especialmente. La empresa combinada tendría un valor de unos 3,5 billones de dólares a los valores actuales de mercado, según cuenta el New York Times, y sería la mayor operación corporativa de la historia en términos económicos. De momento no se ha acordado nada, pero el tema está desde luego encima de la mesa.
Por qué importa. Musk quiere reunir bajo un mismo techo sus coches eléctricos, cohetes, satélites y la IA. SpaceX está valorada en unos 2 billones de dólares y Tesla en 1,5 billones de dólares, según los datos actuales del mercado. La operación también resolvería un problema que Musk arrastra desde hace años, pues en SpaceX controla el 80% del derecho a voto en decisiones importantes, mientras que solo posee alrededor del 20% de Tesla, tal y como comparte el NYT.
La lógica empresarial. El argumento de Musk es que ambas empresas se necesitan cada vez más mutuamente. Para él, Tesla construye la “IA física” (taxis autónomos y robots humanoides), mientras que SpaceX proporciona la infraestructura de soporte con centros de datos y conectividad por satélite.
Terafab, una fábrica de chips en Texas con el potencial de costar hasta 119.000 millones de dólares, según el Financial Times, ya está en construcción por parte de la compañía. Y Tesla también vende baterías Megapack a SpaceX. El año pasado de hecho les vendieron baterías por valor de 430 millones de dólares a los centros de datos de SpaceX, según informa el WSJ.
Musk afirma que la lógica es simple, pues según el magnate, “Hay mucho mérito en combinar las empresas”, declaraba en la llamada con inversores, según pudo recoger el NYT.
Las cifras. Los últimos resultados de SpaceX demuestran lo mucho que ha avanzado más allá de los cohetes. Recientemente repasábamos en esta casa lo que ha logrado la compañía en su división de IA. En sus resultados financieros del último trimestre vimos un aumento del 161% en sus ingresos, alcanzando los 14.600 millones de dólares, y el beneficio neto alcanzó los 4.400 millones de dólares.
El motor de ese crecimiento fue la IA, pues su división de “Super Intelligence” alcanzó unos 7.600 millones de dólares, más de la mitad de los ingresos totales, y a medida que rivales como Anthropic y Google le alquilaban su capacidad de centros de datos. El trimestre de Tesla fue más flojo. El NYT informa de que el beneficio cayó a 787 millones de dólares frente a los 1.400 millones de dólares del año anterior, a medida que aumentaba el gasto en coches autónomos y robots.
Precio. La gran pregunta que se hace Wall Street no es si se acabará formando el acuerdo, es cuándo, según admiten desde Reuters, pero nadie se pone de acuerdo sobre lo que deberían recibir los accionistas de Tesla. RBC y JPMorgan esperan que los inversores exijan una prima de entre el 20% y el 35%. Otros esperan poca o ninguna prima porque las bases de accionistas de ambas empresas se solapan en gran medida.
Ross Gerber, cuya firma posee acciones de ambas compañías, sostiene que una prima diluiría a los accionistas de SpaceX a medida que aumente su gasto. Y SpaceX ya está gastando muchísimo, pues su gasto de capital alcanzó los 19.600 millones de dólares el trimestre pasado, y Musk prevé entre 35.000 y 40.000 millones de dólares en el siguiente.
Votación. Musk afirma que un acuerdo con Tesla necesita una mayoría de todas las acciones en circulación, no solo de las emitidas y votadas, según comparte el NYT. Eso significa que cada accionista que no vote cuenta efectivamente en contra. Reuters señala que los analistas ven la participación como un riesgo, así que estarán atentos a la junta anual de Tesla del 3 de diciembre.
El propio control de Musk añade complejidad al problema, pues según comparte el medio, la estimaciones están en que una fusión elevaría su poder de voto a alrededor del 57-58%. Y luego está el tema del conflicto de interés, pues el NYT informa de que, además de Musk, en ambos consejos de administración hay antiguos aliados y amigos. Reuters recuerda la jugada de cuando Tesla compró SolarCity en 2016, empresa fundada por los primos de Musk. Ahí un tribunal de Delaware dio luz verde al acuerdo, pero indicó que se debería haber formado un comité independiente.
Reguladores y la política. Tal y como bien señala The Independent, SpaceX trabaja para la NASA, el ejército estadounidense y las agencias de inteligencia, mientras que Tesla cuenta con una importante fábrica en Shanghái. Tener un cóctel en el que se mezcla Washington y Pekín podría plantear importantes problemas de políticos y de seguridad.
Qué pasa ahora. Ambos comités, asesorados por abogados y banqueros, deben acordar los términos y presentarlos a sus respectivos consejos de administración, según explica el WSJ. Queda esperar para saber si las partes se ponen de acuerdo y ver qué tiene Tesla preparado para la junta anual del 3 de diciembre.

articles.title: Ai2 releases OlmoEarth v1.3 state-of-the-art AI-ready satellite embeddings for the whole planet - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Ai2 releases OlmoEarth v1.3 state-of-the-art AI-ready satellite embeddings for the whole planet
Ai2, the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, today released a satellite map embedding model called OlmoEarth v1.3 and precomputed annual embeddings for the whole planet at various resolutions with a browser-based map-making tool.
The model compresses a year of satellite observations into a numerical fingerprint for each 10-by-10-meter patch of ground at the smallest resolution, with 64-square-meter and 128-meter also available. That fingerprint captures patterns that other software can use to distinguish crops, forests, mines and other types of land cover.
Until now, the primary way to use OlmoEarth was to fine-tune in OlmoEarth Studio, train a model for each task and run it over satellite data to make a map. That requires access to vast graphics processing unit resources and the ability to download and store imagery.
With today’s launch, users can use OlmoEarth Embeddings Explorer, a browser-based map-making tool. That means anyone can turn OlmoEarth into real work, from tracking change over time to finding similar places – no sign-in required.
An embedding represents what a model learned from millions of satellite images. OlmoEarth reads a year of radar images from data, including Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Landsat. Sentinel and Landsat are satellite missions that provide complementary views of Earth: Sentinel-1 measures radar reflections, while Sentinel-2 and Landsat capture light in visible and infrared wavelengths.
The company said that, compared with previous generations of the OlmoEarth model, 1.3 is its cheapest model to train. It took 53% of the computing time of the latest version (v1.2) and 18% of the first (v1), with 50% and 22% of the carbon emissions. It also remains a strong fine-tuning model, making v1.2’s performance valuable for research and partner labs.
Where these models fit into the real world
These satellite models help compress large swaths of data across time and space, which is useful for understanding how the Earth changes.
In Peru’s Madre de Dios region, illegal gold mining around La Pampa peaked in 2017 and 2018, clearing more than 1,200 hectares of forest in the buffer zone of the Tambopata National Reserve. The Amazon Conservation Team’s MAAP monitoring program reports this activity. In February 2019, Peru’s Operation Mercurio shut most of it down. How do we know that happened?
Embeddings give this a clear answer. Comparing pixels within the data across years, no model training required, looking across 2016 to 2020 and there’s a clear eastward push within the southern mining belt: 34 square kilometers of significant change. The same comparison from 2020 to 2024 shows that area falls to 9 square kilometers. The shutdown is visible.
Equivalently, an agricultural analyst could map where oil palm is being grown and identify areas for closer examination where plantation expansion may have replaced forest. These questions could determine where the environmental impact is affecting the world at large.
Ai2 said for many teams testing an idea against OlmoEarth has meant a fine-tuning run, which is an expensive, arduous venture on the order of hours. In the explorer, a first pass takes seconds.
Analysis of a region from a handful of labels requires no GPU. When a task calls for fine-tuning that experiment, the embeddings can help decide whether it deserves the compute time and where the model falls short.

articles.title: iPhone Duo : ses deux écrans réservent une mauvaise surprise aux premiers acheteurs
articles.text:
iPhone Duo : ses deux écrans réservent une mauvaise surprise aux premiers acheteurs
Prise en main
L'iPhone Duo, premier smartphone pliant d'Apple, arrive en France ce 23 octobre 2026. Son format promet beaucoup, tout comme son affichage, mais nos premiers essais invitent à regarder au-delà de la fiche technique.
L'iPhone Duo intrigue avec son cover display de 5,4 pouces et sa dalle intérieure de 7,6 pouces, qui se déplie comme un passeport. Mais un écran immense, exempt de reflets qui plus est, ne garantit pas que vos apps préférées pourront en tirer parti immédiatement.
Apple iPhone Duo
Des idées brillantes… quand les apps suivent
Apple a remodelé iOS 27 pour ce format. Téléphone fermé, le dock, l'heure et les commandes passent à droite ; ouvert, il affiche deux apps côte à côte et gère plusieurs angles de pliage. Contacts juxtapose répertoire et fiches. Calendrier, Horloge, Calculatrice, Fichiers et Apple TV tirent aussi parti de cette surface.
Instagram, Netflix et Canal+ ont déjà suivi. Ailleurs, en revanche, gare à la douche froide : certains logiciels s'ouvrent en fenêtre minuscule, cernée de noir. Nous en avons fait le constat avec notre app viSer. D'autres occupent presque tout l'écran, mais conservent leurs boutons mal placés. Contrairement à beaucoup de pliants Android, l'iPhone Duo n'étire pas toujours l'affichage automatiquement. Il faut donc parfois intervenir.
Les ratés touchent également des usages bien français : certains services de streaming, comme Free TV, refusent parfois le plein écran, et les apps bancaires risquent également de traîner. Waze et Uber figurent parmi les retardataires des premiers tests. On comprend désormais pourquoi jusqu’ici les démonstrations étaient très contrôlées et se concentraient sur les outils made in Cupertino.
Petites mains et gauchers, patience
La largeur du Duo et ses commandes à droite compliquent aussi certains gestes, notamment pour les gauchers, soit environ 10 % des utilisateurs. Apple prévoit d'ici fin 2026 un mode Accès facile qui devrait rapprocher les boutons du pouce, en réduisant l'interface en hauteur et en largeur, probablement sur l'écran externe. iOS 27.2 doit également permettre d'utiliser l’Apple Pencil.
Pas d’inquiétude donc, même s’ils sont rageants, ces quelques couacs au démarrage sont avant tout logiciels. Comme à l'arrivée des iPhone 6 et X, les développeurs devront adapter leurs créations, parfois pendant plusieurs mois. De nombreuses corrections sont attendues. À 2339 €, mieux vaut toutefois vérifier la compatibilité de ses apps préférées avant de craquer. Les délais de livraisons désormais fixés à janvier 2027 semblent finalement un mal pour un bien.

articles.title: Amazon Polly delivers a major upgrade to its Generative engine | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Amazon Polly delivers a major upgrade to its Generative engine
Amazon Polly Generative engine now offers more natural and accurate speech output. We’re introducing an upgrade to the Amazon Polly Generative engine that delivers more expressive, more accurate speech output with low latency. The upgrade adds 14 new voices across 9 locales, including general availability of Generative voices in Hindi and Finnish for the first time. The upgrade is now generally available in production.
Importantly, this is a drop-in upgrade for existing generative voices. Voice names and API calls are unchanged, so your existing applications continue to work as they do today.
Amazon Polly is a fully managed AWS service that converts text into natural-sounding speech for contact centers, large language model (LLM)-based agentic applications, media and entertainment, e-learning, accessibility, and other applications that require reliable voice output at scale.
Hear the difference
You can use sample audio to evaluate the improvements directly.
- The more natural, authentic, and expressive voices. Hear how Tiffany welcomes you in a delightful tone. 
         
  - “Hi there! I’m Tiffany, one of Polly’s generative voices. I was built to sound natural, expressive, and a little bit delightful. What should we talk about?”
- Accurate speech generation for numbers, currency, addresses, and so on. Kenneth reads back an order confirmation, including the tracking number, date and time, currency and address accurately. 
         
  - “Thanks for calling. Your order, number 4471 9902 ships today to 85 Harbor View Drive, Apartment 4B, Portland, Oregon 97209. It should arrive on Thursday, October 22nd, between 9 AM and 1 PM. Your total was $1,284.50 and your confirmation code is K-7-Q-2-X-9.”
- Net new languages. Arjun and Kiara for Hindi, and Suvi for Finnish. Hindi and Finnish are generally available for the first time on the Amazon Polly Generative engine. 
         
  - Arjun: नमस्कार, आप सुन रहे हैं आज की मुख्य ख़बरें। देश के कई हिस्सों में मानसून की विदाई के साथ मौसम सुहाना हो गया है। (Hello, you’re listening to today’s top stories. As the monsoon retreats across much of the country, the weather has turned pleasant.)
  - Kiara: नमस्ते! मेरा नाम कियारा है। आइए, आज मैं आपको एक छोटी सी कहानी सुनाती हूँ।(Hello! My name is Kiara. Come, let me tell you a little story today.)
  - Suvi: Majakanvartija ei ollut nähnyt laivaa yhteentoista päivään. Sitten, vähän puolenyön jälkeen, horisontissa välähti yksi ainoa valo. Kerran. Kahdesti. Ja sitten, uskomatonta kyllä, se vilkutti takaisin hänen nimensä. (The lighthouse keeper hadn’t seen a ship in eleven days. Then, just after midnight, a single light blinked on the horizon. Once. Twice. And then, impossibly, it blinked back his name.)
- Different styles of speech delivery based on textual context. Powered by the new Amazon Polly Generative engine, the voices can reflect emotion and prosody even better based on the text input, without manual setup. 
         
  - Neutral: “Your package arrived early.”
  - Uncertainty: “So, um… your package arrived early. I think?”
  - Surprised: “Wait, what? Your package arrived early?”
New voices, languages, and Region availability
- A larger catalog overall for Amazon Polly Generative engine – Totaling 57 generative voices across 11 languages and 25 locales.
- 14 new voices across 9 locales – US English (Kenneth, Nate), Australian English (Russell, Curtis), Indian English (Kiara, Arjun), German (Tina), US Spanish (Carlos), Brazilian Portuguese (Leo, Carolina), Korean (Hyunduk), Hindi (Kiara, Arjun) and Finnish (Suvi).
- Net new languages generally available in Generative engine – Hindi and Finnish.
- Region expansion to AWS GovCloud (US-West) – Totaling 11 AWS Regions.
Built for production-ready speech workflows for enterprise
The upgraded Amazon Polly Generative engine uses a standard Amazon Polly API call to build your speech applications. With Amazon Polly, you can continue to build with familiar AWS patterns: call the same Amazon Polly API, manage access with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), use the output in your existing applications and contact-center flows, and monitor the workloads that synthesize speech for your customers.
This launch is designed to elevate the speech output quality that you can hear with your existing Amazon Polly implementation. No changes to your code are required to get the upgraded voices. For applications that already use Amazon Polly Generative voices, the upgrade happens in place. For new applications, the same SynthesizeSpeech API gives you access to a larger set of generative voice catalogs. With the Bi-Di Streaming API StartSpeechSynthesisStream, you can stream text to Amazon Polly and receive synthesized audio back simultaneously. This is well-suited for real-time applications like voice agents and bespoke characters in games.
Competitive price-performance
The Amazon Polly Generative engine offers competitive pricing on a pay-as-you-go basis. With this model upgrade, you get improved voice quality and accuracy at the same price. There’s no cost increase, no new SKU, and no changes to your existing integration. You can cache and replay synthesized static prompts with no additional cost. Refer to Amazon Polly pricing for complete cost information.
The Amazon Polly Generative engine now delivers more natural, expressive speech alongside low-latency streaming for real-time applications, Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) support for fine-grained control, and the operational reliability of a fully managed AWS service. This combination of quality, performance, and cost efficiency supports a wide range of production use cases.
What you can build
Contact centers. Accuracy matters most in customer service conversations. When a caller checks an order, a voice that reads back the tracking number, address, and confirmation code correctly helps resolve the call in self-service rather than escalating to a human agent. Amazon Polly Generative voice’s accurate entity pronunciation and low-latency generation make automated interactive voice response (IVR) interactions sound more conversational.
Cascaded voice agents. Using Amazon Polly in a voice agent framework, you can convert LLM response text into clear, natural-sounding speech and stream it back to users in near real time over WebSockets or telephony channels. This makes live conversational voice possible. The primary benefits are low-latency playback, high scalability, and cost efficiency.
Media, localization, and dubbing. Convert scripts into finished audio for video, advertising, podcasts, product overviews, and audiobooks. You can use one voice or many, without a studio session. More natural intonation reduces post-production. The expanded locale coverage, including first-time generative Hindi and Finnish, means you can localize a single piece of content into more markets from the same pipeline.
E-learning and training. Narrate courseware, onboarding, and knowledge-based articles at scale, and update them as soon as the source text changes. No re-recording is required. More expressive delivery supports engagement through long-form material.
Accessibility. Provide a clear, natural spoken version of articles, documents, and applications so more people can consume your content by listening: read aloud, on the go, or with a screen reader.
Interactive and transactional experiences. Voice-enable games, kiosks, IVR menus, and IoT devices with responses generated on demand. Use Amazon Polly when the voice needs to sound natural and read names, numbers, product details, addresses, and confirmations reliably.
        “At Sanoma Media Finland, we use Amazon Polly to turn our real-time news articles into audio, giving the listener the choice to listen whenever it suits them better. Today we publish over 10,000 articles per month using Polly’s Finnish neural voice. Based on our testing, Suvi’s new generative voice is a clear improvement over the previous neural voice – it sounds noticeably more natural and makes for a more enjoyable experience for the listener.”
— Justus Reinikainen, Product Manager, Sanoma Media Finland
Getting started
You can access the new voices using the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), or the AWS SDKs.
Prerequisites:
- Active AWS account with Amazon Polly access.
- AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) installed and configured.
- Python 3.10+.
- Boto3 installed: pip install boto3.
- AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions: polly:SynthesizeSpeech.
Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) with the SynthesizeSpeech API and a generative voice:
You can also make the same request with the AWS CLI:
To retrieve the full, current voice list programmatically, call DescribeVoices. You can use this in deployment checks to confirm that a selected generative voice is available in the Region where your application runs.
Availability
The next-generation Generative engine and the new voices are now generally available. The 14 new Generative voices are available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Zurich), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). Getting started, by audience:
- Developers – Call synthesize_speech with Engine="generative" in your existing application. No other changes are required.
- Contact-center teams – The improvements reach Amazon Connect and Genesys flows automatically.
- Everyone – Access any voice in the Amazon Polly console.
A few things to know:
- Standard and neural voices are unaffected.
- Speech marks are not available on generative voices (unchanged from today). If your application requires them, standard and neural voices continue to support them.
- Generative engine continues to support SSML tags. See supported SSML tags for more details.
- Use current voice availability at runtime. Call DescribeVoices or check the console when deploying across Regions.
Conclusion
The next-generation Generative engine of Amazon Polly is available today, delivering more natural and more accurate voices, adding 14 new voices, including generative voices generally available in Hindi and Finnish for the first time, and requires no change to your code. See Amazon Polly pricing page for pricing information. To get started, open the Amazon Polly console to try the voices, and see the Amazon Polly documentation to build with them.

articles.title: Cómo instalar la APK de XUPER TV en un Smart TV: una búsqueda que oculta fraudes y daños en el dispositivo
articles.text:
Buscar la forma de instalar XUPER TV, antes conocida como Magis TV, en un Smart TV puede exponer al usuario a descargas desde sitios no oficiales, archivos modificados y ofertas fraudulentas que prometen acceso gratuito o de bajo costo a contenidos exclusivos.
La instalación de una APK para ver películas gratis desde una fuente no verificada puede abrir la puerta al robo de datos, fraudes financieros y daños en el televisor o en la red doméstica.
La Organización Internacional de Policía Criminal (Interpol) señala que los sitios vinculados con contenidos pirateados representan un riesgo para la seguridad digital, porque pueden distribuir malware y captar información confidencial.
Por qué una APK descargada fuera de la tienda oficial puede afectar al Smart TV
Los televisores inteligentes funcionan con sistemas operativos, aplicaciones y conexiones permanentes a internet. Cuando el usuario instala una APK procedente de un sitio desconocido, concede acceso a un archivo cuya composición y permisos no puede comprobar con facilidad.
Ese archivo puede alterar el funcionamiento del dispositivo, mostrar publicidad invasiva o instalar programas adicionales sin autorización. Interpol advierte que muchos sitios web y redes de intercambio de archivos que ofrecen material pirateado incluyen malware o virus capaces de dañar el dispositivo o extraer información personal.
En un Smart TV, el problema puede ir más allá de la aplicación: una amenaza informática puede aprovechar la conexión WiFi y alcanzar otros dispositivos conectados a la misma red.
Qué datos pueden quedar expuestos durante la descarga de XUPER TV
Las plataformas de origen incierto suelen solicitar datos de contacto, correos, contraseñas o información de pago con la promesa de habilitar una cuenta, activar un período de prueba o desbloquear contenido. Esos formularios pueden funcionar como una trampa para reunir datos personales, bancarios u otra información sensible.
El riesgo aumenta si el usuario reutiliza la misma contraseña que usa en servicios de correo, redes sociales o bancos. Según Interpol, el malware distribuido desde sitios piratas puede facilitar el robo o la falsificación de identidad. La exposición de una cuenta puede derivar en intentos de acceso a servicios vinculados al mismo correo.
Por qué hay riesgos de fraudes con tarjetas y medios de pago
Algunos sitios ofrecen suscripciones, códigos de activación o supuestas versiones premium de XUPER TV mediante métodos de pago que no cuentan con controles verificables.
El usuario puede entregar los datos de su tarjeta sin saber quién administra la plataforma, dónde se almacena esa información ni qué mecanismos existen para reclamar ante un cobro no autorizado.
Interpol señala que los métodos de pago inseguros pueden derivar en fraudes con tarjetas de crédito y otras estafas financieras. Las señales de alerta incluyen precios muy bajos, pagos solo con criptomonedas, transferencias a particulares, falta de información sobre la empresa y ausencia de canales de atención al cliente identificables.
Cómo identificar una página web pirata
Una de las señales es la promesa de un catálogo amplio de películas, series, deportes o canales a cambio de una suma muy inferior a la que cobran los servicios autorizados, o incluso sin costo.
Interpol sugiere desconfiar de las plataformas que ofrecen grandes cantidades de contenido por precios mínimos, sumado a verificar si los proveedores poseen derechos para operar en el territorio del usuario.
Asimismo, conviene revisar si el servicio cuenta con sitio oficial, condiciones de uso, política de privacidad, datos de contacto y presencia en tiendas de aplicaciones reconocidas.
Los contenidos legítimos suelen tener un precio mayor, pero incluyen soporte, estabilidad y mecanismos de seguridad. Un enlace compartido por redes sociales, grupos de mensajería o páginas que obligan a desactivar protecciones del dispositivo debe considerarse una señal de riesgo.

articles.title: Apple says more than 50 apps will be updated for the iPhone Duo at launch
articles.text:
TL;DR: Apple's first foldable iPhone is due out this Friday and when it arrives, users will have access to "more than 50 apps" that have been updated to leverage the device's unique form factor. That number is clearly not enough, but Apple and iOS app developers do have a positive track record of promptly optimizing apps for new devices.
Unfolded, the iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR display with nano-texture finish – in other words, it's essentially a pocketable mini tablet. That much real estate will make it ideal for media consumption, and it's no surprise that Apple has partnered with several of the top streaming services to dial in their apps ahead of launch.
 – Marques Brownlee (@MKBHD) October 21, 2026
Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Paramount+ were all mentioned by name in Apple's announcement, as were sports organizations like the PGA Tour and MLB. With the latter, fans can engage with live action and game stats simultaneously – simply set the iPhone Duo partially folded on a table and enjoy.
The Duo's big screen is also expected to have a big impact on mobile gaming. Apple Arcade titles like Retrocade and Sneaky Sasquatch are fully playable on the outer screen, but are said to deliver an even more immersive experience when played on the folding display. Other games like Asphalt Legends tap into the power of the A20 Pro SoC to maximize car and track detail.
Apple's latest is more than just a glorified toy, however. When productivity calls, apps from Microsoft, Zoom, Slack, and Salesforce can deliver a desktop-like experience on the portable screen. In Word, formatting tools sit alongside open documents for easy editing. When using Zoom, the inner display can serve as an immersive video conference room where users can share content with other meeting participants.
Apple isn't the first to market with an appealing foldable – in fact, they're quite late to the game. As other big brands pioneered in the emerging space, Cupertino sat back and took notes on what worked and what didn't. The Duo is the result of all those years of market research and for many, it'll be their first time interacting with a foldable.
The hardware looks solid enough for a first outing, but the software is what could make or break the folding iPhone. Apple holds a key advantage over rival Android device makers in that they control hardware and software under a single roof, allowing for seamless integration between the two. With the Duo due out later this week, we won't have to wait long to know if Apple has another hit on their hands.

articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg's creative plan to pay California’s proposed billionaire tax without losing control of Meta | TechCrunch
articles.text:
During Meta’s earnings call on Wednesday, the company revealed its board had approved a new class of nonvoting stock, called Class C common stock. The shares give the holder an ownership stake but no vote on company decisions. This class takes effect in January. Meta says it will use the stock for capital raising, employee pay, and acquisitions — including its expensive push into AI — while maintaining the current voting structure that favors its founder and CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, who controls around 60% of the vote.
Now, however, the New York Times has reported there’s another reason for the new class: helping Zuckerberg pay for California’s proposed “billionaire tax,” if voters approve it. Because the new shares carry no votes, he could sell some of them to cover the tax without giving up voting control.
Proposition 40, which was drafted by Berkeley tax law professors and is being sponsored by California’s largest healthcare union (SEIU United Healthcare Workers West), would level a one-time 5% wealth tax on the net worth of several hundred California billionaires who primarily live in the state. Backers say the policy could generate as much as $100 billion over five years, the bulk of which would be used to pay for the state’s healthcare needs, with the rest being used for food assistance and education.
The Times also reports that Zuckerberg pressed Meta’s board to come up with a plan to protect him from the tax. According to the paper, he told board members in September that if they couldn’t reach an agreement, he’d list his Palo Alto property for sale, potentially kicking off a media firestorm. Not long afterward, the stock plan materialized, the newspaper writes.
The Times reporting is partially based on a recent SEC filing that Meta made, which documents the concern surrounding Proposition 40 and how it informed discussions that led to the new stock class.
The filing says that as far back as July, Zuckerberg was discussing the billionaire tax with board members. The topic came up again in additional meetings and communications throughout that month and August.
The filing also describes how the plan would work. Meta is creating a new class of nonvoting shares, called Class C, and will give shareholders one of them for every Class A or Class B share they own. The company calls this a one-time stock dividend and says it should work out to a two-for-one stock split. The dividend “will not change the voting power of any shareholder,” Meta says.
That is where Prop 40 comes in. The filing says the dividend “will allow Mr. Zuckerberg to immediately sell or transfer up to 20% of the shares of Class C common stock that he receives in the Dividend, representing 10% of his overall economic stake in the Company, for any reason, including so that he may pay his potential tax liability under California Proposition 40, if enacted into law, without affecting his majority voting control.” Because the dividend is one-for-one, half of his post-dividend shares will be Class C, so the 20% cap equals 10% of his total economic stake.
When reached for comment by TechCrunch, Meta referred us to a quote included in its recent earnings press release that reiterates that part of the motivation for the creation of the stock was to keep Zuckerberg onboard: “The Special Committee affirmed its belief that it was important for Mr. Zuckerberg to continue to lead the Company from California, including because it was crucial that Mr. Zuckerberg remains in close coordination with the Company’s management and in close proximity to Meta Superintelligence Labs.”
It’s been estimated that Zuckerberg would have to pay as much as $11 billion as part of the tax.
Prop 40 has notably riled many of Silicon Valley’s most prominent businesspeople. Google co-founder Sergey Brin has aggressively campaigned against the measure, even spending a small fortune in an effort to defeat it. Other business leaders and critics of the proposal have criticized it online, with many claiming that it amounts to economic suicide for California, driving a capital flight from the state. However, as Meta’s new policy would appear to show, the state’s mega-companies and the people who run them have creative ways of dealing with the tax, should it materialize.
“Looks like billionaires will stay and figure out a way to pay the tax,” Democratic U.S. Representative Ro Khanna, a vocal proponent of the tax, wrote on X, after news of Meta’s strategy spread online. “If we pass Prop 40, poor California kids can have healthcare,” he added.

articles.title: Micron pulls the plug on future 4F² DRAM after two decades of research in dramatic shift — company says architecture offers no meaningful density advantages, increases manufacturing complexity and costs, and has fundamental scaling limitations
articles.text:
Micron pulls the plug on future 4F² DRAM after two decades of research in dramatic shift — company says architecture offers no meaningful density advantages, increases manufacturing complexity and costs, and has fundamental scaling limitations
Micron goes against the industry?
DRAM featuring 4F² memory cells has long been considered one of the holy grails of the DRAM industry, as they promise to reduce cell area by 33% compared with conventional 6F² designs and therefore enable building DRAMs with more memory cells in the same area. However, after working on 4F² memory cells for a couple of decades, Micron has concluded that the architecture offers no meaningful density advantages, increases manufacturing complexity and costs, and has fundamental scaling limitations. This has a dramatic impact on Micron's future plans.
"Micron invented 4F² DRAM," said Scott DeBoer, president and chief technology and products officer at Micron, during the company's event on Wednesday. "The path with 4F² DRAM is always been an option through time, and we have evaluated it and not pursued it due to increased complexity and cost through this past two-decade period of time."
Interestingly, both Samsung and SK hynix still have 4F² memory cells in their roadmaps (according to TechInsights), so Micron's rejection of the technology puts the company on a unique trajectory. Several years ago, the company delayed integration of EUV lithography into its manufacturing flow, contrary to what its rivals did, and still managed to retain competitive positions both in terms of costs and in terms of performance. Therefore, skipping 4F² memory cells is not completely surprising.
4F² is not the future of Micron's DRAM
The main attraction of 4F² DRAM is its theoretically smaller memory cell. The 4F² naming refers to a cell area equivalent to four times the square of the minimum lithographic feature size (F), compared with six times F² for conventional DRAM.
At identical feature dimensions, a 4F² cell occupies approximately 33% less area than a 6F² cell, which could theoretically increase the number of memory cells per wafer by 50%. Such an improvement would reduce manufacturing costs per bit and increase per-device memory capacity even without an equivalent reduction in feature dimensions. However, to make these advantages possible, DRAM makers must develop a suitable transistor architecture and a sufficiently compact capacitor arrangement. This is not easy at all.
The CTO of Micron says that the theoretical advantages of 4F² DRAM do not necessarily translate into higher memory density in practice. DeBoer explained that dimensions and pitch of DRAM capacitors, rather than the nominal area of DRAM transistors, ultimately determine how many memory cells can fit on a wafer. Both 4F² and 6F² transistor structures must fit beneath the capacitors, which means that reducing transistor area alone does not guarantee a corresponding reduction in overall cell size because transistors need a capacitor. Furthermore, Micron believes that 4F² introduces additional manufacturing steps and complexity that increase costs without delivering sufficient benefits.
"It is important to understand the capacitor pitch, the capacitor size, and dimensions, is what sets the DRAM bit density, not whether it is 6F², 4F², 8F²," DeBoer said. "From our investigation of this technology over the past couple of decades, it is a bit of a myth that 4F² actually provides anything versus 6F². It is capacitor pitch that defines the DRAM. You can build the cells, the transistors underlying them in different ways, but they still have to fit under the capacitor pitch, which sets the DRAM [cell size]. So, some of that is just smoke and mirrors in terms of talking about 6F² versus 4F²."
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
4F² memory cells may curb new process technologies
Instead of adopting the 4F² DRAM cell architecture, Micron plans to continue scaling conventional 6F² DRAM. The company believes it can increase bit density by reducing capacitor pitch and shrinking process technologies even without introducing a fundamentally different transistor architecture.
Advanced lithography, new materials, and wafer bonding should allow Micron to extend planar DRAM scaling for several more generations, according to the company. For example, its upcoming 1δ process technology, scheduled to enter volume production in the second half of 2027, promises a mid-20% improvement in bit density compared with its predecessor. Micron also plans to adopt High-NA EUV lithography for future DRAM generations.
Interestingly, DeBoer fully acknowledges that 4F² DRAM is technically feasible and that Micron itself has manufactured experimental devices based on the architecture. However, its manufacturing complexity and costs become increasingly problematic as feature dimensions shrink, so essentially Micron claims that it can either adopt 4F² or use more sophisticated process technologies, a claim that perhaps implies why China-based CXMT recently praised 4F². Although DeBoer did not identify any specific physical limitations involved, he stated that 4F² has no sustainable scaling path beyond a certain point. This suggests that Micron sees little value in introducing an intermediate architecture that would eventually require another major transition.
"When you look at a scaling path, you can go back a few nodes and absolutely, 4F² can be built back a few nodes, no question about it," DeBoer noted. "It is more complicated, it is more complex, it is more costly, but you can do that. When we look at scaling 4F² beyond where we are sitting today, there it is; it is physics. There are fundamental problems with 4F² scaling that ultimately will lead to 3D DRAM coming in instead of 4F²."
3D DRAM is the future
Indeed, Micron's preferred long-term solution is 3D DRAM, which would increase memory density by stacking memory cells vertically rather than relying exclusively on reductions in their lateral dimensions. Alongside development of multiple next-generation planar DRAM process technologies, the company is already developing multiple generations of 3D DRAM production nodes (which is not surprising, as 3D NAND nodes will rely on fundamental innovations developed for planar processes), although it has not disclosed when the new architecture will enter commercial production. DeBoer indicated that Micron will make the transition when 3D DRAM offers the right combination of density, manufacturing complexity, and cost.
Although both Samsung and SK hynix have 4F² DRAM products in their roadmaps, Micron believes that the assumption that reducing the nominal footprint of DRAM cells improves manufacturing economics is wrong and that extending 6F² scaling and eventually adopting 3D DRAM offers a better long-term strategy.

articles.title: How IskayPet unified corporate knowledge with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
How IskayPet unified corporate knowledge with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases
IskayPet’s office teams had a knowledge challenge. Answers to everyday operational questions, such as a return policy, a veterinary protocol, or an onboarding step, lived in hundreds of Microsoft SharePoint documents spread across four languages and three countries. Finding the right information in large document repositories took a long time. Every new store, country, or procedure made the problem bigger.
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is the usual way to solve this. But running RAG in production normally means operating vector databases, embedding pipelines, and ingestion jobs yourself.
In this post, we show how IskayPet, a leading pet care company in Iberia, built a corporate knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases. The assistant answers employee questions across retail operations, veterinary care, people and onboarding, and procurement, in four languages and across three countries, with no RAG infrastructure to manage. The team built the whole solution, from the store-facing frontend to the AWS architecture and deployment, using Kiro with Claude Haiku 4.5. We cover the architecture, the SharePoint integration, the retrieval configuration decisions, and the results in production.
About IskayPet
IskayPet is a leading pet care company in Iberia. It operates more than 330 stores across Spain, Portugal, and France under the Kiwoko, Tiendanimal, Kivet, Clinicanimal and Animalis brands. With more than 4,500 employees and 7 million customers, IskayPet runs operations that span retail, veterinary clinics, animal care, procurement, and people and onboarding. Each area has its own policies and procedures, in Spanish, Portuguese, French, and English.
The challenge
Across every business area, IskayPet office staff searched hundreds of SharePoint documents by hand to answer operational questions about procedures, policies, contracts, and onboarding. With operations in three countries and four languages, this took real time, and the answer was often outdated or wrong.
There was no reliable way to query corporate knowledge, and the problem grew with every country, area, or document added. IskayPet needed a solution that could do the following:
- Answer natural-language questions grounded in their own corporate documents.
- Work across four languages without maintaining separate systems.
- Route each question to the right body of knowledge (an area, a country) without cross-contamination.
- Scale to new areas and countries without re-architecting.
- Cite its sources so employees can trust and verify answers.
- Reuse their existing SharePoint repositories without a costly migration.
Why Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases
IskayPet chose Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases for its managed RAG infrastructure, which removed the need to run vector stores, embeddings, or ingestion pipelines. The main reasons were:
- Managed RAG: Amazon Bedrock handles data ingestion, multimodal parsing, vector storage, embedding generation, and retrieval. IskayPet pays only for what it stores and retrieves.
- Native SharePoint connector: The connector ingests documents directly from IskayPet’s existing SharePoint environment, which avoided a data migration. With advanced indexing enabled, it also processes content from images embedded in documents.
- Built-in hybrid search: Combining semantic and keyword (BM25) search at no extra cost recovers exact terms, such as product codes and references, that pure semantic search can miss.
- Managed reranking: Retrieved passages are reordered by relevance at no additional charge.
- Document-level access control: The knowledge base can enforce the source system’s own permissions at retrieval time, so a query returns only passages from documents the requesting user is already allowed to read. This lets IskayPet reuse SharePoint permissions instead of rebuilding an authorization model.
- Model flexibility: IskayPet can start with a cost-effective model and change it later without rewriting infrastructure.
- Native RAG evaluation: The team measured quality at each step with the built-in evaluation tools.
Solution overview
The following diagram shows the end-to-end flow, from the employee’s question through permission-aware retrieval to the grounded, cited answer.
The solution is an assistant that employees reach through their existing channels. When an employee asks a question, the assistant retrieves the most relevant passages from its knowledge base, restricted to the documents the employee is allowed to read. It then generates a grounded, cited answer in the employee’s language.
At a high level, the flow works as follows:
- An employee submits a natural-language question through the chat interface.
- The application calls the knowledge base for the requested assistant, passing the employee’s identity so that document-level permissions are applied to the retrieval.
- The knowledge base runs hybrid search (semantic and keyword) over the indexed content, reranks the results, and returns the most relevant passages with their source references.
- A foundation model (FM) generates a grounded answer from the retrieved passages. The prompt requires source citation and tells the model to say when the answer isn’t in the retrieved content.
- The employee receives the answer along with the source documents and can leave feedback (thumbs up or down) that feeds the evaluation set.
Building the solution with Kiro and Claude Haiku 4.5
IskayPet built the whole solution, from the store-facing frontend to the AWS architecture and service deployment, using Kiro, the agentic development environment, running on Claude Haiku 4.5 on Amazon Bedrock. As new models become available on Amazon Bedrock, IskayPet plans to evaluate and adopt them for each use case.
For model availability by AWS Region, see Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock.
- Store-facing frontend – The team used Kiro to build the frontend that store employees use to interact with the assistant, generating and iterating on the UI code with Claude Haiku 4.5.
- Architecture and deployment – Kiro also helped design the AWS architecture and provision the services behind the solution: knowledge base configuration, data sources, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles, and the application layer.
An agentic workflow with Kiro and a fast, cost-effective model like Claude Haiku 4.5 helped a small team move from concept to production quickly. It also kept the application code and the infrastructure consistent and maintainable.
Ingestion: The SharePoint connector with advanced indexing
IskayPet’s documents already lived in SharePoint, organized by area and country. Rather than migrate them, the team used the native SharePoint connector in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases.
In the data source’s Advanced configurations, under Content indexing and Advanced indexing, IskayPet enabled Visual content in documents. This setting extracts content from images embedded in documents (PDF, DOCX, PPTX) and from standalone images. Figures and scanned content inside procedure documents became searchable without a separate preprocessing pipeline.
The connector syncs incrementally, so new and updated documents are picked up on each sync.
Multi-country, multi-area architecture
A key design decision was how to structure knowledge for four languages, several business areas, and three countries. IskayPet weighed two approaches:
- A single shared knowledge base, with every document tagged by country and area and a retrieval filter applied per query. This maximizes reuse of shared content but couples all domains into one index.
- A dedicated knowledge base per assistant, each scoped to the relevant SharePoint sites or libraries. This keeps each body of knowledge isolated end to end and lets each assistant be tuned independently.
IskayPet chose a knowledge base per assistant. Each assistant points at specific SharePoint sites and can be narrowed further to specific document libraries or folders through inclusion paths, so it indexes only the intended content and not the whole corporate site. Adding a new area or country means adding an assistant and pointing it at the right content, not re-architecting the system.
Access control
Access is governed by the users’ existing SharePoint permissions. The assistant doesn’t grant access to anything new: It only makes it more straightforward to query documents an employee could already open. This works on two levels.
- Which assistants a user sees – An employee is shown only the assistants whose underlying documentation they’re entitled to read, whether that entitlement comes from direct permission, group membership, or access to a specific folder. If access can’t be confirmed, the assistant is hidden rather than shown.
- Which documents inform an answer – Access is enforced again at retrieval time, per document: The employee’s identity is passed to the knowledge base, which returns passages only from documents that person is authorized to see. Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases supports this document-level access control natively, so the same answer to the same question can legitimately differ between two employees with different permissions.
Because permissions are read from SharePoint on every access check, revoking or granting access in SharePoint is reflected in the assistant without changes to the application.
Retrieval and generation configuration
The quality of a RAG system is decided mainly at ingestion, retrieval, and generation. Fine-tuning is a complementary technique. For this use case, IskayPet tuned the following settings:
- Chunking – Handled by the managed knowledge base, so the team didn’t build or tune a chunking pipeline. This removed a component that’s usually significant operational effort in a self-managed RAG.
- Hybrid search – The knowledge base combines semantic and keyword retrieval, which recovers exact terms such as product codes that pure semantic search can miss.
- Number of results – Tuned against an evaluation set. The assistant retrieves 25 passages and, after removing duplicates and fragments too short to add context, injects up to 15 into the prompt. This number is the main cost lever, because it multiplies input tokens on every question.
- Generation prompt – Enforces a corporate tone, requires source citation, and tells the model to say when the answer isn’t in the retrieved content, which reduces hallucination and adds traceability.
As a production control, the team is adding Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to apply content filtering and responsible AI policies to the generated answers.
- Evaluation– Native Amazon Bedrock RAG evaluation, using the thumbs up and down feedback from real usage as an evaluation set to measure quality before and after each change.
Generating the response
For answer generation, IskayPet uses a cost-effective foundation model on Amazon Bedrock. Because the knowledge base decouples retrieval from generation, IskayPet can switch or upgrade the generation model without touching the ingestion or retrieval layers. This lets the team balance cost and answer quality as usage grows.
Cost efficiency
The knowledge base includes multimodal parsing, embedding generation, and reranking at no additional charge, so IskayPet’s ongoing cost comes mainly from index storage, retrieval API calls, and generation-model tokens. In production, input tokens dominate that cost, because of the passages injected into each prompt. The team is evaluating further optimizations as usage grows, including prompt caching for the stable part of the prompt and batch inference for non-interactive workloads.
Results
In roughly the first two months in production, IskayPet has seen:
- Faster answers – Time to find an operational answer dropped from 3–5 minutes to about 7 seconds.
- Higher productivity – Around 95 percent less time spent searching for procedures and policies.
- Scale – The solution is expected to handle roughly 100,000 queries per month across all business areas and countries.
Conclusion
IskayPet built a production corporate knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases that serves three countries, four languages, and several business areas, with no RAG infrastructure to run. The native SharePoint connector reused their existing repositories. A dedicated knowledge base per assistant gave them a clean multi-country design with each domain isolated end to end. Managed parsing, embedding, and reranking kept both operational effort and cost low. Building the frontend and the AWS architecture with Kiro and Claude Haiku 4.5 lets a small team reach production quickly.
If you’re facing a similar knowledge-retrieval challenge, you can start on the AWS Free Tier and build your first knowledge base on the Amazon Bedrock console. To go deeper, see the following resources and try the SharePoint connector and document-level access control against your own documents.
To learn more, see Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and Evaluate the performance of RAG sources using Amazon Bedrock evaluations.

articles.title: Vous montez un PC de jeu sur AM5 ? Le Ryzen 7 7800X3D passe à 269,42€ chez ce marchand
articles.text:
Avec l’arrivée des Ryzen 9000X3D, la génération précédente de processeurs à 3D V-Cache reste une piste sérieuse pour un PC de jeu qui veut garder du budget pour sa carte graphique. AliExpress affiche le Ryzen 7 7800X3D à 269,42 €, 13 % sous son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours, sans ventirad fourni et en retrait hors du jeu, comme l’avait montré notre test.
Testé chez nous en avril 2023, le Ryzen 7 7800X3D est le processeur Zen 4 qu’AMD destine d’abord au jeu : 8 cœurs, 16 threads et 96 Mo de cache L3, dont 64 Mo empilés grâce à la 3D V-Cache. AliExpress l’affiche à 269,42 €, soit 13 % de moins que son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, fixé à 310 €.
Ce n’est pas pour autant son prix plancher : pendant les French Days, mi-septembre, il était descendu à 236,64 € avec un code promo. L’offre vise surtout les joueurs qui montent ou font évoluer une configuration AM5 et préfèrent réserver l’essentiel de leur budget à la carte graphique.
Le Ryzen 7 7800X3D est proposé à 269,42 € chez AliExpress, contre 310 € pour son prix le plus bas relevé sur les 30 derniers jours.
Pourquoi choisir le Ryzen 7 7800X3D ?
- Un cache taillé pour le jeu : La 3D V-Cache porte le cache L3 à 96 Mo, et c’est en jeu que son apport se mesure. Dans notre test, il prenait la première place sur Cyberpunk 2077 en Full HD.
- Une consommation contenue : Malgré un TDP de 120 W, il n’a pas dépassé 84,62 W en charge lors de nos mesures, pour une température maximale de 82,4 °C. Un point appréciable si votre alimentation a peu de marge.
- Une plateforme récente : La DDR5 et le PCIe 5.0 sont pris en charge par le socket AM5. Ses deux unités graphiques RDNA2 permettent aussi d’afficher une image en attendant la carte graphique, sans prétendre la remplacer.
Un processeur pensé pour le jeu, moins pour la création
En jeu, l’avantage tient à la 3D V-Cache plus qu’à la fréquence : 4,2 GHz de base et 5 GHz en pointe, soit moins que le Ryzen 7 7700X. Dans notre test du Ryzen 7 7800X3D, il passait pourtant devant ce dernier dans la plupart des jeux, et devançait même son grand frère, le Ryzen 9 7950X3D, sur F1 22 comme sur Forza Horizon 5. Nous lui avions attribué la note de 8/10, en soulignant aussi son efficacité énergétique.
Le profil idéal est celui d’un joueur qui monte un PC AM5 et veut placer le gros du budget dans la carte graphique. Pour le montage vidéo, le rendu 3D ou la compression de fichiers, il reste en retrait face au Ryzen 7 7700X dans nos mesures sous Cinebench, Blender, Handbrake et WinRAR. Son coefficient bloqué limite par ailleurs l’overclocking. Si la création compte autant que le jeu, un modèle à 16 cœurs comme le Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 répond mieux à ce double usage, selon notre guide de la rentrée.
Face au Ryzen 7 9800X3D, une affaire de budget
Son successeur, le Ryzen 7 9800X3D, figure en tête de notre comparatif des meilleurs processeurs, où il apparaît à partir de 395 € au moment de notre relevé. Ce même comparatif le juge meilleur que le 7800X3D en production, mais plus cher et plus gourmand en énergie. À 269,42 €, l’écart dépasse 120 €, une somme que notre guide de la rentrée conseille de reporter sur la carte graphique dans une configuration équilibrée. Reste à compter une carte mère AM5 et de la DDR5, deux postes qui alourdissent la facture face à une plateforme plus ancienne.
✅ Les points forts
- Premier de notre test sur Cyberpunk 2077 en Full HD
- 96 Mo de cache L3 grâce à la 3D V-Cache
- 84,62 W au maximum mesurés, pour un TDP de 120 W
- DDR5 et PCIe 5.0 pris en charge
- 40,58 € sous son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours
❌ Les limites
- En retrait face au Ryzen 7 7700X en création
- Aucun ventirad fourni, à acheter en plus
- Overclocking contraint par un coefficient bloqué
- Déjà vu à 236,64 € avec un code en septembre
Avant de valider, vérifiez sur la fiche AliExpress que le Ryzen 7 7800X3D est toujours à 269,42 € et prenez connaissance des conditions du vendeur.
À 269,42 €, le Ryzen 7 7800X3D reste une pièce de choix pour un PC de jeu sur AM5. Ses résultats en jeu, salués dans notre test, en font la porte d’entrée de la 3D V-Cache que retient notre guide de la rentrée. La remise de 13 % est réelle au regard des 30 derniers jours, sans constituer un record, puisque le prix était tombé plus bas en septembre.
L’offre s’adresse avant tout aux joueurs qui disposent déjà d’une carte mère AM5 ou s’apprêtent à en acheter une, et qui prévoient un refroidissement à part. Les créateurs qui encodent ou font du rendu chaque semaine auront intérêt à regarder une puce dotée de plus de cœurs. Sur AliExpress, prenez aussi le temps de lire la garantie et le délai de livraison indiqués par le vendeur avant de commander.

articles.title: L’heure d’hiver est de retour ce week-end : non, ce n'est toujours pas la dernière fois
articles.text:
Plus que quelques jours avant le prochain changement d’heure. Nous vivons à l’heure d’été depuis la fin mars 2026, mais c’est bientôt terminé. La bascule aura lieu ce week-end, dans la nuit du samedi 24 au dimanche 25 octobre. La France passera alors à l’heure d’hiver.
Passage à l’heure d’hiver le 25 octobre 2026 : on dort plus ou moins ?
Comme à chaque changement d’heure, toute la question est de savoir dans quel sens s’effectue la bascule. Le site officiel de l’administration, Service public, donne la réponse : « Il faudra penser à reculer vos montres d’une heure dans la nuit du samedi 24 au dimanche 25 octobre 2026. » À 3 heures du matin, il sera donc 2 heures : la nuit de samedi à dimanche durera une heure de plus !
Faut-il pour autant se relever en pleine nuit pour régler toutes ses horloges ? Pas pour les smartphones, ordinateurs et tablettes : ils se mettent généralement à l’heure tout seuls, à condition que le réglage automatique de la date et de l’heure soit activé. En revanche, les montres classiques, les réveils, les horloges murales, les fours, les micro-ondes et les tableaux de bord des voitures non connectées devront encore être réglés à la main dimanche matin.
Ce changement d’heure peut donner l’impression qu’il intervient particulièrement tôt, et ce n’est pas totalement faux. Effectivement, l’an dernier nous sommes passés à l’heure d’hiver dans la nuit du 25 au 26 octobre.
Mais pourquoi change-t-on d’heure, au fait ?
La mesure a été instaurée en France en 1976, après le choc pétrolier de 1973-1974, pour économiser de l’énergie en profitant davantage de la lumière du jour. Le gain est désormais modeste : une étude du Service de recherche du Parlement européen publiée en 2017 l’estime entre 0,5 % et 2,5 % de la consommation étudiée selon les pays, l’effet étant plus marqué dans le sud du continent.
Tout tient à la règle européenne (directive 2000/84/CE) : dans toute l’Union européenne, le passage à l’heure d’hiver a lieu le dernier dimanche d’octobre. Or, octobre 2026 s’achève un samedi 31 : son dernier dimanche tombe donc le 25, la date la plus précoce possible. Cela ne s’était plus produit depuis 2020. En 2027, à l’inverse, la bascule tombera le 31 octobre.
La fin du changement d’heure ? Ce ne sera pas pour 2026
N’était-on pas censés en finir avec le changement d’heure ? Le sujet est sur la table des institutions européennes depuis 2018, quand la Commission européenne a proposé de supprimer les changements d’heure saisonniers. En mars 2019, le Parlement européen a voté la fin du changement d’heure pour 2021, par 410 voix contre 192. Le texte devait ensuite être adopté par le Conseil de l’UE, qui réunit les gouvernements des Vingt-Sept. Il y est bloqué depuis décembre 2019, faute d’accord entre les États sur l’heure à conserver, et la crise du covid-19 a ensuite relégué le dossier au second plan.
Le dossier est pourtant revenu devant les ministres européens au premier semestre 2025, sous la présidence polonaise du Conseil. À la demande des États, la Commission européenne a lancé en février 2026 une étude d’impact qui examine 10 scénarios de suppression, avec leurs effets sur les transports, l’énergie ou la santé publique. Ses conclusions sont attendues d’ici à la fin de l’année 2026.
En attendant, les Français, et le reste de l’Union européenne, continuent de changer d’heure deux fois par an, fin mars et fin octobre. Le passage à l’heure d’hiver de ce dimanche 25 octobre ne sera pas le dernier. Pendant ce temps, les États-Unis avancent pour en finir avec le changement d’heure.

articles.title: Wenn Erdkruste und Erdmantel über den Erdkern gleiten: Warum die geografischen Pole um 10 Zentimeter pro Jahr wandern
articles.text:
Zehn Zentimeter pro Jahr: Warum die geografischen Pole der Erde wandern
Die geografischen Pole der Erde verschieben sich derzeit mit einer per Satellit gemessenen Geschwindigkeit von rund zehn Zentimetern pro Jahr, was die durchschnittliche Driftgeschwindigkeit tektonischer Platten übersteigt. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, handelt es sich bei solchen Geschwindigkeiten nicht bloß um kurzlebige Ausreißer der Gegenwart, da vergleichbare Verschiebungen in den vergangenen 320 Millionen Jahren mehrfach über Zeiträume von jeweils zehn Millionen Jahren auftraten.
Ein Forschungsteam um den Geowissenschaftler Mathew Domeier, den Geologen Leandro C. Gallo, die Geowissenschaftlerin Chloé M. Marcilly und den Geophysiker Trond H. Torsvik von der norwegischen Universität Oslo wies insgesamt vier solcher Phasen anhand urzeitlicher Meeresspiegelschwankungen nach. Diese Episoden lagen in den Zeitfenstern vor 200 bis 190 Millionen, vor 150 bis 140 Millionen, vor 100 bis 90 Millionen sowie vor 30 bis 20 Millionen Jahren und erreichten Raten von mindestens 0,6 Breitengraden pro einer Million Jahre, was mindestens 6,7 Zentimetern pro Jahr entspricht.
Echte Polwanderung: Warum Erdkruste und Erdmantel über den Erdkern gleiten
In den Geowissenschaften trägt dieser Vorgang die Bezeichnung echte Polwanderung (auf Englisch: „True Polar Wander“) und unterscheidet sich grundlegend von der Bewegung der Magnetpole, die durch Strömungen im flüssigen äußeren Erdkern entsteht. Bei der echten Polwanderung bleibt die Rotationsachse der Erde im Weltraum stabil ausgerichtet, während sich die rund 2.800 Kilometer dicke feste äußere Schale aus Erdkruste und Erdmantel als Ganzes um den Erdkern dreht.
Auslöser für diese Drehung sind Massenverlagerungen im Erdmantel oder an der Oberfläche: Da der Planet durch die Eigenrotation am Äquator leicht ausgewölbt ist, kippt die feste Erdhülle bei einer Unwucht so lange nach, bis große Massenüberschüsse wieder möglichst nah am Äquator liegen. In den vergangenen Jahrzehnten trug neben abschmelzenden Eisschilden auch die Entnahme von rund 2.150 Gigatonnen Grundwasser messbar zu dieser Verschiebung bei.
„Die Erdkruste und der Erdmantel gleiten während eines Ereignisses echter Polwanderung gewissermaßen über den Erdkern“, wird Erstautor Mathew Domeier von New Scientist zitiert. Laut dem Geodynamiker Sabin Zahirovic von der australischen Universität Sydney hilft der Nachweis über historische Küstenlinien dabei, Prozesse im tiefen Erdinneren mit langfristigen Veränderungen von Klima und Meeresspiegel zu verknüpfen.
Meeresspiegel und Zentrifugalkraft: Wie das Datenmodell die Erdrotation rekonstruiert
Bisherige Versuche, frühere Polwanderungen über in Gestein gespeicherte Magnetfeldrichtungen nachzuweisen, lieferten oft widersprüchliche Ergebnisse, weil die gleichzeitige Bewegung einzelner Kontinentalplatten die Messdaten überlagert. Das Team aus Oslo wählte deshalb einen anderen physikalischen Ansatz: Wenn sich die feste Erdhülle relativ zur Rotationsachse verschiebt, ändert sich vor Ort die Fliehkraft – in der Fachsprache das Zentrifugalpotenzial –, worauf das flüssige Wasser der Weltmeere sofort reagiert, während das feste Gestein des Meeresbodens erst mit großer Verzögerung nachgibt.
Dadurch entsteht bei einer schnellen Polwanderung ein charakteristisches globales Vier-Felder-Muster, das Geolog:innen als Quadrupol-Signal bezeichnen und das optisch den Segmenten eines Wasserballs ähnelt. Während Kontinentalflächen, die sich in Richtung Äquator bewegen, überflutet werden, zieht sich das Meer in Regionen zurück, die näher an die Pole rücken, Dabei verhalten sich Nord- und Südhalbkugel jeweils gegenläufig.
Um dieses Muster in geologischen Überflutungskarten der vergangenen 320 Millionen Jahre aufzuspüren, teilten die Forscher:innen die Erdoberfläche mithilfe der Open-Source-Programmbibliothek h3-py in ein Raster aus sechseckigen Zellen mit rund 119 Kilometern Abstand ein, wie aus den Begleitmaterialien der Untersuchung hervorgeht. Bei der Auswertung dieser Zellen musste das Team zunächst ein Störsignal herausfiltern. Wenn etwa globale Eisschilde schmelzen, steigt das Wasser weltweit gleichzeitig an und überdeckt das gesuchte Vier-Felder-Muster der Polwanderung. Ein Berechnungsverfahren zog solche allgemeinen Schwankungen der gesamten Wassermenge deshalb rechnerisch ab, um zu prüfen, ob darunter tatsächlich das gegenläufige Wasserball-Muster einer kippenden Erdhülle sichtbar wird.
Zudem mussten die Wissenschaftler:innen berücksichtigen, dass die feste Erdkruste starr wie eine durchgehende Platte reagiert. Wird ein Küstenabschnitt überflutet oder angehoben, zieht das Gestein benachbarte Gebiete im Umkreis automatisch mit, sodass viele nebeneinanderliegende Messzellen denselben Wert zeigen, ohne unabhängige Einzelbeweise zu liefern. Damit solche zusammenhängenden Regionen die Statistik nicht verfälschen, fasste eine Analyse-Software direkt benachbarte Messpunkte jeweils zu einem gemeinsamen Block zusammen und würfelte die Ergebnisse für jeden untersuchten Zeitraum 10.000-mal zufällig durcheinander, um einen Zufallstreffer auszuschließen.
Superkontinent Pangäa und methodische blinde Flecken der Geologie
Neben den vier nachgewiesenen Verschiebungsphasen widerlegen die auf der Forschungsplattform Zenodo hinterlegten Daten und Programmiercodes auch eine verbreitete Annahme zum Urkontinent Pangäa, der einst fast alle Landmassen der Erde vereinte. Weil in den Karten für die Zeit vor 320 bis 250 Millionen Jahren das typische Vier-Felder-Muster der Meere fehlt, wanderte diese zusammenhängende Landmasse damals offenbar durch gewöhnliche Plattentektonik nach Norden und nicht durch ein Kippen der gesamten Erdhülle. Gegenüber Earth.com erklärte Mathew Domeier, er habe das Projekt ursprünglich mit der Erwartung begonnen, überhaupt keine Belege für schnelle Polwanderungen in den vergangenen paar hundert Millionen Jahren zu finden.
Allerdings hat auch das neue Verfahren blinde Flecken, weil die verwendeten Überflutungskarten die Erdgeschichte nur in groben Zeitschritten von jeweils zehn Millionen Jahren abbilden. Kippt die Erdhülle innerhalb einer kürzeren Zeitspanne in eine Richtung und schwingt anschließend direkt wieder zurück – wie es andere Wissenschaftler:innen etwa für ein Ereignis vor rund 84 Millionen Jahren vermuten –, steigt und fällt der Meeresspiegel genau zwischen zwei Kartenaufnahmen, sodass die Bewegung für das Modell unsichtbar bleibt.
Zudem ist das älteste der vier gefundenen Signale aus der Zeit vor 200 bis 190 Millionen Jahren nach Einschätzung der Autor:innen selbst ein unsicherer Kandidat. Da der gemessene Ausschlag nur knapp über dem Wert liegt, den auch normale Zufallsschwankungen erzeugen können, handelt es sich hierbei möglicherweise um einen bloßen Zufallstreffer. Noch weiter als 320 Millionen Jahre lässt sich mit der Methode derzeit gar nicht in die Vergangenheit blicken, weil vor der Entstehung von Pangäa zwar die Nord-Süd-Lage früherer Kontinente bekannt ist, Geolog:innen deren damalige Ost-West-Position auf dem Globus aber nicht mehr verlässlich bestimmen können.

articles.title: 1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents log in without ever seeing the password - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents log in without ever seeing the password
Identity security company 1Password today launched 1Password for Agents, its new sign-in platform for personal artificial intelligence agents.
Agents from Meta Platforms Inc., Anthropic PBC, OpenAI Group PBC and Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI will be able to log in to people’s accounts through it without ever seeing the password.
1Password for Agents is aimed at a habit that took hold once agents started paying bills and planning vacations for people. Most of those jobs mean getting into an account. The easy route has been to paste the password into the agent’s chat window, which leaves a copy saved somewhere outside the owner’s control.
Aashish Tripathi, chief product officer at 1Password, said agents are “starting to do real work on our behalf.” In his view, an agent asked to do one task has no reason to walk away with permanent access to the whole account.
Under the new setup, the password never travels to the agent at all. A unique digital key identifies the agent to 1Password when it hits a login page, and the request that follows tells the person which account is wanted and for what. Nothing goes ahead until the person approves it on their own device, at which point 1Password types the password into the page itself.
OpenAI has connected ChatGPT Work and its always-on Dots agents to 1Password, and Meta’s Muse requests logins from 1Password whenever the integration is switched on. Work assistant startup Town.com Inc., which raised $108 million this week, has signed up too. With 1Password connected, SpaceXSI’s Grok Bot can sign in without anyone pasting a password into it, according to head of product Tido Carriero.
Claude has worked with 1Password in the browser since July. Anthropic’s Claude Duet agent, released Wednesday, comes next. Duet asks before signing in anywhere, and Anthropic Chief Product Officer Ami Vora said 1Password will “soon” fill in those sign-ins using passwords people have already set up. Anthropic wants that kind of help within reach of people “who’ve never before let an agent near their accounts,” she said.
Beyond the launch partners, nine more companies are building their own integrations. Perplexity AI Inc. and Browserbase Inc. are on that list, and their browser-based agents have been connected to 1Password since late 2025.
Canva Pty Ltd. and Stripe Inc. are among more than 200,000 businesses that use 1Password. The company did not say when each partner integration will reach users.
The launch follows an argument for tying agent access to individual tasks that 1Password Chief Technology Officer Nancy Wang made last month at Okta Inc.’s Oktane conference. Speaking with theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio, she described an agent as “probably both” machine and human. Under task-based access, an agent should have to “prove that it actually finished its last task with the right level of permissions” before it gets more, Wang said.
