articles.title: The secret to fast startup growth isn't early sales, top names in tech say | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The AI era has changed how fast startups can grow. Startups can grow so fast that they hit high annual recurring revenue (ARR) numbers, only to crash and burn a few months later. At this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt, Lovable go-to-market lead Luke Arno, Ben Broca of the AI platform Polsia, and Theory Ventures’ Tomasz Tunguz gave founders some tips on how to set their companies up for success in those first 90 days.
Broca, whose company Polsia uses AI agents to build and run businesses with almost no human staff (Broca says he is its only employee), said that product-market fit is one of the hardest things to find right now, especially in an era when so many products can easily be copied by competitors. In response, Arno said that durable go-to-market strategies are those that can be reliably repeated.
“The most critical thing for founders or earlier-stage companies to do is develop learning density or pattern recognition for where your customers are,” Arno said. “Don’t rush to build out a top-down go-to-market motion if you’re not there yet.”
That’s why, in those first 90 days after launching a commercial product that’s ready to sell, founders should not mistake early, fast revenue for a sign that the startup is ready to scale, Arno said.
Once a startup finds use cases that work, it will only be ready to build out a sales team and go for growth after it can attract new customers by repeating what has worked. If every sale requires new tactics, the startup hasn’t truly hit product-market fit.
“If I bring on 10 new customers in 10 different ways to solve 10 different problems, sure, I brought revenue in, but I don’t have a way to go scale a go-to-market,” Arno said. “If I bring three customers in with a similar motion to solve a similar problem, now I have high confidence that I can go scale.”
Lovable, the AI app-building startup, set a lot of those early benchmarks with how fast it grew, and now founders everywhere are feeling the pressure to do the same. Lovable is valued at more than $13 billion by its investors, says its ARR has passed $600 million, and has raised more than $700 million in funding to date.
“The expectations for overall execution speed are absolutely tremendous,” Tunguz said.
But Tunguz said growth like Lovable’s is still the exception, though founders should still move fast. The pressure they feel is real, he said, because far more money flows through the startup ecosystem at every stage than when he began investing in 2008. Today, a seed deal brought in by one of his partners could just as easily be a $5 million raise, a $50 million raise, or a $500 million raise.
The winners all focus on one thing: understanding their customers well enough to know what will keep them around even after any hype subsides.
“Community building is very important and being close to customers is very important,” Broca said. He said founders can send emails and throw events, and he personally likes to talk to a lot of his customers: “The general rule is always to be talking to customers.”

articles.title: Mass Effect, Dragon Age... après 31 ans, BioWare ferme ses portes et laisse des millions de joueurs orphelins
articles.text:
Electronic Arts ferme BioWare, le studio d’Edmonton à l’origine de Baldur’s Gate, Mass Effect et Dragon Age, et abandonne le prochain Mass Effect. Environ 400 postes sont supprimés chez l’éditeur, dont une cinquantaine chez BioWare.
C’est une page de l’histoire du jeu vidéo qui se tourne, annoncée dans un mémo interne puis confirmée par BioWare sur ses réseaux. Fondé en 1995 et racheté par EA en 2007, le studio disparaît quelques mois après le passage d’EA sous capitaux privés, dans un rachat de 55 milliards de dollars. La direction y voit un recentrage sur ses valeurs sûres : Battlefield, Apex Legends et les jeux de sport. Le projet Mass Effect, lui, n’en était qu’à un stade précoce de développement.
La direction d’EA ne veut plus d’un Mass Effect en développement
Dans leur mémo, Cam Weber (chief studios officer) et David Tinson (COO) expliquent qu’une « petite équipe » de BioWare travaillait sur les premiers développements de Mass Effect, et qu’EA a décidé de ne pas aller plus loin. Conséquence : fermeture du studio et de ses locaux d’Edmonton. Les deux dirigeants parlent d’un « studio légendaire » et assurent ne pas prendre la décision « à la légère ».
Le calendrier est cruel pour les fans. Il y a moins d’un an, Mike Gamble, producteur exécutif de Mass Effect, affirmait encore que le prochain épisode était en développement et qu’EA et BioWare restaient engagés à raconter de nouvelles histoires dans cet univers. Le jeu devait se dérouler plusieurs centaines d’années après Mass Effect 3 et recentrer l’action sur la Voie lactée. La série télévisée Prime Video reste, elle, en développement chez Amazon MGM Studios.
Anthem, Andromeda, Veilguard : des années de résultats en dessous des attentes
La fermeture n’arrive pas comme un cheveu sur la soupe. Mass Effect: Andromeda (2017) a reçu un accueil mitigé, Anthem (2019) a été le pari raté du studio sur le jeu service, et Dragon Age: The Veilguard n’a pas atteint les objectifs de vente, ce qui avait déjà valu des licenciements chez BioWare en 2025. Seule la Legendary Edition de la trilogie Mass Effect, sortie en 2021, a été bien accueillie. La dernière grande réussite commerciale du studio, Dragon Age: Inquisition, remonte à plusieurs années.
Le contexte financier pèse aussi. Le rachat par le fonds saoudien PIF, Silver Lake et Affinity Partners a laissé EA avec environ 18 milliards de dollars de dette. L’éditeur s’est engagé à réduire ses coûts annuels de 700 millions de dollars, dont 170 millions d’« efficacités organisationnelles » qui se traduisent désormais en suppressions de postes. EA aurait déjà licencié environ 970 personnes au cours des deux dernières années.
Ce qu’EA garde au catalogue : Battlefield, Apex, sport et Star Wars
Le mémo de BioWare détaille les priorités : Battlefield 6 est qualifié de « grand succès », et Respawn et DICE vont collaborer sur un futur projet qui pourrait « probablement » être un nouveau Star Wars: Battlefront. EA promet aussi d’« investir massivement » dans Apex Legends avec de nouveaux modes de jeu. Marvel’s Iron Man et le prochain Star Wars Jedi sont maintenus, mais l’éditeur annonce moins de grands projets simultanés dans l’action-aventure.
Côté sport, deux projets seront dévoilés dans les prochains mois : « Project Gridiron », une expérience de football américain en monde ouvert à dimension sociale, et un retour de Fight Night, en préproduction. Pour Les Sims, « Project Lotus » est mis en pause au profit de « Project Evergreen », tandis que skate. Va être confié à une équipe plus petite et plus ciblée. Tous les jeux de BioWare ont été sacrifiés d’un coup : EA n’a rien précisé sur l’avenir des licences Dragon Age et Mass Effect.
Pour les fans de Mass Effect, difficile toutefois de ne pas tourner désormais les regards vers Exodus. Attendu le 7 avril 2027 sur PC, PS5 et Xbox Series, ce RPG de science-fiction développé par Archetype Entertainment a tout d’un héritier spirituel de la saga. Et pour cause : le studio réunit plusieurs anciens de BioWare, dont James Ohlen, figure historique du studio, et surtout Drew Karpyshyn, scénariste des deux premiers Mass Effect. Exploration spatiale, compagnons, choix aux lourdes conséquences… Tous les ingrédients semblent réunis pour faire renaître un peu de cette magie. BioWare disparaît, mais son héritage pourrait bien lui survivre.

articles.title: Des rafales à plus de 100 km/h : la tempête Austen s'apprête à balayer le nord-ouest de la France
articles.text:
La France se prépare à l’arrivée de la tempête Austen. Météo-France a prévenu ce mercredi 21 octobre que la « première tempête de l’automne » arrivait sur l’hexagone. Le service de météorologie annonce un « risque de rafales dépassant 100 km/h sur la Bretagne, la Normandie et les Hauts-de-France dès la nuit de jeudi et dans la journée de vendredi ».
Ce jeudi 22 octobre, 3 départements sont placés en vigilance orange vent, en raison de l’arrivée de cette tempête. Vendredi, la vigilance orange concernera 15 départements.
La tempête a été nommée Austen par le Met Office, le service national britannique de météorologie, le 20 octobre. « Une zone de basse pression se formant dans l’Atlantique va rapidement s’intensifier sous l’effet du courant-jet », a prévenu le Met Office.
Pourquoi un nom choisi par les Britanniques ? Météo-France baptise elle aussi des tempêtes, avec ses homologues d’Espagne, du Portugal, de Belgique, du Luxembourg et d’Andorre, pour les dépressions susceptibles de toucher l’un de ces pays. Austen vient de la liste du Met Office, qui l’a nommée le premier : le Royaume-Uni est lui aussi sur sa trajectoire, et une alerte jaune au vent y a été émise pour le sud de l’Angleterre et le sud du pays de Galles.
Les cartes prévoyant la tempête Austen en France
Sur les réseaux sociaux, des spécialistes et passionnés de météorologie partagent des cartes issues des modèles de prévision, qui montrent la trajectoire attendue de la tempête vers les côtes françaises et le Royaume-Uni.
Des vents à plus de 100 km/h en France
« La tempête Austen se rapproche de la Bretagne dans les dernières sorties de modèles », écrit Guillaume Jauseau, étudiant à l’université de Toulon, anciennement chargé de contenu scientifique en climatologie pour Météo-Contact. Il évoque des rafales de 130 à 140 km/h sur la côte, à « des niveaux capables de causer des dégâts ».
Selon l’association Infoclimat, la probabilité que les rafales dépassent 100 km/h est importante dans le Finistère, le Morbihan, l’Ille-et-Vilaine et la Manche, jusque dans les terres. « Le scénario actuellement envisagé fait apparaître une dégradation débutant par la Bretagne, avant une propagation progressive des vents forts vers les Pays de la Loire, la Normandie, puis les régions situées plus à l’est. »
Météo-France invite à la plus grande prudence
Des chutes d’arbres sont possibles, « d’autant que la végétation porte encore une grande partie de ses feuilles », souligne Météo-France. Les habitations ou infrastructures pourraient être endommagées, notamment au niveau des toitures. Les autorités recommandent de limiter les déplacements, de s’éloigner du littoral exposé et de suivre l’évolution de la situation sur la carte de vigilance de Météo-France. À noter que des coupures d’électricité sont possibles.
Les transports sont déjà touchés. La SNCF a annoncé que la circulation des trains serait interrompue vendredi sur les lignes normandes, et en partie sur les lignes bretonnes et du Nord, avec des perturbations à prévoir samedi.
Pour rappel, Météo-France estime qu’un vent est dangereux « lorsque sa vitesse atteint environ 100 km/h en rafales dans l’intérieur des terres ». Un seuil variable selon les régions : « Il est par exemple plus élevé pour les régions littorales ou la région sud-est, plus habituées aux vents forts. »
Cet article a été mis à jour à 16h45 avec le nouveau nombre de départements placés en vigilance orange pour le vendredi 23 octobre.

articles.title: Microsoft shares how to fix broken Exchange Online EWS apps
articles.text:
Microsoft says IT admins can re-enable the retired Exchange Web Services (EWS) API in Exchange Online to fix EWS apps that have stopped working.
EWS is an API for developing apps that can access Exchange mailbox items (e.g., email messages, meetings, and contacts) from Exchange Online and on-premises Exchange servers.
This API is used by various apps, including but not limited to Outlook desktop add-ins, older versions of Outlook for Windows, the Apple Mail / Calendar on macOS, and various other apps.
In February, the company announced it will start blocking the EWS API by default on October 1, 2026, but will let IT administrators temporarily maintain access via an app allowlist until the final shutdown on April 1, 2027. However, when EWS is disabled, the apps show errors ranging from alerts that the EWS protocol is unavailable to repeated prompts to enter the username or password.
To avoid these issues and fix EWS apps that are no longer working, Microsoft says tenant administrators can re-enable EWS in the Microsoft 365 admin center Baseline Security Mode by unchecking "Block your entire organization from using EWS" on the Baseline Security Mode page.
Another option is to use Exchange Online PowerShell to run the "Set-OrganizationConfig -EWSEnabled $true" command, which should re-enable EWS within 4 hours.
"We are now in the first stage of EWS disablement, where customers are still able to re-enable EWS. Re-enabling EWS will stop working in April 2027," Microsoft said.
"The long-term solution is to update your applications to the application versions that do not use EWS. You must contact your application vendor to get the updated application version, or if you created the application yourself, you must change the code to not use EWS anymore."
Microsoft also advised app developers using the EWS API to switch to the Microsoft Graph API before EWS shuts down, since it has near-complete feature parity with EWS for most scenarios.
The company also added that the EWS retirement process affects only Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online environments, and the API will continue to work in on-premises Exchange Server installations.
The EWS retirement announcement followed a 2018 warning that EWS would stop receiving functionality updates and Microsoft's September 2023 announcement that it planned to begin shutting down the EWS API in October 2026.
In October 2021, Microsoft revealed that it had deprecated the 25 least-used EWS Exchange Online APIs and removed support for them in March 2022 for security reasons.

articles.title: Pourquoi certains smartphones ne pourront bientôt plus faire tourner l'application Revolut
articles.text:
Après une panne de grande envergure ce mardi 20 octobre, la banque en ligne Revolut est de nouveau sous le feu des projecteurs. Le compte X (Twitter) de Webologie a remarqué que les conditions générales de la néo-banque allaient changer.
La nouvelle clause figure dans les conditions générales de Revolut Bank S.A., l’entité bancaire française de Revolut, vers laquelle la néo-banque transfère les comptes de ses clients français. Cette version s’applique à partir du 2 décembre 2026.
Parmi les ajouts, une ligne qui confirme la position de l’établissement à l’encontre des systèmes d’exploitation alternatifs pour smartphone comme GrapheneOS. Les équipes de ce dernier accusent Revolut de bloquer son application sur leur OS depuis le 6 août 2026. Ce n’est visiblement pas près de s’arranger.
L’application Revolut seulement utilisable sur un appareil dont l’OS n’a pas été modifié
Au point 5 des nouvelles conditions générales, intitulé « Comment obtenir des informations sur les paiements depuis et vers mon compte ? », on trouve la mention suivante : « Pour utiliser l’application Revolut, recevoir nos communications et garantir la sécurité de votre compte et de vos données, votre appareil mobile doit répondre à certaines exigences techniques et logicielles ».
Parmi les trois points cités, l’un d’eux dispose que vous devez « utiliser le système d’exploitation d’origine de votre appareil, pris en charge par le fabricant ». Pas de root, de jailbreak ou de ROM custom donc. C’est le cas aussi bien pour un compte Revolut Personnel que Business.
Revolut prévient aussi des conséquences. Selon ses conditions, contourner les protections de sécurité du téléphone ou installer un système non officiel « augmente considérablement le risque » pour vos données, et la banque ne sera pas responsable des failles de sécurité de l’appareil ni des pertes qui en découlent. En clair, un client victime d’une fraude depuis un téléphone rooté ou sous ROM custom pourrait se voir opposer cette clause.
    À lire aussi : 
Votre compte bancaire Revolut va être transféré : qu’est-ce que ça change ?
L’argument de sécurité peut étonner, puisque l’application Revolut accepte encore Android 9, une version sortie en 2018. Plusieurs des versions prises en charge ne reçoivent donc plus de mises à jour de sécurité depuis des années.
C’est moins vrai sur iOS, qui demande iOS 15 ou plus. Apple a encore publié une mise à jour de sécurité pour cette version le 11 mai 2026 (iOS 15.8.8), destinée aux iPhone 6s, iPhone 7 et iPhone SE de première génération.
GrapheneOS relève une autre incohérence. D’après le projet, l’application Revolut refuse les téléphones dont le bootloader est reverrouillé avec une clé autre que celle du constructeur (l’état « yellow » du démarrage vérifié), mais laisse passer ceux dont le bootloader est déverrouillé, pourtant bien moins protégés.
Revolut n’est pas la seule banque à demander un appareil non modifié pour l’utilisation de son application. Les restrictions varient en fonction de l’établissement, mais d’une manière générale, root, jailbreak et ROM custom empêchent de s’en servir pleinement, voire tout court.
Les conditions générales de BoursoBank, par exemple, disent que Samsung Pay, Google Pay et Garmin Pay cessent de fonctionner « lorsque l’Appareil Compatible a subi des modifications non-autorisées sur le système d’exploitation (telles qu’un débridage du 
système d’exploitation ou « jailbreak ») ».
Les clients Revolut qui utilisent un téléphone modifié ont encore un peu de temps. La banque doit envoyer les nouvelles conditions par e-mail au moins deux mois avant leur entrée en vigueur, le 2 décembre 2026. Sans réaction de leur part, elles sont considérées comme acceptées. Ceux qui les refusent peuvent fermer leur compte avant cette date, sans frais.

articles.title: Google Pixel : cette fonctionnalité qu'on attend depuis des années arrive bientôt sur le Pixel Launcher
articles.text:
Depuis l’arrivée d’Android 8.0 Oreo, le système d’exploitation mobile de Google utilise les pastilles de notification sur les icônes d’applications pour signaler les messages en attente. Contrairement à d’autres interfaces concurrentes qui proposent le chiffre exact depuis des années, les smartphones Pixel sont restés bloqués sur cet indicateur visuel très basique. Mais la dernière version QPR3 Beta 2 d’Android 17 montre que Google prépare un changement bienvenu pour personnaliser ces notifications.
Une nouvelle manière d’afficher les notifications sur les icônes d’applications
L’analyse de la dernière version bêta d’Android 17 a permis de révéler un menu dans l’onglet « Pastille de notification sur l’icône de l’application ». Cette rubrique, pour l’instant cachée, se trouve dans les réglages actuels qui permettent de régler la façon dont s’affichent les notifications sur les icônes du bureau.
Source : Android Authority
Selon le code, trois choix seront proposés à l’utilisateur des smartphones Pixel : afficher le nombre exact de messages en attente, conserver le point classique que l’on connaît aujourd’hui, ou désactiver totalement les notifications sur les icônes.
Une fonctionnalité qui demande encore à être peaufinée
Cette nouveauté n’en est peut-être pas une pour ceux qui ont déjà eu entre les mains plusieurs marques de smartphones Android, mais son arrivée sera néanmoins une excellente nouvelle pour les utilisateurs de smartphones Google Pixel qui profitent de beaucoup de fonctionnalités, mais toujours pas de cette dernière, pourtant assez basique.
Comme souvent avec ces trouvailles dans les versions bêta d’Android, la fonctionnalité va encore demander quelques peaufinages avant d’arriver sur la version stable du Pixel Launcher. Une fois de plus, la patience des heureux possesseurs de téléphones Pixel devrait être récompensée.

articles.title: Africa’s stablecoin promise breaks at the off-ramp
articles.text: On paper, it was a revolution. Over the past three years, three of Africa’s largest multi-licensed payment service providers each independently piloted a stablecoin rail. Between them, they process cross-border payments for merchants, e-commerce platforms, and remittance companies, as well as trade settlements, totalling billions of dollars annually. Their models promised to cut the cost of cross-border money movement by 10x. After stress-testing the off-ramp, each settled on a mix of stablecoin and traditional bank rails. The blockchain worked, but the off-ramp did not. Converting back into local currency costs more than 8%, and in thin markets, the savings disappear. Their experience exposes a truth the industry keeps skipping: stablecoins will not fix African cross-border finance until founders fix local liquidity. I sit on a venture fund’s investment committee and back startups as an angel investor. Every cross-border fintech and payments startup that pitches me today is a stablecoin startup. Stablecoins are now table stakes for anyone building across borders. The case is not imaginary. Sub-Saharan Africa remains the most expensive region to send money to, averaging 8.5% on a $200 transfer compared with 6% globally, according to the World Bank . Chainalysis estimates that a $200 remittance sent from the region costs about 60% less when using stablecoins. But that estimate prices the conversion off a single day’s closing rate: a snapshot of the quoted price, not the price you get at size. Every cross-border payment does three jobs: messaging, compliance and settlement into locally spendable money. Stablecoins handle the first job well and make the second no easier. On the third, a USDC/USDT transfer is final within seconds, but finality does not equal spendability. A trader in Lagos does not pay rent in USDT. The freelancer in Nairobi cannot pay for their child’s school fees in USDC. Someone has to sell their naira or shillings, and someone has to deliver it. The blockchain gives you finality. It does not give you naira or shillings. The real cost sits in two places. The first is FX. Converting a dollar stablecoin into cedis or kwacha requires a counterparty who holds the local currency, wants dollars, and can trade at that moment and in that size. Outside a handful of the region’s largest markets, that pair is thin. Thin pairs produce slippage: the gap between the price you are quoted and the price you actually get, as a large order eats through the best offers and fills at progressively worse ones. Across the CFA region, at typical transfers of $100,000, spread, slippage and payout fees together exceeded 8%. Even vetted counterparties often lack depth, so prices are haggled over WhatsApp DMs, group chats, and phone calls between treasury desks before a trade settles. That is not a market. It is a negotiation. Then there is someone who sits on the other side. Some liquidity pools are anonymous, and some participants are there to launder money. The leading liquidity providers deal only with businesses that have passed know-your-business (KYB) checks. That keeps the pool clean and small. The temptation is an open marketplace such as Binance P2P, with more counterparties, but many of them are PSPs whose compliance team may not be able to clear. Some providers trade with unknown entities anyway. So the stricter your compliance, the shallower the market you can legally touch. Chainalysis reports that Sub-Saharan Africa led the world in crypto growth through June 2026, driven by peer-to-peer activity. Much of that depth is off-limits to a licensed PSP. And informal venues vanish: Binance delisted the naira from its P2P market in February 2024. The second cost is the last mile. Local payment rails carry fixed costs and regulatory requirements that only pay off at scale. Below that scale, much of the volume is routed through cross-border rails, which the PSPs found can cost 10 times as much as a local payment. A stablecoin does not remove that cost. It moves it to the end of the journey. The bigger mistake is the benchmark. Pitch decks measure stablecoins against the 8.5% regional average. The PSPs’ clients were not choosing the average. Globally, digital-only money transfer operators charged 3.54%, and payouts into mobile wallets cost 3.92%, the World Bank reports. Against those rails, an 8% off-ramp is priced at twice the rate. So the PSPs now run a mix of stablecoin rails, where local liquidity is deep, and traditional bank rails, where it is not. Client costs fell from [X]% to [Y]%. It is less exciting than a revolution. It is also real. Stablecoins still earn their place in business treasury, dollar savings and corridors with deep, licensed liquidity. But before launching one for payments, founders should price conversions at their actual ticket price on the worst day of the week, count the licensed counterparties they can use, model what happens if their main venue disappears, and benchmark against the cheapest rail their customer already has. Where a stablecoin corridor cannot beat traditional rails, do not force it. The next breakthrough in African payments will not come from a faster chain. It will come from whoever makes local liquidity deep, licensed and boring. Gwera Kiwana is Partnerships Lead at Morse. She serves on the investment committee of Launch Africa Ventures and has angel-invested in more than a dozen Africa-focused startups over the past seven years. She previously worked at Monzo, 11:FS and Onafriq, and co-founded Women Who Build Africa.

articles.title: Des scientifiques analysent des débris de l’explosion d’Hiroshima et découvrent un alliage métallique qui n’avait jamais été observé auparavant
articles.text:
Des scientifiques analysent des débris de l’explosion d’Hiroshima et découvrent un alliage métallique qui n’avait jamais été observé auparavant
C’est dans les débris de l’explosion atomique d’Hiroshima que des scientifiques ont fait une découverte étonnante. Dedans, ils ont trouvé un alliage métallique jamais observé jusque-là. C’est dans une minuscule bille vitrifiée retrouvée dans les sables de la baie d’Hiroshima que les scientifiques ont fait leur découverte. Et sa composition, tout comme son organisation atomique, montre ce qu’il s’est produit dans les secondes après l’explosion de la bombe nucléaire des États-Unis sur le Japon.
Dans cette étude publiée dans Science Advances, les scientifiques se sont penchés sur des fragments formés suite à la destruction d’Hiroshima puis conservés dans les sédiments de la baie. Pour le rappel historique, c’est le 6 août 1945 que les États-Unis larguent une bombe sur Hiroshima, une attaque qui a créé une énorme boule de feu dont la température a dépassé 7 000 degrés en quelques secondes.
Un alliage inédit découvert à Hiroshima
La chaleur a vaporisé des matériaux de construction, des métaux, des sols, du verre et de l’eau. Un mélange qui a ensuite formé un nuage de matière chauffée à haute température avant de refroidir rapidement. Une minuscule partie s’est transformée en minuscules grains qui ont atterri dans les sables de la baie. Les chercheurs appellent ces débris des hiroshimaites. Il s’agit de petites billes de verre produites par l’explosion et figées par le refroidissement rapide.
L’équipe a étudié 34 échantillons grâce à plusieurs techniques pour révéler leur composition et l’organisation de leurs atomes. Dans un seul échantillon, on trouvait de nombreux fragments métalliques riches en fer et en chrome. Les scientifiques ont extrait quatre grains d’environ 10 micromètres, soit bien moins que l’épaisseur d’un cheveu.
Si trois des grains extraits avaient une structure typique pour ce type de métal, c’est le quatrième grain qui a surtout retenu l’attention des scientifiques. Le fer représentait 62,69 % de sa masse et 14,71 % pour le chrome. Le nickel était à 8,95 % et le silicium à 7,02 %.
On trouvait aussi du molybdène, du manganèse et de l’aluminium dans cet alliage très complexe. Les mesures faites à plusieurs endroits du grain montraient une composition homogène, ce qui veut dire que les éléments se sont mélangés puis la matière s’est figée très vite.
Les rayons X ont également montré que les atomes suivent une organisation cubique très précise appelée structure de type AlAu4. Une organisation qui existe dans d’autres matériaux mais ce qui est surprenant ici, c’est que les chercheurs n’ont jamais décrit cet assemblage avec une combinaison de fer, chrome, nickel, silicium, molybdène, manganèse, aluminium.
Le grain a beau ne mesurer que quelques micromètres, son organisation atomique a survécu près de huit décennies dans le verre qui l’entoure.
Un alliage né de l’explosion nucléaire
Les scientifiques ont une hypothèse pour expliquer sa naissance. Dans la boule de feu de l’explosion d’Hiroshima, des métaux de sources différentes furent vaporisés puis mélangés. Lors du refroidissement, une petite quantité de cette vapeur métallique s’est condensée sous forme de gouttes.
La chute brutale de température a figé trop rapidement les atomes pour qu’ils adoptent des structures plus simples que l’on retrouve dans des conditions ordinaires. Le résultat, c’est cet alliage complexe gardé dans le verre pendant toutes ces années.
Mais l’échantillon nous donne aussi une idée du chaos chimique créé par l’explosion. La diversité de composition indique que de petites gouttes de métal se sont séparées du matériau fondu, se sont heurtées puis mélangées ou se sont mélangées puis ont durci.
Les auteurs expliquent que les explosions nucléaires créent brièvement des conditions similaires à des impacts de météorites ou des collisions planétaires à très grande vitesse. Des cas où l’on retrouve des températures extrêmes, des changements rapides de pression et un refroidissement brutal.
Les débris d’Hiroshima permettent désormais aux scientifiques d’étudier comment se forment les matériaux en dehors de l’équilibre, c’est-à-dire des structures qui n’ont pas le temps d’atteindre leur état habituel.

articles.title: OpenAI’s COBOL migration score has made a striking leap
articles.text:
OpenAI’s COBOL migration score has made a striking leap
This week, OpenAI put COBOL in the spotlight. It announced benchmark results suggesting its latest models are getting much better at migrating COBOL programs and building software in languages with less code and documentation for models to learn from.
On OpenAI’s own COBOL migration test, GPT-6.1 Sol reached 86.6% accuracy at low reasoning effort, up from GPT-5.6 Sol’s 5.4%, while costing 39% less. At higher reasoning effort, the newer model reached 97.9%.
But the evidence behind the two evaluations is uneven.
OpenAI has not published the details of its evaluation of COBOL (“Common Business-Oriented Language”; the programming language that AI coding tools may help maintain or migrate). It has released the MultiLangBench setup and test suite on GitHub. That benchmark tests whether models can build a SQLite-compatible database engine from scratch across 20 programming languages.
OpenAI’s announcement calls the results “substantial improvements across both evaluations, delivering much higher accuracy at lower cost.”
Those results could matter to teams maintaining and modernizing legacy software. But without public COBOL test cases, developers cannot independently inspect that evaluation.
Is there finally some hope for modernizing COBOL?
Per OpenAI, its new COBOL migration evaluation “tests whether a model can migrate existing programs to another language while preserving their behavior.” Specifically, it’s testing migrations from COBOL to C++, Java, Kotlin, Python, and Rust.
To succeed, each migration must pass a series of hidden tests that require “byte-for-byte parity on observable outputs.” And with markedly greater accuracy than its predecessor, GPT-6.1 Sol is, indeed, showing substantial progress.
The measured gains are striking, though OpenAI is not the first company to bring AI to COBOL modernization.
Even though COBOL underpins much of the world’s financial transactions and business records — IBM reports COBOL underpins over 40% of all online banking systems, supports 80% of in-person credit card transactions, and handles 95% of all ATM transactions — it remains a difficult target for AI coding tools.
Compared with Python and JavaScript, models have less COBOL code and documentation to learn from. Experienced COBOL developers can also be hard to find, and documentation often lags behind the systems they maintain.
AI coding gains across 20 languages
Alongside its COBOL migration tests, OpenAI developed a second evaluation to measure models’ ability to build software from scratch, MultiLangBench. This benchmark “tests whether a model can build a SQLite-compatible database engine across 20 different programming languages.”
First, the program gets a database and SQL query. Then, it produces a modified database. The reference SQLite implementation serves as the ground truth to check if the resulting database contains the expected data.
On average, GPT-6 Astra — OpenAI’s flagship model — achieved an 87.4% test pass rate across 20 programming languages, a hefty jump from GPT-5.6 Sol’s modest 26.8%. It scored above 83% on 19 out of 20 languages and made improvements on all of them.
GPT-6 Luna, predictably, didn’t do as well as Astra, with the lower-cost option only achieving an average pass rate of 40.3%. That said, it did manage to outperform GPT-5.6 Sol on every language tested, with an approximate 78% lower estimated API cost.
All right, then. Keep your secrets.
OpenAI reports promising results from its COBOL migration evaluation and MultiLangBench, but benchmarks don’t tell the whole story. As of Thursday, Real-SWE 1.1, which uses private codebases, lists Claude Opus 5.5 in first place at 56.8% resolution. An earlier Real-SWE run covered by The New Stack had a different leader and lower scores.
Plus, developers still can’t inspect OpenAI’s COBOL migration benchmark. The announcement credits feedback from developers and enterprise customers for guiding the work, but without the underlying tests and dataset, outsiders can’t independently check the results.
OpenAI acknowledges a key limitation, noting that “applying it to production software still requires expert review and testing against the system’s business rules and dependencies.”
OpenAI is entering a field others have been working on for some time. Anthropic outlined how Claude Code could assist COBOL modernization on February 23. As The New Stack reported, AWS introduced AI agents for mainframe migrations in 2024.

articles.title: Amsterdam’s Indurex raises €7 million to strengthen cybersecurity and safety across cyber-physical systems | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Indurex, an Amsterdam-based startup building an AI-native platform for Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) security, has raised €7 million in funding, less than nine months after coming out of stealth.
The round was led by Contrarian Ventures, the European early-stage firm that backs energy and industrial technology companies, with participation from Axeleo Capital and Dutch venture capital firm Curiosity.
“Electrification is putting more critical infrastructure online, and attacks on it are rising, with the damage felt in the physical world: cold homes, dark hospitals, water that stops flowing. Detection alone is no longer enough. Operators need to understand what an alert means for the physical process behind it. Having built and sold a company in this space, Jalal knows what operators across oil and gas, power and manufacturing need, which makes Indurex one of very few companies that understands both the network packet and the physical process,” said Rokas Peciulaitis, Founder and Managing Partner at Contrarian Ventures.
Indurex was founded by Jalal Bouhdada and Maarten Oosterink, seasoned practitioners in operational technology (OT), process safety, and cybersecurity. The company launched in January 2026 with a stated goal of keeping complex cyber-physical systems resilient, safe, and secure for operators in oil and gas, energy, utilities, manufacturing, and data centres. The company brings together cybersecurity, process safety, and engineering operations under a single layer of intelligence called Engineering Intelligence.
Its offering is called Indurex SafeGuard AI, a platform that ingests data from distributed control systems, safety instrumented systems, historians, alarm management systems, and IT security tools. It then uses AI agents to surface anomalies and engineering deviations, giving operators a unified view that links cybersecurity alerts directly to the physical process behind them, something conventional OT security systems have failed to address.
“Cyber defences in these critical sectors have focused solely on the network. We focus on the core industrial data itself: the engineering, process and safety signals that determine whether a plant is operating within safe limits. Cybersecurity and operational excellence have too often been managed as separate disciplines — Engineering Intelligence is the missing layer, and this funding allows us to bring that capability to more operators across critical infrastructure,” said Bouhdada, co-founder and CEO of Indurex.
Indurex says its early customers range from mid-sized energy and manufacturing companies to large multinational enterprises. With Indurex’s AI platform, these customers are reportedly seeing value across three areas: operational excellence and safety integrity, through unified situational awareness; cyber resilience via detection and response aligned to operational and safety impact; and compliance through automated reporting against frameworks including IEC 62443, IEC 61511/61508, NIS2, NIST CSF and NERC CIP.
The funding comes as cyber threats to industrial environments intensify. According to the SANS Institute’s State of ICS/OT Security 2025 survey, more than one in five industrial organisations experienced an ICS or OT cyber incident in the past year, with 40% of those incidents disrupting operations and close to 20% taking more than a month to fully remediate.
Indurex says it will deploy the fresh capital toward research and development and expand its commercial operations across Europe and the Middle East, ahead of a subsequent expansion into the United States and Asia-Pacific.

articles.title: New Serious PHP Vulnerabilities Released and Patched - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
New Serious PHP Vulnerabilities Released and Patched
PHP maintainers have released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities:
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately.
Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.
The vulnerabilities:
- RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.
- RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.
Updating PHP is the only way to regain security. Do it now.

articles.title: Apagar el rastreo del Smart TV no sirve en Samsung y Vizio, según estudio de Estados Unidos
articles.text:
Un estudio de la Universidad Northeastern encontró que los televisores inteligentes con sistemas operativos de Samsung y Vizio siguen enviando datos hacia sus servidores de reconocimiento de contenido, incluso después de que el usuario desactiva el rastreo en la configuración.
La investigación, titulada “Watching the Watchers”, analizó 12 televisores de diez fabricantes que cubren ocho sistemas operativos distintos: Amazon, Hisense, LG, Roku, Samsung, Sony, Supersonic, TCL, Vizio y Westinghouse. En conjunto representan cerca del 95% del mercado estadounidense.
Los autores corrieron 5.943 experimentos controlados con guiones automáticos que manejaban cada televisor por Wi-Fi, mientras un software de monitoreo de red capturaba todo el tráfico entrante y saliente de los equipos.
La tecnología evaluada se llama reconocimiento automático de contenido (ACR, por su sigla en inglés). Toma capturas periódicas de audio o video de lo que se ve en pantalla, las compara con una base de datos de contenidos y así identifica qué está mirando cada usuario, información que luego sirve para medir audiencias y vender publicidad dirigida.
El opt-out de Samsung y Vizio no corta el envío de datos
En los televisores con Tizen, el sistema operativo de Samsung, el tráfico asociado al ACR continuó en los 30 de 30 ensayos de su servicio de streaming propio después de que los usuarios desactivaron el rastreo. También, persistió en 41 de 60 pruebas con antena y en 18 de 30 con conexión HDMI.
En Vizio OS, antes llamado SmartCast, el resultado fue más extremo: el tráfico hacia el servidor identificado como el más asociado al ACR, alojado en Amazon Kinesis, no mostró ninguna disminución en el 100% de las mediciones con la opción de rastreo desactivada. Esa señal incluso aparecía con el televisor encendido pero sin uso, solo en la pantalla de inicio.
Ilgar Mammadov, investigador de Northeastern y autor principal del trabajo, dijo a Ars Technica que, si los televisores efectivamente siguen rastreando a quienes rechazaron el rastreo, eso “plantearía serias dudas sobre el consentimiento y la transparencia hacia los usuarios”.
Mammadov consideró poco probable que los datos se transmitan y luego se descarten sin usarse, porque esa práctica consumiría el ancho de banda del usuario y la capacidad de los servidores de la empresa sin ningún propósito. El cifrado de la mayor parte del tráfico impidió a los investigadores confirmar qué contenido llevan esos envíos.
Roku fue la única excepción parcialmente avisada
En los televisores con Roku OS, el tráfico siguió apareciendo tras la desactivación solo cuando el usuario usaba el canal gratuito propio de la plataforma, The Roku Channel. A diferencia de Samsung y Vizio, ese comportamiento está descrito en los términos de servicio de Roku.
La diferencia entre marcas está en el aviso al usuario: los televisores TCL, que usan Roku OS, informan esa excepción en el propio menú de configuración, mientras que los Roku TV no lo hacen. El estudio encontró además tráfico continuado en 9 de 90 pruebas de antena en los equipos TCL.
El opt-out funcionó sin excepciones en otros cuatro sistemas operativos: webOS de LG, Google TV en los televisores de Sony, Fire TV OS de Amazon y VIDAA.
VIDAA envía datos sin cifrar y sin pedir autenticación
El caso de VIDAA fue distinto: aunque el apagado del rastreo sí detiene el envío, cuando el ACR está activo manda la información sin cifrar, por el protocolo MQTT, a servidores operados por la empresa Unruly.
Esos mensajes incluyen un identificador permanente del televisor, el huso horario, el nombre de la aplicación en uso, el tipo de entrada, el canal de antena y una huella de audio.
Los investigadores detectaron que un servidor de VIDAA exponía más de 57 millones de resultados de reconocimiento de contenido provenientes de más de un millón de televisores, accesible sin necesidad de iniciar sesión. Tras ser notificada, la empresa exigió autenticación para acceder a ese servidor, aunque las transmisiones siguen sin cifrarse.
Para que los usuarios puedan reducir este tipo de rastreo, los autores del estudio publicaron una lista de dominios y direcciones de red que pueden bloquearse sin afectar la calidad de la imagen, disponible en el sitio del proyecto junto con el código usado en las pruebas.

articles.title: Developer Behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready
articles.text:
Brandon Thomas put his AI-built open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications in front of Hacker News and immediately deflated them. "I wasn’t ready to post this to HN," he wrote. "It’s not anywhere close to read" He said he would post again once the project clears beta.
Announcement posts had gone up across five subreddits days earlier carrying a different message, projecting beta and roughly 100% parity within a month. The repository sides with the Hacker News version.
Thomas used Claude Opus 5.5 to build the applications in Rust, with WebAssembly builds for the browser, mirroring Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign and Acrobat Pro. All of it ships under MIT and Apache licenses.
PhotoCraft’s ROADMAP.md, updated October 11, puts feature breadth at roughly 76%, from counts: 628 of 628 menus, 56 of 68 tools, 30 of 35 panels, 13 plus 4 of 31 formats. Then comes a second number. Readiness for real work is about 45%. A mainstream practitioner gets 43%; someone using core features only gets 61%. Beta is 1,100 to 1,800 hours out and full parity 2,300 to 4,100, counted as Opus 5.5 agent wall-clock hours for one agent working sequentially. The target is named exactly: Photoshop 2026, version 27.11.0, measured from the installed application on October 10.
Screenshot of PhotoCraft, an open-source Photoshop clone, editing a Hokusai print with adjustment, type and shape layers visible in the layers panel. (Source: GitHub)
The roadmap’s own account of why the project is still alpha is harder on it than its critics are. Users of 0.5 and 0.6 have filed 579 open issues. Twenty-two of twenty-five performance budgets are missed. And "PSDs we write are not yet reliably accepted by Photoshop." For software meant to replace Photoshop, file interchange is not a rough edge.
The scale is real regardless. First commit September 30, latest October 13. In those fourteen days the repository took 2,152 commits, 1,004 merged pull requests and 539,017 lines of Rust across 1,306 files. Git records 317 distinct contributor identities, so the "solo developer" framing stopped being true almost at once. Claude appears as a named commit author 277 times.
People who installed the apps split along a line that matches the roadmap. Reddit commenter Painted-Arcana went at the Photoshop clone directly:
It’s bad. You can’t even eye dropper by pressing alt. You can’t change the layouts much beyond the static presets. I could go on and on but after 2 minutes with the app it is very clear this isn’t a photoshop replacement at all.
Photographers hit the RAW pipeline. Commenter Sea-Temporary-6995 found that raising shadows on a Sony a7c file produced noise and banding. Commenter OspreyChaser found no RAW support for several Nikon bodies. The simplest app fares best: on Hacker News, commenter Krasnol reported PDFCraft working without bugs.
Little of the coverage mentioned how much process sits in the repository. AGENTS.md carries a clean-room rule: the team "studied Photoshop and other proprietary editors for behaviour and look only," never copying code, shaders, profiles or assets, implementing "from public specs (Adobe PSD spec, ICC, ISO 32000 blend modes, papers) and observation." Tests gate every change, a panic_hunt test fuzzes every command with adversarial parameters, and format work is checked against a corpus of Photoshop-authored PSDs. The apps also expose a JSON control channel and an MCP server, so the coding agent can drive the running app and screenshot it to check its own interface work.
That language is where opinion divides. Commenter kmeisthax was flat about it: "There is no such thing as clean-room vibe coding." The doctrine normally assumes two separated teams, one writing specs and another implementing without seeing the original.
The most measured voice came from someone running the same experiment. Commenter az_liberal_geek is building Hew, an open-source SketchUp replacement, also with Claude:
The very first version of Hew came out fast and looked and worked fantastic. But it was also super buggy and failed in unexpected ways. Adding a major feature takes a prompt + several hours of Claude develop, followed by many more hours of my own testing and refining.
He put parity at a year, not a month. The repository’s own estimate lands in similar territory.
Thomas has since adjusted the public figure too, telling Hacker News that "99% parity will take a while, but I’m sure it’ll be measured in months and not years."

articles.title: Falha grave no PHP fez sites e serviços públicos saírem do ar • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Falha grave no PHP fez sites e serviços públicos saírem do ar
Cloudflare ativou proteções, mas servidores precisam ser atualizados.
Duas vulnerabilidades no PHP, linguagem de programação open source usada pela maioria dos sites, foram reveladas nesta quarta-feira (21/10). Elas podem permitir a interrupção de serviços, o vazamento de dados e até a execução remota de código malicioso.
Os desenvolvedores voluntários do PHP escreveram em um comunicado hoje que os problemas têm gravidade 9,2 de uma escala de 10 e afetam servidores que executam PHP 5.4 e versões posteriores.
As falhas permitem que hackers controlem servidores de sites remotamente, sem precisar de senha, e estão relacionadas ao gerenciamento de memória durante o processamento de requisições HTTP. De acordo com os desenvolvedores, “não existem soluções definitivas; a atualização é a única opção segura”.
A Cloudflare, empresa de infraestrutura e segurança web, afirmou que também identificou as falhas, rastreadas como CVE-2026-109618 e CVE-2026-109619 e conhecidas como php2shell. A companhia ativou proteções automáticas em seu firewall de aplicações web (WAF) cerca de nove horas antes da divulgação pública. A medida abrange usuários do plano gratuito que têm o recurso ativado, mas não dispensa a atualização dos servidores.
O PHP é uma tecnologia usada na criação de sites e plataformas populares, como o WordPress, e está presente em cerca de 70% dos sites, segundo a Cloudflare. Por isso, as vulnerabilidades podem atingir diferentes tipos de páginas, de lojas virtuais e portais de notícias a sistemas governamentais. Serviços da Anatel, por exemplo, ficaram inacessíveis hoje. O Sistema Eletrônico de Informações (SEI) continua fora do ar.
As falhas foram identificadas de forma independente meses atrás, pela empresa de segurança Calif e pela OpenAI, criadora do ChatGPT. Antes da divulgação oficial, porém, informações sobre os problemas vazaram, o que levou alguns sites a sair do ar temporariamente para que seus responsáveis atualizassem os servidores.

articles.title: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up.
Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials.
The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents, accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand.
1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. The company says it is working with other companies to expand the service.
“Handing over a password, secret, or credential is a common shortcut to an agent, but can leave people with sensitive information in places they can no longer control as a copy gets saved for the next time,” the company said in a blog post. “1Password for Agents gives people a trusted way to delegate tasks to personal AI agents while keeping control of the passwords, secrets, and credentials those tasks require.”
Online agentic activity has increasingly unsettled major institutions. Indeed, 1Password’s new platform is launching on the same day that Axios reports that U.S. banks have begun to detect agentic activity inside user accounts.
This isn’t necessarily a case of rogue agents pilfering accounts but, rather, an example of how consumers are increasingly allowing automated services to act on their behalf, including on financial matters. However, the potential for agent-related problems is still large. The big issue appears to be that most banks cannot tell if the agentic activity is tied to user requests or not.
Bankers interviewed by the outlet described the situation as “horrifying,” and a Chase spokesperson interviewed by Axios additionally told the outlet that customers “should not give their usernames and passwords to anyone.”

articles.title: 9 Minuten Laden, 90 Minuten Arbeit: Neue Akkus sollen den Digits 5 zum echten Haushaltshelfer machen
articles.text:
9 Minuten laden für 90 Minuten Arbeit: Wie neue Akkus humanoide Roboter alltagstauglich machen
Der humanoide Roboter Digit 5 von Agility Robotics hat eine besonders lange Laufzeit bei kurzem Aufladen. Die Batterietechnik dafür liefert das Unternehmen Nyobolt. Damit kommt der Roboter auf ein Verhältnis von Laufzeit zu Ladezeit von ungefähr 10:1. Für jede Minute an der Ladestation stehen also zehn Minuten Arbeit zur Verfügung. Lädt man neun Minuten, läuft der Humanoid 90 Minuten. Der Vorgänger Digit 4 schaffte lediglich ein Verhältnis von 2:1 – er verbrachte rund ein Drittel des Tages am Ladegerät.
Warum Akkus bei Humanoiden das Hauptproblem sind
Humanoide Roboter brauchen viel Strom. Weil sie sich frei bewegen sollen, kommt der aus Batterien. Die halten allerdings nicht lange und müssen regelmäßig nachgeladen oder getauscht werden. Agility Robotics setzt deshalb auf besonders leichte Akkus mit hoher Leistungsdichte, die also viel Energie pro Kilogramm abgeben können.
Mit der neuen Technik könne Digit 5 täglich mehr als zwei komplette Arbeitsschichten absolvieren, teilt Agility Robotics mit. Die Auslastung einer Roboterflotte im Unternehmen steige dadurch deutlich. Die Akkus von Nyobolt sollen zudem viele Ladezyklen überstehen. Konkrete Zahlen nannten allerdings weder Agility Robotics noch Nyobolt: Weder zur Kapazität noch zur Zahl der möglichen Ladevorgänge gibt es Angaben.
Warum kein Wechselakku?
Offen bleibt auch, warum der Hersteller nicht auf ein Wechselsystem setzt. Dabei tauscht der Roboter seinen leeren Akku selbstständig gegen einen vollen – das geht in der Regel schneller als jeder Ladevorgang. Der chinesische Hersteller UBTech nutzt ein solches System bereits bei seinem humanoiden Roboter Walker S2.
Erste ausgewählte Kunden sollen den Digit 5 mit der neuen Batterietechnik im ersten Halbjahr 2027 bekommen. In den sechs bis neun Monaten danach will Agility Robotics den Roboter breiter verfügbar machen. Der Preis ist allerdings nur was für Profis: Angeblich deutlich sechsstellig. Dafür gibt es einen Wartungsvertrag.

articles.title: Beyond The EPE Budget: Building The Next Generation Of Computational Lithography
articles.text:
Why better models, richer metrology, explainable AI, and cross-industry collaboration must come together to extend semiconductor scaling.
At the recent SPIE Photomask Technology + Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography conference, an expert panel discussed the growing importance of edge placement error (EPE). I had the pleasure of joining moderator Jed Rankin of IBM and fellow panelists Hans Stiepan of Carl Zeiss SMT, Ezequiel Vidal-Russell of Micron Technology, Jo Finders of ASML, Il-Yong Jang of Tekscend, and Vivek Balasubramanian of Applied Materials. Together, we brought perspectives spanning OPC and EDA, mask technology, lithography systems, materials, and metrology. One point quickly became clear: EPE is no longer a narrow lithography metric. It is becoming a system-level measure of how well our industry can translate design intent into a manufacturable, high-yielding device. The mask, scanner, resist, etch process, metrology, OPC, and downstream integration all contribute. Each discipline can optimize its own part, but a collection of local optima does not automatically produce the best device—even if everyone arrives with an excellent slide explaining why their part is already optimized.
As pitch scaling becomes more difficult, tighter control of placement, variability, and pattern fidelity becomes one of the main paths to continued scaling. The challenge is that EPE is an unbounded budget. Mask three-dimensional effects, absorber profile, sidewall angle, critical-dimension uniformity, registration, scanner behavior, resist variability, etch, stochastic effects, process-induced stress, and even wafer or die bonding can all move an edge or change its electrical consequence. Yet the audience survey delivered a wonderfully familiar verdict: OPC was viewed both as a major source of EPE and as the leading place from which future EPE reduction would come. In other words, OPC was cast as both the villain and the superhero. Jed leaned into the joke, asking what Ezequiel and I would need from the rest of the industry to carry that superhero burden. By the final poll, confidence in OPC had risen to 58 percent—prompting the prediction that I might appear next time in tights. I am happy to accept the confidence; the cape may be negotiable.
Today, many effects that are difficult to isolate are absorbed into empirical corrections, rule tables, or an “etch” term. This is pragmatic and often necessary in production, where repeatability, runtime, yield, and schedule outweigh a perfect explanation. Ezequiel captured the dilemma well: after seeing the poll, he was not sure whether the OPC community should feel encouraged or concerned. The audience clearly expected OPC to take care of every systematic and correctable effect—and, where possible, reduce sensitivity to the uncorrectable ones too. That is an impressive job description for any superhero. But even OPC needs good physics, good data, and a process window; it cannot leap an inaccurate model in a single bound. As tolerances shrink, the effects we sweep into the correction bucket become large relative to the remaining process window. EDA must therefore represent the real manufacturing system more completely: not an idealized mask with uniform properties, but pattern-dependent mask profiles, realistic metrology behavior, scanner effects, process variability, and the interactions among them.
More data alone is not the answer. We need data that is physically meaningful, sufficiently repeatable for manufacturing, and connected to the patterns that matter on the wafer. A single SEM image contains far more information than one extracted CD. Contours, profiles, roughness, placement, local geometry, and pattern context can all inform better models. At the same time, no fab can measure everything. OPC and process models should help identify the patterns with the highest wafer sensitivity, rank the hotspots, and translate that sensitivity into mask and wafer metrology requirements. This closes a critical loop: modeling guides measurement, measurement improves modeling, and both focus resources on yield-relevant problems.
I believe artificial intelligence will deliver one of the largest future gains in EPE reduction. Machine learning can capture residual systematic behavior that is difficult to model directly, while agentic systems can coordinate optimization across traditionally separate domains. But semiconductor manufacturing cannot rely on an unexplained black box. A model that reports zero EPE without showing why it is trustworthy is not production-ready. The path forward is explainable AI anchored by rigorous simulation, validated against appropriate metrology, bounded by known physics, and monitored for the conditions in which it can safely be applied.
Agentic AI should not be turned loose across the ecosystem with the assumption that it will discover a global optimum on its own. Adoption will begin with well-defined problems: reducing global CDU, selecting robust mask geometries, optimizing source and mask together, prioritizing metrology, or connecting pattern variation to electrical impact. For each problem, we must define the objective, the data required, the knobs the system may turn, the physical constraints, and the validation criteria. Confidence will grow locally, and successful agents can then be connected into broader workflows.
Our customers do not sell EPE; they sell products defined by power, performance, area, cost, and yield. Some EPE limits are hard geometric boundaries: exceed them and a structure shorts, opens, or fails. Other errors occupy a gray zone where their importance depends on device behavior. EDA has an opportunity to bridge that gap by bringing electrical simulation, stochastic analysis, lithography, mask optimization, process modeling, and design technology co-optimization into a common decision flow. The goal is not simply the smallest geometric error everywhere. It is the right allocation of process margin where it creates the greatest product value.
Fig. 1: Process simulations using stochastic modeling techniques can predict process characteristics that lead to electrical problems with a design before reticles are built.
Foundries and IDMs sit at the center of this opportunity because they see the complete manufacturing flow and hold the data that connects mask, scanner, process, device, and yield. EDA providers need deeper partnerships with them, as well as with mask makers, metrology suppliers, and lithography equipment providers. Those partnerships must enable secure, purposeful sharing of data and context—not data collection for its own sake. The highest-value collaboration will define common EPE frameworks, expose the relevant process sensitivities, prioritize the dominant contributors, and establish closed feedback loops at the stage where each error can still be understood and corrected.
EPE scaling is not a temporary phase. As the industry moves from planar scaling to three-dimensional integration and eventually to time-dependent, system-level optimization, the definition of EPE will continue to evolve. Wafer-to-die bonding, new device architectures, curvilinear masks, high-NA lithography, and tighter coupling between manufacturing and electrical performance will create new correction and optimization problems. The opportunity for EDA is to become the connective intelligence across these domains—combining physics, data, and purposeful AI to turn fragmented process knowledge into manufacturable outcomes. The audience may be ready to call OPC the savior of EPE, and I appreciate the vote of confidence. But the real superpower will come from giving OPC better mask knowledge, better metrology, better process context, and tighter links to device performance. That is how we extend scaling: not by asking one team to wear the cape, but by enabling every part of the ecosystem to work together.
Leave a Reply

articles.title: Un mini PC très compact à moins de 420€ : le NiPoGi P2 avec son SSD de 512 Go est en promotion sur Amazon
articles.text:
Le NiPoGi P2 est un mini-ordinateur de bureau qui intègre une configuration bureautique associée à Windows 11 Pro préinstallé. Sur Amazon, son prix de référence de 499,99 € passe à 419,99 € grâce à l’association d’une remise immédiate et d’un coupon.
Pour travailler à domicile sans encombrer votre petit espace bureau, vous pouvez choisir de vous équiper d’un mini-PC. Le NiPoGi P2 n’a pas à rougir en matière de configuration bureautique : il embarque un processeur Intel Core 3 304, 12 Go de mémoire LPDDR5 et un SSD NVMe de 512 Go. En ce moment, le NiPoGi P2 est proposé à 419,99 € sur Amazon : un tarif qui s’obtient en activant le coupon de réduction présent sur sa fiche produit.
Le NiPoGi P2 avec 12 Go de RAM et SSD de 512 Go revient à 419,99 € après activation du coupon sur Amazon.
Pourquoi choisir le mini-PC NiPoGi P2 ?
- Pour son encombrement réduit : le support VESA fourni permet même de fixer le boîtier derrière un écran compatible.
- Pour sa configuration bureautique : le Core 3 304 et les 12 Go de RAM conviennent à la bureautique, aux recherches sur Internet et aux visioconférences.
- Pour ses sorties vidéo : les connexions HDMI, DisplayPort et USB-C permettent de raccorder jusqu’à trois écrans 4K.
Un poste de travail compact doté d’une connectique complète
Pour utiliser le NiPoGi P2, il suffit d’y connecter au moins un écran, un clavier et une souris. Il fonctionne ensuite comme une tour classique. Le Wi-Fi 6 et le Bluetooth 5.2 assurent les connexions sans fil au réseau et aux périphériques compatibles.
Quant à son SSD de 512 Go, il offre l’espace suffisant pour y installer des logiciels de bureautique et stocker de nombreux fichiers. Il est possible de remplacer le SSD par un modèle de plus grande capacité en cas de besoin. L’alimentation, le câble HDMI et le support VESA sont fournis.
Une machine réellement dédiée à la bureautique
Avec son processeur et ses 12 Go de RAM, le NiPoGi P2 est surtout adapté aux usages bureautiques classiques pour travailler, étudier et surfer sur Internet. Il ne s’agit pas d’un PC dédié aux jeux vidéo exigeants : sa puce graphique intégrée reste limitée. Par ailleurs, sa mémoire vive est soudée et non extensible.
✅ Les points forts
- Format compact et support VESA fourni.
- SSD NVMe de 512 Go remplaçable.
- Jusqu’à trois écrans 4K raccordés simultanément.
❌ Les limites
- Mémoire vive soudée et non extensible.
- Performances graphiques limitées pour les jeux exigeants.
À 419,99 €, ce mini-PC NiPoGi P2 peut rendre de fiers services aux télétravailleurs et aux étudiants.
Cet ordinateur compact NiPoGi P2 est adapté à des usages simples, et il peut facilement trouver sa place dans un petit espace de travail. Sa connectique complète est l’un de ses atouts.
En revanche, pour du multitâche intensif ou pour l’utilisation de logiciels puissants, cette configuration peut rapidement montrer ses limites.

articles.title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
articles.text:
TL;DR: Our analysis shows attackers are now enumerating or pulling data within 15 minutes of getting into an environment, and the tools that should have caught them were not effective. We will discuss three common attack patterns in which we observed this behavior.
- Stolen developer tokens. Poisoned npm packages and infostealers pull GitHub tokens from developer laptops; attackers later use those tokens to exfiltrate data from GitHub. GitHub has no native detections for how a token is used, leaving enterprises vulnerable to code exfiltration.
- ClickFix lures for AI tools. Fake Claude Code install commands in shared Claude chats load a macOS stealer that takes browser cookies and cloud credentials. The victim runs the commands themselves, much like they would when installing any tool, which may or may not trigger an endpoint detection.
- Help desk vishing. Attackers leverage social engineering and pose as IT to get an employee to approve a real MFA prompt on a look-alike sign-in page. Identity providers can treat the attacker's login as legitimate, making them ineffective at detecting these issues.
Catching these incidents takes detection built on data and behavior. Stopping them takes an autonomous response. We cover both of these topics.
In March, a developer installed GitHub Desktop, signed in, and stopped using it the same day. The OAuth token it created sat in the Mac's keychain for 95 days. On June 19, someone else started using it.
The token pulled 76 repositories in about 15 seconds through residential proxies in more than two dozen European cities. GitHub raised no alert because nothing in GitHub watches how tokens are used. The Exaforce platform flagged it within five minutes and had it triaged within 10 minutes.
Our MDR analysts confirmed the exfiltration and notified the customer minutes after the detection fired. But by the time any action was taken, the attacker had exfiltrated data from 472 of the 638 repos.
This case shows both halves of the problem. Without anomaly detection, nobody would have known the token was in use. With proper detection in place, containment would still have required human approval, giving the attacker sufficient time to exfiltrate data.
Sleeper tokens on developer laptops
GitHub's security features are focused on inspecting code and secrets, not token misuse. We caught this GitHub token compromise by stacking weak signals on a single GitHub session. Sign-ins to the account came from networks and cities never seen before.
It was pulling ZIP archives at machine speed, with a Windows user agent, on an account that had only ever used macOS. Each of these signals can potentially be explained, but all of them combined are indicative of something malicious.
OAuth app tokens like this one, prefixed gho_, don't expire, and GitHub revokes them on its own only after a year. In our testing, the organization's SSO page does not even list these tokens, and they are visible only through the CLI. Disabling the developer in the identity provider doesn't stop the token either.
Without SCIM, GitHub keeps honoring tokens until someone revokes them or removes the user from the org.
Developers using AI coding tools install npm packages and connect MCP servers all day, mostly outside the pipelines that security teams monitor, and worms like Shai-Hulud sweep a machine for GitHub and cloud tokens the moment a poisoned package is installed.
This happens before anything is committed, which is why scanning your repositories to determine whether a compromised npm package may have affected you is not sufficient.
ClickFix goes after AI tool installs
Stealing a token from the macOS keychain usually requires an infostealer that phishes for the login password.
The latest ClickFix lures leverage trust from AI tools. In one such incident, an employee who was searching for Claude Code install instructions landed on a shared Claude conversation with a one-line install command.
The command loads a macOS stealer (we did a deep analysis with indicators) that fakes a System Preferences prompt for the password, then copies the keychain, browser cookies, saved passwords, and cloud credentials.
Because the victim runs the command, email filtering and download controls are bypassed. The most effective approach to catching these types of attacks is an endpoint detection solution. Assessing the scope of the impact should involve a comprehensive analysis of all tokens/credentials minted by the user.
See How Exaforce Agents Contain Identity Attacks
A hijacked session gives an attacker access to every app your users sign in to.
Book a demo to see how Exaforce agents detect and contain identity attacks across your environment.
Request a Demo
Fake IT calls that end in stolen sessions
In the vishing cases we worked this year, the attacker registered their own MFA device and started a bulk download script 2.5 to 7 minutes after the victim approved the push. In one such case, the attacker exfiltrated 140,000 files and requested a ransom for the leaked data.
Most of these calls follow the help desk script commonly leveraged by the Scattered Spider group. A caller posing as IT sends the employee to a sign-in page with the company's name in the URL, such as the passkey-themed contoso.add-passkey[.]com in Microsoft's September write-up.
The page either relays the login through an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) proxy, or the attacker guides the victim through a device-code sign-in.
One kit we took apart, hosted on oskeysetup[.]com, was written from scratch, so detections built for Evilginx and the other public kits are not going to be effective.
In most instances, we observed that detections from identity providers are ineffective because victims approve a real MFA prompt. In a July session hijack we worked on, Microsoft flagged the attacker's first sign-in as risky, then marked the risk remediated because the user had passed MFA. Within minutes, the stolen token was replayed from two other countries within one second, and Microsoft's later alerts raised the user's risk level.
Exaforce caught it by tying the Okta and Microsoft sign-ins together and checking them against the user's history: this was the account's first-ever sign-in from the United States, on a Linux device, and through a home ISP the account had never used. In these cases the earliest strong signal is usually a new MFA method from a device and network the user has never touched.
We also noticed that attackers target the same company through multiple employees, often using the same servers and domains.
Autonomous response actions
An effective approach to counter the incidents discussed so far is to move toward autonomous response. Automating response is certainly not new, but the fear has always been about the consequences of a wrong action that can lock out an executive or break a production integration.
We find it's better to sort actions by friction instead: how much would a mistaken response action cost the person who owns the credential? If it costs them a fresh sign-in or a re-enrolled phone, the action is low-friction and can fire on a high-confidence finding. That covers revoking sessions, removing an MFA method registered during the flagged session, and deactivating a key that can be switched back on.
Password resets, account disablement, permanent deletions, and anything a production service depends on should require human approval. The human can be the target user and their manager, confirming in a quick message that the sign-in wasn't theirs.
Although most of the actions discussed are related to an identity or its associated credentials, they cannot be limited to the identity provider. Resetting the user's Okta password or killing their Okta session doesn't revoke tokens that Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, or GitHub already issued, and AWS and Snowflake sessions started through SSO keep running.
In our vishing cases, we found that data exfiltration continued for between 44 minutes and 3 hours after the user's IdP session was revoked, and in one case the attacker's inbox rules survived a password reset. Okta's Universal Logout reaches some apps, like Google Workspace and Slack, but not GitHub, Snowflake, or the AI model providers.
It's best to build each application's revocation actions ahead of time, along with the account that runs them. We've watched a response action fail mid-incident with a 403 because nobody had granted the required permissions.
It may be daunting to build these responses for every source of data. We recommend starting with services that hold your most critical data.
- Productivity: Google Workspace, Office 365, Box, Dropbox, Slack
- Cloud: AWS, GCP, Azure
- AI services: Anthropic, OpenAI
- Data: Snowflake, Databricks
- Code: GitHub, GitLab
Recommended low-friction responses to start with and how to implement them:
Okta
Action: Revoke sessions and the OAuth tokens Okta issued
API: DELETE /api/v1/users/{id}/sessions?oauthTokens=true
Permissions it needs: okta.users.read and okta.users.manage scopes, plus a custom admin role holding only okta.users.read and okta.users.lifecycle.clearSessions
Action: Reset all of the user's factors, including the attacker's
API: POST /api/v1/users/{id}/lifecycle/reset_factors
Permissions it needs: Same scopes, with okta.users.credentials.resetFactors added to the role
Microsoft Entra ID
Action: Revoke refresh tokens and session cookies
API: POST /users/{id}/revokeSignInSessions
Permissions it needs: User.RevokeSessions.All, plus User.Read.All to look up the user
Action: Delete the user's MFA methods, including the attacker's
API: DELETE /users/{id}/authentication/{type}Methods/{methodId} for each phone, Authenticator app, software OATH, FIDO2, Windows Hello, and Temporary Access Pass method
Permissions it needs: UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All, plus User.Read.All
Google Workspace
Action: End web and device sessions, and revoke the app's OAuth tokens
API: POST /admin/directory/v1/users/{userKey}/signOut, DELETE /admin/directory/v1/users/{userKey}/tokens/{clientId}
Permissions it needs: admin.directory.user.security scope, plus a delegated admin role
GitHub Enterprise Cloud, org-level SAML SSO
Action: Delete the stolen token from the organization
API: GET /orgs/{org}/credential-authorizations?login={user} to find it, then DELETE /orgs/{org}/credential-authorizations/{credential_id}
Permissions it needs: Org owner with admin:org, or a GitHub App with org Administration (write). There's no narrower option
Snowflake
Action: Disable a programmatic access token
API: Your own SQL, such as ALTER USER {name} MODIFY PAT {token} SET DISABLED = TRUE, sent through the SQL API (POST /api/v2/statements)
Permissions it needs: A dedicated service user whose role has MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS on the user
AWS
Action: End the STS sessions already issued to an IAM user
API: PutUserPolicy with an inline deny on sessions issued before now (aws:TokenIssueTime)
Permissions it needs: iam:PutUserPolicy, plus iam:GetUser and iam:GetUserPolicy
Anthropic
Action: Deactivate an API key
API: POST /v1/organizations/api_keys/{id} with {"status":"inactive"}
Permissions it needs: Admin API key
How Exaforce handled these attacks
Exaforce is an Agentic SOC platform with an optional MDR service. Our agents (Exabots) handle detection engineering, alert triage, investigations, threat hunting, and response. The agents work on a unified data platform that can act as your SIEM or work alongside your SIEM.
The platform comes with 800+ AI/ML anomaly detections that help detect the types of incidents we described across critical Cloud, SaaS, Identity, Endpoint, and AI services. There are 100+ dynamic response actions that agents can execute, so you don't have to build and maintain them yourselves for all your critical services.
You can read about more similar incidents under our ExaFiles research blogs here.
