articles.title: Everspin Expands MRAM into AI Servers, Data Centers, Satellites- EE Times
articles.text:
Everspin Technologies is looking to expand its magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) beyond established industrial applications into AI servers, data centers, and satellite systems, as AI workloads increase demand for faster, persistent memory.
Everspin president and CEO Sanjeev Aggarwal sees the technology as a way to address limitations in existing memory. “If you care for performance, I think that MRAM is the only solution we have,” he told EE Times in an exclusive interview.
Aggarwal claimed that customers are considering MRAM both for its performance and reliability and because they have been unable to obtain some NOR flash products. A TrendForce report estimated that NOR flash contract prices rose by a cumulative 100% to 120% in the first half of 2026. It stated that AI-related demand consumed much of the limited supply, and NOR flash was among the first products to experience longer lead times and allocation. The report also mentioned that suppliers have not announced significant capacity expansion.
Aggarwal said sees an opportunity for MRAM to fill up the gap created by the NOR flash shortages, and that opportunity could amount to $3 billion in 2028 or 2029. He said Everspin has been developing a product for this market using TSMC’s manufacturing process.
“Now people cannot buy NOR flash,” he said. “Most of the fabs in Asia have converted from NOR flash to DRAM. Much better profit margins. Then what is the alternative? MRAM is the only alternative for standalone or discrete products. And that is where they approach us.”
He said MRAM had previously cost about three times as much as NOR flash, but the price difference had narrowed to about 1.5 times as NOR flash prices rose amid supply constraints.
“If you are going to use two NOR flash chips, you might as well just use one MRAM and be more cost-effective,” he said.
The economics depend on the application, including the number of chips required and the performance and reliability specifications. Aggarwal said Everspin’s distributors had begun requesting cross-reference information to help customers identify MRAM alternatives when particular NOR flash components were unavailable.
He added that other non-volatile memory technologies could also be unsuitable for some applications. Ferroelectric RAM (FRAM), for example, has lower available densities in the products he described, while non-volatile static random-access memory (NVSRAM) can present tradeoffs in reliability and operating conditions.
Everspin specifies an operating temperature range of minus 40°C to 125°C for the parts Aggarwal discussed. He cited reliability, SRAM- and DRAM-like performance, and read-write endurance as reasons customers select MRAM.
Everspin reported revenue of $55.2 million for 2025, up 9.5% from $50.4 million in 2024, according to its annual report filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Aggarwal said he expects the company to double revenue over three to four years, with the NOR flash opportunity and demand from data centers, aerospace and defense, low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, and industrial automation contributing to its growth ambitions.
CXL demonstration explores MRAM’s role in AI memory
At the Storage Networking Industry Association (SNIA) Developer Conference in Santa Clara, California, Everspin demonstrated MRAM modules combined with a Compute Express Link (CXL) controller. The setup created a pool of persistent memory accessible through CXL.mem, a protocol that allows a system to access memory over a CXL connection.
Aggarwal said the demonstration was intended to show how MRAM could function as an additional memory tier between dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), which serves as working memory, and NAND flash, which provides storage. DRAM operates on a timescale of nanoseconds, while NAND flash access can take hundreds of microseconds, according to Aggarwal. Moving data between processing and slower storage can delay workloads.
“Our memory is 20 to 30 nanoseconds,” he said. “You can use it for storage as well as compute, reducing the gap between NAND storage and DRAM working memory.”
The proposed role for MRAM is to hold data generated during AI processing before transferring it to longer-term storage. Aggarwal said this could include key-value (KV) caches, checkpoints, and data awaiting a write to storage. A KV cache retains information that an AI model reuses while generating a response; checkpoints allow a computing job to resume after a failure.
MRAM’s capacity remains a limitation. Everspin’s densities currently reach one gigabit, although Aggarwal said devices could potentially be stacked to provide 8 Gb or 16 Gb. He argued that the technology would not need to match NAND flash capacity if it held intermediate data only temporarily.
The company is also developing a roadmap for higher-density memory and newer interfaces. Everspin has supplied IBM’s FlashCore Modules, Aggarwal said, and wants to expand its data center business with products that go beyond its existing DDR4 interface.
“Our demonstration of the CXL protocol with our existing DDR4 chip will start getting us some entry into the data center market,” he said. “And by the time we have a good foothold, we will have a 4-Gb DDR6 part ready to go right behind it.” Aggarwal estimated that this development would take about three years.
At the edge, Aggarwal said, MRAM could reduce the need to transfer data between devices and central servers for processing. He cited OpenMV as an example of an application in which Everspin has replaced SRAM and added MRAM for configuration.
Satellite deployment of MRAM
Earlier this year, Astro Digital selected Everspin’s 64Mb PERSYST spin-transfer torque MRAM (STT-MRAM), part number EM064LXQADG13IS1T, as the primary fail-safe memory for the boot process on its Raven satellite bus for a geosynchronous Earth orbit (GEO) mission. Boot memory stores the code needed to start a spacecraft’s electronics and support system recovery.
“What Astro Digital did recently was, they took our part and sent it into geosynchronous orbit,” Aggarwal said. “So, not low Earth, but they sent those to geosynchronous orbit.”
He said MRAM’s radiation tolerance is useful in space, while adding that the surrounding silicon can still be vulnerable to radiation damage. In the satellite configuration he described, a backup memory provides an additional safeguard if the surrounding circuitry is affected.
Aggarwal also cited MRAM’s write speed and reliability as advantages over NOR flash in satellite applications. He said the memory can be written almost three orders of magnitude faster than NOR flash and consumes less power in the applications he described.
Everspin lists 64-Mb, 128-Mb, and 256-Mb capacities in its PERSYST family, which uses a quad serial peripheral interface (QSPI).
Aggarwal also gave a general example of how MRAM could reduce chip count in some applications, but the comparison should not be read as a description of Astro Digital’s actual satellite configuration.
Exploring AI server workloads
The company has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with MaxLinear to evaluate MRAM alongside MaxLinear’s storage compression, encryption, and hardware acceleration platform for AI servers. The MoU will focus on metadata management, log data, write buffering, cache, and other data-intensive workloads.
The companies also plan technical validation and market development aimed at hyperscale cloud providers, AI infrastructure developers, and enterprise server customers. The agreement includes potential longer-term manufacturing, supply, and commercialization opportunities.
Aggarwal said MaxLinear was the first target for the work because of its accelerator technology. “They have accelerators, so they were very interested in the technology,” he said. “We are working with them to find the first use case.”
The MoU establishes an evaluation framework; it does not announce a finished product or a volume commitment.
Manufacturing expansion and supply
Everspin produces two main MRAM families: field-switched, or toggle, MRAM, and STT-MRAM. It manufactures toggle MRAM at its 8-inch facility in Chandler, Arizona. The company’s portfolio ranges from 128 kilobits to 1 Gb, spanning several densities and interfaces. Aggarwal said the company had shipped more than 200 million units over 20 years, with only a handful of returns.
Earlier this year, the company signed an initial 10-year foundry services agreement with Microchip Technology to establish an 8-inch MRAM and tunnelling magnetoresistance (TMR) sensor manufacturing line at Microchip’s Fab 4 facility in Gresham, Oregon. The agreement is intended to provide a second U.S. manufacturing source for toggle MRAM. The U.S. SEC filing stated that the first products are expected to ship in the second half of 2027.
“We signed a foundry services agreement with Microchip, which allows me to manufacture twice the amount of toggle MRAM that I could manufacture in Chandler,” Aggarwal said.
The agreement is also connected to a $40 million U.S. government contract awarded through Amentum Services, with Everspin acting as a subcontractor. Aggarwal said the work will qualify Everspin’s process at Microchip and provide the government with access to the company’s intellectual property and a second manufacturing line for future government products.
For STT-MRAM, Everspin has worked with GlobalFoundries on 12-inch wafers since 2016. It also plans to tape out a product using TSMC’s 16-nm process, which Aggarwal said would diversify supply.
The company’s aim is to have two manufacturing sources for both product families: Chandler and Oregon for toggle MRAM, and GlobalFoundries and TSMC for STT-MRAM. Aggarwal said capacity was not currently a constraint.
Everspin also faces competition in the commercial MRAM market. South Korean company Netsol, which uses Samsung Foundry, offers a 16-Mb product, Aggarwal said. He expects a 1-Gb product from the competitor to reach the market in 2028 or 2029.
India offers opportunities in aerospace, automotive, and rail
India is another potential market, particularly in aerospace and defense, electric vehicles, and railways. Aggarwal said he was seeking connections with the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), and Indian satellite companies.
He also identified battery management systems and vehicle data recorders as possible applications, alongside flight control systems. Everspin is working to expand its Indian distribution network. Aggarwal said the company was exploring local partnerships, including discussions involving Indian distributors and possible outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) arrangements.
Aggarwal said the company was also speaking with Indian automotive groups and exploring opportunities in rail. He cited existing deployments in rail systems in Europe, Japan, and China, where memory stores operational data.
“We are always in discussions about these potential opportunities,” he said of Indian railway opportunities. “There is nothing that I can talk about openly, but obviously the conversations are ongoing.”
For now, Everspin’s challenge is to turn MRAM’s performance and reliability advantages into broader adoption across these markets. Aggarwal expects demand to grow as manufacturing efficiencies reduce cost per bit.

articles.title: Etsy is cracking down on AI slop listings
articles.text:
Etsy is announcing stricter rules about how AI can be used in listings to reduce the volume of AI slop on the platform. In a post, the company says that “many active buyers say they can’t tell which items involve AI-generated content” and that sellers are “concerned about your work appearing alongside items that use AI in misleading ways,” spurring the new policies and restrictions.
Etsy is cracking down on AI slop listings
Etsy’s new AI policies, among other changes, require that a listing’s first photo is unedited.
Under the new policies, every listing must include “at least one unedited photo of the actual item against a real background,” and all photos must “accurately represent the item a buyer will receive.” The photos that aren’t the first one can be edited with software or AI-powered tools, as long as “the final result remains an accurate representation of the physical product.” The company shared a few examples to demonstrate the type of misleading images that are prohibited, including the cat stuffed animal at the top of this post.
While uploading images for a listing, if Etsy detects that any may be AI-generated, the platform will show a pop-up where you can note if an image was made with AI or not, as shown in a video. If a buyer reports that what they receive is “materially different” from a listing, a seller may be responsible for a refund.
For sellers who offer “functional guides,” which include patterns, recipes, or instructions,” Etsy says that the information in those products “must be your own work, not generated by AI.” Sellers will have to show an “actual result” made from a guide. The company also says that listings made by bots are no longer allowed.
Selling AI-generated art is still allowed on the platform, but a seller must disclose that it was made with AI, Etsy says.

articles.title: PVTW: Extending Silicon Characterization From PVT To Real-World Workload
articles.text:
Two devices operating at exactly the same voltage, frequency, and temperature can behave differently depending on what they are being asked to do.
For decades, silicon characterization has been built around Process, Voltage, and Temperature, or PVT. We characterize devices across process variation, sweep voltage and frequency, control temperature, generate SHMOO plots, and establish the operating envelope of the silicon.
That methodology remains fundamental. But today’s high-performance processors are increasingly systems in their own right. An AI accelerator may contain thousands of compute elements, distributed SRAM, high-speed SerDes, PCIe and Ethernet interfaces, multiple clock and power domains, advanced packaging, firmware, operating systems, compilers and application software.
This suggests adding another dimension: PVTW: Process × Voltage × Temperature × Workload
Frequency can be swept within this characterization space to determine operating margin.
The objective is not to replace traditional ATE characterization with System Level Test. It is to combine the electrical precision and control available from ATE with the realistic operating environment available from SLT, while retaining the ability to use either independently.
One way to implement PVTW is through a hybrid characterization architecture integrating ATE resources and SLT capability.
There is no reason to recreate resources that already exist in ATE. Existing ATE infrastructure, including older generation platforms, can provide programmable device power supplies, individual rail control and measurement, variable frequency clocks, digital stimulus and capture, ATPG and structural content, parametric measurements, and conventional SHMOO characterization.
SLT provides something fundamentally different: the application environment.
The processor can boot firmware and an operating system, load drivers and runtime software, and execute deterministic workloads designed to exercise specific parts of the architecture. For an AI processor, those workloads might emphasize compute, SRAM, external memory, PCIe, Ethernet, or chip-to-chip communication. Other workloads could intentionally activate several simultaneously to create realistic system stress.
The architecture therefore provides three modes. ATE mode performs conventional electrical, structural, and parametric characterization. SLT mode executes controlled system workloads. Combined mode uses ATE resources to control and measure electrical conditions while the device executes an SLT workload.
Combined mode is where PVTW becomes particularly interesting.
Consider a conventional voltage and frequency SHMOO using ATPG or appropriate functional content. At a controlled temperature, establish the operating boundary.
Now boot the processor, establish a deterministic workload, and repeat the sweep.
Start with a compute-intensive workload. Repeat with SRAM, external memory, PCIe, and Ethernet-intensive workloads. Finally, create combinations that deliberately generate simultaneous compute, memory, and I/O activity.
Suppose an ATPG SHMOO indicates that a device operates correctly down to 0.72 V at a particular frequency, while an SRAM-intensive application begins producing errors at 0.76 V.
That 40 mV difference is not simply a disagreement between ATE and SLT. It is characterization information.
Something about the workload is consuming margin. Is it SRAM timing? Clock distribution? IR drop? Simultaneous switching noise? A thermal gradient? Power delivery? Or an interaction among several subsystems?
There is an important distinction between testing and characterization.
Booting Linux, running an AI workload, and observing whether the processor crashes is useful testing. Characterization requires controlled variables, repeatability, and the ability to deliberately move the operating boundary.
Hold workload, temperature, and frequency constant while sweeping a selected voltage rail. Then hold workload, temperature, and voltage constant while sweeping frequency. Change temperature and repeat.
The hybrid architecture can go deeper. Hold I/O and memory rails constant while margining the core rail during a compute workload. Then margin a memory-related rail while executing a memory-intensive workload.
We can begin creating subsystem-specific workload SHMOOs that connect:
Consider a device that passes Wafer Sort and Final Test but develops errors after a sustained application workload. Cooling reduces the failure rate, while increasing the core voltage does not eliminate the problem. Telemetry indicates that most errors are associated with the same memory interface or byte lane, although the failing addresses move.
The device does not necessarily have to leave the characterization platform.
SLT mode can expose the system behavior and help isolate the subsystem. The platform can operate in ATE mode to investigate electrical and structural characteristics using programmable power, clock control, ATPG, functional patterns, and parametric measurements.
Or both capabilities can operate together. The workload can reproduce the marginal condition while ATE resources manipulate selected rails and clocks.
The three modes therefore answer different questions. SLT exposes the behavior. ATE investigates the electrical and structural characteristics. Combined mode characterizes their interaction.
This creates a tight engineering loop:
Create workload → Observe marginality → Isolate subsystem → Characterize electrically → Modify conditions → Repeat workload → Establish correlation → Determine root cause
For me, that is the interesting possibility behind PVTW. SLT no longer needs to be viewed only as a downstream production screen. Combined intelligently with ATE resources, it can become part of a controlled silicon characterization environment.
But this leads to another question. If two devices both PASS, are they actually equivalent?
That is the subject of Part 2: Beyond Pass/Fail: Characterizing Silicon Margin with PVTW.
Leave a Reply

articles.title: Leaked Mass Effect: Universe trailer gives a taste of what we're all missing
articles.text:
Those mourning yesterday’s shuttering of highly praised and influential developer BioWare also had to deal with the cancellation of the next Mass Effect game, which was first teased back in 2020. Today, we got our best look at what that game could have been with a short, leaked trailer for Mass Effect: Universe.
In the roughly two-minute montage—which describes itself as “in-engine footage from our small team” that “uses our pre-production assets”—an ex-military officer wearing an N7 trenchcoat (similar to the one seen in that 2020 teaser) encounters an Asari at a bar. He talks of his frustration with military life—“by the time you put out one fire, another had already started”—before discussing his new line of work “stopping [the fires] before they start” and “making the choices no one else is willing to make. Going where others are afraid to go.”
Mass Effect: Universe Trailer
by
u/Random_Hyabusa_Ninja in
masseffect
As the intriguing Asari at the bar reveals herself to be the one who metaphorically “start[s] the fires,” N7 allies reveal themselves as backup. The cutscene transitions seamlessly into an all-out group gunfight in the bar, complete with hostiles being stuck in place inside mass effect fields and others being crushed by furniture brought down on top of them.
The action-packed bar scene is interspersed with short vignettes from around the game’s universe, including a hovercraft speeding over an icy planet, an examination of a truly gigantic alien suspended in a glass cylinder, and a team looking at a holographic map dotted with dozens of points of interest.
We hardly knew ye
The existence of the internal Mass Effect: Universe trailer was first revealed by an anonymous Reddit poster yesterday and then confirmed by IGN early Thursday morning. The trailer video appeared on Reddit slightly before noon Eastern time, with mods there saying they couldn’t “independently verify the authenticity” but that it “seems legitimate.” Within hours, both IGN and Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier had confirmed that the trailer was authentic and came from someone inside EA.

articles.title: One UI 9.0 aterriza en los Galaxy A más vendidos: estos son los Samsung compatibles con Android 17
articles.text:
Samsung continúa ampliando la disponibilidad de One UI 9.0 en sus móviles de gama media y de entrada. A unos días de lanzar la actualización para el Galaxy A56, ahora toca el turno de otros dispositivos de la familia A entre los que se encuentran algunos de los modelos más vendidos. El nuevo sistema basado en Android 17 ya está disponible en los Galaxy A16, Galaxy A17 y Galaxy A07, mientras que el Galaxy A35 también ya recibió la versión definitiva.
Según recoge SamMobile, Samsung ha lanzado una nueva fase en su estrategia de actualización a One UI 9.0. Uno de los primeros en recibirla ha sido el Galaxy A16, cuya versión estable ya se liberó a los usuarios de Corea del Sur, tanto para las variantes LTE como 5G. El móvil fue uno de los que modelos que entraron en la fase beta, recibiendo tres versiones de prueba antes de la distribución final que se identifica con el firmware A176LKSU4CZJ5.
Siguiendo la tendencia, el Galaxy A17 5G también ya recibió One UI 9.0 en el país asiático mediante distribución OTA. Samsung suele priorizar sus actualizaciones a quienes viven en Corea del Sur, por lo que siempre son los primeros en acceder a las pruebas beta o versiones definitivas. Sumado a este móvil, Android 17 ya está disponible para el Galaxy A07 a través del firmware A075FXXU7DZJ5, un gama de entrada que tuvo la fortuna de contar con una fase beta.
Aunque estos móviles cuentan con distintas prestaciones, la actualización a One UI 9.0 ofrece casi las mismas funciones orientadas a esta gama de dispositivos. Entre ellas se incluyen ajustes visuales en la interfaz de usuario, nuevas opciones de personalización para el Panel Rápido y mejoras en las aplicaciones de Samsung y la seguridad de DeX.
El Galaxy A35 completa la transición a One UI 9.0 con Android 17
Otro de los protagonistas de esta oleada de actualizaciones es el Galaxy A35. Samsung dio fin al programa beta de One UI 9.0 y comenzó el despliegue de la versión estable basada en Android 17. El resto de modelos que completan la lista de actualizaciones son el Galaxy M16, Galaxy M30 y Galaxy F70, mientras que el Galaxy Z Flip 5 también está ampliando su disponibilidad fuera de Asia.

articles.title: Airbnb ne veut plus que les voyageurs fassent le ménage : les propriétaires sont furieux
articles.text:
Airbnb va interdire aux propriétaires d’imposer certaines corvées ménagères à leurs voyageurs, comme défaire les lits ou laver la vaisselle avant leur départ. Une décision qui devrait soulager les vacanciers, mais qui provoque déjà la colère de nombreux hôtes.
Vous avez déjà loué un Airbnb et découvert, la veille de votre départ, une liste de tâches ménagères longue comme le bras ? Entre les draps à retirer, la vaisselle à laver et les poubelles à sortir, certains séjours se terminent parfois par une petite séance de ménage. Le tout alors que des frais de nettoyage figurent déjà sur la facture. Airbnb semble avoir entendu les critiques et vient d’annoncer de nouvelles règles pour encadrer les demandes des propriétaires. Ces derniers, en revanche, ne voient pas forcément cette décision d’un très bon œil.
Airbnb met fin aux listes de corvées interminables
À compter du 20 novembre 2026, Airbnb appliquera une nouvelle politique concernant les règles imposées aux voyageurs. Elle concernera les réservations effectuées à partir de cette date, y compris lorsque le séjour est prévu plusieurs mois plus tard.
Les propriétaires ne pourront plus exiger des tâches nécessitant un effort ou un temps important, normalement prises en charge par une personne chargée du ménage. Airbnb cite plusieurs exemples : défaire les lits, laver et ranger la vaisselle ou encore transporter les poubelles à l’extérieur de la propriété.
En revanche, pas question de transformer les logements en dépotoirs. Les voyageurs devront toujours respecter les lieux et les laisser dans un état raisonnable. Il restera également possible de leur demander de déposer la vaisselle sale dans l’évier ou de jeter leurs déchets dans les conteneurs prévus.
Autre changement important : toutes les règles devront être indiquées clairement sur l’annonce avant la réservation. Impossible, donc, de découvrir une nouvelle liste d’obligations dans un message envoyé la veille du départ ou sur une feuille placardée dans la cuisine.
Les propriétaires qui ne respecteraient pas ces consignes s’exposent à des avertissements, à une réduction de la visibilité de leur annonce et, en cas de manquements persistants, à des sanctions plus importantes.
Les propriétaires dénoncent une décision injuste
Ces nouvelles règles s’inscrivent dans une stratégie plus large d’Airbnb, qui entend simplifier le quotidien de ses utilisateurs. Après avoir élargi son application aux hôtels, aux transports et même à la livraison de courses, la plateforme s’attaque désormais à un autre irritant bien connu des voyageurs : les corvées imposées avant le départ. Une initiative qui ne fait pourtant pas l’unanimité. Comme le rapporte WIRED, ces nouvelles règles provoquent une véritable levée de boucliers chez certains propriétaires.
Sur les forums et les réseaux sociaux, plusieurs hôtes estiment qu’Airbnb les empêche désormais de faire respecter des consignes élémentaires. D’autres craignent une augmentation des coûts de nettoyage, qu’ils pourraient être tentés de répercuter sur le prix des locations. Certains envisagent même de quitter la plateforme.
La contestation ne se limite d’ailleurs pas aux États-Unis. Sur le forum communautaire français d'Airbnb, des propriétaires appellent déjà à protester contre cette nouvelle politique.
Du côté des voyageurs, l’accueil est nettement plus favorable. Beaucoup dénonçaient depuis longtemps une contradiction assez agaçante : payer des frais de ménage parfois conséquents, puis devoir nettoyer une bonne partie du logement avant de rendre les clés.
Ces frais ne disparaissent pas pour autant. Airbnb autorise toujours les propriétaires à les facturer pour couvrir le nettoyage habituel entre deux réservations. La plateforme rappelle cependant qu'ils ne peuvent pas imposer de pénalité supplémentaire simplement parce qu’un voyageur n’a pas effectué une corvée précise.
Il faudra voir comment ces nouvelles règles seront appliquées dans les logements présentant des contraintes particulières. Airbnb se réserve la possibilité d’accorder certaines exceptions, notamment lorsque les caractéristiques du lieu le justifient.
Pour les prochaines vacances, il faudra donc toujours faire preuve d’un minimum de savoir-vivre. Un coup d’éponge ne fait pas de mal, mais vous ne devriez plus avoir à passer l’aspirateur avant de quitter un appartement dont vous avez déjà payé le ménage.
- Le plus grand choix de logements au monde
- Variété des hébergements proposés
- Système d'avis authentiques

articles.title: Calls and texts no longer the main priority for young Australian smartphone users - Tech Guide
articles.text:
New research by Samsung shows calls and texts are no longer the primary use of smartphones for almost a quarter of Australians aged 18 to 24.
For 22 per cent of young Australians between 18 and 24, calls and texts – the first features enabled when mobile phones became a popular consumer product – is now not the top priority.
For everyone else, calls and texts as the main use of their device have fallen from 67 per cent in 2019 to 53 per cent in 2026.
This is a significant shift in how Australians use mobile phone technology.
The study shows smartphones are increasingly becoming more work-centric but also designed for entertainment, creativity, and everyday life.
As a result Australians are demanding more from their mobile devices than ever before.
The change in behaviour in the past seven years has coincided with the period when Samsung released its first foldable phone.
In fact, foldable phones have emerged as the new all-in-one solution for productivity, creativity, and entertainment.
Apple has also just entered the foldable market with the release of the iPhone Duo.
It will certainly bring a lot more attention to the category and attract more customers to adopt the new form factor.
Social media recorded the biggest increase as a primary smartphone usage, rising from 17 per cent in 2019 to 24 per cent in 2026.
Meanwhile smartphone use for work purposes increased by more than 50 per cent in the same period.
“In just seven years, Australians have shifted from using smartphones primarily to call and text to relying on them as all-in-one tools for work, payments, navigation, social connection and AI-powered assistance,” says Gary Mortimer, Queensland University of Technology, Professor of Marketing and Consumer Behaviour.
“The smartphone has evolved from a communication device into a digital life hub.”
The research also showed 60 per cent of Australians say smartphone productivity is more important today than it was in 2019, while 63 per cent see the improvement in smartphone photography as a key feature.
Another 40 per cent say they their smartphone replacing their wallet, keys, and ID is also an important smartphone innovation that they didn’t know they needed seven years ago.
The findings also play into the growing appeal of a foldable smartphone.
Earlier this year Samsung introduced the Galaxy Z Fold8 – a passport-shaped foldable smartphone which has been a huge success around the world.
It was also joined by the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra and the Galaxy Z Flip8 which expanded Samsung’s portfolio to support different customers and different lifestyles to suit their productivity, multitasking, creativity and entertainment needs.

articles.title: Les Microsoft PowerToys inaugurent deux nouvelles fonctions pour votre souris
articles.text:
Les PowerToys viennent tout juste d’être mis à jour. Estampillée 0.102.2933, la dernière mouture de la trousse à outils de Microsoft introduit deux nouvelles fonctionnalités dans les Utilitaires de souris : CursorHide et le verrouillage du bouton de la souris. Les développeurs de la firme de Redmond en ont également profité pour améliorer la barre d’accès rapide de la Palette de commande ainsi que pour moderniser plusieurs modules vers WinUI 3.
Deux nouveaux utilitaires pour la souris
Le premier module des PowerToys à profiter de nouveautés est celui qui concerne les Utilitaires de souris. Microsoft y a en effet intégré deux nouvelles fonctionnalités très pratiques qui devraient améliorer sensiblement votre quotidien. La première, CursorHide, permet de masquer automatiquement le pointeur de la souris pendant que vous saisissez du contenu au clavier, après une période d’inactivité dont il est possible de personnaliser la durée, ou ces deux critères combinés.
Le pointeur réapparaît ensuite aussitôt que vous déplacez de nouveau la souris.
La deuxième nouveauté introduite dans les Utilitaires de souris est le Verrouillage du bouton de la souris. Concrètement, en maintenant un bouton de la souris enfoncé un court instant puis en relâchant celui-ci, Windows 11 continue de le considérer comme maintenu jusqu’au prochain clic. Cette nouveauté, qui permet de réduire la fatigue lors de glisser-déposer répétitifs ou pendant une sélection prolongée est entièrement personnalisable.
Vous pourrez ainsi choisir le bouton auquel attribuer le verrouillage, ajuster la durée du maintien du bouton avant son verrouillage, et même définir un seuil de glissement (en pixels) au-delà duquel « tout déplacement supérieur à cette distance pendant que vous maintenez le bouton enfoncé annule le verrouillage » explique Microsoft.
Une mise à jour majeure pour la Palette de commande
Cette mise à jour des PowerToys introduit par ailleurs plusieurs évolutions pour la Palette de commande. Après avoir introduit le mode compact pour une Palette de commande plus discrète jusqu’à ce qu’elle affiche des résultats, Microsoft a eu la bonne idée d’y intégrer dans cette mise à jour vos commandes favorites.
Pour en profiter, vous devrez vous rendre dans les Paramètres de Personnalisation de la Palette de commande, puis de sélectionner Zone de recherche compacte. Vous retrouverez ainsi toutes vos commandes épinglées directement sous la barre de recherche. Vous pourrez en outre lancer rapidement l’une d’elles en utilisant des raccourcis clavier, allant de Alt + 1 à Alt + 9.
Microsoft précise également avoir intégré de nombreuses autres nouveautés dans sa mise à jour de la Palette de commandes. Les recherches approximatives permettent désormais de trouver des options, des extensions, des commandes, etc. pour y accéder directement. En utilisant le raccourci clavier Windows + Alt + J vous pouvez à présent donner le focus au dock et naviguer entre ses différents éléments au clavier.
Autre nouveauté qui devrait en intéresser plus d’un, il est maintenant possible d’utiliser la touche Copilot des PC qui en possèdent une pour ouvrir directement la palette de commandes. Il faudra a priori se rendre dans les Paramètres de Windows pour modifier le comportement de celle-ci.
Autre nouveauté intéressante, il est à présent possible d’épingler plusieurs horloges dans le dock, avec pour chacune leur propre fuseau horaire et un format d’affiche propre.
Pour le reste, Microsoft introduit une nouvelle option Capture avec dictée dans ZoomIt, pour enregistrer et transcrire votre voix directement en local sur votre PC, ainsi que de nouveaux outils en ligne de commande pour plusieurs modules comme Advanced

articles.title: Amazon says PHP2Shell exploitation began 4 days before patches
articles.text:
Security researchers at Amazon Threat Intelligence say attackers began targeting the PHP2Shell flaws four days before security patches were released on Wednesday.
Tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, the two critical vulnerabilities let attackers gain remote code execution (RCE) on vulnerable systems. The PHP security team patched them on October 21 after urging admins one day earlier to prepare to install the updates as soon as they became available.
PHP core developer Gina Peter Banyard warned before disclosure that applying the official security patches is the only permanent defense, while the UK National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) asked UK organizations to immediately update PHP servers or take them offline until they can be patched.
The PHP team says that everything went according to plan until two days before the coordinated disclosure, when it had to speed up the targeted release date starting October 20 after some details on the PHP2Shell security flaws (including the two CVE IDs and mitigation advice provided to some critical infrastructure providers) leaked online.
While some proof of concepts were also published before patches were released, the PHP security team said none were functional.
Amazon Threat Intelligence's report comes after multiple cybersecurity companies (including Cloudflare, watchTowr, Previdian, Hadrian, and Patchstack) detected unsuccessful exploitation attempts before public disclosure.
Exploitation in the wild?
According to Amazon, the first exploitation attempts began on Saturday, October 17 (four days before the PHP2Shell patches were released), and attackers deployed multiple proof-of-concept PHP2Shell exploits hours after disclosure from VPN IP addresses.
"The exploit attempt originated from an IP address associated with a commercial anonymization network. While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure," said AWS chief information security officer CJ Moses.
"The actual payloads and choices in anonymization infrastructure varied, suggesting these were multiple actors. Technical analysis is ongoing, and it's unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems."
Moses added the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities are "now being broadly exploited in the wild," though it's unclear how many attacks are successful, and warned that "defenders should not assume the public disclosure date is the earliest date of exploitation."
Today, Dataminr's Threat Research and Cyber Engineering (TRACE) team also published a report pointing out that "observed activity since vulnerability disclosure remains limited to scanning, fingerprinting, and use of non-working exploits, with no known compromises," and adding that "it remains only a matter of time for working POCs or successful exploitation activity to emerge."
PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is an open-source web development language that powers up to 80% of all websites on the Internet, including those using popular Content Management Systems (CMS) like WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla.
VirusTotal now tracks more than 5.1 million PHP hosts exposed online, with roughly 3.8 million with at least one port open to attacks.
Update October 22, 17:31 EDT: Added more details from Dataminr TRACE.

articles.title: AI found a critical PHP flaw. The bigger failure began in 2024.
articles.text:
AI found a critical PHP flaw. The bigger failure began in 2024.
Did one of your favorite websites go dark on Wednesday? Some did, as operators took services offline while they waited for fixes to two critical flaws in PHP, the language behind much of the web.
The precaution didn’t mean those sites were hacked. The holes themselves were bad news with a capital B. But the bigger long-term concern might be how the embargo on the patches was handled.
PHP powers roughly 70% of websites, but that figure describes PHP’s reach, not the number of vulnerable or compromised sites.
WordPress told site owners to update PHP; these flaws don’t require a WordPress update.
The flaws are CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The PHP project’s fixed releases are 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12; users of older PHP branches need a supported upgrade or a distributor’s backport.
The PHP security emergency, aka PHP2Shell, exposed more than dangerous bugs in a widely used language. The release also set off a dispute over coordinated disclosure and underscored the pressure on open-source maintainers as AI-assisted researchers find and develop exploits faster.
The road to this emergency ran through OpenAI’s Patch the Planet initiative. Working in that program, security firm Calif used GPT-5.6 Sol to find a route to remote code execution and reported it to PHP on August 11. OpenAI independently reported the same underlying issue that day; Wiz reported its findings on August 24. PHP’s maintainers led the fixes. They had spotted signs of the underlying out-of-memory problem in 2024, but its full impact became clear only this August.
“This is about as broad as a critical vulnerability gets.”
“This is about as broad as a critical vulnerability gets,” Moshe Siman Tov Bustan of OX Security said in a statement. “If you have a publicly accessible PHP instance and haven’t patched it, start from the assumption that you’re exposed. If you find evidence of exploitation, assume compromise, not just exposure.”
OX Security CEO Neatsun Ziv added: “This is what an internet-scale vulnerability looks like. When a flaw hits technology this ubiquitous, the blast radius isn’t one product or one industry. It’s the web itself.”
Behind those warnings, open-source leaders are debating how the industry should respond when discovery outpaces remediation. The New Stack has reported on the flood of AI-generated vulnerability reports facing maintainers; PHP’s case adds a dispute over whether an embargo still protected users once details began to leak.
A disclosure dispute and an admission of failure
Before the patches were released, details of PHP2Shell began to leak. The PHP Foundation says two CVE IDs circulated on October 20, followed by an accidentally published proof-of-concept video.
Chainguard CEO and co-founder Dan Lorenc then released patched container images more than six hours before the October 21 coordinated release. He says he believed reports of active exploitation justified the decision to break the embargo.
The speed concern is real: After WordPress released version 7.1.2 on September 22 to fix CVE-2026-87902, Patchstack observed probes against WordPress sites that same day and attempts to write files the next day.
That, by the way, is bad enough. But the WordPress episode doesn’t establish whether attackers successfully exploited these PHP flaws when Chainguard published its images.
Why Lorenc jumped the clock
In an email to The New Stack, later reflected in his LinkedIn post, Lorenc said Chainguard independently discovered the same issue with its testing harness and a frontier AI model prompted to “find bad vulnerabilities in PHP.”
Lorenc said Chainguard first heard on Friday, October 16, that a PHP issue was coming. It independently found the issue that night, received a full briefing on Saturday, October 17, and helped test fixes.
He said news began leaking Monday, October 19, and discussion intensified Tuesday night, when several vendors reported what they believed were exploits in the wild.
Lorenc wites that, after a video call with other researchers, he decided to ship the fixes and immediately notified the disclosure group. He said he believed the coordinated disclosure guidelines allowed early release when there was evidence of exploitation in the wild.
Lorenc said three considerations drove the decision. These were how easily Chainguard had independently discovered the vulnerability and built an exploit, how much information was already circulating about the vulnerabilities and fixes, and the evidence shared about active exploitation.
Chainguard made its patched images publicly accessible, rather than restricting them to customers. Lorenc acknowledged that the PHP Foundation disagreed with his decision.
They certainly didn’t agree. The PHP Foundation’s account was blunter: “Chainguard unilaterally broke the embargo and published built images containing the fix.” It said Chainguard had received the patch early so customers could update at the agreed disclosure time.
In the foundation’s view, publishing the built images gave attackers a chance to study the fix while other PHP users were still waiting for patches.
“We’re not always going to get it right, and not everyone is going to agree with our decisions.”
Lorenc wrote that he was sorry his decision added stress for PHP’s maintainers. “We’re not always going to get it right, and not everyone is going to agree with our decisions,” he said, adding that Chainguard’s goal was to protect the most people.
What counts as an exploit?
The disagreement centered on what counted as evidence of active exploitation. Lorenc said other vendors had seen exploits in the wild. The PHP Foundation said its security team had not identified a functional exploit among the circulating proofs of concept at the time of release.
Amazon Threat Intelligence later reported an apparent exploit attempt against one of its honeypots on October 17 and more attempts early on October 21. Still, it said it was unclear whether those attempts would have succeeded on real systems.
The competing risks are clear. Yes, holding an embargo gives distributors time to prepare updates together. And, true, releasing a fix early may protect users who can obtain it. But it also gives attackers clues while other PHP users are still waiting for patches.
The capital-B problem underneath
The PHP Foundation also acknowledged a separate failure in its response. Developers noticed signs of the out-of-memory problem behind one CVE during a 2024 audit, but had not found a concrete route to remote code execution.
The foundation said competing fixes carried difficult compatibility and security trade-offs, and work repeatedly stalled. It called the delay “a structural failure” caused by its decision process and lack of resources.
The New Stack has previously reported on the link between paid maintenance and security practices. The foundation is now seeking more support from companies, hosts and governments that depend on PHP.
Canonical, Ubuntu Linux‘s parent company, offers a less critical assessment of the overall response. In an e-mail, Luci Stanescu, Canonical’s security engineering manager, says, “Canonical supports and recommends coordinated vulnerability disclosure according to best practices. The early embargo leak by a third-party was unfortunate, but we believe the disclosure process worked well.”
That assessment differs in emphasis from the PHP Foundation’s criticism: a leak can undermine part of the process without necessarily invalidating the broader coordination effort.
For CIQ Chief Technology Officer Peter Nelson, whose company is Rocky Linux’s founding sponsor, the PHP episode fits a broader change already underway in Linux security.
“We have seen AI used in exploiting vulnerabilities in the kernel space for the past six months,” Nelson says. “This represents more research going into other widely used software programs like PHP. We expect to see more of it as open-source projects continue to use AI and other means to harden the code and provide a greater defense against vulnerabilities like this.”
“Today, such vulnerability exploitation requires a frontier model. Tomorrow that won’t be the case.”
Nelson expects that pressure to continue as advanced vulnerability-research capabilities become more accessible. “Today, such vulnerability exploitation requires a frontier model. Tomorrow that won’t be the case.”
Lorenc also frames the challenge as an industry-wide problem rather than one confined to PHP. “This is unfortunately the new normal for the industry, and we’re going to need to work together as one team to have a chance at securing our critical infrastructure fast enough to stop attackers from causing real harm.”
Patching cannot wait for the usual maintenance window.
For enterprise users, the immediate consequences are operational. Gunnar Hellekson, Red Hat’s vice president and general manager for Lightwell, a joint Red Hat–IBM effort to address vulnerable open-source dependencies, tells The New Stack in an email that the PHP flaws illustrate the risk in dependable software that organizations may rarely think about.
Hellekson said that stable production software can be easy to overlook even as AI-driven discovery increases the volume and speed of vulnerability findings. The PHP issues, he said, remind us how deeply open source is woven into the systems that run businesses.
He emphasized getting tested updates from trusted suppliers, especially when vulnerabilities affect vital programs like PHP. “Given the potential impact of these vulnerabilities, Red Hat recommends that customers deploy validated, tested patches as soon as they are available from trusted sources including Red Hat, even outside of normal patching windows.”
“Software that supports millions of websites cannot depend on a handful of maintainers to manage increasingly sophisticated threats alone.”
Beyond that, we need more resources, in general, for open-source software maintenance and security. As Kara Sprague, CEO of HackerOne, says in a statement sent to the media, “The PHP discoveries are also a reminder that open-source security is everyone’s responsibility. Software that supports millions of websites cannot depend on a handful of maintainers to manage increasingly sophisticated threats alone.”
No, no it can’t.
For organizations running affected PHP systems, the “patch it right now!” problem remains: deploy a fixed build and review systems for signs of attempted exploitation, including activity dating back to October 17.
This is where the competing assessments converge. Better-funded maintainers, more resilient disclosure procedures, and broader access to defensive tools could address the longer-term problem. And that’s the capital-B problem underneath this week’s patch.

articles.title: Linkbuilding ausgelagert und trotzdem keine Zeit gespart? Daran liegt’s
articles.text:
Linkbuilding auslagern: Warum es oft scheitert und wie du es richtig machst
Die Ernüchterung folgt jedoch oft schnell: Wer Prozesse auslagert, spart erst dann wirklich Zeit, wenn die internen Abläufe nahtlos andocken und klare Verantwortlichkeiten vorhanden sind.
Schlägt ein Linkbuilding-Partner beispielsweise drei potenzielle Publisher vor, im eigenen Team fehlt jedoch die Zeit zur Prüfung von Zielseite und Umfeld, kippt das Modell: Die ausgelagerte Aufgabe wird prompt wieder zum internen Zeitfresser.
Um das zu verhindern, müssen Verantwortlichkeiten rund um Textfreigaben, Zielseiten-Anpassungen und Ankertexte vorab glasklar definiert sein – inklusive fester Vertretungsregelungen. Denn oft sind es schlicht unvorhergesehene Engpässe wie Urlaube oder Krankheitsfälle, die eingespielte Abläufe ins Chaos stürzen und Platzierungen verzögern. Nur mit strukturierten Freigabeprozessen, klar benannten Vertretungen und kurzen Kommunikationswegen landen die Inhalte pünktlich beim Publisher – ohne dass das eigene Marketing-Team im Mikromanagement oder Vertretungs-Chaos versinkt.
Verantwortung abgeben – aber wie viel?
Erfolgreiches Linkbuilding erfordert weit mehr als den bloßen Einkauf von Platzierungen. Es braucht ein präzises Briefing und eine verlässliche interne Qualitätssicherung. Gute Partner-Modelle, wie sie eine spezialisierte Linkbuilding-Agentur oder Managed Services bieten, setzen deshalb bereits bei der Strategie an: Sie verknüpfen eine fundierte Linkprofilanalyse und strategische Priorisierung direkt mit der operativen Umsetzung und dem anschließenden Monitoring, damit die Platzierungen auch ihre nachhaltige Wirkung erzielen können.
Damit die Zusammenarbeit reibungslos funktioniert, müssen vor Kampagnenstart glasklare Leitplanken definiert werden:
- Aufgabenverteilung: Welche operativen Schritte übernimmt der Partner, was bleibt inhouse?
- Freigaben & Veto: Wer sichert die Zielseiten (Landingpages) ab und wer darf unpassende Publisher-Quellen ablehnen?
- Eskalationspfade: Bei welchen Sonderfällen oder Abweichungen ist eine direkte Rücksprache erforderlich?
Den tatsächlichen Engpass im Prozess finden
Bevor du dich für ein externes Modell entscheidest, lohnt sich ein Blick auf die Historie. Analysiere die letzten Kampagnen rückwirkend, um herauszufinden, an welcher Stelle im Prozess konkret Zeit verloren ging – und um typische Prozess- und Strategiefehler beim Linkbuilding künftig systematisch zu vermeiden. Stell dir dabei wichtige Fragen:
- Quellenauswahl: Wie viele Publisher-Vorschläge wurden verworfen – und aus welchen fachlichen Gründen?
- Freigabelaufzeiten: Wie lange lagen Themenkonzepte, Zielseiten (Landingpages) oder Ankertexte zur Prüfung im eigenen Team?
- Nacharbeit: Wer bemerkte im Nachgang fehlerhafte Verlinkungen, schwachen Content oder fehlende Werbekennzeichnungen (z. B. fehlende rel=“sponsored“-Attribute)?
Vier Modelle im Vergleich
Ob Freelancer, Agentur oder Managed Service: Die reine Bezeichnung des Betriebsmodells sagt im Linkbuilding noch wenig darüber aus, wie viel Arbeit tatsächlich abgegeben wird. Entscheidend ist, wie hoch der verbleibende interne Ressourcenaufwand im Unternehmen ist.
| Modell | Strategiebedarf | Interne Ressourcen | Qualitätskontrolle | Skalierbarkeit | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inhouse | intern | hoch | vollständig intern | nur mit Personal | 
| Freelancer | vorgegeben | mittel | interne Endabnahme | begrenzt | 
| Agentur | gemeinsam | niedrig bis mittel | interne Endabnahme | nach Kapazität | 
| Managed Service | extern begleitet | niedrig bis mittel | interne Endabnahme | flexibel | 
Ein Freelancer eignet sich ideal für klar abgegrenzte Einzelpakete, sofern Strategie und Qualitätskontrolle fest inhouse verankert sind. Eine Agentur fängt schwankendes Auftragsvolumen gut ab. Bei einem Managed Service wandern zusätzlich die laufende strategische Beratung und Priorisierung nach außen – was maximale Flexibilität bei geringer interner Belastung ermöglicht.
“Auch das beste Dienstleister-Modell löst keine trägen internen Freigabeprozesse.”
Qualität lässt sich nicht delegieren
Das Vetorecht – also das gezielte „Nein“-Sagen – ist eine Kernaufgabe, die zwingend im eigenen Unternehmen verbleiben muss. Benenne intern eine feste Person, die Publisher-Quellen, Themenumfeld, Zielseiten und Ankertexte rigoros prüft.
Der Grund ist simpel: Google führt den Kauf von Links zu Rankingzwecken explizit als Verstoß in den Google Search Essentials (Spamrichtlinien) auf. Eine verantwortungsvolle Auswahl der Quellseiten ist daher essenziell. Die Entscheidung über eine Platzierung sollte idealerweise vor der Content-Erstellung fallen – doch auch unmittelbar vor dem Go-Live muss ein finales Veto möglich sein.
Im Bericht zählen auch die Umwege
Grüne Statusfelder in Excel-Listen erzählen nur die halbe Wahrheit. Ein sauberes Indexierungs-Monitoring gehört heute zwar zum Standard, ein aussagekräftiger Report muss aber weit darüber hinausgehen: Auch abgelehnte Quellen, Kostenstrukturen, Zielseiten, Nachbearbeitungsschleifen und interne Wartezeiten gehören transparent in die Auswertung.
Nur so lässt sich objektiv analysieren, ob ein Engpass beim Dienstleister lag oder das interne Briefing mehrfach angepasst werden musste. Tipp: Vereinbare vorab eine klare Stoppregel für den Fall, dass qualitativ passende Quellen knapp werden oder die Standards sichtbar sinken.

articles.title: CANAL+: Africa growth slows in biggest Pay-TV market
articles.text:
CANAL+ is struggling to turn around MultiChoice South Africa, the country’s biggest pay-TV operator, with revenue falling 3% in the nine months to September as lower subscription income weighed on performance.
The France-based media group is relying on revamped DStv packages and stronger content to reverse the decline. MultiChoice’s revenue fell 3% on a like-for-like basis to September 2026, according to CANAL+’s latest trading update released on Thursday.
The decline reflects underlying performance after adjusting for currency movements and changes in the scope of the business. On a reported basis, MultiChoice revenue rose 0.4% to €1.81 billion ($2.03 billion), benefiting from a material positive currency effect.
CANAL+ said the like-for-like decline was driven by lower subscription revenue in South Africa, partly offset by higher revenue in most other English-speaking African markets.
The decline moderated to 2% in the third quarter, from 3.4% in the first half. CANAL+ attributed part of the improvement to more favourable comparisons with the sporting events line-up in the previous year, rather than solely to the effects of its turnaround strategy.
The figures come as CANAL+ attempts to simplify MultiChoice’s offerings and strengthen the value proposition for subscribers following its acquisition of the South African pay-TV operator.
“We are making good progress with the MultiChoice turnaround plan,” CANAL+ chief executive officer (CEO) Maxime Saada said in the trading update. “In September, a new, simplified value proposition was launched in South Africa, providing subscribers with more content, greater choice, and better value for the same price.”
MultiChoice introduced the new packages on September 7, towards the end of the reporting period, leaving little time for their impact to reflect in the nine-month results. CANAL+ said the rollout would continue across English- and Portuguese-speaking African markets over the coming months.
The strategy comes amid wider changes to MultiChoice’s entertainment business, including the discontinuation of Showmax, MultiChoice’s subscription video streaming service, in April. CANAL+ has treated Showmax as a discontinued operation in its financial reporting.
The group has said it intends to continue investing in premium content, technology and strategic partnerships as it reshapes its entertainment offering. However, the latest trading update does not provide subscriber numbers or average revenue per user. This limits the available evidence on whether the changes are improving customer retention or spending.
At group level, CANAL+ reported revenue of €6.41 billion ($7.2 billion) for the nine months, up 37.5% from the same period last year. The increase primarily reflected the consolidation of MultiChoice following the acquisition, rather than equivalent growth in the underlying business.
On a like-for-like basis, group revenue declined 0.3%. Excluding MultiChoice, revenue increased 0.8% on a like-for-like basis, supported by French-speaking Africa and the group’s content production and distribution operations.
Africa and Asia revenue, including MultiChoice, rose 3.1% on a restated basis. But the figures conceal diverging performances across the continent: CANAL+’s Africa and Asia operations excluding MultiChoice recorded like-for-like revenue growth of 10.2%, while MultiChoice declined.
In French-speaking Africa, the group said subscriber growth was supported by a compelling content line-up and improved distribution efficiency. CANAL+ Telecom Africa, an African telecommunications and fibre broadband operator, also recorded double-digit revenue growth, driven by the expansion of its fibre-to-the-home network and stronger commercial momentum.
“We delivered a solid performance in the first nine months of the year as we continued to execute our strategy. Revenue was in line with our expectations, supported by strong momentum in French-speaking Africa and at STUDIOCANAL,” said Saada.
CANAL+ is also strengthening its sports offering to protect its position in the African entertainment market. The group secured exclusive rights to all UEFA men’s football club competitions across more than 40 countries for 2027 to 2031, alongside rights across Africa for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations and its qualifying campaign.
CANAL+ said it remained on track to deliver its 2026 financial guidance, including €735 million ($825 million) in adjusted earnings before interest and tax and €250 million ($281 million) in targeted synergies measured by adjusted earnings before interest and tax.

articles.title: The Foundations of Scalable AI
articles.text:
Sponsored
The Foundations of Scalable AI
Presented byVanguard
A scalable AI system requires a strong foundation. Data, engineering, platforms, operating models, and governance must converge to work as one. This session from MIT Technology Review's EmTech Future conference explores what it takes to build that foundation in a highly regulated environment and how a responsible, trustworthy implementation can turn emerging capabilities, including agentic systems, into lasting value for investors.
About the speaker
Jing Wang, Principal, Center for AI and Insights, Vanguard
Jing Wang leads Vanguard's Center for AI & Insights (CAI), advancing the firm's AI, machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science capabilities. Her team drives enterprise-wide innovation, research, and delivery, enabling Vanguard to translate emerging technologies into trusted solutions that enhance client experiences, improve investor outcomes, and create measurable business value.
Before her current position, Jing served in a range of leadership roles across Vanguard's Financial Services, Workplace Solutions, International, and Corporate Services divisions. Throughout her tenure, she has led teams and enterprise initiatives that advanced strategic priorities, strengthened client outcomes, and drove business performance across the firm.
She joined Vanguard in 2009 after several years as a Principal at the Boston Consulting Group. Jing earned a B.S. in Physics from the University of Science and Technology of China, a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania, and an M.B.A. in Finance and Marketing from the Wharton School of Business at the University of Pennsylvania. Jing holds Series 7, 24, and 65 licenses.
