articles.title: 480,000 phishing emails sent from a PC hidden behind a fridge in a Japanese hotel room — Chinese couple arrested over fraud operation, scammers remotely leech Wi-Fi to target 2.4 million victims
articles.text:
480,000 phishing emails sent from a PC hidden behind a fridge in a Japanese hotel room — Chinese couple arrested over fraud operation, scammers remotely leech Wi-Fi to target 2.4 million victims
Police arrested a Chinese couple for placing the computer that was found in a Kobe hotel and using stolen credit cards to make purchases.
A computer, found hidden behind a fridge in a Japanese hotel room, was responsible for sending around 480,000 phishing emails, Hackread reports. The computer was placed there by a Chinese couple who lived locally, and the pair have now been arrested for both the hidden phishing PC and a separate slew of purchases that were made using stolen credit card details. Ye Jiafeng, 39, and his wife, Shen Qi, 39, now face multiple charges including fraudulent obstruction of business and trespass as well as computer fraud.
The scam began on 15 May, 2025, when Ye connected the computer to hotel Wi-Fi and then hid it behind a fridge. There it stayed, sending around 480,000 emails. When it was discovered, the machine had around 2.4 million email addresses, presumably just waiting to be phished. The emails claimed to be from credit card companies and sent unsuspecting recipients to fake websites in an attempt to capture their credit card information. It's believed that the computer was administered remotely, allowing it to remain in situ without any in-person maintenance required.
Ultimately, the computer would likely have remained in place if the recipient of one of the phishing emails hadn't reached out to the hotel. The hotel's IP address was found in metadata linked to the messages, and staff discovered the computer before reporting it to the police. Police are still investigating whether the two scammers were the brains of the operation or simply working for someone else.
While phishing was the couple's chosen scam this time around, it isn't their first foray into using technology to part victims from their cash. Ye and Shen are claimed to have used credit card details stored on a smartphone to buy items in Kobe. But that wasn't the only phone that they had — media reports claim that police found 74 of them at their home, and the couple had spent 10 million yen (around $63,000) of other people's money using stolen card details since 2024. It's unknown whether the phones found by police account for all of those that were used, or if there were others that have yet to be identified.
Phishing has long been a lucrative option for criminals around the globe, but it has also spawned a spin-off industry recently. A China-based phishing-as-a-service operation was dismantled by the FBI earlier this year. The service made it easier for criminals to create scam sites using AI and is believed to have been responsible for almost $2 billion in losses and 3.87 million stolen credit cards.

articles.title: Oracle Patches Over 1,200 Vulnerabilities With October 2026 CPU
articles.text:
Oracle has released its Critical Patch Update (CPU) for October 2026. The latest updates bring 1,295 new fixes across dozens of products.
According to an analysis conducted by Tenable, the new CPU addresses 1,209 unique CVEs, including 95 critical-severity flaws.
Tenable says 439 CVEs have been assigned a high severity rating and 582 are medium severity.
Oracle Fusion Middleware received the most fixes, 206, including 134 that can be exploited remotely without authentication.
A significant number of patches were also rolled out for E-Business Suite (194), Siebel CRM (122), Communications (110), PeopleSoft (109), JD Edwards (102), MySQL (98), Java SE (55), and Supply Chain (50).
Oracle Essbase, REST Data Services, Analytics, Systems, Database Server, Construction and Engineering, Enterprise Manager, GoldenGate, Trusted Answer Search, Utilities Applications, Secure Backup, Virtualization, Autonomous Health Framework, Financial Services Applications, Retail Applications, TimesTen In-Memory Database, Healthcare Applications, Hospitality Applications, Commerce, APEX, Application Testing Suite, Global Lifecycle Management, NoSQL Database, and SQL Developer also received patches.
Oracle has not flagged any of these vulnerabilities as exploited in the wild, but the software giant has reminded customers that it periodically receives reports of exploitation attempts targeting its products.
On Wednesday, one day after announcing the CPU, Oracle published a separate advisory and security alert for CVE-2026-91403, which is Java’s (and Oracle’s) response to the eMudhra weak-key incident.
Oracle will release Critical Security Patch Updates (CSPUs) on November 17 and December 15. These types of updates go out on the third Tuesday of every month. The next CPU is scheduled for January 19, 2027.

articles.title: Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The bad week for cybersecurity just got worse for thousands more companies, who were spied on by Chinese hackers following the breach of IT management and remote access giant ConnectWise.
Security researchers at Microsoft say the China state-aligned hackers broke into ConnectWise’s cloud backup service and stole application credentials that are used to establish data links between ConnectWise and its corporate customers, who rely on the cloud service to back up their company’s data.
By stealing the credentials, the hackers could log in to the customer’s Microsoft-hosted environment as if they were an authorized user and access their emails and other files.
According to Microsoft, the hackers used AI agents to rapidly hack into around 2,250 organizations at a rate of almost 3,000 attempted sign-ins per minute. Microsoft said this speed gives defenders “little time to detect and respond.”
The speed of the mass-hacks was attributed to the use of AI agents, specifically ARTEX, an open source AI framework that works with AI models to stress-test cyber defenses. The same AI software was used in a recent compromise of South Korea’s financial systems, many of which had weak security and lacked multi-factor authentication.
ConnectWise said it’s paused access to its cloud backup system and is investigating the breach. As of Thursday, the company said it was working on restoring the service.

articles.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
articles.text:
People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science
- Summary:
- Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.
- Share:
An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting users willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.
The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.
One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.
AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports
"Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.
However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.
There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.
"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit users are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.
Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.
"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," says Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.
How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts
The project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.
That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.
"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," says Sehgal.
Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.
To investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 users who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.
The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.
After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 users who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.
"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," says Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize."
A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges
The most striking difference involved hunger.
In retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.
But among Reddit users who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.
The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.
These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.
"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," says Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.
"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean."
Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?
Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.
Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.
Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.
The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.
In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.
The follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.
The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.
"That's what we hope will happen with this study," says Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing."
The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Neil K. R. Sehgal, Jena Shaw Tronieri, Benjamin Rader, Lyle Ungar, Sharath Chandra Guntuku. Self-Reported Adverse Effects Among Social Media Users Taking Nonapproved Retatrutide. JAMA Network Open, 2026; 9 (10): e2638929 DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.38929

articles.title: Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
articles.text:
Meta has tweaked its business terms to remove language suggesting that it could freely train its AI models on news sites, like The Verge — but legal experts say these changes aren’t enough to address their concerns. “This does nothing to restrict the ‘associated with your products or services’ [language] that would let Meta scrape entire sites,” James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell Law School, tells Nieman Lab.
Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
Meta’s new business terms could still help it justify training AI on scraped sites.
Initially, Meta’s new terms for business accounts appeared to give the company permission to train its AI on news sites. The terms, which go into effect October 30th, stated that Meta “may use any content” from the websites associated with a business account to “develop, research” and “train” Meta’s products. At the time, legal experts told Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta “to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions,” such as the robots.txt file that has historically told scrapers (including search engines like Google) what they are allowed to crawl.
Following fierce backlash from the publishing industry, Meta removed language saying it would “train” its products with scraped content. But the tweaks might not be enough to rule out that possibility. “The revised version of the new terms still allows Meta to use that scraped content to develop any ‘business product.’ That doesn’t seem to be a defined term, and presumably Meta is developing AI business products. I think ‘develop’ is broad enough to include ‘train,’” Matt Topic, a media and intellectual property attorney at Loevy & Loevy, tells Nieman Lab.
Meta has maintained that its new terms aren’t designed to scrape news content for free. In a statement to The Verge today, Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts reiterated that “content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences,” adding that the update “is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

articles.title: This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display
articles.text:
Last year, we reported on Red Viper, a Virtual Boy emulator that added a splash of Super Game Boy-style color to Nintendo’s famously failed red-on-black “portable” 3D headset from the ’90s. Now, a new emulation experiment, VBoy Color, has taken the concept to a higher level, using a tile-based palette system that allows for many more distinct colors in each individual Virtual Boy frame.
Rather than simply replacing the Virtual Boy’s four shades of red with four different colors, VBoy Color’s readme files explain how the emulator’s game-specific Color Packs can assign a distinct four-color palette to each 8×8 tile in a Virtual Boy scene. That means the emulator can differentiate between green pipes, grey platforms, and red brick wall in Mario Clash, for instance, even though all those in-game objects share the same overlapping red hues in the original game.
The Game Boy Color-esque results feel like being transported into an alternate history where Nintendo invested in a full-color display rather than cheaper red LEDs for the Virtual Boy hardware. The increased contrast between differently colored elements is particularly welcome in games like Jack Bros. or Vertical Force, where the original red-on-red display often makes it hard to differentiate the player-character from busy red background elements.

articles.title: Whatsapp-Fake von 500.000 Usern heruntergeladen: Was du tun musst, wenn du darunter bist
articles.text:
Whatsapp-Fake von 500.000 Usern heruntergeladen: Was du tun musst, wenn du darunter bist
Der Großteil an Malware landet auf Smartphones und anderen Endgeräten, wenn User:innen Fake-Apps von dubiosen Webseiten herunterladen. Doch was, wenn sogar eigentlich geschützte Bereiche wie der Google Play Store plötzlich täuschend echte Anwendungen zeigen und sogar ins Rampenlicht stellen? So ist es jetzt bei einer App passiert, die sich als Whatsapp getarnt und so zahlreiche User:innen in die Falle gelockt hat.
Fake-Whatsapp löst 500.000 Downloads aus
Die gefälschte Whatsapp-Anwendung wurde zunächst von einem Reddit-User entdeckt und gepostet. Die Fake-App trägt denselben Namen wie das Meta-Original und nutzt auch dasselbe Icon. Selbst auf der eigentlichen Store-Page sind Beschreibungen und Screenshots identisch. Zum Zeitpunkt der Entdeckung tauchte der Whatsapp-Fake dabei sogar vor der echten App auf, weil die Verantwortlichen dahinter Geld für ein Sponsoring ausgegeben hatten. So rückte die App auf den ersten Platz der Suchergebnisse.
Um nicht aufzufliegen, haben die Verantwortlichen hinter der Fake-Whatsapp-App einen Trick angewandt. Ihre Anwendung haben sie im Betaprogramm des Google Play Stores veröffentlicht. Dadurch können User:innen keine Bewertungen abgeben. So stellten die Verantwortlichen sicher, dass sie nicht durch negative Reviews als Fake herausstechen würden.
Erkennbare Unterschiede gab es nur, wenn User:innen genauer hinschauten. Als Entwickler war „Agment Assets sallu“ bei der Fake-Version von Whatsapp eingetragen. Zudem lag die Downloadzahl deutlich unter dem Original. Während Whatsapp von Meta mehr als zehn Milliarden Downloads verzeichnen kann, kam der Fake „nur“ auf eine halbe Million. Da es sich aber um eine potenziell schädliche App handelt, sind alle, die sie heruntergeladen haben, gefährdet.
Was du tun solltest, wenn du den Whatsapp-Fake geladen hast
Mittlerweile hat Google auf die Fake-App reagiert und sowohl die Anwendung selbst als auch den Account der Entwickler aus dem Play Store geworfen. User:innen laufen also vorerst nicht mehr Gefahr, die gefälschte Whatsapp-Version versehentlich herunterzuladen. Achte dabei dennoch darauf, dass es sich um die Version vom Entwickler „Whatsapp LLC“ handelt und sie Bewertungen und Milliarden von Downloads zeigt.
Welchen Zweck die App genau verfolgt und welche Aktionen sie auf Endgeräten vornimmt, ist derzeit nicht klar. Denkbar wäre es, dass es sich um einen Infostealer handelt, der unbemerkt im Hintergrund sensible Daten sammelt und extrahiert. Oder die App ist nur ein Vehikel, um weitere Malware auf Geräte herunterzuladen.
In jedem Fall sollten alle, die die App heruntergeladen haben, sie schnellstmöglich wieder deinstallieren. Solltest du ein Antivirenprogramm auf deinem Smartphone nutzen, lohnt sich ein Scan des gesamten Geräts. Hast du keine, gibt es auch Gratis-Apps von Avast oder Avira, die du dafür herunterladen kannst. Auch wenn diese nichts finden, solltest du deine Logins und Passwörter, die du seit dem Herunterladen der Fake-App auf dem Smartphone genutzt hast, ändern. Behalte auch danach noch Konten im Blick, ob sich jemand unbefugten Zugriff darauf verschaffen konnte.

articles.title: Engineers Guard the Line Between Fast Demos and Safe Products
articles.text:
This article is crossposted from IEEE Spectrum’s careers newsletter. Sign up now to get insider tips, expert advice, and practical strategies, written in partnership with tech career development company Parsity and delivered to your inbox for free!
If you’re an engineer, you may feel like your skills aren’t commanding the premium they once did. Many engineers have faced layoffs or restructuring. But even for those of us who still have jobs, something corrosive is happening. You may have heard some version of this:
“ChatGPT answered that in five seconds. Why can’t you?”
Or, “I made this app in a weekend. Why is our team taking so long?”
I worked on a team where leadership said things like this directly to engineers. This was in 2024 and 2025, when the AI craze was in full swing and Claude and ChatGPT adoption was rising.
Demo-Driven Development
Generative AI (and the marketing behind it) gives people the illusion that the work is simpler than it is. A working demo hides complexity, and once someone has a website that works, they may decide they no longer need engineers, or start to distrust the ones they do have.
Some CEOs want to believe they can replace an engineering team with a few sexy prompts. Many companies also want them to believe this.
That website works great in the demo—under specific conditions and without users with thumbs for fingers. Then it has to plug into a system with millions of lines of old code, satisfy legal requirements, meet accessibility standards, and be delivered in a complex deployment process.
Thinking that writing code was the only bottleneck for deploying new software is like the Titanic seeing the tip of the iceberg and assuming there was nothing underneath it.
What you can do about it
Engineers have a unique position in the AI space, because you have the capacity to understand how these models work much better than the average person. Use this to your advantage.
Learn how AI models work. If you can’t already explain that LLMs are probabilistic, what tokens are, or why training data matters, spend a weekend fixing that. You don’t need to become a full-blown AI researcher. A few fundamentals will put you ahead of most people making the AI decisions.
Teach upward. Turn that knowledge into teaching moments for the people who lead you. Explain the limits of these tools, and why a demo and a production system are different animals. It keeps people from truly believing that a notebook full of prompts can replace an engineering team.
Consider the criticism of today’s processes. Some of what we do has been treated as ceremony for too long. Be willing to say, “you know what, maybe you’re right, this process is too slow for the speed we can work at now.” Conceding that earns you the credibility to defend the steps that matter.
I still believe that speed at the cost of everything else is harmful—but that’s a topic for another time.
Find your voice. Engineers at the forefront of AI adoption need to push back and explain why we do things the way we do. Nobody else in the room is going to do it for us.
Don’t chase (too many) shiny objects
Your goal, in my opinion, is to save your organization from buying into the hype so much that they chase the wrong thing. Our job, before and after AI, is building safe and useful products for human beings, and engineers are still best suited for that.
—Brian

The need to educate engineering students about ethics and social responsibility is widely recognized, but today’s curricula often miss the mark. Three professors propose a new approach: adding ethics training directly to core technical coursework.

articles.title: Hackers got a four-day head start on epic PHP2Shell vulnerability
articles.text:
Amazon has warned that vulnerabilities in a programming language that underpins much of the Internet, discovered using AI tools, are being “broadly exploited” as governments and companies rush to secure their systems.
The world’s largest cloud computing provider on Wednesday said it had identified an attempt by hackers to exploit the bug four days before the weakness was disclosed to the public.
Amazon added the flaws were “now being broadly exploited in the wild.”
The US National Security Agency and UK authorities earlier on Wednesday warned that the vulnerabilities had left websites around the world critically exposed to hacking, as some governments in Europe were reportedly taking sites offline while they patched the two security flaws.
The vast impact of the bugs, uncovered with the help of OpenAI and Google models after being undetected for more than a decade, highlights the ability of AI to upend cybersecurity.
The release of new models earlier this year from Anthropic and OpenAI with powerful cyber capabilities prompted warnings from politicians and financial regulators and led the US government to temporarily limit their rollout.
The NSA on Wednesday warned all organizations using the programming language known as PHP to immediately update their systems or take them offline.
The developers responsible for maintaining PHP released software updates to patch the vulnerabilities earlier on Wednesday.

articles.title: Trump intervém após Musk limitar Starlink na Ucrânia
articles.text:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ligou para Elon Musk na quarta-feira (21) e pediu que o empresário suspendesse as restrições impostas a uma versão militar do sistema de internet via satélite Starlink utilizada pela Ucrânia. Segundo autoridades estadunidenses e ucranianas ouvidas pelo The Wall Street Journal, o serviço começou a funcionar de maneira mais regular na quinta-feira (22), pouco depois da conversa.
A melhora, porém, não foi uniforme. Enquanto alguns militares ucranianos relataram velocidades mais altas, outros continuaram enfrentando as mesmas limitações. Autoridades do país também afirmaram que o sistema ainda não havia recuperado totalmente sua capacidade.
Segundo fontes ouvidas pelo jornal, Trump demonstrou frustração com o limite de velocidade. A restrição impedia que alguns drones de ataque e interceptadores ucranianos mantivessem a conexão com a rede de satélites durante deslocamentos rápidos, reduzindo sua capacidade de responder aos ataques russos.
Em declaração a jornalistas nesta quinta-feira (22), Trump evitou comentar diretamente a ligação com Musk, mas afirmou: “Não comento nem de um lado nem de outro”. Em seguida, acrescentou: “O resultado final: ele colocou de volta”.
Musk e a SpaceX não responderam aos pedidos de comentário do Journal.
Starlink voltou a funcionar melhor, mas não totalmente
- A retomada parcial do serviço pode ampliar a capacidade militar ucraniana de utilizar drones e interceptadores movidos a jato. Esses equipamentos dependem da conexão via satélite para determinadas operações, e a limitação de velocidade dificultava seu funcionamento;
- Michael Kofman, especialista em guerra da organização Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, afirmou que a retirada da restrição pode ajudar a Ucrânia a ampliar sua capacidade de ataque a alvos em profundidade operacional, além de acelerar a expansão do uso de interceptadores a jato;
- Segundo o especialista, unidades militares ucranianas relataram que os primeiros testes indicavam um funcionamento mais regular do sistema;
- Um representante ucraniano, porém, afirmou que algumas unidades já haviam registrado velocidades maiores, enquanto outras continuavam submetidas ao limite anterior;
- “Continuamos aguardando informações e esclarecimentos do lado estadunidense sobre a situação. Ainda não houve resposta”, declarou o funcionário.
Leia mais:
- Dependência da Starlink preocupa governos e expõe poder de Elon Musk
- Musk ordenou restrição do Starlink usado pela Ucrânia, diz jornal
- SpaceSail: rival chinesa da Starlink avança no mercado brasileiro
Governo Trump apresenta versões diferentes
A ligação ocorre em meio a uma semana de questionamentos sobre quem ordenou a redução da velocidade do Starlink e qual foi o papel do governo estadunidense na decisão.
Trump e Musk haviam criticado publicamente o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, depois de ataques ucranianos a refinarias russas de diesel. Trump atribuiu a esses ataques parte da responsabilidade pelos preços elevados da energia.
A redução da velocidade do Starlink veio dias depois dessas declarações e contribuiu para agravar as relações entre Washington e Kiev, que chegaram ao nível mais baixo em meses.
Trump negou repetidamente ter ordenado a restrição ou saber quem havia tomado a decisão. A Casa Branca também remeteu o Journal às declarações anteriores do presidente.
O vice-presidente estadunidense, JD Vance, defendeu a posição de Musk na quinta-feira. Segundo ele, é compreensível que o empresário não queira se envolver em uma guerra sem que o governo dos Estados Unidos determine efetivamente como sua empresa deve atuar.
“Não acho que isso seja sobre Elon. Acho que se trata fundamentalmente de qual será a política dos Estados Unidos em relação à Ucrânia e à Rússia”, afirmou Vance.
A declaração contrasta com as posições apresentadas pelo secretário de Defesa, Pete Hegseth, e pelo secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio. Ambos afirmaram que Musk tinha autoridade para aplicar os termos de serviço da empresa sem orientação do governo. “Existem termos de serviço que precisam ser cumpridos e, em última análise, é a Starlink que tem a opção de tomar essas decisões”, declarou Hegseth no início da semana.
As versões divergentes mantêm em aberto a questão sobre se a redução da conectividade foi uma decisão independente da SpaceX ou se houve participação da administração Trump.
Senador estadunidense abre investigação
O caso também levantou preocupações sobre a dependência do Pentágono em relação à SpaceX para comunicações via satélite consideradas críticas.
Na quinta-feira, o senador Richard Blumenthal, democrata de Connecticut, anunciou investigação sobre a redução da capacidade da Starlink na Ucrânia sem aviso prévio. A apuração também examinará as implicações da dependência do Departamento de Defesa em relação à empresa de Musk.
Enquanto isso, a Ucrânia continua enfrentando ataques russos. Na madrugada de quinta-feira, Moscou lançou outra grande ofensiva contra Kiev, a capital ucraniana, um dia depois de a Rússia afirmar que havia concordado com negociações trilaterais com os Estados Unidos e a Ucrânia para tentar encerrar a guerra.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Startup Battlefield 200: Celebrating outstanding achievements | TechCrunch
articles.text:
This year, TechCrunch Disrupt showcased the incredible talent and groundbreaking ideas of our 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 cohort.
Out of thousands of applications, we selected 200 of the most promising startups, each bringing unique innovations to their respective industries. The competition culminated in an electrifying event where these startups had the opportunity to pitch and demonstrate their solutions live over three days.
From the top 20 finalists, TechCrunch editorial selected the top five companies that then battled it out for the $100,000 equity-free prize and the coveted Disrupt Cup. The well-deserved win went to Intero Biosystems, with a strong runner-up, Apate.
Among the Startup Battlefield 200 were many industry-defining companies exhibiting and pitching on the Showcase Stage. Here are the standouts:
Best Showcase Stage pitch by industry group
Built World
Lola Vision Systems provides a full-stack AI platform delivering sensor fusion, secure communications, and real-time inference on today’s hardware, with purpose-built silicon on the horizon.
Sustainability
Krokos Bio is growing nature’s most valuable ingredients, in a way that is cheaper and more reliable, starting with saffron.
Enterprise Group 1
Rein Security is the security layer for custom-built enterprise agents — the production AI agents running businesses worldwide.
Enterprise Group 2
Lumai is the optical compute company addressing scalable AI in the inference era.
Health
Uhura Bionics has developed a bionic larynx for singing, laughing, and translating emotions.
Consumer
Maka is delivering developmentally curated shows parents trust and kids love — powered by AI.
Best Booth
Legali AI is providing a trauma-informed AI legal companion and ecosystem for the middle class and AI-native firms, with a focus on women who’ve faced abuse. Their all-pink, female-focused booth was a standout on the Expo Floor. Visitors would write empowering messages to women on sticky notes and place them on Legali AI’s banner while learning more about the wonderful work they’re doing. Founder Ira Puteri also made a point of coordinating different pink outfits each day. Love the commitment!
Spirit of Disrupt award
The Spirit of Disrupt award unanimously goes to Shogher Atanesyan, founder and CEO of Ardook Data. Her journey to the Startup Battlefield 200 is inspiring, with her first exposure to Disrupt as a volunteer back in 2023. She had reached out to the Battlefield team last year, with a simple request to make “Social Impact” a stand-alone category in the Event App. We were happy to oblige, and just a few short months later she applied for the competition. She made it in on her own merits, as the review team loved the concept of capturing real-world household training data from a willing and paid caregiver network. The data is then sold to physical AI and robotics companies in need of it.
Atanesyan may be the most selfless founder we’ve seen in five years of managing the Startup Battlefield 200. Specifically, what she did for visitors to San Francisco. She organized dozens of student volunteers to help these startups manage their booths, coordinated numerous items shipped to her house to circumvent steep shipping costs, and hosted a party for these founders at her house. Additionally, she consistently helped founders who had questions in our community Discord and weekly calls.
The Startup Battlefield is more than a pitch competition; it’s an opportunity to build relationships with investors, potential customers, and fellow founders to support each other on their entrepreneurial journeys. 
As we celebrate the achievements of this year’s winners, we are excited to see how they will shape their industries and drive innovation in the months and years to come. Congratulations to all the participants of the Startup Battlefield 200, and a special thank-you to our judges and sponsors for their support in making TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 a resounding success.

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.text:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness
Published in the journal Cognition, the study was led by Dr. Louis Longin of LMU's Chair of Philosophy of Mind, working alongside Dr. Bahador Bahrami, Professor Ophelia Deroy, and other researchers.
"Whereas previous studies have typically asked general questions about whether AI actually has mental states, our study is the first to directly compare how people attribute the same mental states to AI and humans behaving in exactly the same way, under identical circumstances," says Longin.
"We may be using mental terms to refer to AI, but this may only be because we lack better words," says Ophelia Deroy, philosopher and a senior author of the study. "After all, AI is trained to act and speak like a human, so these descriptions seem natural."
To investigate how people judge consciousness, the researchers conducted experiments involving nearly 1,100 participants. One group read brief descriptions of artificial agents that showed different levels of responsiveness to their environments. For example, some agents reacted to sounds or recognized the emotional states of others.
Another group encountered the same situations, except the characters were described as humans rather than AI systems. Participants then evaluated how conscious or aware each character seemed to be of its surroundings.
A Surprising Gap Between Human and AI Consciousness
The experiments revealed that responsiveness influenced how participants judged both humans and artificial intelligence. Characters that reacted more actively to their surroundings were generally considered more conscious and more aware.
However, a striking difference emerged when participants evaluated consciousness specifically. Even the most responsive AI was rated as less conscious than the least responsive human. In other words, identical behavior did not lead people to assign the same level of consciousness to humans and machines.
The results changed considerably when participants were asked about awareness instead. For this characteristic, judgments of humans and AI followed largely similar patterns, suggesting that people interpret awareness and consciousness in fundamentally different ways.
"There is a growing worry in public discussion that people will see AI behaving in a human-like way and start treating these systems as if they had human-like mental states," says Longin, lead author of the study. "We found something much more nuanced: People are quite willing to say that an AI notices things and is aware of its surroundings. But they clearly draw a line when it comes to the term 'consciousness'. People consistently attribute less consciousness to AI than humans -- even when their behavior is identical."
Although people sometimes describe AI as conscious when discussing its actions, the findings indicate that they still distinguish between artificial systems and human minds.
Why One Word Changes How We Perceive AI
The researchers believe the difference between consciousness and awareness offers an important insight into how people understand artificial intelligence.
Awareness is a relatively neutral term that can describe an agent's ability to detect and respond to information in its environment. Consciousness, however, carries deeper implications about subjective experience and what it means to have an inner mental life.
Because awareness focuses more directly on observable behavior, people appear comfortable applying it to both humans and AI. Consciousness carries a different meaning, leading people to judge the two much less similarly.
The findings also highlight why the language used to discuss artificial intelligence matters, particularly as AI systems become increasingly capable of producing convincing human behavior.
"Our study teaches us lessons for how we communicate about AI," says Bahador Bahrami, who is also a senior author of the study and an expert in social neuroscience. "Companies and journalists often reach for hyped descriptions of AI models, and credit them with intentions, plans, or even moral conscience and hesitation. What our study shows is that everyday judgments are much more discriminating: People do not simply put AI and humans on the same mental scale. But the boundary also depends on which terms we use. For more neutral descriptors such as 'awareness', the distinction can largely disappear. That makes our choice of language important."
Story Source:
Materials provided by Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Louis Longin, Jurgis Karpus, Nadine Meertens, Bahador Bahrami, Ophelia Deroy. AI is not as conscious as humans: Essentialism in mental state attributions to artificial systems. Cognition, 2027; 278: 106733 DOI: 10.1016/j.cognition.2026.106733

articles.title: Meta turns Muse sharing back on
articles.text:
Meta has re-enabled Muse sharing after security researchers had reported that public conversation links could be easy to find. The researchers said they had been able to find Muse pages like a marketing company’s internal revenue review and a small business owner’s loan application.
Meta turns Muse sharing back on
Meta has given new URLs to shared Muse ‘artifacts’ after security researchers reported that public links could be easy to find.
Researchers at Claroc reported earlier this week that Muse the web addresses for shared conversations from Muse were named after a conversation’s title and written into public DNS. Ars Technica said Tuesday that Meta paused the sharing feature after it reached out about what was going on.
In a post today on X, Meta’s David Singleton says that “The underlying issue is now fixed, and sharing is back on.” According to Singleton, the issue was with URLs for shared Muse artifacts, which Meta says are things like documents and images inside Muse, and wasn’t a flaw with chat sharing.
“If you shared an artifact before the fix: it now has a new URL,” Singleton says. “Anyone visiting the old link will see a note asking them to get the new one from you. We know that’s a pain, and we’re sorry for the disruption — but protecting user data has to come first.”

articles.title: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence
articles.text:
At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure.
Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA, powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs, Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x.
“Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.”
Training on Accelerated Infrastructure
Starling Bank, the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data.
Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM, a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases.
SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls.
Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost
Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them.
Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer.
NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR.
Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model.
Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads.
Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research
LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the Polars GPU engine, accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs.
RavenPack built a dataset generation pipeline on Bigdata.com that takes a plain-language research hypothesis and returns a labeled, backtest-ready dataset — running on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron model. Investors can use these datasets to identify, analyze and visualize market trends.
Speeding Data Pipelines to Improve Fraud Detection
RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and NVIDIA cuDF help accelerate data processing across multi-terabyte-scale, siloed, regulated sources, compressing the time from data to decision for fraud and other scenarios.
HSBC provides near-real-time client insights that support customer processes and on-demand decision-making while minimizing risk and fraud, powered by 5x faster data processing on Starburst Enterprise’s GPU Engine.
Stripe, a global provider of programmable financial services, sees 42x faster data pipelines and 92% cost savings for its Stripe Radar fraud-detection platform with NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Ray Data in offline testing. This enables Stripe Radar’s machine learning pipelines to continuously optimize model training and improve fraud detection.
Learn more about NVIDIA accelerated computing in financial services.

articles.title: What Breaks When Packaging Moves From Wafer To Panel?
articles.text:
Engineers are discovering many things they thought were process assumptions were actually wafer assumptions.
Key Takeaways:
Moving advanced packaging from wafer to panel sounds, at first, like a geometry problem. Large AI and HPC packages are increasingly rectangular, while the 300mm wafer underneath them is still round. As the package size grows, more of that expensive processing ends up around the circle’s edges where nothing useful can be built.
A panel gives that area back. It can fit more large packages into the same process cycle, and unlike a wafer, its dimensions don’t impose the same hard limit on the size of a square or rectangular package. For advanced packages that keep getting larger, the economics are difficult to ignore.
But the semiconductor packaging sector has spent decades learning how to process wafers, not panels. Equipment, materials, recipes, handling systems, and process controls were all developed around the geometry and mechanical behavior of a round workpiece.
“The risk of doing the assembly on the 600mm panel is high, and I don’t think we have all the equipment today to run the process,” said Teck Chong Lee, technical director of advanced fan-out development for HPC applications at ASE, in a recent presentation. “One of the options is, once you complete the interposer in large format in 600, then you divide it into four pieces to run the assembly and the C4 process. This is a much lower-risk approach.”
The economics behind that compromise are substantial. In the same study, a 5.5×-reticle-size interposer produced 9 units on a 300mm wafer, compared with 16 on a 300mm panel. A 600mm panel divided into four 300mm pieces produces 64, while processing the full 600mm area intact raises that to 72. In pure utilization, the intact panel produces 8 times as many units as the wafer, a gain well beyond the roughly fivefold difference in raw area, because the rectangular panel wastes almost nothing at its edges.
The flow therefore takes the area advantage where it can use it, then gives some of it back before assembly because the manufacturing infrastructure isn’t ready to follow the larger format all the way through. That compromise exposes the larger transition underway. Moving packaging from wafer to panel isn’t simply making the process bigger. It is discovering which parts of the process were dependent on the wafer dimensions all along.
The process was built around the wafer
The utilization advantage grows as the package does. In one comparison, Intel Foundry used a 510 × 515mm panel and showed that a roughly 4× reticle package would produce about 10 units on a 300mm wafer and approximately 48 on the panel. Eventually the wafer imposes a harder geometric limit, since the largest square that fits on a 300mm wafer is only about 210 × 210mm.
“For certain form factors, we believe a wafer is more economical,” said Tarek Ibrahim, senior principal engineer at Intel, in a conference presentation. “However, when you go beyond a certain form factor, you can see quickly that the panel becomes more effective, mainly because you can get more units out of a panel. Because of the way AI is heading and the need for a very large system, panels became an obvious choice for scale.”
Fig. 1: Intel’s Tarek Ibrahim discusses substrate scaling for heterogeneous integration. Source: Semiconductor Engineering
The economic crossover doesn’t mean the manufacturing process crosses over with it. Much of the equipment and process knowledge used in advanced packaging was developed for a round wafer, and changing the shape and scale of the substrate changes what those processes have to do. Over time, many of those wafer-specific assumptions became invisible because the workpiece underneath them rarely changed. What looked like a requirement of the process was often just a requirement of the wafer.
“At wafer level, it’s a single-sided process,” Ibrahim said. “On panel, it’s actually a dual-sided process. Managing the process at that panel scale with the right uniformity and the right Cpk [process capability index] is definitely a challenge.”
Part of the challenge is that familiar wafer processes don’t always transfer cleanly to a larger rectangular surface. Spin coating, for example, relies on radial symmetry, so a rectangular substrate produces uneven film thickness toward the corners while most of the dispensed resist is thrown away. In a 600mm panel flow, photoresist is instead deposited by slit or slot-die coating across an active area of roughly 586 × 586mm. Lithography also changes, with maskless direct imaging displacing the conventional wafer stepper in many panel flows.
Those differences propagate into the materials and equipment surrounding the process. Fine-line RDL on glass panels is pushing toward new photoresists and application methods, tighter overlay control, and equipment that can maintain temperature and process uniformity across a much larger area. Large hot plates become a development problem of their own. As line and space moves from roughly 5µm toward 2µm and below, processes that historically belonged farther back in the packaging flow begin demanding something closer to front-end precision.
The awkward part is that the panel can’t simply inherit the front-end equipment built to provide that precision. Much of that infrastructure assumes a round 300mm wafer, while traditional substrate equipment was designed around different feature sizes and process tolerances. Panel-level packaging is landing somewhere between the two.
The result is less a scaled-up wafer flow than a new manufacturing process being assembled from pieces of several older ones. The panel solves an increasingly expensive geometry problem, but it also exposes how many coating, exposure, handling, and uniformity assumptions were tied to the wafer that came before it.
Yield decides how big is useful
The simplest argument for a larger panel is that more packages fit on it. The real economic question is how many good packages come off.
That matters more as the value assembled onto the workpiece rises. A panel carrying logic and HBM can contain tens of thousands of dollars of known-good silicon before some package-level failures become visible. At that point, even a small yield loss can erase the savings created by processing more area at once.
“There’s so much money in chips going onto a wafer or panel that a tiny yield hit, and the loss of some of that super-expensive silicon, will just blow all the benefits from a larger scale that you had right out the window,” said Mike Kelly, vice president of chiplets and FCBGA integration at Amkor. “Defects are going to happen. It’s not defect-free, so you’ve got to have a great way to repair and not suffer yield loss. Otherwise, you’ve lost the whole benefit of getting large.”
That makes rework capability a design requirement, instead of a contingency. A panel that cannot be repaired converts every localized defect into a loss proportional to how much value the panel is carrying, which is precisely the value the larger format was adopted to accumulate.
ASE’s numbers show the tradeoff directly. Preserving the extra 12.5% of usable area that comes with keeping the 600mm panel intact also carries the process into the format that Lee describes as more difficult to control and not yet supported by all the necessary assembly equipment.
The largest manufacturable panel therefore may not be the most economical one. More area makes each process cycle more productive, but it also puts more value at risk when something goes wrong. The practical limit is set by yield as much as geometry.
The panel carries its history forward
Yield at the panel scale depends on more than defect density. It also depends on how predictably the panel behaves as it moves through the flow, because every operation leaves it slightly different for the next one.
Materials are heated, cured, deposited, plated, and cleaned as the package advances. Dimensions can shift, stress can build, and material properties can change with temperature and processing. What arrives at the next tool therefore isn’t quite the same structure that arrived at the one before it.
It therefore makes sense to take measurements when the package changes state. But those state changes become harder to manage as the workpiece gets larger. At wafer scale, decades of manufacturing experience have established how much movement particular processes tend to create and how much the next operation can tolerate. A panel adds a much larger area across which those changes have to remain predictable and uniform, often using materials and process combinations with far less production history.
Glass can reduce part of that movement. In tests simulating the formation of two RDL layers, dimensional stability improved significantly as the substrate moved from standard high-Tg organic material to ultra-low-CTE material and then to glass.
“The standard high-Tg material showed an average shift of about 22 microns at three sigma,” said Lars Boettcher, group manager for substrate and panel technologies at Fraunhofer Institute for Reliability and Microintegration (IZM), in a conference presentation. “The ultra-low-CTE material was much better and more homogeneous, but still in the range of seven microns. With the glass core, it was very uniform and somewhere around three microns, although that may already be approaching the measurement accuracy of the machine we used.”
Better dimensional stability doesn’t mean the rest of the structure stops moving, however. Thermal processing can still change where dies end up, and on a large panel that movement may vary across the surface rather than behaving like a single offset that can be corrected in the next step.
“The glass carrier is rigid and could be CTE-matched to silicon or other structures on the package. It is very stable with a smooth surface, which allows for fine-pitch processing,” said Hamed Gholami Derami, business development engineer for packaging solutions at Brewer Science. “However, one of the limits of using glass could be the non-linear die shift during thermal processing, which makes it hard to correct for die shift, especially for large glass panels.”
That turns process history into an alignment problem. A die can be placed correctly early in the flow and still arrive somewhere else later because curing, deposition, or another thermal step changed the surrounding structure. The next layer has to be built on the panel that actually exists at that moment, not on the coordinates carried forward from the original design.
The same history complicates simulation. Mechanical properties such as Young’s modulus and shear modulus, which describe a material’s stiffness under tensile and shear loading, can change with temperature, and newer glass and polymer systems don’t always have the mature characterization data available for silicon. Generic properties can provide a starting point, but the model still has to estimate how much stress and warpage each process step will introduce before engineers commit material and equipment to an actual build.
“Before you fail your manufacturing or your yield, do simulation. Don’t speculate,” said Lang Lin, product management principal at Synopsys. “Do a simulation with general properties and general processes and see how much warpage and stress each process creates, and then start your experiment.”
The limitation is that a generic model can only go so far. Accurate prediction eventually depends on the behavior of the actual materials in the stack, including how those properties change with temperature and processing. Some of the best data for doing that also may be proprietary. A material or substrate supplier can provide enough characterization data to improve the model without necessarily revealing the formulation or manufacturing details that produced it.
That leaves panel manufacturing as much a feedback problem as a modeling problem. Each process changes the physical structure that the next process receives, while measurements and models must keep catching up with those changes. The larger the panel becomes, the more expensive it is to discover late in the flow that one of those earlier assumptions was wrong.
Dicing the panel creates another problem
ASE’s mixed-format flow manages that risk by creating a new boundary in the process, but it only works if the 600mm glass panel can survive becoming four smaller ones.
“You have to design the layout of the 600mm panel from the start around how it will eventually be separated into four 300mm panels,” said ASE’s Lee. “It’s not a single dicing process. It involves several steps, plus some edge processing to remove the sharp edge.”
That makes the cut an upstream design constraint. The panel layout has to anticipate where the eventual separation will occur, while the dicing process must avoid leaving chips or damaged edges that can turn into breakage during the assembly steps that follow. ASE found that simply cutting the panel wasn’t enough. The separation process required multiple operations followed by edge treatment before the smaller panels could continue through the flow.
The cut edge isn’t the only place glass can carry damage forward. Through-glass vias introduce another stress concentration inside the material, because copper and glass expand at different rates as temperature changes. During heating, the copper expands more rapidly and protrudes, concentrating compressive stress in the surrounding glass. As the structure cools, the copper contracts and pulls on the glass sidewall, creating tensile stress that can drive a circumferential crack into the surrounding material. Finding those cracks introduces its own process-control problem.
“There is no standardization in the industry today,” said Poulomi Mukherjee, process integration engineer for advanced packaging at Applied Materials, in a conference presentation. “We need to figure out what would be the correct thermal testing, because finding the glass cracks is not that easy. So there’s a lot of metrology there, as well.”
That pushes inspection upstream for much the same reason dicing moved upstream. A panel can survive one operation while carrying edge damage or an internal crack that becomes consequential only after another thermal cycle, handling step, or assembly operation. By the time the failure becomes obvious, substantially more value may already have been added to the panel.
Some of the necessary controls do not exist yet. Important defects can be buried inside interconnects, while unfamiliar combinations of materials create correlations manufacturers are still learning how to recognize. A recipe can also work in a controlled demonstration and then encounter variation once it begins moving across lots and multiple tools.
“When it became mass production, there was still a learning curve to be done,” said Tiago Tavares, program and project manager at Critical Manufacturing. “You have to implement the controls ahead, and some of the controls you need to invent because they are not yet there.”
The larger economic argument for panel processing therefore depends on more than getting additional packages onto a larger workpiece. The process also has to find damage early enough that the additional area doesn’t simply create more expensive material to lose.
Conclusion
The usual picture of panel-level packaging assumes the industry eventually settles on a standard large format and builds an equipment ecosystem around it, much as semiconductor manufacturing converged on 300mm wafers.
ASE’s mixed-format approach suggests the transition may be less tidy. A 600mm panel can be the right answer when utilization dominates the economics, but not the right answer later, when yield, handling, or equipment availability become more important. Cutting it down sacrifices some area efficiency but returns the workpiece to a manufacturing environment that is easier to control.
Different parts of the flow may arrive at different answers. Coating and RDL benefit from the larger area, while assembly may favor a smaller format. Dicing has to anticipate what comes afterward. Inspection has to find damage before more value is added. Repair has to be possible once it does. And the accumulated thermal and mechanical history of the panel can change what the next tool is actually being asked to process.
For years, the wafer made many of those choices invisible because the equipment, materials, and process assumptions had already converged around it. Panel-level packaging is forcing engineers to make them explicit again. The industry may eventually standardize the panel, but first it has to separate what belongs to the process from what only looked like it did because there was always a wafer underneath it.

articles.title: Telstra to enable RCS to enrich messaging between iPhone and Android users - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Telstra has announced it will be enabling Rich Communication Services (RCS) from next month to allow a better messaging experience between Android smartphones and iPhones.
This comes almost 3 years after Apple officially decided to adopt RCS to improve texting between iPhone and Android with higher quality and security.
The difference between iPhone and Android messaging has been clearly obvious without RCS with blue and green bubbles in the message thread.
The blue bubbles indicate it came from an iPhone or was part of iMessage and green showing the message came from an Android device.
RCS not only provides greater security but also other features like read receipts and indications when the other person is typing their reply.
Will also allow sharing of images and videos in their full quality. Pre-RCS communication between iPhone and Android users meant attachments were severely compressed.
Until now these messaging features were only available for iPhone-to-iPhone and Android-to-Android messaging.
RCS will finally fill the great divide between iPhone and Android messaging.
Telstra to roll out RCS for Android customers from November 16, with iOS customers able to use RCS after the December iOS release.
Telstra’s RCS rollout is scheduled for completion by the end of 2026.
No word on when Optus and Vodafone will run their own respective RCS rollouts.
With Telstra being the first mover, the RCS experience between iPhone and Android users will likely be restricted to communication between Telstra customers.
The RCS upgrade will also apply to MVNOs (mobile virtual network operators) using the Telstra network, including Belong and Aldi Mobile.

articles.title: Fermeture de BioWare : la série Mass Effect de Prime Video est-elle condamnée ?
articles.text:
Fermeture de BioWare : la série Mass Effect de Prime Video est-elle condamnée ?
En développement depuis 2024, le projet de série adaptée de la franchise de jeux vidéo Mass Effect est toujours d'actualité chez Prime Video malgré la fermeture de BioWare et l'annulation du jeu Mass Effect 5.
Electronic Arts a annoncé hier le licenciement de 400 personnes et la fermeture de BioWare, ce qui signifie que le cinquième jeu de la franchise Mass Effect ne verra pas le jour.
Cependant, cela ne devrait pas affecter la série Mass Effect en prises de vues réelles en développement chez Prime Video depuis plusieurs années.
Tout est encore possible sur Prime Video
Des sources au sein de Prime Video ont confirmé auprès de nos confrères d'IGN que la série Mass Effect en développement chez Amazon MGM Studios demeure d'actualité.
Tous les membres de l'équipe créative sont toujours rattachés au projet, sous la direction des co-showrunners Doug Jung (Mindhunter) et Daniel Casey (Fast & Furious 9), avec Karim Zreik, Ari Arad et Michael Gamble en tant que producteurs exécutifs.
En développement depuis 2024, cette série Mass Effect devrait se dérouler après les événements de la première trilogie de jeux vidéo, qui se concentre sur le commandant Shepard, un soldat du XXIIe siècle tentant de sauver l'humanité d'une espèce extraterrestre appelée les Moissonneurs.
La rumeur voulait que la série Mass Effect entre en tournage d'ici à la fin 2026 mais aux dernières nouvelles, sa production n'est pas encore programmée, pas plus que sa date de sortie en streaming.

articles.title: Arnaques sur Booking : l'Europe ouvre une enquête suite à une vague d'escroqueries
articles.text:
Ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026, la Commission européenne a ouvert une enquête visant la plateforme de réservation d’hébergement Booking. C’est la première fois que l’Europe cible cette plateforme. Concrètement, dans le cadre du Digital Services Act (DSA), l’enquête a pour objectif de déterminer si Booking met en place assez de mesures pour protéger ses clients des arnaques et autres annonces trompeuses qui circulent sur le web. Pour Henna Virkkunen, vice-présidente de la Commission européenne chargée de la souveraineté technologique : « Les Européens doivent pouvoir réserver leurs vacances sans craindre d’être arnaqués ».
Booking visé par une enquête de la Commission européenne
Une responsable de la Commission européenne, qui a désiré rester anonyme, explique : « De nombreuses plaintes ont été déposées, notamment par des associations de consommateurs et des organisations d’hôteliers ». Ce sont ces plaintes qui ont abouti à l’ouverture de cette enquête visant Booking.
La Commission européenne veut donc s’assurer que la plateforme a mis en place des mesures efficaces pour protéger ses clients des arnaques en ligne. Certains arnaqueurs usurpent par exemple l’identité de Booking pour ensuite poster de fausses annonces d’hébergement. La plateforme a d’ailleurs elle-même alerté les Français concernant une potentielle nouvelle vague d’arnaques cet hiver. Bruxelles veut également se pencher sur la façon dont Booking lutte contre les tentatives d’hameçonnage. Les mails provenant soi-disant de Booking et demandant de cliquer sur un lien (frauduleux) ne sont malheureusement pas rares.
Enfin, la Commission européenne va étudier la façon dont les annonces boostées sur les réseaux sociaux sont mises en avant par Booking. L’exécutif européen explique que « les utilisateurs devraient pouvoir reconnaître clairement que ces “annonces boostées” sont en réalité des publicités ». Si la Commission remarque des manquements, Booking pourrait se voir infliger une amende.
Booking réagit
La plateforme Booking a annoncé auprès de l’AFP qu’elle « coopère pleinement avec la Commission européenne et répond de manière constructive à ses questions ». Elle précise ensuite : « La sécurité, la confiance et la protection des données personnelles sont des priorités absolues. Nous restons déterminés à travailler avec les gouvernements concernés, les autorités de régulation, les forces de l’ordre et les acteurs du secteur afin de lutter contre la cybercriminalité et la fraude en ligne et de protéger les voyageurs ainsi que nos partenaires ».
Avant l’ouverture de cette enquête, Booking avait assuré auprès du Parisien avoir neutralisé 26 000 tentatives d’arnaques en 2025. La plateforme a par ailleurs annoncé avoir renforcé ses systèmes de contrôle à l’aide de l’intelligence artificielle. Il reste maintenant à voir si la Commission européenne sera convaincue.

articles.title: Fin du suspense pour les Gardiens : Chris Pratt confirme le retour de Star-Lord
articles.text:
En pleine promotion de la saison 2 de The Terminal List, sortie ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026 sur Prime Video, Chris Pratt s’est confié au podcast The Bingeworthy, du site The Playlist. Ses propos ont été relayés par Variety le même jour.
Pas de langue de bois ni de fausse modestie : Kevin Feige et Lou D’Esposito orchestrent activement la réintroduction du personnage. « Il y a des conversations continues sur la façon de tenir cette promesse, mais aussi des actions concrètes déjà engagées », a-t-il balancé sans détour, avant d’enfoncer le clou : « Vous reverrez Star-Lord, il ne va nulle part. »
Avengers: Doomsday et Secret Wars en ligne de mire
Pour la maison Marvel, l’équation est presque trop simple. Après le départ de James Gunn parti diriger l’écurie concurrente chez DC, le personnage de Peter Quill s’était retiré sur Terre pour couler des jours paisibles auprès de son grand-père. Mais face à la déferlante du multivers et l’arrivée de Robert Downey Jr. sous le masque du Doctor Doom, la retraite sera de courte durée.
Joe et Anthony Russo, réalisateurs d’Infinity War et d’Endgame, ont laissé entendre que tout le casting d’Avengers: Doomsday n’avait pas encore été dévoilé. Ramener la caution comico-cosmique des Gardiens au milieu du chaos multiversel permettrait d’apporter un liant nostalgique précieux à une franchise en quête désespérée de repères.
La piste Nova
Si l’appel aux armes face à Doom dans Avengers Doomsday reste la fenêtre de tir la plus évidente, une autre porte de sortie se dessine dans les bureaux de Marvel Studios. Le scénariste Michael Waldron (Loki) planche actuellement sur le projet Nova, centré sur Richard Rider.
L’introduction de la célèbre police intergalactique, dont les bases avaient été posées dès le premier film de James Gunn avant d’être rasées hors champ par Thanos offre le prétexte idéal pour sortir Peter Quill de sa torpeur terrienne. Qu’il s’agisse de jouer les mentors usés ou de reprendre le volant d’un vaisseau pour prêter main-forte aux centurions de Xandar, Star-Lord n’a clairement pas fini de squatter les écrans.
